gn.1.1	Genesis 1:1	In the beginning God created the Heauen, and the Earth.
gn.1.2	Genesis 1:2	And the earth was without forme, and voyd, and darkenesse was vpon the face of the deepe: and the Spirit of God mooued vpon the face of the waters.
gn.1.3	Genesis 1:3	And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
gn.1.4	Genesis 1:4	And God saw the light, that it was good: and God diuided the light from the darkenesse.
gn.1.5	Genesis 1:5	And God called the light, Day, and the darknesse he called Night: and the euening and the morning were the first day.
gn.1.6	Genesis 1:6	¶ And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters: and let it diuide the waters from the waters.
gn.1.7	Genesis 1:7	And God made the firmament; and diuided the waters, which were vnder the firmament, from the waters, which were aboue the firmament: and it was so.
gn.1.8	Genesis 1:8	And God called the firmament, Heauen: and the euening and the morning were the second day.
gn.1.9	Genesis 1:9	¶ And God said, Let the waters vnder the heauen be gathered together vnto one place, and let the dry land appeare: and it was so.
gn.1.10	Genesis 1:10	And God called the drie land, Earth, and the gathering together of the waters called hee, Seas: and God saw that it was good.
gn.1.11	Genesis 1:11	And God said, Let the Earth bring foorth grasse, the herbe yeelding seed, and the fruit tree, yeelding fruit after his kinde, whose seed is in it selfe, vpon the earth: and it was so.
gn.1.12	Genesis 1:12	And the earth brought foorth grasse, and herbe yeelding seed after his kinde, and the tree yeelding fruit, whose seed was in it selfe, after his kinde: and God saw that it was good.
gn.1.13	Genesis 1:13	And the euening and the morning were the third day.
gn.1.14	Genesis 1:14	¶ And God said, Let there bee lights in the firmament of the heauen, to diuide the day from the night: and let them be for signes and for seasons, and for dayes and yeeres.
gn.1.15	Genesis 1:15	And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heauen, to giue light vpon the earth: and it was so.
gn.1.16	Genesis 1:16	And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the starres also.
gn.1.17	Genesis 1:17	And God set them in the firmament of the heauen, to giue light vpon the earth:
gn.1.18	Genesis 1:18	And to rule ouer the day, and ouer the night, and to diuide the light from the darkenesse: and God saw that it was good.
gn.1.19	Genesis 1:19	And the euening and the morning were the fourth day.
gn.1.20	Genesis 1:20	And God said, Let the waters bring foorth aboundantly the mouing creature that hath life, and foule that may flie aboue the earth in the open firmament of heauen.
gn.1.21	Genesis 1:21	And God created great whales, and euery liuing creature that moueth, which the waters brought forth aboundantly after their kinde, and euery winged foule after his kinde: and God saw that it was good.
gn.1.22	Genesis 1:22	And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitfull, and multiply, and fill the waters in the Seas, and let foule multiply in the earth.
gn.1.23	Genesis 1:23	And the euening and the morning were the fift day.
gn.1.24	Genesis 1:24	¶ And God said, Let the earth bring forth the liuing creature after his kinde, cattell, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kinde: and it was so.
gn.1.25	Genesis 1:25	And God made the beast of the earth after his kinde, and cattell after their kinde, and euery thing that creepeth vpon the earth, after his kinde: and God saw that it was good.
gn.1.26	Genesis 1:26	¶ And God said, Let vs make man in our Image, after our likenesse: and let them haue dominion ouer the fish of the sea, and ouer the foule of the aire, and ouer the cattell, and ouer all the earth, and ouer euery creeping thing that creepeth vpon the earth.
gn.1.27	Genesis 1:27	So God created man in his owne Image, in the Image of God created hee him; male and female created hee them.
gn.1.28	Genesis 1:28	And God blessed them, and God said vnto them, Be fruitfull, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and haue dominion ouer the fish of the sea, and ouer the foule of the aire, and ouer euery liuing thing that mooueth vpon the earth.
gn.1.29	Genesis 1:29	¶ And God said, Behold, I haue giuen you euery herbe bearing seede, which is vpon the face of all the earth, and euery tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yeelding seed, to you it shall be for meat:
gn.1.30	Genesis 1:30	And to euery beast of the earth, and to euery foule of the aire, and to euery thing that creepeth vpon the earth, wherein there is life, I haue giuen euery greene herbe for meat: and it was so.
gn.1.31	Genesis 1:31	And God saw euery thing that hee had made: and behold, it was very good. And the euening and the morning were the sixth day.
gn.2.1	Genesis 2:1	Thus the heauens and the earth were finished, and all the hoste of them.
gn.2.2	Genesis 2:2	And on the seuenth day God ended his worke, which hee had made: And he rested on the seuenth day from all his worke, which he had made.
gn.2.3	Genesis 2:3	And God blessed the seuenth day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his worke, which God created and made.
gn.2.4	Genesis 2:4	¶ These are the generations of the heauens, & of the earth, when they were created; in the day that the LORD God made the earth, and the heauens,
gn.2.5	Genesis 2:5	And euery plant of the field, before it was in the earth, and euery herbe of the field, before it grew: for the LORD God had not caused it to raine vpon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground.
gn.2.6	Genesis 2:6	But there went vp a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.
gn.2.7	Genesis 2:7	And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, & breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a liuing soule.
gn.2.8	Genesis 2:8	¶ And the LORD God planted a garden Eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.
gn.2.9	Genesis 2:9	And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow euery tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food: the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and euill.
gn.2.10	Genesis 2:10	And a riuer went out of Eden to water the garden, and from thence it was parted, and became into foure heads.
gn.2.11	Genesis 2:11	The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Hauilah, where there is gold.
gn.2.12	Genesis 2:12	And the gold of that land is good: There is Bdellium and the Onix stone.
gn.2.13	Genesis 2:13	And the name of the second riuer is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.
gn.2.14	Genesis 2:14	And the name of the third riuer is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the East of Assyria: and the fourth riuer is Euphrates.
gn.2.15	Genesis 2:15	And the LORD God tooke the man, and put him into the garden of Eden, to dresse it, and to keepe it.
gn.2.16	Genesis 2:16	And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of euery tree of the garden thou mayest freely eate.
gn.2.17	Genesis 2:17	But of the tree of the knowledge of good and euill, thou shalt not eate of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof, thou shalt surely die.
gn.2.18	Genesis 2:18	¶ And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone: I will make him an helpe meet for him.
gn.2.19	Genesis 2:19	And out of þ ground the LORD God formed euery beast of the field, and euery foule of the aire, and brought them vnto Adam, to see what he would call them: and whatsoeuer Adam called euery liuing creature, that was the name thereof.
gn.2.20	Genesis 2:20	And Adam gaue names to all cattell, and to the foule of the aire, and to euery beast of the fielde: but for Adam there was not found an helpe meete for him.
gn.2.21	Genesis 2:21	And the LORD God caused a deepe sleepe to fall vpon Adam, and hee slept; and he tooke one of his ribs, and closed vp the flesh in stead thereof.
gn.2.22	Genesis 2:22	And the rib which the LORD God had taken from man, made hee a woman, & brought her vnto the man.
gn.2.23	Genesis 2:23	And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shalbe called woman, because shee was taken out of man.
gn.2.24	Genesis 2:24	Therefore shall a man leaue his father and his mother, and shall cleaue vnto his wife: and they shalbe one flesh.
gn.2.25	Genesis 2:25	And they were both naked, the man & his wife, and were not ashamed.
gn.3.1	Genesis 3:1	Now the serpent was more subtill then any beast of the field, which the LORD God had made, and he said vnto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of euery tree of the garden?
gn.3.2	Genesis 3:2	And the woman said vnto the serpent, Wee may eate of the fruite of the trees of the garden:
gn.3.3	Genesis 3:3	But of the fruit of the tree, which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shal not eate of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
gn.3.4	Genesis 3:4	And the Serpent said vnto the woman, Ye shall not surely die.
gn.3.5	Genesis 3:5	For God doeth know, that in the day ye eate thereof, then your eyes shalbee opened: and yee shall bee as Gods, knowing good and euill.
gn.3.6	Genesis 3:6	And when the woman saw, that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she tooke of the fruit thereof, and did eate, and gaue also vnto her husband with her, and hee did eate.
gn.3.7	Genesis 3:7	And the eyes of them both were opened, & they knew that they were naked, and they sewed figge leaues together, and made themselues aprons.
gn.3.8	Genesis 3:8	And they heard the voyce of the LORD God, walking in the garden in the coole of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselues from the presence of the LORD God, amongst the trees of the garden.
gn.3.9	Genesis 3:9	And the LORD God called vnto Adam, and said vnto him, Where art thou?
gn.3.10	Genesis 3:10	And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden: and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid my selfe.
gn.3.11	Genesis 3:11	And he said, Who told thee, that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee, that thou shouldest not eate?
gn.3.12	Genesis 3:12	And the man said, The woman whom thou gauest to be with mee, shee gaue me of the tree, and I did eate.
gn.3.13	Genesis 3:13	And the LORD God said vnto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The Serpent beguiled me, and I did eate.
gn.3.14	Genesis 3:14	And the LORD God said vnto the Serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed aboue all cattel, and aboue euery beast of the field: vpon thy belly shalt thou goe, and dust shalt thou eate, all the dayes of thy life.
gn.3.15	Genesis 3:15	And I will put enmitie betweene thee and the woman, and betweene thy seed and her seed: it shal bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heele.
gn.3.16	Genesis 3:16	Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorowe and thy conception. In sorow thou shalt bring forth children: and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and hee shall rule ouer thee.
gn.3.17	Genesis 3:17	And vnto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened vnto the voyce of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commaunded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eate of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake: in sorow shalt thou eate of it all the dayes of thy life.
gn.3.18	Genesis 3:18	Thornes also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee: and thou shalt eate the herbe of the field.
gn.3.19	Genesis 3:19	In the sweate of thy face shalt thou eate bread, till thou returne vnto the ground: for out of it wast thou taken, for dust thou art, and vnto dust shalt thou returne.
gn.3.20	Genesis 3:20	And Adam called his wiues name Eue, because she was the mother of all liuing.
gn.3.21	Genesis 3:21	Unto Adam also, and to his wife, did the LORD God make coates of skinnes, and cloathed them.
gn.3.22	Genesis 3:22	¶ And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of vs, to know good & euill. And now lest hee put foorth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eate and liue for euer:
gn.3.23	Genesis 3:23	Therefore the LORD God sent him foorth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground, from whence he was taken.
gn.3.24	Genesis 3:24	So he droue out the man: and he placed at the East of the garden of Eden, Cherubims, and a flaming sword, which turned euery way, to keepe the way of the tree of life.
gn.4.1	Genesis 4:1	And Adam knew Eue his wife, and shee conceiued, and bare Cain, and said, I haue gotten a man from the LORD.
gn.4.2	Genesis 4:2	And she againe bare his brother Abel, and Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
gn.4.3	Genesis 4:3	And in processe of time it came to passe, that Cain brought of the fruite of the ground, an offering vnto the LORD.
gn.4.4	Genesis 4:4	And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flocke, and of the fat thereof: and the LORD had respect vnto Abel, and to his offering.
gn.4.5	Genesis 4:5	But vnto Cain, and to his offring he had not respect: and Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
gn.4.6	Genesis 4:6	And the LORD said vnto Cain, Why art thou wroth? And why is thy countenance fallen?
gn.4.7	Genesis 4:7	If thou doe well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sinne lieth at the doore: And vnto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule ouer him.
gn.4.8	Genesis 4:8	And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to passe when they were in the field, that Cain rose vp against Abel his brother, and slew him.
gn.4.9	Genesis 4:9	¶ And the LORD said vnto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And hee said, I know not: Am I my brothers keeper?
gn.4.10	Genesis 4:10	And he said, What hast thou done? the voyce of thy brothers blood cryeth vnto me, from the ground.
gn.4.11	Genesis 4:11	And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receiue thy brothers blood from thy hand.
gn.4.12	Genesis 4:12	When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yeeld vnto thee her strength: A fugitiue and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
gn.4.13	Genesis 4:13	And Cain said vnto the LORD, My punishment is greater, then I can beare.
gn.4.14	Genesis 4:14	Behold, thou hast driuen me out this day from the face of the earth, and from thy face shall I be hid, and I shall be a fugitiue, and a vagabond in the earth: and it shall come to passe, that euery one that findeth me, shall slay me.
gn.4.15	Genesis 4:15	And the LORD said vnto him, Therefore whosoeuer slayeth Cain, vengeance shalbe taken on him seuen fold. And the LORD set a marke vpon Cain, lest any finding him, should kill him.
gn.4.16	Genesis 4:16	¶ And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the East of Eden.
gn.4.17	Genesis 4:17	And Cain knew his wife, and she conceiued and bare Enoch, and hee builded a City, and called the name of the City, after the name of his sonne, Enoch.
gn.4.18	Genesis 4:18	And vnto Enoch was borne Irad: and Irad begate Mehuiael, and Mehuiael begate Methusael, and Methusael begate Lamech.
gn.4.19	Genesis 4:19	¶ And Lamech tooke vnto him two wiues: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
gn.4.20	Genesis 4:20	And Adah bare Iabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as haue cattell.
gn.4.21	Genesis 4:21	And his brothers name was Iubal: hee was the father of all such as handle the harpe and organ.
gn.4.22	Genesis 4:22	And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-Cain, an instructer of euery artificer in brasse and iron: and the sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.
gn.4.23	Genesis 4:23	And Lamech sayd vnto his wiues, Adah and Zillah, Heare my voyce, yee wiues of Lamech, hearken vnto my speech: for I haue slaine a man to my wounding, and a yong man to my hurt.
gn.4.24	Genesis 4:24	If Cain shall bee auenged seuen fold, truely Lamech seuenty and seuen folde.
gn.4.25	Genesis 4:25	¶ And Adam knew his wife againe, and she bare a sonne, & called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed mee another seed in stead of Abel, whom Cain slew.
gn.4.26	Genesis 4:26	And to Seth, to him also there was borne a sonne, and he called his name Enos: then began men to call vpon the Name of the LORD.
gn.5.1	Genesis 5:1	This is the booke of the generations of Adam: In the day that God created man, in the likenes of God made he him.
gn.5.2	Genesis 5:2	Male and female created hee them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
gn.5.3	Genesis 5:3	¶ And Adam liued an hundred and thirtie yeeres, and begate a sonne in his owne likenesse, after his image; and called his name Seth.
gn.5.4	Genesis 5:4	And the dayes of Adam, after he had begotten Seth, were eight hundred yeeres: and he begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.5	Genesis 5:5	And all the dayes that Adam liued, were nine hundred and thirtie yeeres: and he died.
gn.5.6	Genesis 5:6	And Seth liued an hundred and fiue yeeres: and begate Enos.
gn.5.7	Genesis 5:7	And Seth liued, after he begate Enos, eight hundred and seuen yeeres, and begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.8	Genesis 5:8	And all the dayes of Seth, were nine hundred and twelue yeeres, and he died.
gn.5.9	Genesis 5:9	¶ And Enos liued ninetie yeeres, and begate Cainan.
gn.5.10	Genesis 5:10	And Enos liued after hee begate Cainan, eight hundred and fifteene yeeres, and begate sonnes & daughters.
gn.5.11	Genesis 5:11	And all the dayes of Enos were nine hundred & fiue yeres; and he died.
gn.5.12	Genesis 5:12	¶ And Cainan liued seuentie yeeres, and begate Mahalaleel.
gn.5.13	Genesis 5:13	And Cainan liued after he begate Mahalaleel, eight hundred and fourtie yeeres, & begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.14	Genesis 5:14	And al the dayes of Cainan were nine hundred & ten yeres; and he died.
gn.5.15	Genesis 5:15	¶ And Mahalaleel liued sixtie and fiue yeeres, and begat Iared.
gn.5.16	Genesis 5:16	And Mahalaleel liued after he begate Iared, eight hundred and thirtie yeeres, and begate sonnes & daughters.
gn.5.17	Genesis 5:17	And all the dayes of Mahalaleel, were eight hundred ninetie and fiue yeeres, and he died.
gn.5.18	Genesis 5:18	¶ And Iared liued an hundred sixtie and two yeeres, & he begat Enoch.
gn.5.19	Genesis 5:19	And Iared liued after he begate Enoch, eight hundred yeres, and begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.20	Genesis 5:20	And all the dayes of Iared were nine hundred sixtie and two yeeres, and he died.
gn.5.21	Genesis 5:21	¶ And Enoch liued sixtie and fiue yeeres, and begate Methuselah.
gn.5.22	Genesis 5:22	And Enoch walked with God, after he begate Methuselah, three hundred yeeres, and begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.23	Genesis 5:23	And all the dayes of Enoch, were three hundred sixtie and fiue yeeres.
gn.5.24	Genesis 5:24	And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God tooke him.
gn.5.25	Genesis 5:25	And Methuselah liued an hundred eightie and seuen yeeres, and begat Lamech.
gn.5.26	Genesis 5:26	And Methuselah liued, after hee begate Lamech, seuen hundred, eightie and two yeeres, and begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.27	Genesis 5:27	And all the dayes of Methuselah were nine hundred, sixtie and nine yeeres, and he died.
gn.5.28	Genesis 5:28	¶ And Lamech liued an hundred eightie and two yeeres: and begate a sonne.
gn.5.29	Genesis 5:29	And he called his name Noah, saying; This same shall comfort vs, concerning our woorke and toyle of our hands, because of the ground, which the LORD hath cursed.
gn.5.30	Genesis 5:30	And Lamech liued, after hee begate Noah, fiue hundred ninetie and fiue yeeres, and begate sonnes and daughters.
gn.5.31	Genesis 5:31	And all the dayes of Lamech were seuen hundred seuentie and seuen yeeres, and he died.
gn.5.32	Genesis 5:32	And Noah was fiue hundred yeeres olde: and Noah begate Sem, Ham, and Iapheth.
gn.6.1	Genesis 6:1	And it came to passe, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were borne vnto them:
gn.6.2	Genesis 6:2	That the sonnes of God saw the daughters of men, that they were faire, and they took them wiues, of all which they chose.
gn.6.3	Genesis 6:3	And the LORD said, My Spirit shall not alwayes striue with man; for that hee also is flesh: yet his dayes shalbe an hundred and twenty yeeres.
gn.6.4	Genesis 6:4	There were Giants in the earth in those daies: and also after that, when the sonnes of God came in vnto the daughters of men, & they bare children to them; the same became mightie men, which were of old, men of renowme.
gn.6.5	Genesis 6:5	¶ And GOD saw, that the wickednes of man was great in the earth, and that euery imagination of the thoughts of his heart was onely euill continually.
gn.6.6	Genesis 6:6	And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieued him at his heart.
gn.6.7	Genesis 6:7	And the LORD said, I will destroy man, whom I haue created, from the face of the earth: both man and beast, and the creeping thing, and the foules of the aire: for it repenteth me that I haue made them.
gn.6.8	Genesis 6:8	But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
gn.6.9	Genesis 6:9	¶ These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a iust man, and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
gn.6.10	Genesis 6:10	And Noah begate three sonnes: Sem, Ham, and Iapheth.
gn.6.11	Genesis 6:11	The earth also was corrupt before God; and the earth was filled with violence.
gn.6.12	Genesis 6:12	And God looked vpon the earth, and behold, it was corrupt: for all flesh had corrupted his way vpon the earth.
gn.6.13	Genesis 6:13	And God said vnto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before mee; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
gn.6.14	Genesis 6:14	¶ Make thee an Arke of Gopher-wood: roomes shalt thou make in the arke, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
gn.6.15	Genesis 6:15	And this is the fashion, which thou shalt make it of: the length of the arke shalbe three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirtie cubits.
gn.6.16	Genesis 6:16	A window shalt thou make to the arke, and in a cubite shalt thou finish it aboue; and the doore of the arke shalt thou set in the side thereof: With lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
gn.6.17	Genesis 6:17	And behold, I, euen I doe bring a flood of waters vpon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life from vnder heauen, and euery thing that is in the earth shall die.
gn.6.18	Genesis 6:18	But with thee wil I establish my Couenant: and thou shalt come into the Arke, thou, and thy sonnes, and thy wife, and thy sonnes wiues with thee.
gn.6.19	Genesis 6:19	And of euery liuing thing of all flesh, two of euery sort shalt thou bring into the Arke, to keepe them aliue with thee: they shall be male and female.
gn.6.20	Genesis 6:20	Of fowles after their kinde, and of cattel after their kinde: of euery creeping thing of the earth after his kinde, two of euery sort shall come vnto thee, to keepe them aliue.
gn.6.21	Genesis 6:21	And take thou vnto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou shalt gather it to thee; and it shall be for food, for thee, and for them.
gn.6.22	Genesis 6:22	Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
gn.7.1	Genesis 7:1	And the LORD saide vnto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the Arke: for thee haue I seene righteous before me, in this generation.
gn.7.2	Genesis 7:2	Of euery cleane beast thou shalt take to thee by seuens, the male and his female: and of beastes that are not cleane, by two, the male and his female.
gn.7.3	Genesis 7:3	Of fowles also of the aire, by seuens, the male & the female; to keepe seed aliue vpon the face of all the earth.
gn.7.4	Genesis 7:4	For yet seuen dayes, and I will cause it to raine vpon the earth, fortie dayes, and forty nights: and euery liuing substance that I haue made, will I destroy, frō off the face of the earth.
gn.7.5	Genesis 7:5	And Noah did according vnto all that the LORD commanded him.
gn.7.6	Genesis 7:6	And Noah was sixe hundred yeeres old, when the flood of waters was vpon the earth.
gn.7.7	Genesis 7:7	¶ And Noah went in, and his sonnes, and his wife, and his sonnes wiues with him, into the Arke, because of the waters of the Flood.
gn.7.8	Genesis 7:8	Of cleane beasts, & of beasts that are not cleane, & of fowles, and of euery thing that creepeth vpon the earth,

gn.7.11	Genesis 7:11	¶ In the sixe hundredth yeere of Noahs life, in the second moneth, the seuenteenth day of the moneth, the same day, were al the fountaines of the great deepe broken vp, and the windowes of heauen were opened.

gn.7.17	Genesis 7:17	And the Flood was fortie dayes vpon the earth, and the waters increased, and bare vp the Arke, and it was lift vp aboue the earth.

gn.7.20	Genesis 7:20	Fifteene cubits vpward, did the waters preuaile; and the mountaines were couered.
gn.7.21	Genesis 7:21	And all flesh died, that mooued vpon the earth, both of fowle, & of cattell, and of beast, and of euery creeping thing that creepeth vpon the earth, and euery man.

gn.7.23	Genesis 7:23	And euery liuing substance was destroyed, which was vpon the face of the ground, both man and cattell, and the creeping things, and the foule of the heauen; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah onely remained aliue, and they that were with him in the Arke.
gn.7.24	Genesis 7:24	And the waters preuailed vpon the earth, an hundred and fifty dayes.
gn.8.1	Genesis 8:1	And God remembred Noah, and euery liuing thing, and all the cattell that was with him in the Arke: and God made a winde to passe ouer the earth, and the waters asswaged.
gn.8.2	Genesis 8:2	The fountaines also of the deepe, and the windowes of heauen were stopped, and the raine from heauen was restrained.
gn.8.3	Genesis 8:3	And the waters returned from off the earth, continually: and after the end of the hundred and fiftie dayes, the waters were abated.
gn.8.4	Genesis 8:4	And the Arke rested in the seuenth moneth, on the seuenteenth day of the moneth, vpon the mountaines of Ararat.
gn.8.5	Genesis 8:5	And the waters decreased continually vntill the tenth moneth: in the tenth moneth, on the first day of the moneth, were the tops of the mountaines seene.
gn.8.6	Genesis 8:6	¶ And it came to passe at the end of forty dayes, that Noah opened the window of the Arke which he had made.
gn.8.7	Genesis 8:7	And he sent forth a Rauen, which went foorth to and fro, vntill the waters were dried vp from off the earth.
gn.8.8	Genesis 8:8	Also hee sent foorth a doue from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground.
gn.8.9	Genesis 8:9	But the doue found no rest for the sole of her foote, and she returned vnto him into the Arke: for the waters were on the face of the whole earth. Then he put foorth his hand, and tooke her, and pulled her in vnto him, into the Arke.
gn.8.10	Genesis 8:10	And hee stayed yet other seuen dayes; and againe hee sent foorth the doue out of the Arke.
gn.8.11	Genesis 8:11	And the doue came in to him in the euening, and loe, in her mouth was an Oliue leafe pluckt off: So Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
gn.8.12	Genesis 8:12	And hee stayed yet other seuen dayes, and sent forth the doue, which returned not againe vnto him any more.
gn.8.13	Genesis 8:13	¶ And it came to passe in the sixe hundredth and one yeere, in the first moneth, the first day of the moneth, the waters were dryed vp from off the earth: and Noah remooued the couering of the Arke, and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was drie.
gn.8.14	Genesis 8:14	And in the second moneth, on the seuen and twentieth day of the moneth, was the earth dried.

gn.47.13	Genesis 47:13	¶ And there was no bread in all the land: for the famine was very sore, so that the land of Egypt and all the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
gn.47.14	Genesis 47:14	And Ioseph gathered vp all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corne which they bought: and Ioseph brought the money into Pharaohs house.
gn.47.15	Genesis 47:15	And when money failed in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came vnto Ioseph, and said, Giue vs bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for the money faileth.
gn.47.16	Genesis 47:16	And Ioseph said, Giue your cattell: and I will giue you for your catell, if money faile.
gn.47.17	Genesis 47:17	And they brought their cattel vnto Ioseph: and Ioseph gaue them bread in exchange for horses, and for the flockes, and for the cattell of the heards, and for the asses, and he fed them with bread, for all their cattel, for that yeere.
gn.47.18	Genesis 47:18	When that yeere was ended, they came vnto him the second yeere, and said vnto him, We will not hide it from my lord, how that our money is spent, my lord also had our heards of cattell: there is not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.
gn.47.19	Genesis 47:19	Wherfore shall we die before thine eyes, both we, and our land? buy vs and our land for bread, and we and our land will be seruants vnto Pharaoh: and giue vs seede that we may liue and not die, that the land be not desolate.
gn.47.20	Genesis 47:20	And Ioseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh: for the Egyptians sold euery man his field, because the famine preuailed ouer them: so the land became Pharaohs.
gn.47.21	Genesis 47:21	And as for the people, he remoued them to cities from one end of the borders of Egypt, euen to the other ende thereof.
gn.47.22	Genesis 47:22	Onely the land of the Priests bought he not: for the priests had a portion assigned them of Pharaoh, and did eate their portion which Pharaoh gaue them: wherefore they solde not their lands.

gn.47.24	Genesis 47:24	And it shall come to passe in the increase, that you shall giue the fift part vnto Pharaoh, and foure parts shall be your owne, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your litle ones.
gn.47.25	Genesis 47:25	And they said, Thou hast saued our liues: let vs find grace in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaohs seruants.
gn.47.26	Genesis 47:26	And Ioseph made it a law ouer the land of Egypt vnto this day, that Pharaoh should haue the fift part: except the land of the priests onely, which became not Pharaohs.
gn.47.27	Genesis 47:27	¶ And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt in the countrey of Goshen, and they had possessions therein, and grew, and multiplied exceedingly.

gn.47.30	Genesis 47:30	But I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carie mee out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place: and he said, I will doe as thou hast said.

ex.1.9	Exodus 1:9	And he said vnto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are moe and mightier then we.
ex.1.10	Exodus 1:10	Come on, let vs deale wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it come to passe that when there falleth out any warre, they ioyne also vnto our enemies, and fight against vs, and so get them vp out of the land.

ex.1.12	Exodus 1:12	But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew: and they were grieued because of the children of Israel.
ex.1.13	Exodus 1:13	And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serue with rigour.
ex.1.14	Exodus 1:14	And they made their liues bitter, with hard bondage, in morter and in bricke, and in all maner of seruice in the fielde: all their seruice wherein they made them serue, was with rigour.
ex.1.15	Exodus 1:15	¶ And the King of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwiues, (of which the name of one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah.)
ex.1.16	Exodus 1:16	And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew-women, and see them vpon the stooles, if it be a sonne, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then shee shall liue.
ex.1.17	Exodus 1:17	But the midwiues feared God, and did not as the King of Egypt commanded them, but saued the men children aliue.
ex.1.18	Exodus 1:18	And the King of Egypt called for the midwiues, & said vnto them, Why haue ye done this thing, and haue saued the men children aliue?
ex.1.19	Exodus 1:19	And the midwiues said vnto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women: for they are liuely, and are deliuered ere the midwiues come in vnto them.
ex.1.20	Exodus 1:20	Therefore God dealt well with the midwiues: and the people multiplied and waxed very mighty.
ex.1.21	Exodus 1:21	And it came to passe, because the midwiues feared God, that hee made them houses.
ex.1.22	Exodus 1:22	And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Euery sonne that is borne, yee shall cast into the riuer, and euery daughter ye shall saue aliue.
ex.2.1	Exodus 2:1	And there went a man of the house of Leui, & tooke to wife a daughter of Leui.

ex.2.3	Exodus 2:3	And when shee could not longer hide him, she tooke for him an arke of bul-rushes, and daubed it with slime, and with pitch, and put the childe therein, and shee layd it in the flags by the riuers brinke.
ex.2.4	Exodus 2:4	And his sister stood afarre off, to wit what would be done to him.
ex.2.5	Exodus 2:5	¶ And the daughter of Pharaoh came downe to wash her selfe at the riuer, and her maydens walked along by the riuer side: and when shee saw the arke among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
ex.2.6	Exodus 2:6	And when she had opened it, she saw the childe: and beholde, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrewes children.

ex.2.9	Exodus 2:9	And Pharaohs daughter said vnto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will giue thee thy wages. And the woman tooke the childe, and nursed it.
ex.2.10	Exodus 2:10	And the childe grew, and shee brought him vnto Pharaohs daughter, and he became her sonne. And she called his name Moses: And she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
ex.2.11	Exodus 2:11	¶ And it came to passe in those dayes, when Moses was growen, that he went out vnto his brethren, and looked on their burdens, and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.
ex.2.12	Exodus 2:12	And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
ex.2.13	Exodus 2:13	And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrewes stroue together: And hee said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
ex.2.14	Exodus 2:14	And he said, Who made thee a Prince and a iudge ouer vs? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is knowen.
ex.2.15	Exodus 2:15	Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sate downe by a well.

ex.2.18	Exodus 2:18	And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that you are come so soone to day?
ex.2.19	Exodus 2:19	And they said, An Egyptian deliuered vs out of the hand of the shepheards, and also drew water enough for vs, and watered the flocke.
ex.2.20	Exodus 2:20	And he said vnto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that yee haue left the man? Call him, that hee may eate bread.
ex.2.21	Exodus 2:21	And Moses was content to dwel with the man, and he gaue Moses Zipporah his daughter.
ex.2.22	Exodus 2:22	And she bare him a sonne, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I haue bene a stranger in a strange land.
ex.2.23	Exodus 2:23	¶ And it came to passe in processe of time, that the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came vp vnto God, by reason of the bondage.
ex.2.24	Exodus 2:24	And God heard their groning, and God remembred his Couenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Iacob.

ex.3.1	Exodus 3:1	Nowe Moses kept the flocke of Iethro his father in law, the Priest of Midian: and hee led the flocke to the backeside of the desert, and came to the mountaine of God, euen to Horeb.
ex.3.2	Exodus 3:2	And the Angel of the LORD appeared vnto him, in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush, and he looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
ex.3.3	Exodus 3:3	And Moses saide, I will nowe turne aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
ex.3.4	Exodus 3:4	And when the LORD sawe that he turned aside to see, God called vnto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he saide, Here am I.
ex.3.5	Exodus 3:5	And he said, Drawe not nigh hither: put off thy shooes from off thy feete, for the place whereon thou standest, is holy ground.
ex.3.6	Exodus 3:6	Moreouer hee said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob. And Moses hid his face: for he was afraid to looke vpon God.
ex.3.7	Exodus 3:7	¶ And the LORD said, I haue surely seene the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and haue heard their crie, by reason of their taske-masters: for I know their sorrowes,
ex.3.8	Exodus 3:8	And I am come downe to deliuer them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them vp out of that land, vnto a good land and a large, vnto a lande flowing with milke and hony, vnto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hiuites, and the Iebusites.
ex.3.9	Exodus 3:9	Now therefore behold, the crie of the children of Israel is come vnto me: and I haue also seene the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppresse them.
ex.3.10	Exodus 3:10	Come now therefore, and I will send thee vnto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
ex.3.11	Exodus 3:11	¶ And Moses saide vnto God, Who am I, that I should goe vnto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
ex.3.12	Exodus 3:12	And he said, Certainely I will be with thee, and this shall be a token vnto thee, that I haue sent thee: When thou hast brought foorth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serue God vpon this mountaine.
ex.3.13	Exodus 3:13	And Moses saide vnto God, Behold, when I come vnto the children of Israel, and shall say vnto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me vnto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say vnto them?
ex.3.14	Exodus 3:14	And God saide vnto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: And he said, Thus shalt thou say vnto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me vnto you.
ex.3.15	Exodus 3:15	And God said moreouer vnto Moses, Thus shalt thou say vnto the children of Israel; The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob hath sent me vnto you: this is my name for euer, and this is my memoriall vnto all generations.
ex.3.16	Exodus 3:16	Goe and gather the Elders of Israel together, and say vnto them, The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Iacob appeared vnto me, saying, I haue surely visited you, and seene that which is done to you in Egypt.
ex.3.17	Exodus 3:17	And I haue said, I will bring you vp out of the affliction of Egypt, vnto the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hiuites, and the Iebusites, vnto a land flowing with milke and hony.
ex.3.18	Exodus 3:18	And they shall hearken to thy voyce: and thou shalt come, thou and the Elders of Israel vnto the King of Egypt, and you shall say vnto him, The LORD God of the Hebrewes hath met with vs: and now let vs goe, (wee beseech thee) three dayes iourney into the wildernes, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.
ex.3.19	Exodus 3:19	¶ And I am sure that the King of Egypt will not let you goe, no not by a mightie hand.
ex.3.20	Exodus 3:20	And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will doe in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you goe.
ex.3.21	Exodus 3:21	And I will giue this people fauour in the sight of the Egyptians, and it shall come to passe that when ye goe, ye shall not goe empty:
ex.3.22	Exodus 3:22	But euery woman shal borrow of her neighbour, and of her that soiourneth in her house, iewels of siluer, and iewels of gold, and rayment: and ye shall put them vpon your sonnes and vpon your daughters, and yee shall spoile the Egyptians.
ex.4.1	Exodus 4:1	And Moses answered, and said, But behold, they will not beleeue mee, nor hearken vnto my voice: for they will say, The LORD hath not appeared vnto thee.
ex.4.2	Exodus 4:2	And the LORD said vnto him, What is that in thine hand? and hee said, A rod.
ex.4.3	Exodus 4:3	And he said, Cast it on the ground: And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent: and Moses fled from before it.
ex.4.4	Exodus 4:4	And the LORD said vnto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the taile: And he put foorth his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:
ex.4.5	Exodus 4:5	That they may beleeue that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob hath appeared vnto thee.
ex.4.6	Exodus 4:6	¶ And the LORD said furthermore vnto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosome. And he put his hand into his bosome: and when hee tooke it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snowe.
ex.4.7	Exodus 4:7	And he said, Put thine hand into thy bosome againe. And hee put his hand into his bosome againe, and plucked it out of his bosome, and behold, it was turned againe as his other flesh.
ex.4.8	Exodus 4:8	And it shall come to passe, if they wil not beleeue thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first signe, that they will beleeue the voice of the latter signe.
ex.4.9	Exodus 4:9	And it shall come to passe, if they will not beleeue also these two signes, neither hearken vnto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the riuer, and powre it vpon the drie land: and the water which thou takest out of the riuer, shall become blood vpon the drie land.
ex.4.10	Exodus 4:10	¶ And Moses saide vnto the Lord, O my lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken vnto thy seruant: but I am slow of speach, and of a slow tongue.
ex.4.11	Exodus 4:11	And the LORD said vnto him, Who hath made mans mouth? or who maketh the dumbe or deafe, or the seeing, or þ blind? haue not I the LORD?
ex.4.12	Exodus 4:12	Now therefore goe, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
ex.4.13	Exodus 4:13	And he said, O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.
ex.4.14	Exodus 4:14	And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and hee said, Is not Aaron the Leuite thy brother? I know that he can speake well. And also behold, he commeth foorth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, hee will be glad in his heart.
ex.4.15	Exodus 4:15	And thou shalt speake vnto him, and put words in his mouth, and I wil be with thy mouth, & with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall doe.
ex.4.16	Exodus 4:16	And he shal be thy spokesman vnto the people: and he shall be, euen hee shall be to thee in stead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him in stead of God.
ex.4.17	Exodus 4:17	And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt doe signes.
ex.4.18	Exodus 4:18	¶ And Moses went and returned to Iethro his father in law, and said vnto him, Let me goe, I pray thee, and returne vnto my brethren, which are in Egypt, and see whether they bee yet aliue. And Iethro said to Moses, Goe in peace.
ex.4.19	Exodus 4:19	And the LORD said vnto Moses in Midian, Goe, returne into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.
ex.4.20	Exodus 4:20	And Moses tooke his wife, and his sonnes, and set them vpon an asse, and he returned to the land of Egypt. And Moses tooke the rod of God in his hand.
ex.4.21	Exodus 4:21	And the LORD said vnto Moses, When thou goest to returne into Egypt, see that thou doe all those wonders before Pharaoh, which I haue put in thine hand: but I wil harden his heart, that hee shall not let the people goe.
ex.4.22	Exodus 4:22	And thou shalt say vnto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my sonne, euen my first borne.
ex.4.23	Exodus 4:23	And I say vnto thee, let my sonne goe, that he may serue mee: and if thou refuse to let him goe, behold, I will slay thy sonne, euen thy first borne.
ex.4.24	Exodus 4:24	¶ And it came to passe by the way in the Inne, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him.
ex.4.25	Exodus 4:25	Then Zipporah tooke a sharpe stone, and cut off the foreskinne of her sonne, and cast it at his feete, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to mee.
ex.4.26	Exodus 4:26	So he let him goe: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the Circumcision.
ex.4.27	Exodus 4:27	¶ And the LORD said to Aaron, Goe into the wildernesse to meete Moses. And hee went and met him in the mount of God, and kissed him.
ex.4.28	Exodus 4:28	And Moses tolde Aaron all the wordes of the LORD, who had sent him, and all the signes which hee had commanded him.
ex.4.29	Exodus 4:29	¶ And Moses and Aaron went, and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.
ex.4.30	Exodus 4:30	And Aaron spake all the wordes which the LORD had spoken vnto Moses, and did the signes in the sight of the people.
ex.4.31	Exodus 4:31	And the people beleeued: And when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked vpon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.
ex.5.1	Exodus 5:1	And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and tolde Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people goe, that they may holde a feast vnto mee in the wildernesse.
ex.5.2	Exodus 5:2	And Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voyce to let Israel goe? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel goe.
ex.5.3	Exodus 5:3	And they said, The God of the Hebrewes hath met with vs: let vs goe, we pray thee, three dayes iourney into the desert, and sacrifice vnto the LORD our God, lest hee fall vpon vs with pestilence, or with the sword.
ex.5.4	Exodus 5:4	And the King of Egypt said vnto them, Wherfore doe ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their workes? get you vnto your burdens.
ex.5.5	Exodus 5:5	And Pharaoh said, Behold, the people of the land now are many, & you make them rest from their burdens.
ex.5.6	Exodus 5:6	And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taske-masters of the people, and their officers, saying;
ex.5.7	Exodus 5:7	Yee shall no more giue the people straw to make bricke, as heretofore: let them goe and gather straw for themselues.
ex.5.8	Exodus 5:8	And the tale of the brickes which they did make heretofore, you shall lay vpon them: you shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us goe and sacrifice to our God.
ex.5.9	Exodus 5:9	Let there more worke be layde vpon the men, that they may labour therein, and let them not regard vaine wordes.
ex.5.10	Exodus 5:10	¶ And the taske-masters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spake to the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will not giue you straw.
ex.5.11	Exodus 5:11	Goe ye, get you straw where you can find it: yet not ought of your worke shall be diminished.
ex.5.12	Exodus 5:12	So the people were scattered abroad throughout al the land of Egypt, to gather stubble in stead of straw.
ex.5.13	Exodus 5:13	And the taske-masters hasted them, saying; Fulfill your workes, your dayly taskes, as when there was straw.
ex.5.14	Exodus 5:14	And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaohs task-masters had set ouer them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore haue ye not fulfilled your taske, in making bricke, both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?
ex.5.15	Exodus 5:15	¶ Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cryed vnto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy seruants?
ex.5.16	Exodus 5:16	There is no straw giuen vnto thy seruants, and they say to vs, Make bricke: and beholde, thy seruants are beaten; but the fault is in thine owne people.
ex.5.17	Exodus 5:17	But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let vs goe and doe sacrifice to the LORD.
ex.5.18	Exodus 5:18	Goe therefore now and worke: for there shall no straw bee giuen you, yet shall ye deliuer the tale of brickes.
ex.5.19	Exodus 5:19	And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in euill case, after it was said, Yee shall not minish ought from your brickes of your dayly taske.
ex.5.20	Exodus 5:20	¶ And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came foorth from Pharaoh.
ex.5.21	Exodus 5:21	And they said vnto them; The LORD looke vpon you, and iudge, because you haue made our sauour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his seruants, to put a sword in their hand to slay vs.
ex.5.22	Exodus 5:22	And Moses returned vnto the LORD, and said, Lord, Wherefore hast thou so euill intreated this people? Why is it that thou hast sent me?
ex.5.23	Exodus 5:23	For since I came to Pharaoh to speake in thy Name, he hath done euill to this people, neither hast thou deliuered thy people at all.

ex.7.17	Exodus 7:17	Thus saith the LORD, In this thou shalt know that I am the LORD: behold, I will smite with the rod that is in my hand, vpon the waters which are in the riuer, and they shalbe turned to blood.

ex.7.20	Exodus 7:20	And Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded: and he lift vp the rod and smote the waters that were in the riuer, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his seruants: and all the waters that were in the riuer, were turned to blood.

ex.8.1	Exodus 8:1	And the LORD spake vnto Moses, Goe vnto Pharaoh, and say vnto him; Thus sayeth the LORD, Let my people goe, that they may serue me.
ex.8.2	Exodus 8:2	And if thou refuse to let them goe, beholde, I will smite all thy borders with frogges.
ex.8.3	Exodus 8:3	And the riuer shall bring foorth frogges abundantly, which shall goe vp and come into thine house, and into thy bed-chamber, and vpon thy bed, and into the house of thy seruants, and vpon thy people, and into thine ouens, and into thy kneading troughes.
ex.8.4	Exodus 8:4	And the frogges shall come vp both on thee, and vpon thy people, and vpon all thy seruants.
ex.8.5	Exodus 8:5	¶ And the LORD spake vnto Moses; Say vnto Aaron, Stretch foorth thine hand with thy rodde ouer the streames, ouer the riuers, and ouer the ponds, and cause frogges to come vp vpon the land of Egypt.
ex.8.6	Exodus 8:6	And Aaron stretched out his hand ouer the waters of Egypt, and the frogges came vp, and couered the land of Egypt.
ex.8.7	Exodus 8:7	And the Magicians did so with their inchantments, and brought vp frogges vpon the land of Egypt.
ex.8.8	Exodus 8:8	¶ Then Pharaoh called for Moses, and Aaron, and said, Intreat the LORD, that hee may take away the frogges from me, and from my people: and I will let the people goe, that they may doe sacrifice vnto the LORD.
ex.8.9	Exodus 8:9	And Moses saide vnto Pharaoh, Glory ouer mee: when shall I entreat for thee, and for thy seruants, and for thy people, to destroy the frogges from thee, and thy houses, that they may remaine in the riuer onely?
ex.8.10	Exodus 8:10	And he said, To morrow. And hee said, Bee it according to thy word: That thou mayest know that there is none like vnto the LORD our God.
ex.8.11	Exodus 8:11	And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy seruants, and from thy people; they shall remaine in the riuer onely.
ex.8.12	Exodus 8:12	And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried vnto the LORD because of the frogs which he had brought against Pharaoh.
ex.8.13	Exodus 8:13	And the LORD did according to the word of Moses: and the frogges died out of the houses, out of the villages, and out of the fields.

ex.8.17	Exodus 8:17	And they did so: for Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice, in man and in beast: all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

ex.8.24	Exodus 8:24	And the LORD did so: and there came a grieuous swarme of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his seruants houses, and into all the lande of Egypt: the land was corrupted by reason of the swarme of flies.

ex.8.26	Exodus 8:26	And Moses said, It is not meete so to doe; for we shal sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians, to the LORD our God: Loe, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone vs?

ex.9.14	Exodus 9:14	For I will at this time send all my plagues vpon thine heart, and vpon thy seruants, and vpon thy people: that thou mayest knowe that there is none like me in all the earth.

ex.9.30	Exodus 9:30	But as for thee and thy seruants, I know that ye will not yet feare the LORD God.

ex.12.3	Exodus 12:3	¶ Speake ye vnto all the Congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth day of this moneth they shall take to them euery man a lambe, according to the house of their fathers, a lambe for an house.
ex.12.4	Exodus 12:4	And if the houshold be too little for the lambe, let him and his neighbour next vnto his house, take it according to the number of the soules: euery man according to his eating shall make your count for the lambe.

ex.13.3	Exodus 13:3	¶ And Moses said vnto the people, Remember this day, in which yee came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage: for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from this place: there shall no leauened bread be eaten.

ex.13.5	Exodus 13:5	¶ And it shalbe when the LORD shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Hiuites, and the Iebusites, which he sware vnto thy fathers to giue thee, a land flowing with milke and hony, that thou shalt keepe this seruice in this moneth.
ex.13.6	Exodus 13:6	Seuen dayes thou shalt eate vnleauened bread, and in the seuenth day shall be a feast to the LORD.

ex.13.8	Exodus 13:8	¶ And thou shalt shew thy sonne in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the LORD did vnto mee, when I came forth out of Egypt.
ex.13.9	Exodus 13:9	And it shall bee for a signe vnto thee, vpon thine hand, and for a memoriall betweene thine eyes, that the LORDs law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hande hath the LORD brought thee out of Egypt.
ex.13.10	Exodus 13:10	Thou shalt therfore keepe this ordinance in his season from yeere to yere.

ex.13.14	Exodus 13:14	¶ And it shalbe when thy sonne asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? That thou shalt say vnto him; By strength of hand the LORD brought vs out from Egypt, from the house of bondage.

ex.13.16	Exodus 13:16	And it shall be for a token vpon thine hand, and for frontlets betweene thine eyes. For by strength of hand the LORD brought vs foorth out of Egypt.

ex.18.14	Exodus 18:14	And when Moses father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? Why sittest thou thy selfe alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning vnto euen?
ex.18.15	Exodus 18:15	And Moses said vnto his father in law, Because the people come vnto me to enquire of God.
ex.18.16	Exodus 18:16	When they haue a matter, they come vnto mee, and I iudge betweene one and another, and I doe make them know the statutes of God and his Lawes.
ex.18.17	Exodus 18:17	And Moses father in law saide vnto him, The thing that thou doest, is not good.
ex.18.18	Exodus 18:18	Thou wilt surely weare away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heauy for thee; thou art not able to performe it thy selfe alone.
ex.18.19	Exodus 18:19	Hearken now vnto my voyce, I will giue thee counsell, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to Godward, that thou mayest bring the causes vnto God:
ex.18.20	Exodus 18:20	And thou shalt teach them ordinances and lawes, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walke, and the worke that they must doe.
ex.18.21	Exodus 18:21	Moreouer thou shalt prouide out of all the people able men, such as feare God, men of trueth, hating couetousnesse, and place such ouer them, to bee rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tennes.
ex.18.22	Exodus 18:22	And let them iudge the people at all seasons: and it shall bee that euery great matter they shall bring vnto thee, but euery small matter they shal iudge: so shall it be easier for thy selfe, and they shall beare the burden with thee.
ex.18.23	Exodus 18:23	If thou shalt doe this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt bee able to endure, and all this people shall also goe to their place in peace.
ex.18.24	Exodus 18:24	So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.
ex.18.25	Exodus 18:25	And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads ouer the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tennes.
ex.18.26	Exodus 18:26	And they iudged the people at all seasons: the hard causes they brought vnto Moses, but euery small matter they iudged themselues.
ex.18.27	Exodus 18:27	¶ And Moses let his father in law depart, and he went his way into his owne land.
ex.19.1	Exodus 19:1	In the third moneth when the children of Israel were gone forth out of the land of Egypt, the same day came they into the wildernesse of Sinai.
ex.19.2	Exodus 19:2	For they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the desert of Sinai, and had pitched in the wildernesse, and there Israel camped before the mount.
ex.19.3	Exodus 19:3	And Moses went vp vnto God: and the LORD called vnto him out of the mountaine, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Iacob, and tell the children of Israel:
ex.19.4	Exodus 19:4	Ye haue seene what I did vnto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on Eagles wings, and brought you vnto my selfe.
ex.19.5	Exodus 19:5	Now therfore if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keepe my couenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure vnto me aboue all people: for all the earth is mine.
ex.19.6	Exodus 19:6	And ye shall be vnto me a kingdome of Priestes, and an holy nation. These are the wordes which thou shalt speake vnto the children of Israel.
ex.19.7	Exodus 19:7	¶ And Moses came and called for the Elders of the people, and layd before their faces all these wordes which the LORD commanded him.
ex.19.8	Exodus 19:8	And all the people answered together, and said, All that the LORD hath spoken, we will doe. And Moses returned the wordes of the people vnto the LORD.
ex.19.9	Exodus 19:9	And the LORD said vnto Moses, Loe, I come vnto thee in a thicke cloud, that the people may heare when I speake with thee, and beleeue thee for euer: And Moses told the wordes of the people vnto the LORD.
ex.19.10	Exodus 19:10	¶ And the LORD saide vnto Moses, Goe vnto the people, and sanctifie them to day and to morrow, and let them wash their clothes.
ex.19.11	Exodus 19:11	And be ready against the thirde day: for the third day the LORD will come downe in the sight of all the people, vpon mount Sinai.
ex.19.12	Exodus 19:12	And thou shalt set bounds vnto the people round about, saying, Take heed to your selues, that ye goe not vp into the mount, or touch the border of it: whosoeuer toucheth the mount, shall be surely put to death.
ex.19.13	Exodus 19:13	There shall not a hand touch it, but he shall surely be stoned or shot thorow, whether it be beast, or man, it shall not liue: when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come vp to the mount.
ex.19.14	Exodus 19:14	¶ And Moses went downe from the mount vnto the people, and sanctified the people; and they washed their clothes.
ex.19.15	Exodus 19:15	And hee said vnto the people, Be ready against the third day: come not at your wiues.
ex.19.16	Exodus 19:16	¶ And it came to passe on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thicke cloud vpon the mount, and the voyce of the trumpet exceeding lowd, so that all the people that was in the campe, trembled.
ex.19.17	Exodus 19:17	And Moses brought foorth the people out of the campe to meete with God, and they stood at the nether part of the mount.
ex.19.18	Exodus 19:18	And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended vpon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly.
ex.19.19	Exodus 19:19	And when the voyce of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed lowder and lowder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voyce.
ex.19.20	Exodus 19:20	And the LORD came downe vpon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the LORD called Moses vp to the top of the mount, and Moses went vp.
ex.19.21	Exodus 19:21	And the LORD said vnto Moses, Goe downe, charge the people, lest they breake thorow vnto the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
ex.19.22	Exodus 19:22	And let the Priestes also which come neere to the LORD, sanctifie themselues, lest the LORD breake foorth vpon them.
ex.19.23	Exodus 19:23	And Moses said vnto the LORD, The people cannot come vp to mount Sinai: for thou chargedst vs, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctifie it.
ex.19.24	Exodus 19:24	And the LORD said vnto him, Away, get thee downe, and thou shalt come vp, thou, and Aaron with thee: but let not the Priestes and the people breake through, to come vp vnto the LORD, lest hee breake foorth vpon them.
ex.19.25	Exodus 19:25	So Moses went downe vnto the people, and spake vnto them.
ex.20.1	Exodus 20:1	And God spake all these words, saying,
ex.20.2	Exodus 20:2	I am the LORD thy God, which haue brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage:
ex.20.3	Exodus 20:3	Thou shalt haue no other Gods before me.
ex.20.4	Exodus 20:4	Thou shalt not make vnto thee any grauen Image, or any likenesse of any thing that is in heauen aboue, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water vnder the earth.
ex.20.5	Exodus 20:5	Thou shalt not bow downe thy selfe to them, nor serue them: For I the LORD thy God am a iealous God, visiting the iniquitie of the fathers vpon the children, vnto the thirde and fourth generation of them that hate me:
ex.20.6	Exodus 20:6	And shewing mercy vnto thousands of them that loue mee, and keepe my Commandements.
ex.20.7	Exodus 20:7	Thou shalt not take the Name of the LORD thy God in vaine: for the LORD will not holde him guiltlesse, that taketh his Name in vaine.
ex.20.8	Exodus 20:8	Remember the Sabbath day, to keepe it holy.
ex.20.9	Exodus 20:9	Sixe dayes shalt thou labour, and doe all thy worke:
ex.20.10	Exodus 20:10	But the seuenth day is the Sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not doe any worke, thou, nor thy sonne, nor thy daughter, thy man seruant, nor thy mayd seruant, nor thy cattell, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
ex.20.11	Exodus 20:11	For in sixe dayes the LORD made heauen and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seuenth day: wherefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day, and halowed it.
ex.20.12	Exodus 20:12	¶ Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy dayes may bee long vpon the land, which the LORD thy God giueth thee.
ex.20.13	Exodus 20:13	Thou shalt not kill.
ex.20.14	Exodus 20:14	Thou shalt not commit adultery.
ex.20.15	Exodus 20:15	Thou shalt not steale.
ex.20.16	Exodus 20:16	Thou shalt not beare false witnes against thy neighbour.
ex.20.17	Exodus 20:17	Thou shalt not couet thy neighbours house, thou shalt not couet thy neighbours wife, nor his man seruant, nor his maid seruant, nor his oxe, nor his asse, nor any thing that is thy neighbours.
ex.20.18	Exodus 20:18	¶ And all the people saw the thundrings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountaine smoking: and when the people saw it, they remooued, and stood a farre off.
ex.20.19	Exodus 20:19	And they saide vnto Moses, Speake thou with vs, and wee will heare: But let not God speake with vs, lest we die.
ex.20.20	Exodus 20:20	And Moses said vnto the people, Feare not: for God is come to prooue you, and that his feare may bee before your faces, that ye sinne not.
ex.20.21	Exodus 20:21	And the people stood afarre off, and Moses drew neere vnto the thicke darkenes, where God was.
ex.20.22	Exodus 20:22	¶ And the LORD said vnto Moses, Thus thou shalt say vnto the children of Israel, Yee haue seene that I haue talked with you from heauen.
ex.20.23	Exodus 20:23	Ye shall not make with me gods of siluer, neither shall ye make vnto you gods of gold.
ex.20.24	Exodus 20:24	¶ An Altar of earth thou shalt make vnto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings, thy sheepe, and thine oxen: In all places where I record my Name, I will come vnto thee, and I will blesse thee.
ex.20.25	Exodus 20:25	And if thou wilt make mee an Altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewen stone: for if thou lift vp thy toole vpon it, thou hast polluted it.
ex.20.26	Exodus 20:26	Neither shalt thou goe vp by steps vnto mine Altar, that thy nakednesse be not discouered thereon.
ex.21.1	Exodus 21:1	Now these are the Iudgements which thou shalt set before them.
ex.21.2	Exodus 21:2	If thou buy an Hebrew seruant, sixe yeeres he shall serue, and in the seuenth he shall goe out free for nothing.
ex.21.3	Exodus 21:3	If he came in by himselfe, he shal goe out by himselfe: if he were married, then his wife shall goe out with him.
ex.21.4	Exodus 21:4	If his master haue giuen him a wife, and she haue borne him sonnes or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her masters, and he shall go out by himselfe.
ex.21.5	Exodus 21:5	And if the seruant shall plainely say, I loue my master, my wife, and my children, I will not goe out free:
ex.21.6	Exodus 21:6	Then his master shall bring him vnto the Iudges, hee shall also bring him to the doore, or vnto the doore post, and his master shall boare his eare through with an aule, and he shall serue him for euer.
ex.21.7	Exodus 21:7	¶ And if a man sell his daughter to be a mayd seruant, shee shall not goe out as the men seruants doe.
ex.21.8	Exodus 21:8	If she please not her master, who hath betrothed her to himselfe, then shall he let her be redeemed: To sell her vnto a strange nation hee shall haue no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.
ex.21.9	Exodus 21:9	And if he haue betrothed her vnto his sonne, he shall deale with her after the maner of daughters.
ex.21.10	Exodus 21:10	If he take him another wife, her food, her rayment, and her duety of mariage shall he not diminish.
ex.21.11	Exodus 21:11	And if he doe not these three vnto her, then shall she goe out free without money.
ex.21.12	Exodus 21:12	¶ He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shalbe surely put to death.
ex.21.13	Exodus 21:13	And if a man lye not in wait, but God deliuer him into his hand, then I will appoint thee a place whither hee shall flee:
ex.21.14	Exodus 21:14	But if a man come presumptuously vpon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine Altar, that he may die.
ex.21.15	Exodus 21:15	¶ And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall bee surely put to death.
ex.21.16	Exodus 21:16	¶ And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
ex.21.17	Exodus 21:17	¶ And hee that curseth his father or his mother, shall surely bee put to death.
ex.21.18	Exodus 21:18	¶ And if men striue together, and one smite another with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keepeth his bed:
ex.21.19	Exodus 21:19	If hee rise againe, and walke abroad vpon his staffe, then shall hee that smote him, be quit: onely he shall pay for the losse of his time, and shall cause him to be throughly healed.
ex.21.20	Exodus 21:20	¶ And if a man smite his seruant, or his mayd, with a rod, and hee die vnder his hand, hee shall bee surely punished:
ex.21.21	Exodus 21:21	Notwithstanding, if he continue a day or two, hee shall not be punished, for he is his money.
ex.21.22	Exodus 21:22	¶ If men striue, and hurt a woman with child, so that her fruit depart from her, and yet no mischiefe follow, he shalbe surely punished, according as the womans husband will lay vpon him, and hee shall pay as the Iudges determine.
ex.21.23	Exodus 21:23	And if any mischiefe follow, then thou shalt giue life for life,
ex.21.24	Exodus 21:24	Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foote for foote,
ex.21.25	Exodus 21:25	Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
ex.21.26	Exodus 21:26	¶ And if a man smite the eye of his seruant, or the eye of his mayd, that it perish, hee shall let him goe free for his eyes sake.
ex.21.27	Exodus 21:27	And if he smite out his man seruants tooth, or his mayde seruants tooth, hee shal let him goe free for his tooths sake.
ex.21.28	Exodus 21:28	¶ If an oxe gore a man, or a woman, that they die, then the oxe shal be surely stoned, and his flesh shall not be eaten: but the owner of the oxe shall be quitte.
ex.21.29	Exodus 21:29	But if the oxe were wont to push with his horne in time past, and it hath bene testified to his owner, and he hath not kept him in, but that he hath killed a man or a woman; the oxe shall be stoned, and his owner also shall bee put to death.
ex.21.30	Exodus 21:30	If there be layed on him a summe of money, then he shall giue for the ransome of his life, whatsoeuer is layd vpon him.
ex.21.31	Exodus 21:31	Whether hee haue gored a sonne, or haue gored a daughter, according to this iudgement shall it bee done vnto him.
ex.21.32	Exodus 21:32	If the oxe shall push a man seruant, or a mayd seruant, hee shall giue vnto their master thirty shekels, and the oxe shalbe stoned.
ex.21.33	Exodus 21:33	¶ And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall digge a pit, and not couer it, and an oxe or an asse fall therein:
ex.21.34	Exodus 21:34	The owner of the pit shall make it good, and giue money vnto the owner of them, and the dead beast shalbe his.
ex.21.35	Exodus 21:35	¶ And if one mans oxe hurt anothers, that he die, then they shall sell the liue oxe, and diuide the money of it, and the dead oxe also they shall diuide.
ex.21.36	Exodus 21:36	Or if it bee knowen that the oxe hath vsed to push in time past, and his owner hath not kept him in, hee shall surely pay oxe for oxe, and the dead shall be his owne.
ex.22.1	Exodus 22:1	If a man shal steale an oxe, or a sheepe, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore fiue oxen for an oxe, and foure sheepe for a sheepe.
ex.22.2	Exodus 22:2	¶ If a thiefe bee found breaking vp, and be smitten that he die, there shal no blood be shed for him.
ex.22.3	Exodus 22:3	If the Sunne be risen vpon him, there shall be blood shed for him: for hee should make full restitution: if he haue nothing, then he shall bee sold for his theft.
ex.22.4	Exodus 22:4	If the theft be certainely found in his hand aliue, whether it bee oxe or asse, or sheepe, he shall restore double.
ex.22.5	Exodus 22:5	¶ If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall put in his beast, and shall feede in another mans field: of the best of his owne field, and of the best of his owne vineyard shall he make restitution.
ex.22.6	Exodus 22:6	¶ If fire breake out, and catch in thornes, so that the stackes of corne, or the standing corne, or the field be consumed therewith; hee that kindled the fire, shall surely make restitution.
ex.22.7	Exodus 22:7	¶ If a man shal deliuer vnto his neighbour money or stuffe to keepe, and it be stollen out of the mans house; if the thiefe be found, let him pay double.
ex.22.8	Exodus 22:8	If the thiefe be not found, then the master of the house shall be brought vnto the Iudges, to see whether he haue put his hande vnto his neighbours goods.
ex.22.9	Exodus 22:9	For all maner of trespasse, whether it be for oxe, for asse, for sheepe, for raiment, or for any maner of lost thing, which another challengeth to be his: the cause of both parties shall come before the Iudges, and whome the Iudges shall condemne, he shall pay double vnto his neighbour.
ex.22.10	Exodus 22:10	If a man deliuer vnto his neighbour an asse, or an oxe, or a sheepe, or any beast to keepe, and it die, or be hurt, or driuen away, no man seeing it,
ex.22.11	Exodus 22:11	Then shall an othe of the LORD be betweene them both, that hee hath not put his hand vnto his neighbours goods: and the owner of it shall accept thereof, and he shall not make it good.
ex.22.12	Exodus 22:12	And if it be stollen from him, he shall make restitution vnto the owner thereof.
ex.22.13	Exodus 22:13	If it be torne in pieces, then let him bring it for witnesse, and hee shall not make good that which was torne.
ex.22.14	Exodus 22:14	¶ And if a man borrowe ought of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, the owner thereof being not with it, he shall surely make it good.
ex.22.15	Exodus 22:15	But if the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good: If it bee an hired thing, it came for his hire.
ex.22.16	Exodus 22:16	¶ And if a man entice a maide that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.
ex.22.17	Exodus 22:17	If her father vtterly refuse to giue her vnto him, he shall pay money according to the dowrie of virgins.
ex.22.18	Exodus 22:18	¶ Thou shalt not suffer a witch to liue.
ex.22.19	Exodus 22:19	¶ Whosoeuer lieth with a beast, shall surely be put to death.
ex.22.20	Exodus 22:20	¶ Hee that sacrificeth vnto any god saue vnto the LORD onely, hee shall be vtterly destroyed.
ex.22.21	Exodus 22:21	¶ Thou shalt neither vexe a stranger, nor oppresse him: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.
ex.22.22	Exodus 22:22	¶ Yee shall not afflict any widow, or fatherlesse child.
ex.22.23	Exodus 22:23	If thou afflict them in any wise, and they crie at all vnto mee, I will surely heare their crie.
ex.22.24	Exodus 22:24	And my wrath shall waxe hote, and I will kill you with the sword: and your wiues shall be widowes, and your children fatherlesse.
ex.22.25	Exodus 22:25	¶ If thou lend money to any of my people that is poore by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an vsurer, neither shalt thou lay vpon him vsurie.
ex.22.26	Exodus 22:26	If thou at all take thy neighbors raiment to pledge, thou shalt deliuer it vnto him by that the sun goeth downe.
ex.22.27	Exodus 22:27	For that is his couering onely, it is his raiment for his skinne: wherein shal he sleepe? and it shal come to passe, when he crieth vnto mee, that I will heare: for I am gracious.
ex.22.28	Exodus 22:28	¶ Thou shalt not reuile the Gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.
ex.22.29	Exodus 22:29	¶ Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the first borne of thy sonnes shalt thou giue vnto me.
ex.22.30	Exodus 22:30	Likewise shalt thou do with thine oxen, and with thy sheepe: seuen dayes it shall be with his damme, on the eight day thou shalt giue it me.
ex.22.31	Exodus 22:31	¶ And ye shall be holy men vnto me: neither shall ye eate any flesh that is torne of beasts in the field: yee shall cast it to the dogs.
ex.23.1	Exodus 23:1	Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to bee an vnrighteous witnesse.
ex.23.2	Exodus 23:2	¶ Thou shalt not follow a multitude to doe euill: neither shalt thou speake in a cause, to decline after many, to wrest iudgement:
ex.23.3	Exodus 23:3	¶ Neither shalt thou countenance a poore man in his cause.
ex.23.4	Exodus 23:4	¶ If thou meete thine enemies oxe or his asse going astray, thou shalt surely bring it backe to him againe.
ex.23.5	Exodus 23:5	If thou see the asse of him that hateth thee, lying vnder his burden, and wouldest forbeare to helpe him, thou shalt surely helpe with him.
ex.23.6	Exodus 23:6	Thou shalt not wrest the iudgement of thy poore in his cause.
ex.23.7	Exodus 23:7	Keepe thee farre from a false matter: and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not iustifie the wicked.
ex.23.8	Exodus 23:8	¶ And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and peruerteth the words of the righteous.
ex.23.9	Exodus 23:9	¶ Also thou shalt not oppresse a stranger: for yee know the heart of a stranger, seeing yee were strangers in the land of Egypt.
ex.23.10	Exodus 23:10	And sixe yeres thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in the fruites thereof:
ex.23.11	Exodus 23:11	But the seuenth yeere thou shalt let it rest, and lie still, that the poore of thy people may eate, and what they leaue, the beasts of the field shall eate. In like maner thou shalt deale with thy vineyard, and with thy oliue yard.
ex.23.12	Exodus 23:12	Sixe dayes thou shalt doe thy worke, and on the seuenth day thou shalt rest: that thine oxe and thine asse may rest, and the sonne of thy handmayd, & the stranger may be refreshed.
ex.23.13	Exodus 23:13	And in all things that I haue said vnto you, be circumspect: and make no mention of the names of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.
ex.23.14	Exodus 23:14	¶ Three times thou shalt keepe a feast vnto me in the yeere.
ex.23.15	Exodus 23:15	Thou shalt keepe the feast of vnleauened bread: thou shalt eate vnleauened bread seuen daies, as I commanded thee in the time appointed of the moneth Abib: for in it thou camest out from Egypt: and none shall appeare before me emptie:
ex.23.16	Exodus 23:16	And the feast of haruest, the first fruits of thy labours, which thou hast sowen in the field: and the feast of ingathering which is in the end of the yeere, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.
ex.23.17	Exodus 23:17	Three times in the yeere all thy males shall appeare before the Lord GOD.
ex.23.18	Exodus 23:18	Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leauened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remaine vntill the morning.
ex.23.19	Exodus 23:19	The first of the first fruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the LORD thy God: thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mothers milke.
ex.23.20	Exodus 23:20	¶ Behold, I send an Angel before thee to keepe thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I haue prepared.
ex.23.21	Exodus 23:21	Beware of him, and obey his voice, prouoke him not: for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.
ex.23.22	Exodus 23:22	But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and doe all that I speake, then I wil be an enemie vnto thine enemies, and an aduersarie vnto thine aduersaries.
ex.23.23	Exodus 23:23	For mine Angel shall goe before thee, and bring thee in vnto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hiuites, and the Iebusites: and I will cut them off.
ex.23.24	Exodus 23:24	Thou shalt not bow downe to their gods, nor serue them, nor doe after their workes: but thou shalt vtterly ouerthrowe them, and quite breake downe their images.
ex.23.25	Exodus 23:25	And yee shall serue the LORD your God, and he shall blesse thy bread, and thy water: and I will take sicknes away from the midst of thee.
ex.23.26	Exodus 23:26	¶ There shall nothing cast their yong, nor bee barren in thy land: the number of thy dayes I will fulfill.
ex.23.27	Exodus 23:27	I will send my feare before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turne their backes vnto thee.
ex.23.28	Exodus 23:28	And I will send hornets before thee, which shall driue out the Hiuite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite from before thee.
ex.23.29	Exodus 23:29	I will not driue them out from before thee in one yeere, lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee.
ex.23.30	Exodus 23:30	By little and little I will driue them out from before thee, vntill thou be increased and inherit the land.
