ne.12.44	Nehemiah 12:44	¶ And at that time were some appointed ouer the chambers for the treasures, for the offerings, for the first fruits, and for the tithes, to gather into them out of the fields of the cities the portions of the law for the priests and Leuites: for Iudah reioyced for the Priests, & for the Leuites that waited.
ne.12.45	Nehemiah 12:45	And both the singers and the porters kept the ward of their God, and the ward of the purification, according to the commandement of Dauid, and of Solomon his sonne.
ne.12.46	Nehemiah 12:46	For in the dayes of Dauid and Asaph of old, there were chiefe of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiuing vnto God.
ne.12.47	Nehemiah 12:47	And all Israel in the dayes of Zerubbabel, and in the dayes of Nehemiah, gaue the portions of the singers, and the porters, euery day his portion, and they sanctified holy things vnto the Leuites, and the Leuites sanctified them vnto the children of Aaron.
ne.13.1	Nehemiah 13:1	On that day they read in the booke of Moses in the audience of the people, and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the Congregation of God for euer,
ne.13.2	Nehemiah 13:2	Because they met not the children of Israel with bread, and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.
ne.13.3	Nehemiah 13:3	Now it came to passe when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.
ne.13.4	Nehemiah 13:4	¶ And before this Eliashib the priest hauing the ouersight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied vnto Tobiah:
ne.13.5	Nehemiah 13:5	And hee had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meat offrings, the frankincense and the vessels, and the tithes of the corne, the new wine, and the oile, which was commanded to be giuen to the Leuites, and the singers, and the porters, and the offerings of the priests.
ne.13.6	Nehemiah 13:6	But in all this time was not I at Ierusalem: for in the two and thirtieth yeere of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, came I vnto the king, and after certaine dayes, obtained I leaue of the King:
ne.13.7	Nehemiah 13:7	And I came to Ierusalem, and vnderstood of the euil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.
ne.13.8	Nehemiah 13:8	And it grieued me sore, therefore I cast foorth all the houshold stuffe of Tobiah out of the chamber:
ne.13.9	Nehemiah 13:9	Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers, and thither brought I againe the vessels of the house of God, with the meate offering, and the frankincense.
ne.13.10	Nehemiah 13:10	¶ And I perceiued that the portions of the Leuites had not beene giuen them: for the Leuites and the singers that did the worke, were fled euery one to his field.
ne.13.11	Nehemiah 13:11	Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
ne.13.12	Nehemiah 13:12	Then brought all Iudah the tithe of the corne, and the new wine, and the oyle, vnto the treasuries.
ne.13.13	Nehemiah 13:13	And I made treasurers ouer the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Leuites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the sonne of Zaccur, the sonne of Mattaniah: for they were counted faithfull, and their office was to distribute vnto their brethren.
ne.13.14	Nehemiah 13:14	Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds, that I haue done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.
ne.13.15	Nehemiah 13:15	¶ In those dayes sawe I in Iudah, some treading wine presses on the Sabbath, and bringing in sheaues, and lading asses, as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all maner of burdens, which they brought into Ierusalem on the Sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they solde victuals.
ne.13.16	Nehemiah 13:16	There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish and all maner of ware, and solde on the Sabbath vnto the children of Iudah, and in Ierusalem.
ne.13.17	Nehemiah 13:17	Then I contended with the Nobles of Iudah, and sayd vnto them, What euill thing is this that ye doe, and profane the Sabbath day?
ne.13.18	Nehemiah 13:18	Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this euill vpon vs, and vpon this citie? yet ye bring more wrath vpon Israel, by profaning the Sabbath.
ne.13.19	Nehemiah 13:19	And it came to passe, that when the gates of Ierusalem beganne to be darke before the Sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the Sabbath: and some of my seruants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the Sabbath day.
ne.13.20	Nehemiah 13:20	So the merchants, and sellers of all kinde of ware, lodged without Ierusalem once or twice.
ne.13.21	Nehemiah 13:21	Then I testified against them, and said vnto them, Why lodge yee about the wall? If ye doe so againe, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the Sabbath.
ne.13.22	Nehemiah 13:22	And I commanded the Leuites, that they should cleanse themselues, and that they should come and keepe the gates, to sanctifie the Sabbath day: Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me, according to the greatnesse of thy mercie.
ne.13.23	Nehemiah 13:23	¶ In those dayes also sawe I Iewes that had maried wiues of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:
ne.13.24	Nehemiah 13:24	And their children spake halfe in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speake in the Iewes language, but according to the language of ech people.
ne.13.25	Nehemiah 13:25	And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certeine of them, and pluckt off their haire, and made them sweare by God, saying, Yee shall not giue your daughters vnto their sonnes, nor take their daughters vnto your sonnes, or for your selues.
ne.13.26	Nehemiah 13:26	Did not Solomon king of Israel sinne by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloued of his God, and God made him king ouer all Israel: neuerthelesse, euen him did outlandish women cause to sinne.
ne.13.27	Nehemiah 13:27	Shall wee then hearken vnto you, to doe all this great euill, to transgresse against our God, in marrying strange wiues?
ne.13.28	Nehemiah 13:28	And one of the sonnes of Ioiada, the sonne of Eliashib the high Priest, was sonne in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therfore I chased him from me.
ne.13.29	Nehemiah 13:29	Remember them, O my God, because they haue defiled the Priesthood, and the couenant of the Priesthood, and of the Leuites.
ne.13.30	Nehemiah 13:30	Thus cleansed I them from all strangers, and appointed the wards of the Priests and the Leuites, euery one in his businesse:
ne.13.31	Nehemiah 13:31	And for the wood-offering, at times appointed, and for the first fruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
et.1.1	Esther 1:1	Now it came to passe in the dayes of Ahasuerus, (this is Ahasuerus which reigned from India, euen vnto Ethiopia, ouer an hundred, and seuen and twentie prouinces.)
et.1.2	Esther 1:2	That in those dayes, when the King Ahasuerus sate on the throne of his kingdome, which was in Shushan the palace:
et.1.3	Esther 1:3	In the third yeere of his reigne, he made a feast vnto all his Princes, and his seruants, the power of Persia and Media, the Nobles and Princes of the prouinces being before him.
et.1.4	Esther 1:4	When he shewed the riches of his glorious kingdome, and the honour of his excellent maiestie, many dayes, euen an hundred and fourescore dayes.
et.1.5	Esther 1:5	And when these dayes were expired, the king made a feast vnto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both vnto great and small, seuen dayes, in the court of the garden of the kings palace,
et.1.6	Esther 1:6	Where were white, greene and blew hangings, fastened with cords of fine linnen, and purple, to siluer rings, and pillers of marble: the beds were of gold and siluer, vpon a pauement of red, and blewe, and white, and blacke marble.
et.1.7	Esther 1:7	And they gaue them drinke in vessels of gold, (the vessels being diuers one from another) and royall wine in abundance, according to the state of the king.
et.1.8	Esther 1:8	And the drinking was according to the law, none did compell: for the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should doe according to euery mans pleasure.
et.1.9	Esther 1:9	Also Uasthi the Queene made a feast for the women, in the royall house which belonged to king Ahasuerus.
et.1.10	Esther 1:10	¶ On the seuenth day, when the heart of the King was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seuen chamberlens that serued in the presence of Ahasuerus the king,
et.1.11	Esther 1:11	To bring Uasthi the Queene before the king, with the Crowne royall, to shew the people, and the Princes her beautie: for she was faire to looke on.
et.1.12	Esther 1:12	But the Queene Uasthi refused to come at the Kings commandement by his chamberlens: therefore was the King very wroth, and his anger burned in him.
et.1.13	Esther 1:13	¶ Then the king saide to the wise men, which knew the times (for so was the Kings maner towards all that knew law, and iudgement:
et.1.14	Esther 1:14	And the next vnto him, was Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshis, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seuen Princes of Persia, and Media, which saw the Kings face, and which sate the first in the kingdome.)
et.1.15	Esther 1:15	What shall wee doe vnto the Queene Uasthi, according to law, because she hath not performed the commandement of the king Ahasuerus, by the chamberlens?
et.1.16	Esther 1:16	And Memucan answered before the king and the Princes; Uasthi the Queene hath not done wrong to the king onely, but also to all the Princes, and to all the people that are in all the prouinces of the king Ahasuerus.
et.1.17	Esther 1:17	For this deed of the queene shall come abroad vnto all women, so that they shal despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall bee reported; The king Ahasuerus commanded Uasthi the queene to be brought in before him, but she came not.
et.1.18	Esther 1:18	Likewise shall the Ladies of Persia and Media say this day vnto all the kings princes, which haue heard of the deed of the Queene. Thus shall there arise too much contempt and wrath.
et.1.19	Esther 1:19	If it please the king, let there go a royall commandement from him, and let it bee written among the lawes of the Persians, and the Medes, that it be not altered, that Uasthi come no more before king Ahasuerus, and let the king giue her royall estate vnto another that is better then she.
et.1.20	Esther 1:20	And when the kings decree, which he shal make, shalbe published throughout all his empire, (for it is great:) all the wiues shall giue to their husbands honour, both to great and small.
et.1.21	Esther 1:21	And the saying pleased the king and the princes, and the king did according to the word of Memucan:
et.1.22	Esther 1:22	For he sent letters into all the kings prouinces, into euery prouince, according to the writing thereof, and to euery people after their language, that euery man should beare rule in his owne house, and that it should be published according to the language of euerie people.
et.2.1	Esther 2:1	After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased, hee remembred Uasthi, and what shee had done, and what was decreed against her.
et.2.2	Esther 2:2	Then saide the kings seruants, that ministred vnto him, Let there bee faire yong virgins sought for the king:
et.2.3	Esther 2:3	And let the king appoint officers in all the prouinces of his kingdome, that they may gather together all the faire yong virgins vnto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women vnto the custodie of Hege the kings chamberlaine, keeper of the women, and let their things for purification bee giuen them:
et.2.4	Esther 2:4	And let the maiden which pleaseth the king, bee Queene in stead of Uasthi. And the thing pleased the king, and he did so.
et.2.5	Esther 2:5	¶ Now in Shushan the palace, there was a certaine Iew, whose name was Mordecai, the sonne of Iair, the sonne of Shimei, the sonne of Kish, a Beniamite,
et.2.6	Esther 2:6	Who had bene caried away from Ierusalem, with the captiuitie which had bene caried away with Ieconiah king of Iudah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the King of Babylon had caried away.
et.2.7	Esther 2:7	And hee brought vp Hadassah (that is Esther) his vncles daughter, for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was faire and beautiful, whom Mordecai (when her father and mother were dead) tooke for his owne daughter.
et.2.8	Esther 2:8	¶ So it came to passe, when the kings commandement and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together vnto Shushan the palace, to the custodie of Hegai, that Esther was brought also vnto the kings house, to the custodie of Hegai, keeper of the women.
et.2.9	Esther 2:9	And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindnesse of him, and hee speedily gaue her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seuen maidens, which were meet to be giuen her, out of the Kings house, and hee preferred her and her maids, vnto the best place of the house of the women.
et.2.10	Esther 2:10	Esther had not shewed her people, nor her kinred: for Mordecai had charged her, that she should not shew it.
et.2.11	Esther 2:11	And Mordecai walked euery day before the court of the womens house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.
et.2.12	Esther 2:12	¶ Now when euery maids turne was come, to goe in to King Ahasnerus, after that shee had bene twelue moneths, according to the maner of the women (for so were the dayes of their purifications accomplished, to wit, sixe moneths with oile of myrrhe, and sixe moneths with sweet odours, and with other things for the purifying of the women.)
et.2.13	Esther 2:13	Then thus came euery maiden vnto the king, whatsoeuer she desired, was giuen her, to goe with her out of the house of the women, vnto the kings house.
et.2.14	Esther 2:14	In the euening she went, and on the morrowe she returned into the second house of the women, to the custodie of Shaashgaz the kings chamberlen, which kept the concubines: shee came in vnto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that shee were called by name.
et.2.15	Esther 2:15	¶ Now when the turne of Esther, the daughter of Abihail, the vncle of Mordecai (who had taken her for his daughter) was come, to goe in vnto the king: she required nothing, but what Hegai the kings chamberlen the keeper of the women, appointed: And Esther obtained fauour in the sight of all them that looked vpon her.
et.2.16	Esther 2:16	So Esther was taken vnto king Ahasuerus, into his house royall, in the tenth moneth (which is the moneth Tebeth) in the seuenth yeere of his reigne.
et.2.17	Esther 2:17	And the king loued Esther aboue all the women, and she obtained grace and fauour in his sight, more then all the virgins; so that hee set the royall crowne vpon her head, and made her queene, in stead of Uasthi.
et.2.18	Esther 2:18	Then the king made a great feast vnto all his princes and his seruants, euen Esthers feast, and hee made a release to the prouinces, and gaue gifts, according to the state of the king.
et.2.19	Esther 2:19	And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sate in the kings gate.
et.2.20	Esther 2:20	Esther had not yet shewed her kindred, nor her people, as Mordecai had charged her: For Esther did the commandement of Mordecai, like as when she was brought vp with him.
et.2.21	Esther 2:21	¶ In those dayes, (while Mordecai sate in the kings gate) two of the kings chamberlens, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the doore, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus:
et.2.22	Esther 2:22	And the thing was knowen to Mordecai, who told it vnto Esther the Queene, and Esther certified the king thereof, in Mordecais name.
et.2.23	Esther 2:23	And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therfore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the booke of the chronicles before the king.
et.3.1	Esther 3:1	After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman, the sonne of Amedatha the Agagite, and aduanced him, and set his seate aboue all the princes that were with him.
et.3.2	Esther 3:2	And all the kings seruants, that were in the kings gate, bowed, and reuerenced Haman, for the king had so commanded concerning him: but Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reuerence.
et.3.3	Esther 3:3	Then the kings seruants, which were in the kings gate, sayd vnto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the kings commandement?
et.3.4	Esther 3:4	Now it came to passe, when they spake daily vnto him, and he hearkened not vnto them; that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai his matters would stand, for he had told them that he was a Iewe.
et.3.5	Esther 3:5	And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reuerence, then was Haman full of wrath.
et.3.6	Esther 3:6	And hee thought scorne to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Iewes, that were throughout the whole kingdome of Ahasuerus, euen the people of Mordecai.
et.3.7	Esther 3:7	¶ In the first moneth (that is, the moneth Nisan) in the twelfth yeere of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman, from day to day, and from moneth to moneth, to the twelfth moneth, that is the moneth Adar.
et.3.8	Esther 3:8	¶ And Haman saide vnto king Ahasuerus: There is a certaine people scattered abroad, and dispersed among the people, in all the prouinces of thy kingdome, and their lawes are diuerse from all people, neither keepe they the kings lawes; therefore it is not for the kings profit to suffer them.
et.3.9	Esther 3:9	If it please the king, let it be written, that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of siluer to the handes of those that haue the charge of the businesse, to bring it into the kings treasuries.
et.3.10	Esther 3:10	And the king tooke his ring from his hand, and gaue it vnto Haman the sonne of Ammedatha the Agagite, the Iewes enemie.
et.3.11	Esther 3:11	And the king saide vnto Haman, The siluer is giuen to thee, the people also, to doe with them, as it seemeth good to thee.
et.3.12	Esther 3:12	Then were the kings scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first moneth, and there was written, according to all that Haman had commanded, vnto the kings Lieutenants, and to the gouernours, that were ouer euery prouince, and to the rulers of euery people of euery prouince, according to the writing thereof, and to euery people, after their language, in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the kings ring.
et.3.13	Esther 3:13	And the letters were sent by posts into all the kings prouinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish all Iewes, both yong and olde, litle children and women, in one day, euen vpon the thirteenth day of the twelfth moneth (which is the moneth Adar) and to take the spoile of them for a pray.
et.3.14	Esther 3:14	The copie of the writing for a commandement to bee giuen in euery prouince, was published vnto all people, that they should bee ready against that day.
et.3.15	Esther 3:15	The postes went out, being hastened by the kings commandement, and the decree was giuen in Shushan the palace: and the king and Haman sate downe to drinke, but the citie Shushan was perplexed.
et.4.1	Esther 4:1	When Mordecai perceiued all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the citie, and cried with a loud and a bitter crie:
et.4.2	Esther 4:2	And came euen before the kings gate: for none might enter into the kings gate clothed with sackcloth.
et.4.3	Esther 4:3	And in euery prouince, whithersoeuer the kings commaundement, and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Iewes, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
et.4.4	Esther 4:4	¶ So Esthers maides and her chamberlaines came, and told it her: then was the Queene exceedingly grieued, and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take away the sackcloth from him: but he receiued it not.
et.4.5	Esther 4:5	Then called Esther for Hatach, one of the kings chamberlaines, whom he had appointed to attend vpon her, and gaue him a commaundement to Mordecai, to know what it was, and why it was.
et.4.6	Esther 4:6	So Hatach went forth to Mordecai, vnto the street of the citie, which was before the kings gate:
et.4.7	Esther 4:7	And Mordecai tolde him of all that had happened vnto him, and of the summe of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the Kings treasuries for the Iewes, to destroy them.
et.4.8	Esther 4:8	Also he gaue him the copie of the writing of the decree, that was giuen at Shushan to destroy them, to shewe it vnto Esther, and to declare it vnto her, and to charge her that she should goe in vnto the king, to make supplication vnto him, and to make request before him, for her people.
et.4.9	Esther 4:9	And Hatach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
et.4.10	Esther 4:10	¶ Againe Esther spake vnto Hatach, and gaue him commaundement vnto Mordecai;
et.4.11	Esther 4:11	All the Kings seruants, and the people of the kings prouinces do know, that whosoeuer, whether man or woman, shall come vnto the King into the inner court, who is not called, there is one lawe of his to put him to death, except such to whom the King shall hold out the golden scepter, that he may liue: but I haue not beene called to come in vnto the King, these thirtie dayes.
et.4.12	Esther 4:12	And they tolde to Mordecai Esthers words.
et.4.13	Esther 4:13	Then Mordecai commanded to answere Esther; Thinke not with thy selfe that thou shalt escape in the kings house, more then all the Iewes.
et.4.14	Esther 4:14	For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliuerance arise to the Iewes from another place, but thou and thy fathers house shall be destroyed: And who knoweth, whether thou art come to the kingdome for such a time as this?
et.4.15	Esther 4:15	¶ Then Esther bade them returne Mordecai this answere:
et.4.16	Esther 4:16	Goe, gather together all the Iewes that are present in Shushan, and fast yee for me, and neither eate nor drinke three dayes, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise, and so will I goe in vnto the king, which is not according to the Law, and if I perish, I perish.
et.4.17	Esther 4:17	So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.
et.5.1	Esther 5:1	Now it came to passe on the third day, that Esther put on her royall apparell, and stood in the inner court of the kings house, ouer against the kings house: and the King sate vpon his royall throne in the royall house, ouer against the gate of the house.
et.5.2	Esther 5:2	And it was so, when the king saw Esther the Queene standing in the court, that shee obtained fauour in his sight: and the king helde out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand: So Esther drew neere, and touched the top of the scepter.
et.5.3	Esther 5:3	Then sayd the King vnto her, What wilt thou, Queene Esther? and what is thy request? it shall bee euen giuen thee to the halfe of the kingdome.
et.5.4	Esther 5:4	And Esther answered, If it seeme good vnto the King, let the King and Haman come this day vnto the banquet that I haue prepared for him.
et.5.5	Esther 5:5	Then the King sayd, Cause Haman to make haste, that he may doe as Esther hath said: So the king and Haman came to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
et.5.6	Esther 5:6	¶ And the king said vnto Esther at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, and it shall be granted thee? and what is thy request? euen to the halfe of the kingdome it shall be performed.
et.5.7	Esther 5:7	Then answered Esther, and said, My petition, and my request is,
et.5.8	Esther 5:8	If I haue found fauour in the sight of the king, and if it please the king to grant my petition, and to performe my request, let the king, and Haman, come to the banquet that I shall prepare for them, and I wil do to morow, as the king hath said.
et.5.9	Esther 5:9	¶ Then went Haman foorth that day, ioyfull, and with a glad heart: but when Haman saw Mordecai in the kings gate, that hee stood not vp, nor mooued for him, hee was full of indignation against Mordecai.
et.5.10	Esther 5:10	Neuerthelesse Haman refrained himselfe, and when he came home, hee sent and called for his friends, and Zeresh his wife.
et.5.11	Esther 5:11	And Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and the multitude of his children, and all the things wherein the king had promoted him, and how he had aduanced him aboue the Princes, and seruants of the king.
et.5.12	Esther 5:12	Haman said moreouer, Yea Esther the Queene did let no man come in with the king vnto the banquet that she had prepared, but my selfe; and to morrow am I inuited vnto her also with the king.
et.5.13	Esther 5:13	Yet all this auaileth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Iew sitting at the kings gate.
et.5.14	Esther 5:14	¶ Then saide Zeresh his wife, and all his friends vnto him, Let a gallous be made of fifty cubits hie, and to morrow speake thou vnto the king, that Mordecai may be hanged thereon: then goe thou in merily with the king vnto the banquet. And the thing pleased Haman, and hee caused the gallous to be made.
et.6.1	Esther 6:1	On that night could not the King sleepe, and hee commaunded to bring the booke of Records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.
et.6.2	Esther 6:2	And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana, and Teresh, two of the kings chamberleus, the keepers of the doore, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
et.6.3	Esther 6:3	And the king said, What honour and dignitie hath bene done to Mordecai for this? Then said the kings seruants that ministred vnto him, There is nothing done for him.
et.6.4	Esther 6:4	¶ And the king said, Who is in the court? (now Haman was come into the outward court of the kings house, to speake vnto the king, to hang Mordecai on the gallons that hee had prepared for him.)
et.6.5	Esther 6:5	And the kings seruants said vnto him, Behold, Haman standeth in the court. And the King saide, Let him come in.
et.6.6	Esther 6:6	So Haman came in, and the king said vnto him, What shall be done vnto the man whom the king delighteth to honour? (now Haman thought in his heart, To whom would the king delight to doe honour, more then to my selfe?)
et.6.7	Esther 6:7	And Haman answered the king, For the man whom the king delighteth to honour,
et.6.8	Esther 6:8	Let the royall apparell bee brought, which the King vseth to weare, and the horse that the King rideth vpon, and the crowne royal which is set vpon his head:
et.6.9	Esther 6:9	And let this apparell and horse bee deliuered to the hand of one of the kings most noble Princes, that they may aray the man withall, whom the king delighteth to honour, and bring him on horsebacke through the streete of the city, and proclaime before him, Thus shal it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.
et.6.10	Esther 6:10	Then the king saide to Haman, Make haste, and take the apparell, and the horse, as thou hast said, and doe euen so to Mordecai the Iew, that sitteth at the Kings gate: let nothing faile of all that thou hast spoken.
et.6.11	Esther 6:11	Then tooke Haman the apparell, and the horse, & arayed Mordecai, and brought him on hors-backe through the streete of the city, and proclaimed before him: Thus shall it bee done vnto the man whom the King delighteth to honour.
et.6.12	Esther 6:12	¶ And Mordecai came againe to the kings gate: but Haman hasted to his house, mourning, and hauing his head couered.
et.6.13	Esther 6:13	And Haman told Zeresh his wife, and all his friends, euery thing that had befallen him. Then saide his wise men, and Zeresh his wife vnto him, If Mordecai be of the seed of the Iewes, before whom thou hast begun to fall, thou shalt not preuaile against him, but shalt surely fall before him.
et.6.14	Esther 6:14	And while they were yet talking with him, came the kings chamberlens, and hasted to bring Haman vnto the banquet that Esther had prepared.
et.7.1	Esther 7:1	So the King and Haman came to banquet with Esther the Queene.
et.7.2	Esther 7:2	And the king said againe vnto Esther, on the second day at the banquet of wine, What is thy petition, Queene Esther, and it shalbe granted thee? and what is thy request? and it shall bee performed, euen to the halfe of the kingdome.
et.7.3	Esther 7:3	Then Esther the Queene answered, and said; If I haue found fauour in thy sight, O King, and if it please the King, let my life be giuen me at my petition, and my people at my request.
et.7.4	Esther 7:4	For we are sold, I, and my people, to be destroyed, to be slaine, and to perish: but if we had bene sold for bondmen, and bondwomen, I had held my tongue, although the enemy could not counteruaile the kings dammage.
et.7.5	Esther 7:5	¶ Then the king Ahasuerus answered, & said vnto Esther the Queene: Who is he? and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?
et.7.6	Esther 7:6	And Esther said, The aduersary and enemie, is this wicked Haman. Then Haman was afraid before the King and the Queene.
et.7.7	Esther 7:7	¶ And the king arising from the banquet of wine in his wrath, went into the palace garden: and Haman stood vp to make request for his life to Esther the Queene: for he saw that there was euill determined against him by the King.
et.7.8	Esther 7:8	Then the king returned out of the palace garden, into the place of the banquet of wine, and Haman was fallen vpon the bed whereon Esther was. Then said the King, Will hee force the Queene also before me in the house? As the word went out of the Kings mouth, they couered Hamans face.
et.7.9	Esther 7:9	And Harbonah one of the chamberlaines, said before the king; Behold also the gallowes, fiftie cubites high, which Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standeth in the house of Haman. Then the king said, Hang him thereon.
et.7.10	Esther 7:10	So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then was the Kings wrath pacified.
et.8.1	Esther 8:1	On that day did the King Ahasuerus giue the house of Haman, the Iewes enemy, vnto Esther the Queene; and Mordecai came before the King; for Esther hade told what he was vnto her.
et.8.2	Esther 8:2	And the king tooke off his Ring which he had taken from Haman, and gaue it vnto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai ouer the house of Haman.
et.8.3	Esther 8:3	¶ And Esther spake yet againe before the king, and fell downe at his feet, and besought him with teares, to put away the mischiefe of Haman the Agagite, and his deuice, that he had deuised against the Iewes.
et.8.4	Esther 8:4	Then the king helde out the golden scepter toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king,
et.8.5	Esther 8:5	And said, If it please the king, and if I haue found fauour in his sight, and the thing seeme right before the king, and I bee pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reuerse the letters deuised by Haman the sonne of Hammedatha the Agagite, which hee wrote to destroy the Iewes, which are in all the kings prouinces.
et.8.6	Esther 8:6	For how can I endure to see the euill that shall come vnto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kinred?
et.8.7	Esther 8:7	¶ Then the king Ahasuerus said vnto Esther the Queene, and to Mordecai the Iewe, Behold, I haue giuen Esther the house of Haman, and him they haue hanged vpon the gallowes, because hee layde his hand vpon the Iewes.
et.8.8	Esther 8:8	Write ye also for the Iewes, as it liketh you, in the Kings name, and seale it with the Kings ring: for the writing which is written in the Kings name, and sealed with the Kings ring, may no man reuerse.
et.8.9	Esther 8:9	Then were the kings scribes called at that time, in the third moneth, (that is, the month Siuan) on the three and twentieth day thereof, and it was written (according to all that Mordecai commanded) vnto the Iewes, and to the Lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the prouinces, which are from India vnto Ethiopia, an hundred, twentie and seuen prouinces, vnto euery prouince according to the writing thereof, and vnto euery people after their language, and to the Iewes, according to their writing, and according to their language.
et.8.10	Esther 8:10	And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus name, and sealed it with the kings Ring, and sent letters by Postes, on horsebacke, and riders on mules, camels, and yong dromedaries:
et.8.11	Esther 8:11	Wherein the King granted the Iewes, which were in euery citie, to gather themselues together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish all the power of the people and prouince that would assault them, both little ones, and women, and to take the spoile of them for a pray:
et.8.12	Esther 8:12	Upon one day, in all the prouinces of king Ahasuerus, namely vpon the thirteenth day of the twelfth moneth, which is the moneth Adar.
et.8.13	Esther 8:13	The copy of the writing, for a commandement to bee giuen in euery prouince, was published vnto all people, and that the Iewes should be readie against that day, to auenge themselues on their enemies.
et.8.14	Esther 8:14	So the posts that rode vpon mules and camels went out, being hastened, and pressed on by the kings commandement, and the decree was giuen at Shushan the palace.
et.8.15	Esther 8:15	¶ And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king, in royall apparell, of blew and white, and with a great crowne of gold, and with a garment of fine linnen, and purple, and the citie of Shushan reioyced, and was glad:
et.8.16	Esther 8:16	The Iewes had light and gladnesse, and ioy and honour.
et.8.17	Esther 8:17	And in euery prouince, and in euery city, whithersoeuer the kings commandement, and his decree came, the Iewes had ioy and gladnes, a feast and a good day: And many of the people of the land became Iewes; for the feare of the Iewes fell vpon them.
et.9.1	Esther 9:1	Now in the twelfth month (that is the moneth Adar) on the thirteenth day of the same, when the Kings commaundement and his decree drew neere to bee put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Iewes hoped to haue power ouer them: (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Iewes had rule ouer them that hated them.)
et.9.2	Esther 9:2	The Iewes gathered themselues together in their cities, throughout all the prouinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt, and no man could withstand them: for the feare of them fell vpon all people.
et.9.3	Esther 9:3	And all the rulers of the prouinces, and the Lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Iewes: because the feare of Mordecai fell vpon them.
et.9.4	Esther 9:4	For Mordecai was great in the kings house, and his fame went out, throughout all the prouinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater.
et.9.5	Esther 9:5	Thus the Iewes smote all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would vnto those that hated them.
et.9.6	Esther 9:6	And in Shushan the palace the Iewes slew and destroyed fiue hundred men:
et.9.7	Esther 9:7	And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha,
et.9.8	Esther 9:8	And Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
et.9.9	Esther 9:9	And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Uaiezatha,
et.9.10	Esther 9:10	The ten sonnes of Haman the sonne of Hammedatha, the enemie of the Iewes, slew they, but on the spoile laid they not their hand.
et.9.11	Esther 9:11	On that day, the number of those that were slaine in Shushan the palace, was brought before the king.
et.9.12	Esther 9:12	¶ And the king said vnto Esther the Queene; The Iewes haue slaine and destroied fiue hundred men in Shushan the palace, & the ten sonnes of Haman; what haue they done in the rest of the kings prouinces? now what is thy petition? and it shalbe granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done.
et.9.13	Esther 9:13	Then said Esther, If it please the king, Let it bee granted to the Iewes which are in Shushan, to doe to morow also, according vnto this dayes decree, and let Hamans ten sonnes be hanged vpon the gallous.
et.9.14	Esther 9:14	And the king commanded it so to be done; and the decree was giuen at Shushan, and they hanged Hamans ten sonnes.
et.9.15	Esther 9:15	For the Iewes that were in Shushan, gathered themselues together on the fourteenth day also of the moneth Adar, and slewe three hundred men at Shushan: but on the pray they laid not their hand.
et.9.16	Esther 9:16	But the other Iewes that were in the kings prouinces, gathered themselues together, & stood for their liues, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seuenty and fiue thousand, but they laid not their handes on the pray.
et.9.17	Esther 9:17	On the thirteenth day of the moneth Adar, and on the fourteenth day of the same, rested they, and made it a day of feasting and gladnes.
et.9.18	Esther 9:18	But the Iewes that were at Shushan, assembled together on the thirteenth day therof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth day of the same, they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladnesse.
et.9.19	Esther 9:19	Therefore the Iewes of the villages, that dwelt in the vnwalled townes, made the foureteenth day of the moneth Adar, a day of gladnesse and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.
et.9.20	Esther 9:20	¶ And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters vnto all the Iewes, that were in all the prouinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh & farre,
et.9.21	Esther 9:21	To stablish this among them, that they should keepe the fourteenth day of the moneth Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yeerely:
et.9.22	Esther 9:22	As the dayes wherein the Iewes rested from their enemies, & the moneth which was turned vnto them, from sorrow to ioy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them daies of feasting and ioy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poore.
et.9.23	Esther 9:23	And the Iewes vndertooke to doe, as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written vnto them:
et.9.24	Esther 9:24	Because Haman the sonne of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemie of all the Iewes, had deuised against the Iewes to destroy them, and had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to consume them, and to destroy them.
et.9.25	Esther 9:25	But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters, that his wicked deuice which he deuised against the Iewes, should returne vpon his owne head, and that he and his sonnes, should be hanged on the gallous.
et.9.26	Esther 9:26	Wherefore they called these dayes Purim, after the name of Pur: therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seene concerning this matter, and which had come vnto them,
et.9.27	Esther 9:27	The Iewes ordeined, and tooke vpon them, and vpon their seed, and vpon all such as ioyned themselues vnto them, so as it should not faile, that they would keepe these two dayes, according to their writing, and according to their appointed time, euery yeere:
et.9.28	Esther 9:28	And that these dayes should be remembred, and kept throughout euery generation, euery family, euery prouince, and euery citie, and that these dayes of Purim should not faile from among the Iewes, nor the memoriall of them perish from their seed.
et.9.29	Esther 9:29	Then Esther the Queene, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Iew, wrote with all authoritie, to confirme this second letter of Purim.
et.9.30	Esther 9:30	And hee sent the letters vnto all the Iewes, to the hundred, twentie and seuen prouinces of the kingdome of Ahasuerus, with wordes of peace and trueth:
et.9.31	Esther 9:31	To confirme these dayes of Purim, in their times appointed, according as Mordecai the Iew, and Esther the Queene had enioyned them, and as they had decreed for themselues and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry.
et.9.32	Esther 9:32	And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the booke.
et.10.1	Esther 10:1	And the king Ahasuerus layde a tribute vpon the land, and vpon the Isles of the sea.
et.10.2	Esther 10:2	And all the actes of his power, and of his might, and the declaration of the greatnesse of Mordecai, whereunto the king aduanced him, are they not written in the booke of the Chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
et.10.3	Esther 10:3	For Mordecai the Iew was next vnto King Ahasuerus, and great among the Iewes, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.
jb.1.1	Job 1:1	There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Iob, and that man was perfect and vpright, and one that feared God, and eschewed euill.
jb.1.2	Job 1:2	And there were borne vnto him seuen sonnes, and three daughters.
jb.1.3	Job 1:3	His substance also was seuen thousand sheepe, and three thousand camels, and fiue hundred yoke of oxen, and fiue hundred shee asses, and a very great houshold; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the East.
jb.1.4	Job 1:4	And his sonnes went and feasted in their houses, euery one his day, and sent and called for their three sisters, to eate and to drinke with them.
jb.1.5	Job 1:5	And it was so, when the dayes of their feasting were gone about, that Iob sent and sanctified them, and rose vp early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: For Iob said, It may be that my sonnes haue sinned, and cursed God in their hearts: Thus did Iob continually.
jb.1.6	Job 1:6	¶ Now there was a day, when the sons of God came to present themselues before the LORD, and Satan came also among them.
jb.1.7	Job 1:7	And the LORD said vnto Satan, Whence commest thou? Then Satan answered the LORD, and sayde, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking vp and downe in it.
jb.1.8	Job 1:8	And the LORD sayd vnto Satan, Hast thou considered my seruant Iob, that there is none like him in the earth? a perfect and an vpright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth euill?
jb.1.9	Job 1:9	Then Satan answered þ LORD, and sayd, Doeth Iob feare God for nought?
jb.1.10	Job 1:10	Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on euery side? thou hast blessed the worke of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.
jb.1.11	Job 1:11	But put foorth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.
jb.1.12	Job 1:12	And the LORD said vnto Satan, Behold, all that hee hath is in thy power, onely vpon himselfe put not foorth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.
jb.1.13	Job 1:13	¶ And there was a day, when his sonnes and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brothers house:
jb.1.14	Job 1:14	And there came a messenger vnto Iob, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them,
jb.1.15	Job 1:15	And the Sabeans fell vpon them, and tooke them away: yea they haue slaine the seruants with the edge of the sword, and I onely am escaped alone, to tell thee.
jb.1.16	Job 1:16	While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heauen, and hath burnt vp the sheepe, and the seruants, and consumed them, and I onely am escaped alone, to tell thee.
jb.1.17	Job 1:17	While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Caldeans made out three bands, and fell vpon the camels, and haue caried them away, yea, and slaine the seruants with the edge of the sword, and I onely am escaped alone, to tell thee.
jb.1.18	Job 1:18	While he was yet speaking, there came also another, & said, Thy sonnes, and thy daughters, were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brothers house.
jb.1.19	Job 1:19	And beholde, there came a great winde from the wildernes, and smote the foure corners of the house, and it fell vpon the yong men, and they are dead, and I onely am escaped alone to tell thee.
jb.1.20	Job 1:20	Then Iob arose, and rent his mantle, and shaued his head, and fell downe vpon the ground and worshipped,
jb.1.21	Job 1:21	And said, Naked came I out of my mothers wombe, and naked shall I returne thither: the LORD gaue, and the LORD hath taken away, blessed be the Name of the LORD.
jb.1.22	Job 1:22	In all this Iob sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
jb.2.1	Job 2:1	Againe there was a day when the sonnes of God came to present themselues before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himselfe before the LORD.
jb.2.2	Job 2:2	And the LORD said vnto Satan, From whence commest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to & fro in the earth, and from walking vp and downe in it.
jb.2.3	Job 2:3	And the LORD said vnto Satan, Hast thou considered my seruant Iob, that there is none like him in the earth; a perfect and an vpright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth euill? and still hee holdeth fast his integritie, although thou moouedst mee against him, to destroy him without cause.
jb.2.4	Job 2:4	And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skinne for skinne, yea all that a man hath, wil he giue for his life.
jb.2.5	Job 2:5	But put foorth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.
jb.2.6	Job 2:6	And the LORD said vnto Satan, Behold, hee is in thine hand, but saue his life.
jb.2.7	Job 2:7	¶ So went Satan foorth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Iob with sore biles, from the sole of his foote vnto his crowne.
jb.2.8	Job 2:8	And hee tooke him a potsheard to scrape himselfe withall; and hee sate downe among the ashes.
jb.2.9	Job 2:9	¶ Then saide his wife vnto him, Doest thou still reteine thine integritie? Curse God, and die.
jb.2.10	Job 2:10	But he said vnto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh; what? shall wee receiue good at the hand of God, and shall wee not receiue euill? In all this did not Iob sinne with his lippes.
jb.2.11	Job 2:11	¶ Now when Iobs three friends heard of all this euill, that was come vpon him, they came euery one from his owne place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; for they had made an appointment together to come to mourne with him, and to comfort him.
jb.2.12	Job 2:12	And when they lift vp their eyes afarre off, and knew him not, they lifted vp their voice, and wept; and they rent euery one his mantle, and sprinckled dust vpon their heades toward heauen.
jb.2.13	Job 2:13	So they sate downe with him vpon the ground seuen dayes, and seuen nights, and none spake a word vnto him; for they saw that his griefe was very great.
jb.3.1	Job 3:1	After this, opened Iob his mouth, and cursed his day.
jb.3.2	Job 3:2	And Iob spake, and said,
jb.3.3	Job 3:3	Let the day perish, wherein I was borne, and the night in which it was said, There is a man-childe conceiued.
jb.3.4	Job 3:4	Let that day bee darkenesse, let not God regard it from aboue, neither let the light shine vpon it.

jb.3.6	Job 3:6	As for that night, let darkenesse seaze vpon it, let it not be ioyned vnto the dayes of the yeere, let it not come into the number of the moneths.

jb.3.8	Job 3:8	Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise vp their mourning.

jb.3.10	Job 3:10	Because it shut not vp the doores of my mothers wombe, nor hid sorrowe from mine eyes.
jb.3.11	Job 3:11	Why died I not from the wombe? why did I not giue vp the ghost when I came out of the bellie?

jb.3.13	Job 3:13	For now should I haue lien still and beene quiet, I should haue slept; then had I bene at rest,
jb.3.14	Job 3:14	With Kings and counsellers of the earth, which built desolate places for themselues,
jb.3.15	Job 3:15	Or with Princes that had golde, who filled their houses with siluer:

jb.3.17	Job 3:17	There the wicked cease from troubling: and there the wearie be at rest.
jb.3.18	Job 3:18	There the prisoners rest together, they heare not the voice of the oppressour.
jb.3.19	Job 3:19	The small and great are there, and the seruant is free from his master.
jb.3.20	Job 3:20	Wherefore is light giuen to him that is in misery, and life vnto the bitter in soule?
jb.3.21	Job 3:21	Which long for death, but it commeth not, and dig for it more then for hid treasures:
jb.3.22	Job 3:22	Which reioice exceedingly, and are glad when they can finde the graue?
jb.3.23	Job 3:23	Why is light giuen to a man, whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?
jb.3.24	Job 3:24	For my sighing commeth before I eate, and my roarings are powred out like the waters.
jb.3.25	Job 3:25	For the thing which I greatly feared is come vpon me, and that which I was afraid of, is come vnto me.
jb.3.26	Job 3:26	I was not in safetie, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet: yet trouble came.
jb.4.1	Job 4:1	Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered, and said,

jb.7.3	Job 7:3	So am I made to possesse moneths of vanitie, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.
jb.7.4	Job 7:4	When I lie downe, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro, vnto the dawning of the day.

jb.7.10	Job 7:10	Hee shall returne no more to his house: neither shall his place know him any more.
jb.7.11	Job 7:11	Therefore I will not refraine my mouth, I wil speake in the anguish of my spirit, I will complaine in the bitternesse of my soule.
jb.7.12	Job 7:12	Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch ouer me?

jb.7.15	Job 7:15	So that my soule chooseth strangling: and death rather then my life.
jb.7.16	Job 7:16	I loath it, I would not liue alway: let me alone, for my dayes are vanitie.
jb.7.17	Job 7:17	What is man, that thou shouldest magnifie him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart vpon him?

jb.33.18	Job 33:18	Hee keepeth backe his soule from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
jb.33.19	Job 33:19	Hee is chastened also with paine vpon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong paine.
jb.33.20	Job 33:20	So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soule daintie meate.
jb.33.21	Job 33:21	His flesh is consumed away that it cannot be seene; and his bones that were not seene, sticke out.
jb.33.22	Job 33:22	His soule draweth neere vnto the graue, and his life to the destroyers.
jb.33.23	Job 33:23	If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew vnto man his vprightnesse:
jb.33.24	Job 33:24	Then hee is gracious vnto him, and sayth, Deliuer him from going downe to the pit; I haue found a ransome.
jb.33.25	Job 33:25	His flesh shall be fresher then a childes: he shall returne to the dayes of his youth.
jb.33.26	Job 33:26	He shall pray vnto God, and hee will be fauourable vnto him, and hee shall see his face with ioy: for hee will render vnto man his righteousnesse.
jb.33.27	Job 33:27	He looketh vpon men, and if any say, I haue sinned, and peruerted that which was right, and it profited mee not:
jb.33.28	Job 33:28	Hee will deliuer his soule from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
jb.33.29	Job 33:29	Loe, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,
jb.33.30	Job 33:30	To bring backe his soule from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the liuing.
jb.33.31	Job 33:31	Marke well, O Iob, hearken vnto me, hold thy peace, and I wil speake.
jb.33.32	Job 33:32	If thou hast any thing to say, answere me: speake, for I desire to iustifie thee.
jb.33.33	Job 33:33	If not, hearken vnto me: holde thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisedome.
jb.34.1	Job 34:1	Furthermore Elihu answered, and said,
jb.34.2	Job 34:2	Heare my wordes, O yee wise men, and giue eare vnto me, ye that haue knowledge.
jb.34.3	Job 34:3	For the eare trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meate.
jb.34.4	Job 34:4	Let vs chuse to vs iudgement: let vs know among our selues what is good.
jb.34.5	Job 34:5	For Iob hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my iudgement.
jb.34.6	Job 34:6	Should I lye against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.
jb.34.7	Job 34:7	What man is like Iob, who drinketh vp scorning like water?

jb.34.10	Job 34:10	Therefore hearken vnto me, ye men of vnderstanding: farre bee it from God, that he should doe wickednes, and from the Almighty, that hee should commit iniquitie.
jb.34.11	Job 34:11	For the worke of a man shall he render vnto him, and cause euery man to finde according to his wayes.
jb.34.12	Job 34:12	Yea surely God will not doe wickedly, neither will the Almighty peruert iudgement.
jb.34.13	Job 34:13	Who hath giuen him a charge ouer the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

jb.34.17	Job 34:17	Shall euen he that hateth right, gouerne? and wilt thou condemne him that is most iust?
jb.34.18	Job 34:18	Is it fit to say to a King, Thou art wicked? and to Princes, Ye are vngodly?
jb.34.19	Job 34:19	How much lesse to him that accepteth not the persons of Princes, nor regardeth the rich more then the poore? for they all are the woorke of his hands.
jb.34.20	Job 34:20	In a moment shall they die, and the people shalbe troubled at midnight, and passe away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.
jb.34.21	Job 34:21	For his eyes are vpon the wayes of man, and he seeth all his goings.
jb.34.22	Job 34:22	There is no darkenes, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquitie may hide themselues.
jb.34.23	Job 34:23	For hee will not lay vpon man more then right; that he should enter into iudgement with God.
jb.34.24	Job 34:24	He shall breake in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
jb.34.25	Job 34:25	Therefore hee knoweth their workes, and he ouerturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
jb.34.26	Job 34:26	He striketh them as wicked men, in the open sight of others:
jb.34.27	Job 34:27	Because they turned backe from him, and would not consider any of his wayes.
jb.34.28	Job 34:28	So that they cause the cry of the poore to come vnto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
jb.34.29	Job 34:29	When he giueth quietnesse, who then can make trouble? and when hee hideth his face, who then can beholde him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man onely:
jb.34.30	Job 34:30	That the hypocrite raigne not, lest the people be ensnared.
jb.34.31	Job 34:31	Surely it is meete to be said vnto God, I haue borne chastisement, I will not offend any more.

jb.34.34	Job 34:34	Let men of vnderstanding tell mee, and let a wise man hearken vnto mee.
jb.34.35	Job 34:35	Iob hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdome.
jb.34.36	Job 34:36	My desire is that Iob may bee tried vnto the ende, because of his answeres for wicked men.
jb.34.37	Job 34:37	For he addeth rebellion vnto his sinne, hee clappeth his handes amongst vs, and multiplieth his words against God.
jb.35.1	Job 35:1	Elihu spake moreouer, and said,

jb.35.12	Job 35:12	There they crie, (but none giueth answere) because of the pride of euill men.

jb.35.16	Job 35:16	Therefore doeth Iob open his mouth in vaine: he multiplieth words without knowledge.
jb.36.1	Job 36:1	Elihu also proceeded, and said,

jb.37.1	Job 37:1	At this also my heart trembleth, and is moued out of his place.

jb.41.1	Job 41:1	Canst thou draw out Leuiathan with an hooke? or his tongue with a corde which thou lettest downe?
jb.41.2	Job 41:2	Canst thou put an hooke into his nose? or bore his iawe through with a thorne?
jb.41.3	Job 41:3	Will he make many supplications vnto thee? will he speake soft words vnto thee?
jb.41.4	Job 41:4	Will he make a couenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a seruant for euer?
jb.41.5	Job 41:5	Wilt thou play with him as with a birde? wilt thou binde him for thy maydens?
jb.41.6	Job 41:6	Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?
jb.41.7	Job 41:7	Canst thou fill his skinne with barbed irons? or his head with fishspeares?

jb.41.9	Job 41:9	Behold, the hope of him is in vaine: shall not one be cast downe euen at the sight of him?
jb.41.10	Job 41:10	None is so fierce that dare stirre him vp: who then is able to stand before me?
jb.41.11	Job 41:11	Who hath preuented me that I should repay him? whatsoeuer is vnder the whole heauen, is mine.
jb.41.12	Job 41:12	I will not conceale his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
jb.41.13	Job 41:13	Who can discouer the face of his garment? or who can come to him, with his double bridle?
jb.41.14	Job 41:14	Who can open the doores of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.
jb.41.15	Job 41:15	His scales are his pride, shut vp together as with a close seale.
jb.41.16	Job 41:16	One is so neere to another, that no ayre can come betweene them.
jb.41.17	Job 41:17	They are ioyned one to another, they sticke together, that they cannot be sundred.
jb.41.18	Job 41:18	By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eye-liddes of the morning.
jb.41.19	Job 41:19	Out of his mouth goe burning lampes, and sparkes of fire leape out.
jb.41.20	Job 41:20	Out of his nostrels goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.
jb.41.21	Job 41:21	His breath kindleth coales, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.
jb.41.22	Job 41:22	In his necke remaineth strength, and sorrowe is turned into ioy before him.
jb.41.23	Job 41:23	The flakes of his flesh are ioyned together: they are firme in themselues, they cannot be moued.
jb.41.24	Job 41:24	His heart is as firme as a stone, yea as hard as a peece of the nether mil-stone.
jb.41.25	Job 41:25	When he rayseth vp himselfe, the mightie are afraid: by reason of breakings they purifie themselues.
jb.41.26	Job 41:26	The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the speare, the dart, nor the habergeon.
jb.41.27	Job 41:27	He esteemeth iron as straw, and brasse as rotten wood.
jb.41.28	Job 41:28	The arrow cannot make him flee: sling-stones are turned with him into stubble.
jb.41.29	Job 41:29	Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a speare.
jb.41.30	Job 41:30	Sharpe stones are vnder him: he spreadeth sharpe pointed things vpon the mire.
jb.41.31	Job 41:31	He maketh the deepe to boyle like a pot: hee maketh the sea like a pot of oyntment.
jb.41.32	Job 41:32	Hee maketh a path to shine after him; one would thinke the deepe to bee hoarie.
jb.41.33	Job 41:33	Upon earth there is not his like: who is made without feare.

jb.42.1	Job 42:1	Then Iob answered the LORD, and said,
jb.42.2	Job 42:2	I know that thou canst doe euery thing, and that no thought can bee withholden from thee.
jb.42.3	Job 42:3	Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore haue I vttered that I vnderstood not, things too wonderfull for me, which I knew not.
jb.42.4	Job 42:4	Heare, I beseech thee, and I will speake: I will demand of thee, and declare thou vnto me.
jb.42.5	Job 42:5	I haue heard of thee by the hearing of the eare: but now mine eye seeth thee.
jb.42.6	Job 42:6	Wherefore I abhorre my selfe, and repent in dust and ashes.
jb.42.7	Job 42:7	¶ And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words vnto Iob, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, & against thy two friends: for ye haue not spoken of mee the thing that is right, as my seruant Iob hath.
jb.42.8	Job 42:8	Therefore take vnto you now seuen bullocks, and seuen rammes, and goe to my seruant Iob, and offer vp for your selues a burnt offring, and my seruant Iob shal pray for you, for him wil I accept: lest I deale with you after your folly, in that ye haue not spoken of mee the thing which is right, like my seruant Iob.
jb.42.9	Job 42:9	So Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Iob.
jb.42.10	Job 42:10	And the LORD turned the captiuitie of Iob, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gaue Iob twice as much as he had before.
jb.42.11	Job 42:11	Then came there vnto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had bin of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoned him, and comforted him ouer all the euill that the LORD had brought vpon him: euery man also gaue him a piece of money, and euery one an eare-ring of gold.
jb.42.12	Job 42:12	So the LORD blessed the latter end of Iob, more then his beginning: for he had fourteene thousand sheepe, and sixe thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand shee asses.
jb.42.13	Job 42:13	He had also seuen sonnes, and three daughters.
jb.42.14	Job 42:14	And he called the name of the first, Iemima, and the name of the second, Kezia, and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
jb.42.15	Job 42:15	And in all the land were no women found so faire as the daughters of Iob: and their father gaue them inheritance among their brethren.
jb.42.16	Job 42:16	After this liued Iob an hundred and fourtie yeeres, and saw his sonnes, and his sonnes sonnes, euen foure generations.
jb.42.17	Job 42:17	So Iob died being old, and full of dayes.

pr.1.1	Proverbs 1:1	The Prouerbes of Solomon the sonne of Dauid, King of Israel,
pr.1.2	Proverbs 1:2	To knowe wisedome and instruction, to perceiue the words of vnderstanding,
pr.1.3	Proverbs 1:3	To receiue the instruction of wisdome, iustice, and iudgement & equitie,
pr.1.4	Proverbs 1:4	To giue subtiltie to the simple, to the yong man knowledge and discretion.
pr.1.5	Proverbs 1:5	A wise man wil heare, and wil increase learning: and a man of vnderstanding shall attaine vnto wise counsels:
pr.1.6	Proverbs 1:6	To vnderstand a prouerbe, and the interpretation; the wordes of the wise, and their darke sayings.
pr.1.7	Proverbs 1:7	¶ The feare of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fooles despise wisedome and instruction.
pr.1.8	Proverbs 1:8	My sonne, heare the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.
pr.1.9	Proverbs 1:9	For they shall be an ornament of grace vnto thy head, and chaines about thy necke.
pr.1.10	Proverbs 1:10	¶ My sonne, if sinners entise thee, consent thou not.
pr.1.11	Proverbs 1:11	If they say, Come with vs, let vs lay wait for blood, let vs lurke priuily for the innocent without cause:
pr.1.12	Proverbs 1:12	Let vs swallow them vp aliue, as the graue, and whole, as those that goe downe into the pit:
pr.1.13	Proverbs 1:13	Wee shall finde all precious substance, wee shall fill our houses with spoile:
pr.1.14	Proverbs 1:14	Cast in thy lot among vs, let vs all haue one purse:
pr.1.15	Proverbs 1:15	My sonne, walke not thou in the way with them; refraine thy foot from their path:
pr.1.16	Proverbs 1:16	For their feete runne to euil, and make haste to shed blood.
pr.1.17	Proverbs 1:17	Surely in vaine the net is spread in the sight of any bird.
pr.1.18	Proverbs 1:18	And they lay wait for their owne blood, they lurke priuily for their owne liues.
pr.1.19	Proverbs 1:19	So are the waies of euery one that is greedie of gaine: which taketh away the life of the owners thereof.
pr.1.20	Proverbs 1:20	¶ Wisedome crieth without, she vttereth her voice in the streets:
pr.1.21	Proverbs 1:21	Shee crieth in the chiefe place of concourse, in the openings of the gates: in the city she vttereth her words, saying,
pr.1.22	Proverbs 1:22	How long, ye simple ones, will ye loue simplicitie? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fooles hate knowledge?
pr.1.23	Proverbs 1:23	Turne you at my reproofe: behold, I will powre out my spirit vnto you, I will make knowen my wordes vnto you.
pr.1.24	Proverbs 1:24	¶ Because I haue called, and yee refused, I haue stretched out my hand, and no man regarded:
pr.1.25	Proverbs 1:25	But ye haue set at nought all my counsell, & would none of my reproofe:
pr.1.26	Proverbs 1:26	I also will laugh at your calamitie, I wil mocke when your feare commeth.
pr.1.27	Proverbs 1:27	When your feare commeth as desolation, and your destruction commeth as a whirlewinde; when distresse and anguish commeth vpon you:
pr.1.28	Proverbs 1:28	Then shall they call vpon mee, but I will not answere; they shall seeke me early, but they shall not finde me:
pr.1.29	Proverbs 1:29	For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the feare of the LORD.
pr.1.30	Proverbs 1:30	They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproofe.
pr.1.31	Proverbs 1:31	Therefore shall they eate of the fruite of their owne way, and be filled with their owne deuices.
pr.1.32	Proverbs 1:32	For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fooles shall destroy them.
pr.1.33	Proverbs 1:33	But who so hearkneth vnto mee, shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from feare of euill.
pr.2.1	Proverbs 2:1	My sonne, if thou wilt receiue my words, and hide my commaundements with thee;
pr.2.2	Proverbs 2:2	So that thou incline thine eare vnto wisedome, and apply thine heart to vnderstanding:
pr.2.3	Proverbs 2:3	Yea if thou cryest after knowledge, and liftest vp thy voyce for vnderstanding:
pr.2.4	Proverbs 2:4	If thou seekest her as siluer, and searchest for her, as for hid treasures:

pr.2.18	Proverbs 2:18	For her house inclineth vnto death, and her pathes vnto the dead:

pr.2.20	Proverbs 2:20	That thou mayest walke in the way of good men, and keepe the pathes of the righteous.
pr.2.21	Proverbs 2:21	For the vpright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remaine in it.
pr.2.22	Proverbs 2:22	But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth, and the transgressours shalbe rooted out of it.
