pr.31.24	Proverbs 31:24	She maketh fine linnen, and selleth it, and deliuereth girdles vnto the merchant.
pr.31.25	Proverbs 31:25	Strength and honour are her cloathing; and she shall reioyce in time to come.
pr.31.26	Proverbs 31:26	She openeth her mouth with wisedome; and in her tongue is the law of kindnesse.
pr.31.27	Proverbs 31:27	She looketh well to the wayes of her housholde, and eateth not the bread of idlenesse.
pr.31.28	Proverbs 31:28	Her children arise vp, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.
pr.31.29	Proverbs 31:29	Many daughters haue done vertuously, but thou excellest them all.
pr.31.30	Proverbs 31:30	Fauour is deceitfull, and beautie is vaine: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shalbe praised.
pr.31.31	Proverbs 31:31	Giue her of the fruit of her hands, and let her owne workes praise her in the gates.
ec.1.1	Ecclesiastes 1:1	The wordes of the Preacher, the son of Dauid, King in Ierusalem.
ec.1.2	Ecclesiastes 1:2	Uanitie of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanitie of vanities, all is vanitie.
ec.1.3	Ecclesiastes 1:3	What profite hath a man of all his labour which hee taketh vnder the Sunne?
ec.1.4	Ecclesiastes 1:4	One generation passeth away, and another generation commeth: but the earth abideth for euer.
ec.1.5	Ecclesiastes 1:5	The Sunne also ariseth, and the Sunne goeth downe, and hasteth to the place where he arose.
ec.1.6	Ecclesiastes 1:6	The winde goeth toward the South, and turneth about vnto the North; it whirleth about continually, and the winde returneth againe according to his circuits.
ec.1.7	Ecclesiastes 1:7	All the riuers runne into the sea, yet the Sea is not full: vnto the place from whence the riuers come, thither they returne againe.
ec.1.8	Ecclesiastes 1:8	All things are full of labour, man cannot vtter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the eare filled with hearing.
ec.1.9	Ecclesiastes 1:9	The thing that hath beene, it is that which shall be: and that which is done, is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing vnder the sunne.
ec.1.10	Ecclesiastes 1:10	Is there any thing, whereof it may be sayd, See, this is new? it hath beene already of olde time, which was before vs.
ec.1.11	Ecclesiastes 1:11	There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there bee any remembrance of things that are to come, with those that shall come after.
ec.1.12	Ecclesiastes 1:12	¶ I the Preacher was king ouer Israel in Ierusalem.
ec.1.13	Ecclesiastes 1:13	And I gaue my heart to seeke and search out by wisedome, concerning all things that are done vnder heauen: this sore trauell hath God giuen to the sonnes of man, to be exercised therewith.
ec.1.14	Ecclesiastes 1:14	I haue seene all the workes that are done vnder the Sunne, and behold, all is vanitie, and vexation of spirit.
ec.1.15	Ecclesiastes 1:15	That which is crooked, cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbred.
ec.1.16	Ecclesiastes 1:16	I communed with mine owne heart, saying, Loe, I am come to great estate, and haue gotten more wisedome then all they that haue beene before me in Ierusalem: yea my heart had great experience of wisedome & knowledge.
ec.1.17	Ecclesiastes 1:17	And I gaue my heart to know wisedome, and to know madnesse and folly: I perceiued that this also is vexation of spirit.
ec.1.18	Ecclesiastes 1:18	For in much wisedome is much griefe: and hee that increaseth knowledge, increaseth sorrow.
ec.2.1	Ecclesiastes 2:1	I said in mine heart, Goe to now, I wil prooue thee with mirth, therfore enioy pleasure: and behold, this also is vanitie.
ec.2.2	Ecclesiastes 2:2	I saide of laughter, It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
ec.2.3	Ecclesiastes 2:3	I sought in mine heart to giue my selfe vnto wine, (yet acquainting mine heart with wisedome) and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was that good for the sonnes of men, which they should doe vnder the heauen all the dayes of their life.
ec.2.4	Ecclesiastes 2:4	I made me great workes, I builded mee houses, I planted mee Uineyards.
ec.2.5	Ecclesiastes 2:5	I made mee gardens & orchards, and I planted trees in them of all kinde of fruits.
ec.2.6	Ecclesiastes 2:6	I made mee pooles of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth foorth trees:
ec.2.7	Ecclesiastes 2:7	I got me seruants and maydens, and had seruants borne in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattell, aboue all that were in Ierusalem before me.
ec.2.8	Ecclesiastes 2:8	I gathered mee also siluer and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the prouinces: I gate mee men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sonnes of men, as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
ec.2.9	Ecclesiastes 2:9	So I was great, and increased more then all that were before mee in Ierusalem; also my wisedome remained with me.
ec.2.10	Ecclesiastes 2:10	And whatsoeuer mine eyes desired, I kept not from them; I withheld not my heart from any ioy: for my heart reioyced in all my labour; and this was my portion of all my labour.
ec.2.11	Ecclesiastes 2:11	Then I looked on all the workes that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to doe: and behold, all was vanitie, and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit vnder the Sunne.
ec.2.12	Ecclesiastes 2:12	¶ And I turned my selfe to behold wisedome, and madnesse and folly: for what can the man doe, that commeth after the king? euen that which hath bene already done.
ec.2.13	Ecclesiastes 2:13	Then I saw that wisedome excelleth folly, as farre as light excelleth darkenesse.
ec.2.14	Ecclesiastes 2:14	The wise mans eyes are in his head, but the foole walketh in darknes: and I my selfe perceiued also that one euent happeneth to them all.
ec.2.15	Ecclesiastes 2:15	Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the foole, so it happeneth euen to me, and why was I then more wise? then I said in my heart, That this also is vanitie.
ec.2.16	Ecclesiastes 2:16	For there is no remembrance of the wise, more then of the foole for euer; seeing that which now is, in the dayes to come shall be forgotten; and how dieth the wise man? as the foole.
ec.2.17	Ecclesiastes 2:17	Therefore I hated life, because the worke that is wrought vnder the Sunne is grieuous vnto mee: for all is vanitie, and vexation of spirit.
ec.2.18	Ecclesiastes 2:18	¶ Yea I hated all my labour which I had taken vnder the Sunne: because I should leaue it vnto the man that shalbe after mee.
ec.2.19	Ecclesiastes 2:19	And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a foole? yet shall he haue rule ouer all my labour, wherein I haue laboured, and wherein I haue shewed my selfe wise vnder the Sunne. This is also vanitie.
ec.2.20	Ecclesiastes 2:20	Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despaire of all the labour which I tooke vnder the Sunne.
ec.2.21	Ecclesiastes 2:21	For there is a man whose labour is in wisedome and in knowledge, and in equitie: yet to a man that hath not laboured therein, shall hee leaue it for his portion; This also is vanitie, and a great euill.
ec.2.22	Ecclesiastes 2:22	For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart wherein hee hath laboured vnder the Sunne?
ec.2.23	Ecclesiastes 2:23	For all his dayes are sorrowes, and his traueile, griefe; yea his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanitie.
ec.2.24	Ecclesiastes 2:24	¶ There is nothing better for a man, then that he should eat and drinke, and that he should make his soule enioy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.
ec.2.25	Ecclesiastes 2:25	For who can eate? or who else can hasten hereunto more then I?
ec.2.26	Ecclesiastes 2:26	For God giueth to a man that is good in his sight, wisedome, and knowledge, and ioy: but to the sinner hee giueth traueile, to gather and to heape vp that he may giue to him that is good before God: This also is vanitie and vexation of spirit.
ec.3.1	Ecclesiastes 3:1	To euery thing there is a season, and a time to euery purpose vnder the heauen.
ec.3.2	Ecclesiastes 3:2	A time to be borne, and a time to die: a time to plant, and a time to pluck vp that which is planted.
ec.3.3	Ecclesiastes 3:3	A time to kill, and a time to heale: a time to breake downe, and a time to build vp.
ec.3.4	Ecclesiastes 3:4	A time to weepe, and a time to laugh: a time to mourne, and a time to dance.
ec.3.5	Ecclesiastes 3:5	A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together: a time to imbrace, and a time to refraine from imbracing.
ec.3.6	Ecclesiastes 3:6	A time to get, and a time to lose: a time to keepe, and a time to cast away.
ec.3.7	Ecclesiastes 3:7	A time to rent, and a time to sow: a time to keepe silence, and a time to speake.
ec.3.8	Ecclesiastes 3:8	A time to loue, and a time to hate: a time of warre, and a time of peace.
ec.3.9	Ecclesiastes 3:9	What profite hath hee that worketh, in that wherein he laboureth?
ec.3.10	Ecclesiastes 3:10	I haue seene the trauaile which God hath giuen to the sonnes of men, to be exercised in it.
ec.3.11	Ecclesiastes 3:11	He hath made euery thing beautifull in his time: also hee hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can finde out the worke that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
ec.3.12	Ecclesiastes 3:12	I know that there is no good in them, but for a man to reioyce, and to doe good in his life.
ec.3.13	Ecclesiastes 3:13	And also that euery man should eate and drinke, and enioy the good of all his labour: it is the gift of God.
ec.3.14	Ecclesiastes 3:14	I know that whatsoeuer God doeth, it shalbe for euer: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doth it, that men should feare before him.
ec.3.15	Ecclesiastes 3:15	That which hath beene, is now: and that which is to be, hath alreadie beene, and God requireth that which is past.
ec.3.16	Ecclesiastes 3:16	¶ And moreouer, I sawe vnder the Sunne the place of iudgement, that wickednesse was there; and the place of righteousnesse, that iniquitie was there.
ec.3.17	Ecclesiastes 3:17	I said in mine heart, God shall iudge the righteous and the wicked: for there is a time there, for euery purpose and for euery worke.
ec.3.18	Ecclesiastes 3:18	I said in my heart concerning the estate of the sonnes of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselues are beasts.
ec.3.19	Ecclesiastes 3:19	For that which befalleth the sonnes of men, befalleth beastes, euen one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea they haue all one breath, so that a man hath no preheminence aboue a beast; for all is vanitie.
ec.3.20	Ecclesiastes 3:20	All goe vnto one place, all are of the dust, and all turne to dust againe.
ec.3.21	Ecclesiastes 3:21	Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth vpward; and the spirit of the beast that goeth downeward to the earth?
ec.3.22	Ecclesiastes 3:22	Wherefore I perceiue that there is nothing better, then that a man should reioyce in his owne workes: for that is his portion; for who shall bring him to see what shalbe after him?
ec.4.1	Ecclesiastes 4:1	So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done vnder the sunne; & behold the teares of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter: and on the side of their oppressours there was power, but they had no comforter.
ec.4.2	Ecclesiastes 4:2	Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead, more then the liuing which are yet aliue.
ec.4.3	Ecclesiastes 4:3	Yea better is he then both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seene the euill worke that is done vnder the Sunne.
ec.4.4	Ecclesiastes 4:4	¶ Againe I considered all trauaile, and euery right worke, that for this a man is enuied of his neighbour: this is also vanitie, and vexation of spirit.
ec.4.5	Ecclesiastes 4:5	The foole foldeth his hands together, and eateth his owne flesh.
ec.4.6	Ecclesiastes 4:6	Better is an handfull with quietnesse, then both the hands full with trauell and vexation of spirit.
ec.4.7	Ecclesiastes 4:7	¶ Then I returned, and I saw vanitie vnder the Sunne.
ec.4.8	Ecclesiastes 4:8	There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he hath neither childe nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour, neither is his eye satisfied with riches, neither sayth hee, For whom doe I labour, and bereaue my soule of good? this is also vanitie, yea it is a sore trauell.
ec.4.9	Ecclesiastes 4:9	¶ Two are better then one; because they haue a good reward for their labour.
ec.4.10	Ecclesiastes 4:10	For if they fall, the one will lift vp his fellow; but woe to him that is alone, when he falleth: for he hath not another to helpe him vp.
ec.4.11	Ecclesiastes 4:11	Againe, if two lye together, then they haue heate; but howe can one be warme alone?
ec.4.12	Ecclesiastes 4:12	And if one preuaile against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold coard is not quickly broken.
ec.4.13	Ecclesiastes 4:13	¶ Better is a poore and a wise child, then an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished.
ec.4.14	Ecclesiastes 4:14	For out of prison hee commeth to raigne, whereas also he that is borne in his kingdome, becommeth poore.
ec.4.15	Ecclesiastes 4:15	I considered all the liuing which walke vnder the sunne, with the second child that shall stand vp in his stead.
ec.4.16	Ecclesiastes 4:16	There is no end of all the people, euen of all that haue beene before them: they also that come after, shall not reioyce in him: surely this also is vanitie, and vexation of spirit.
ec.5.1	Ecclesiastes 5:1	Kepe thy foote when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to heare, then to giue the sacrifice of fooles: for they consider not that they doe euill.
ec.5.2	Ecclesiastes 5:2	Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to vtter any thing before God: for God is in heauen, and thou vpon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
ec.5.3	Ecclesiastes 5:3	For a dreame commeth through the multitude of businesse, and a fooles voyce is knowen by multitude of words.
ec.5.4	Ecclesiastes 5:4	When thou vowest a vow vnto God, deferre not to pay it: for he hath no pleasure in fooles; pay that which thou hast vowed.
ec.5.5	Ecclesiastes 5:5	Better is it that thou shouldest not vowe, then that thou shouldest vowe and not pay.
ec.5.6	Ecclesiastes 5:6	Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sinne, neither say thou before the Angel, that it was an errour: wherefore should God be angrie at thy voyce, and destroy the worke of thine hands?
ec.5.7	Ecclesiastes 5:7	For in the multitude of dreames and many words, there are also diuers vanities: but feare thou God.
ec.5.8	Ecclesiastes 5:8	¶ If thou seest the oppression of the poore, and violent peruerting of iudgement, and iustice in a prouince, maruell not at the matter: for he that is higher then the highest, regardeth, and there be higher then they.
ec.5.9	Ecclesiastes 5:9	¶ Moreouer the profit of the earth is for all: the king himselfe is serued by the field.
ec.5.10	Ecclesiastes 5:10	Hee that loueth siluer shall not be satisfied with siluer; nor he that loueth abundance, with increase: this is also vanitie.
ec.5.11	Ecclesiastes 5:11	When goods increase, they are increased that eate them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, sauing the beholding of them with their eyes?
ec.5.12	Ecclesiastes 5:12	The sleepe of a labouring man is sweete, whether he eate little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleepe.
ec.5.13	Ecclesiastes 5:13	There is a sore euill which I haue seene vnder the Sun, namely riches kept for the owners therof to their hurt.
ec.5.14	Ecclesiastes 5:14	But those riches perish by euill trauell; and he begetteth a sonne, and there is nothing in his hand.
ec.5.15	Ecclesiastes 5:15	As he came forth of his mothers wombe, naked shall he returne to goe as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
ec.5.16	Ecclesiastes 5:16	And this also is a sore euill, that in all points as he came, so shall hee goe: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the winde?
ec.5.17	Ecclesiastes 5:17	All his dayes also hee eateth in darkenesse, and he hath much sorrowe, and wrath with his sicknesse.
ec.5.18	Ecclesiastes 5:18	¶ Behold that which I haue seene: It is good and comely for one to eate and to drinke, and to enioy the good of all his labour that he taketh vnder the sunne, all the dayes of his life, which God giueth him: for it is his portion.
ec.5.19	Ecclesiastes 5:19	Euery man also to whom God hath giuen riches and wealth, and hath giuen him power to eate thereof, and to take his portion, and to reioyce in his labour; this is the gift of God.
ec.5.20	Ecclesiastes 5:20	For he shall not much remember the dayes of his life: because God answereth him in the ioy of his heart.
ec.6.1	Ecclesiastes 6:1	There is an euill which I haue seen vnder the Sun, and it is common among men:
ec.6.2	Ecclesiastes 6:2	A man to whom God hath giuen riches, wealth and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soule of all that he desireth, yet God giueth him not power to eate thereof, but a stranger eateth it: This is vanitie, and it is an euill disease.
ec.6.3	Ecclesiastes 6:3	¶ If a man beget an hundred children, and liue many yeeres, so that the dayes of his yeeres bee many: and his soule be not filled with good, and also that he haue no buriall, I say, that an vntimely birth is better then he.
ec.6.4	Ecclesiastes 6:4	For he commeth in with vanitie, and departeth in darkenesse, and his name shall be couered with darkenesse.
ec.6.5	Ecclesiastes 6:5	Moreouer hee hath not seene the Sunne, nor knowen any thing: this hath more rest then the other.
ec.6.6	Ecclesiastes 6:6	¶ Yea though he liue a thousand yeeres twice told, yet hath he seene no good: Doe not all goe to one place?
ec.6.7	Ecclesiastes 6:7	All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
ec.6.8	Ecclesiastes 6:8	For what hath the wise more then the foole? what hath the poore, that knoweth to walke before the liuing?
ec.6.9	Ecclesiastes 6:9	¶ Better is the sight of the eyes, then the wandering of the desire: this is also vanitie and vexation of spirit.
ec.6.10	Ecclesiastes 6:10	That which hath bene, is named already, and it is knowen that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier then he.
ec.6.11	Ecclesiastes 6:11	¶ Seeing there be many things that increase vanitie, what is man the better?
ec.6.12	Ecclesiastes 6:12	For who knoweth what is good for man in this life, all the dayes of his vaine life, which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shal be after him vnder the sunne?
ec.7.1	Ecclesiastes 7:1	A Good name is better then precious ointment: and the day of death, then the day of ones birth.
ec.7.2	Ecclesiastes 7:2	¶ It is better to goe to the house of mourning, then to goe to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the liuing will lay it to his heart.
ec.7.3	Ecclesiastes 7:3	Sorrow is better then laughter: for by the sadnesse of the countenance the heart is made better.
ec.7.4	Ecclesiastes 7:4	The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning: but the heart of fooles is in the house of mirth.
ec.7.5	Ecclesiastes 7:5	It is better to heare the rebuke of the wise, then for a man to heare the song of fooles.
ec.7.6	Ecclesiastes 7:6	For as the crackling of thornes vnder a pot, so is the laughter of the foole: this also is vanitie.
ec.7.7	Ecclesiastes 7:7	¶ Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad: and a gift destroyeth the heart.
ec.7.8	Ecclesiastes 7:8	Better is the ende of a thing then the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better then the proude in spirit.
ec.7.9	Ecclesiastes 7:9	Be not hastie in thy spirit to bee angry: for anger resteth in the bosome of fooles.
ec.7.10	Ecclesiastes 7:10	Say not thou, What is the cause that the former dayes were better then these? For thou doest not enquire wisely concerning this.
ec.7.11	Ecclesiastes 7:11	¶ Wisedome is good with an inheritance: and by it there is profite to them that see the sunne.
ec.7.12	Ecclesiastes 7:12	For wisedome is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellencie of knowledge is, that wisedome giueth life to them that haue it.
ec.7.13	Ecclesiastes 7:13	Consider the worke of God: for who can make that straight, which hee hath made crooked?
ec.7.14	Ecclesiastes 7:14	In the day of prosperitie be ioyfull, but in the day of aduersitie consider: God also hath set the one ouer against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
ec.7.15	Ecclesiastes 7:15	All things haue I seene in the dayes of my vanitie: there is a iust man that perisheth in his righteousnes, and there is a wicked man that prolongeth his life in his wickednes.
ec.7.16	Ecclesiastes 7:16	Be not righteous ouer much, neither make thy selfe ouer wise: why shouldest thou destroy thy selfe?
ec.7.17	Ecclesiastes 7:17	Be not ouermuch wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
ec.7.18	Ecclesiastes 7:18	It is good that thou shouldest take holde of this, yea also from this withdraw not thine hand: for hee that feareth God, shall come foorth of them all.
ec.7.19	Ecclesiastes 7:19	Wisedome strengtheneth the wise, more then ten mightie men which are in the citie.
ec.7.20	Ecclesiastes 7:20	For there is not a iust man vpon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
ec.7.21	Ecclesiastes 7:21	Also take no heede vnto all words that are spoken; lest thou heare thy seruant curse thee.
ec.7.22	Ecclesiastes 7:22	For often times also thine owne heart knoweth, that thou thy selfe likewise hast cursed others.
ec.7.23	Ecclesiastes 7:23	¶ All this haue I prooued by wisedome: I said, I will be wise, but it was farre from me.
ec.7.24	Ecclesiastes 7:24	That which is farre off, and exceeding deepe, who can finde it out?
ec.7.25	Ecclesiastes 7:25	I applyed mine heart to know, and to search, and to seeke out wisdome, and the reason of things, aud to know the wickednes of folly, euen of foolishnesse and madnesse.
ec.7.26	Ecclesiastes 7:26	And I finde more bitter then death, the woman whose heart is snares & nets, and her handes as bands: who so pleaseth God, shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her.
ec.7.27	Ecclesiastes 7:27	Behold, this haue I found (saith the Preacher) counting one by one to finde out the account:
ec.7.28	Ecclesiastes 7:28	Which yet my soule seeketh, but I finde not: one man among a thousand haue I found, but a woman among all those haue I not found.
ec.7.29	Ecclesiastes 7:29	Loe, this onely haue I found, that God hath made man vpright: but they haue sought out many inuentions.
ec.8.1	Ecclesiastes 8:1	Who is as the Wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a mans wisedome maketh his face to shine, and the boldnes of his face shalbe changed.
ec.8.2	Ecclesiastes 8:2	I counsell thee, to keepe the kings commandement, and that in regard of the oath of God.
ec.8.3	Ecclesiastes 8:3	Bee not hastie to goe out of his sight: stand not in an euill thing, for he doeth whatsoeuer pleaseth him.
ec.8.4	Ecclesiastes 8:4	Where the word of a king is, there is power: and who may say vnto him, What doest thou?
ec.8.5	Ecclesiastes 8:5	Whoso keepeth the commandement, shall feele no euill thing: and a wise mans heart discerneth both time and iudgement.
ec.8.6	Ecclesiastes 8:6	¶ Because to euery purpose there is time, and iudgement; therefore the misery of man is great vpon him.
ec.8.7	Ecclesiastes 8:7	For hee knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him, when it shall be?
ec.8.8	Ecclesiastes 8:8	There is no man that hath power ouer the spirit to retaine the spirit; neither hath he power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in that warre, neither shall wickednesse deliuer those that are giuen to it.
ec.8.9	Ecclesiastes 8:9	All this haue I seene, and applied my heart vnto euery worke that is done vnder the Sunne: there is a time wherein one man ruleth ouer another to his owne hurt.
ec.8.10	Ecclesiastes 8:10	And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come, and gone from the place of the Holy, and they were forgotten in the city, where they had so done: this is also vanitie.
ec.8.11	Ecclesiastes 8:11	Because sentence against an euill worke is not executed speedily; therefore the heart of the sonnes of men is fully set in them to doe euill.
ec.8.12	Ecclesiastes 8:12	¶ Though a sinner doe euill an hundred times, and his dayes be prolonged; yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that feare God, which feare before him.
ec.8.13	Ecclesiastes 8:13	But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall hee prolong his dayes which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
ec.8.14	Ecclesiastes 8:14	There is a vanitie which is done vpon the earth, that there be iust men vnto whom it happeneth according to the worke of the wicked: againe, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the worke of the righteous: I said, that this also is vanitie.
ec.8.15	Ecclesiastes 8:15	Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing vnder the Sunne, then to eate and to drinke, and to be merrie: for that shall abide with him of his labour, the dayes of his life, which God giueth him vnder the Sunne.
ec.8.16	Ecclesiastes 8:16	¶ When I applied mine heart to know wisedome, and to see the busines that is done vpon the earth: (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleepe with his eyes.)
ec.8.17	Ecclesiastes 8:17	Then I behelde all the worke of God, that a man cannot finde out the worke that is done vnder the Sunne: because though a man labour to seeke it out, yea further though a wise man thinke to know it, yet shall hee not be able to finde it.
ec.9.1	Ecclesiastes 9:1	For all this I considered in my heart, euen to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their workes, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either loue, or hatred, by all that is before them.
ec.9.2	Ecclesiastes 9:2	All things come alike to all: there is one euent to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good and to the cleane, and to the vncleane; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner, and hee that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.
ec.9.3	Ecclesiastes 9:3	This is an euill among all things that are done vnder the Sunne, that there is one euent vnto all: yea also the heart of the sonnes of men is full of euill, and madnesse is in their heart while they liue, and after that they goe to the dead.
ec.9.4	Ecclesiastes 9:4	¶ For to him that is ioyned to all the liuing, there is hope: for a liuing dogge is better then a dead Lion.
ec.9.5	Ecclesiastes 9:5	For the liuing know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither haue they any more a reward, for the memorie of them is forgotten.
ec.9.6	Ecclesiastes 9:6	Also their loue, and their hatred, and their enuy is now perished; neither haue they any more a portion for euer in any thing that is done vnder the Sunne.
ec.9.7	Ecclesiastes 9:7	¶ Goe thy way, eate thy bread with ioy, and drinke thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy workes.
ec.9.8	Ecclesiastes 9:8	Let thy garments bee alwayes white; and let thy head lacke no oyntment.
ec.9.9	Ecclesiastes 9:9	Liue ioyfully with the wife, whom thou louest, all the dayes of the life of thy vanitie, which he hath giuen thee vnder the Sunne, all the dayes of thy vanitie: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest vnder the Sunne.
ec.9.10	Ecclesiastes 9:10	Whatsoeuer thy hand findeth to doe, doe it with thy might: for there is no worke, nor deuice, nor knowledge, nor wisedome in the graue, whither thou goest.
ec.9.11	Ecclesiastes 9:11	¶ I returned, and saw vnder the Sunne, That the race is not to the swift, nor the battell to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of vnderstanding, nor yet fauour to men of skil; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
ec.9.12	Ecclesiastes 9:12	For man also knoweth not his time, as the fishes that are taken in an euil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sonnes of men snared in an euill time, when it falleth suddenly vpon them.
ec.9.13	Ecclesiastes 9:13	¶ This wisedome haue I seene also vnder the Sunne, and it seemed great vnto me:
ec.9.14	Ecclesiastes 9:14	There was a little citie, and few men within it; and there came a great King against it, and besieged it, & built great bulwarks against it:
ec.9.15	Ecclesiastes 9:15	Now there was found in it a poore wise man, and hee by his wisedome deliuered the citie; yet no man remembred that same poore man.
ec.9.16	Ecclesiastes 9:16	Then said I, Wisedome is better then strength: neuerthelesse, the poore mans wisedome is despised, and his words are not heard.
ec.9.17	Ecclesiastes 9:17	The words of wise men are heard in quiet, more then the cry of him that ruleth among fooles.
ec.9.18	Ecclesiastes 9:18	Wisedome is better then weapons of warre: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
ec.10.1	Ecclesiastes 10:1	Dead flies cause the oyntment of the Apothecarie to send foorth a stinking sauour: so doeth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisedome and honour.
ec.10.2	Ecclesiastes 10:2	A wise mans heart is at his right hand: but a fooles heart at his left.
ec.10.3	Ecclesiastes 10:3	Yea also when hee that is a foole walketh by the way, his wisedome faileth him, and hee saith to euery one that he is a foole.
ec.10.4	Ecclesiastes 10:4	If the spirit of the ruler rise vp against thee, leaue not thy place; for yeelding pacifieth great offences.
ec.10.5	Ecclesiastes 10:5	There is an euill which I haue seene vnder the Sunne, as an errour, which proceedeth from the ruler.
ec.10.6	Ecclesiastes 10:6	Folly is set in great dignitie; and the rich sit in lowe place.
ec.10.7	Ecclesiastes 10:7	I haue seene seruants vpon horses, and princes walking as seruants vpon the earth.
ec.10.8	Ecclesiastes 10:8	He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it; and who so breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
ec.10.9	Ecclesiastes 10:9	Who so remoueth stones, shall be hurt therewith: and hee that cleaueth wood, shalbe endangered thereby.
ec.10.10	Ecclesiastes 10:10	If the yron be blunt, and he doe not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisedome is profitable to direct.
ec.10.11	Ecclesiastes 10:11	Surely the serpent will bite without inchauntment, and a babbler is no better.
ec.10.12	Ecclesiastes 10:12	The words of a wise mans mouth are gratious: but the lips of a foole will swallow vp himselfe.
ec.10.13	Ecclesiastes 10:13	The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishnesse: and the end of his talke is mischieuous madnesse.
ec.10.14	Ecclesiastes 10:14	A foole also is full of words; a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall bee after him who can tell him?
ec.10.15	Ecclesiastes 10:15	The labour of the foolish wearyeth euery one of them; because hee knoweth not how to goe to the citie.
ec.10.16	Ecclesiastes 10:16	¶ Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eate in the morning.
ec.10.17	Ecclesiastes 10:17	Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the sonne of nobles, and thy princes eate in due season, for strength, and not for drunkennesse.
ec.10.18	Ecclesiastes 10:18	¶ By much slouthfulnesse the building decayeth; and through idlenesse of the hands the house droppeth through.
ec.10.19	Ecclesiastes 10:19	¶ A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
ec.10.20	Ecclesiastes 10:20	¶ Curse not the king, no not in thy thought, and curse not the rich in thy bed-chamber: for a bird of the aire shall carry the voyce, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
ec.11.1	Ecclesiastes 11:1	Cast thy bread vpon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many dayes.
ec.11.2	Ecclesiastes 11:2	Giue a portion to seuen and also to eight; for thou knowest noc what euill shall be vpon the earth.
ec.11.3	Ecclesiastes 11:3	If the clouds be full of raine, they emptie themselues vpon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the South, or toward the North, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
ec.11.4	Ecclesiastes 11:4	He that obserueth the wind, shall not sow: and hee that regardeth the clouds, shall not reape.
ec.11.5	Ecclesiastes 11:5	As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones doe growe in the wombe of her that is with child: euen so thou knowest not the workes of God who maketh all.
ec.11.6	Ecclesiastes 11:6	In the morning sowe thy seede, and in the euening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
ec.11.7	Ecclesiastes 11:7	¶ Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing is it for the eyes to behold the sunne.
ec.11.8	Ecclesiastes 11:8	But if a man liue many yeeres, and reioyce in them all; yet let him remember the dayes of darkenesse, for they shall be many. All that commeth is vanitie.
ec.11.9	Ecclesiastes 11:9	¶ Reioyce, O young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart cheere thee in the dayes of thy youth, and walke in the wayes of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things, God will bring thee into iudgement.
ec.11.10	Ecclesiastes 11:10	Therefore remoue sorrow from thy heart, and put away euill from thy flesh; for child-hood & youth are vanitie.
ec.12.1	Ecclesiastes 12:1	Remember now thy Creatour in the dayes of thy youth, while the euil daies come not, nor the yeeres drawe nigh, when thou shalt say, I haue no pleasure in them:
ec.12.2	Ecclesiastes 12:2	While the Sunne, or the light, or the moone, or the starres be not darkened, nor the cloudes returne after the raine:
ec.12.3	Ecclesiastes 12:3	In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bowe themselues, and the grinders cease, because they are fewe, and those that looke out of the windowes be darkened:
ec.12.4	Ecclesiastes 12:4	And the doores shal be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise vp at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musicke shall be brought low.
ec.12.5	Ecclesiastes 12:5	Also when they shalbe afraid of that which is high, and feares shall bee in the way, and the Almond tree shall flourish, and the grashopper shall be a burden, and desire shall faile: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners goe about the streets:
ec.12.6	Ecclesiastes 12:6	Or euer the siluer corde be loosed, or the golden bowle be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountaine, or the wheele broken at the cisterne.
ec.12.7	Ecclesiastes 12:7	Then shall the dust returne to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall returne vnto God who gaue it.
ec.12.8	Ecclesiastes 12:8	¶ Uanitie of vanities (saith the preacher) all is vanitie.
ec.12.9	Ecclesiastes 12:9	And moreouer because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge, yea he gaue good heed, and sought out, and set in order many prouerbes.
ec.12.10	Ecclesiastes 12:10	The preacher sought to finde out acceptable words, and that which was written was vpright, euen wordes of trueth.
ec.12.11	Ecclesiastes 12:11	The wordes of the wise are as goads, and as nailes fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are giuen from one shepheard.
ec.12.12	Ecclesiastes 12:12	And further, by these, my sonne, be admonished: of making many bookes there is no end, and much studie is a wearinesse of the flesh.
ec.12.13	Ecclesiastes 12:13	¶ Let vs heare the conclusion of the whole matter: Feare God, and keepe his commandements, for this is the whole duetie of man.
ec.12.14	Ecclesiastes 12:14	For God shal bring euery worke into iudgement, with euer secret thing, whether it bee good, or whether it bee euill.

so.7.2	Song of Solomon 7:2	Thy nauell is like a round goblet, which wanteth not licour: thy belly is like an heape of wheate, set about with lillies.
so.7.3	Song of Solomon 7:3	Thy two breasts are like two yong Roes that are twinnes.
so.7.4	Song of Solomon 7:4	Thy necke is as a towre of yuory: thine eyes like the fish pooles in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose is as the towre of Lebanon, which looketh toward Damascus.
so.7.5	Song of Solomon 7:5	Thine head vpon thee is like Carmel, and the haire of thine head like purple, the king is held in the galleries.
so.7.6	Song of Solomon 7:6	How faire, and how pleasant art thou, O Loue, for delights!
so.7.7	Song of Solomon 7:7	This thy stature is like to a palme tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
so.7.8	Song of Solomon 7:8	I said, I will goe vp to the palme tree, I will take hold of the boughes thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose, like apples.
so.7.9	Song of Solomon 7:9	And the roofe of thy mouth like the best wine, for my beloued, that goeth downe sweetely, causing the lippes of those that are asleepe, to speake.
so.7.10	Song of Solomon 7:10	¶ I am my beloueds, and his desire is towards me.
so.7.11	Song of Solomon 7:11	Come, my beloued, let vs goe forth into the field: let vs lodge in the villages.
so.7.12	Song of Solomon 7:12	Let vs get vp earely to the vineyards, let vs see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appeare, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I giue thee my loues.
so.7.13	Song of Solomon 7:13	The mandrakes giue a smell, and at our gates are all maner of pleasant fruits, new and olde, which I haue laid vp for thee, O my beloued.
so.8.1	Song of Solomon 8:1	O that thou wert as my brother that sucked the brests of my mother, when I should find thee without, I would kisse thee, yet I should not be despised.
so.8.2	Song of Solomon 8:2	I would leade thee, and bring thee into my mothers house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drinke of spiced wine, of the iuice of my pomegranate.
so.8.3	Song of Solomon 8:3	His left hand should be vnder my head, and his right hand should embrace me.
so.8.4	Song of Solomon 8:4	I charge you, O daughters of Ierusalem, that ye stirre not vp, nor awake my loue vntill he please.
so.8.5	Song of Solomon 8:5	(Who is this that commeth vp from the wildernesse, leaning vpon her beloued?) I raised thee vp vnder the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth, there she brought thee forth, that bare thee.
so.8.6	Song of Solomon 8:6	¶ Set mee as a seale vpon thine heart, as a seale vpon thine arme: for loue is strong as death, iealousie is cruel as the graue: the coales thereof are coales of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.
so.8.7	Song of Solomon 8:7	Many waters cannot quench loue, neither can the floods drowne it: if a man would giue all the substance of his house for loue, it would vtterly be contemned.
so.8.8	Song of Solomon 8:8	¶ We haue a litle sister, and shee hath no breasts: what shall we doe for our sister, in the day when she shall bee spoken for?
so.8.9	Song of Solomon 8:9	If she be a wall, we will build vpon her a palace of siluer: and if she bee a dore, we will inclose her with boards of Cedar.
so.8.10	Song of Solomon 8:10	I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found fauour.
so.8.11	Song of Solomon 8:11	Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon, hee let out the vineyard vnto keepers: euery one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of siluer.
so.8.12	Song of Solomon 8:12	My vineyard which is mine, is before me: thou (O Solomon) must haue a thousand, and those that keepe the fruit thereof, two hundred.
so.8.13	Song of Solomon 8:13	Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to heare it.
so.8.14	Song of Solomon 8:14	¶ Make haste, my beloued, and be thou like to a Roe, or to a yong Hart vpon the mountaines of spices.
is.1.1	Isaiah 1:1	The Uision of Isaiah the sonne of Amoz, which hee sawe concerning Iudah and Ierusalem, in the dayes of Uzziah, Iotham, Ahaz, & Hezekiah kings of Iudah.
is.1.2	Isaiah 1:2	Heare, O heauens, and giue eare, O earth: for the LORD hath spoken; I haue nourished and brought vp children, and they haue rebelled against me.
is.1.3	Isaiah 1:3	The oxe knoweth his owner, and the asse his masters cribbe: but Israel doeth not know, my people doeth not consider.
is.1.4	Isaiah 1:4	Ah sinnefull nation, a people laden with iniquitie, a seede of euill doers, children that are corrupters: they haue forsaken the LORD, they haue prouoked the Holy one of Israel vnto anger, they are gone away backward.
is.1.5	Isaiah 1:5	¶ Why should yee be stricken any more? yee will reuolt more and more: the whole head is sicke, and the whole heart faint.
is.1.6	Isaiah 1:6	From the sole of the foote, euen vnto the head, there is no soundnesse in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they haue not beene closed, neither bound vp, neither mollified with oyntment.
is.1.7	Isaiah 1:7	Your countrey is desolate, your cities are burnt with fire: your land, strangers deuoure it in your presence, and it is desolate as ouerthrowen by strangers.
is.1.8	Isaiah 1:8	And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged citie.
is.1.9	Isaiah 1:9	Except the LORD of hostes had left vnto vs a very small remnant, we should haue beene as Sodom, and we should haue bene like vnto Gomorrah.
is.1.10	Isaiah 1:10	¶ Heare the word of the LORD, ye rulers of Sodom, giue eare vnto the Law of our God, yee people of Gomorrah.
is.1.11	Isaiah 1:11	To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices vnto me, sayth the LORD? I am full of the burnt offerings of rammes, and the fat of fedde beasts, and I delight not in the blood of bullockes, or of lambes, or of hee goates.
is.1.12	Isaiah 1:12	When ye come to appeare before mee, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?
is.1.13	Isaiah 1:13	Bring no more vaine oblations, incense is an abomination vnto me: the new Moones, and Sabbaths, the calling of assemblies I cannot away with; it is iniquitie, euen the solemne meeting.
is.1.14	Isaiah 1:14	Your new Moones, and your appointed Feasts my soule hateth: they are a trouble vnto me, I am weary to beare them.
is.1.15	Isaiah 1:15	And when ye spread foorth your handes, I will hide mine eyes from you; yea, when yee make many prayers I will not heare: your hands are full of blood.
is.1.16	Isaiah 1:16	¶ Wash yee, make you cleane, put away the euill of your doings from before mine eyes, cease to doe euill,
is.1.17	Isaiah 1:17	Learne to doe well, seeke iudgement, relieue the oppressed, iudge the fatherlesse, plead for the widow.
is.1.18	Isaiah 1:18	Come now and let vs reason together, saith the LORD: though your sinnes be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimsin, they shall be as wooll.
is.1.19	Isaiah 1:19	If yee be willing and obedient, yee shall eate the good of the land.
is.1.20	Isaiah 1:20	But if yee refuse and rebell, yee shalbe deuoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.
is.1.21	Isaiah 1:21	¶ Howe is the faithfull citie become an harlot? it was full of iudgement, righteousnesse lodged in it; but now murtherers.
is.1.22	Isaiah 1:22	Thy siluer is become drosse, thy wine mixt with water.
is.1.23	Isaiah 1:23	Thy princes are rebellious and companions of theeues: euery one loueth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they iudge not the fatherlesse, neither doth the cause of the widowe come vnto them.
is.1.24	Isaiah 1:24	Therefore, saith the Lord, the LORD of hostes, the mighty one of Israel; Ah, I will ease me of mine aduersaries, and auenge me of mine enemies.
is.1.25	Isaiah 1:25	¶ And I will turne my hand vpon thee, and purely purge away thy drosse, and take away all thy tinne.
is.1.26	Isaiah 1:26	And I will restore thy iudges as at the first, and thy counsellers as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called the citie of righteousnesse, the faithfull citie.
is.1.27	Isaiah 1:27	Zion shall be redeemed with iudgement, and her conuerts with righteousnesse.
is.1.28	Isaiah 1:28	¶ And the destruction of the transgressours and of the sinners shall be together: and they that forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
is.1.29	Isaiah 1:29	For they shall be ashamed of the okes which yee haue desired, and yee shalbe confounded for the gardens that yee haue chosen.
is.1.30	Isaiah 1:30	For yee shall be as an oke whose leafe fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.
is.1.31	Isaiah 1:31	And the strong shall be as towe, and the maker of it as a sparke, and they shall both burne together, and none shall quench them.
is.2.1	Isaiah 2:1	The word that Isaiah, the sonne of Amoz, sawe concerning Iudah and Ierusalem.
is.2.2	Isaiah 2:2	And it shall come to passe in the last dayes, that the mountaine of the LORDs house shall be established in the top of the mountaines, and shall be exalted aboue the hilles; and all nations shall flow vnto it.
is.2.3	Isaiah 2:3	And many people shall goe & say; Come yee and let vs go vp to the mountaine of the LORD, to the house of the God of Iacob, and he will teach vs of his wayes, and we will walke in his pathes: for out of Zion shall goe forth the lawe, and the word of the LORD from Ierusalem.
is.2.4	Isaiah 2:4	And hee shall iudge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beate their swords into plow-shares, and their speares into pruning hookes: nation shall not lift vp sword against nation, neither shall they learne warre any more.
is.2.5	Isaiah 2:5	O house of Iacob, come yee, and let vs walke in the light of the LORD.

is.2.7	Isaiah 2:7	Their land also is full of siluer and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures: their land is also full of horses; neither is there any end of their charets.
is.2.8	Isaiah 2:8	Their land also is full of idoles: they worship the worke of their owne hands, that which their owne fingers haue made.
is.2.9	Isaiah 2:9	And the meane man boweth downe, and the great man humbleth himselfe; therefore forgiue them not.
is.2.10	Isaiah 2:10	¶ Enter into the rocke, and hide thee in the dust, for feare of the LORD, and for the glory of his Maiestie.
is.2.11	Isaiah 2:11	The loftie lookes of man shalbe humbled, and the hautines of men shalbe bowed downe: and the LORD alone shalbe exalted in that day.
is.2.12	Isaiah 2:12	For the day of the LORD of hostes shall bee vpon euery one that is proud and loftie, and vpon euery one that is lifted vp, and he shalbe brought low;
is.2.13	Isaiah 2:13	And vpon all the Cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted vp; and vpon all the okes of Bashan,
is.2.14	Isaiah 2:14	And vpon all the high mountaines, and vpon all the hilles that are lifted vp,
is.2.15	Isaiah 2:15	And vpon euery high tower, and vpon euery fenced wall,
is.2.16	Isaiah 2:16	And vpon all the ships of Tarshish, and vpon all pleasant pictures.
is.2.17	Isaiah 2:17	And the loftinesse of man shall be bowed downe, and the hautinesse of men shalbe made low: and the LORD alone shalbe exalted in that day.
is.2.18	Isaiah 2:18	And the idoles hee shall vtterly abolish.
is.2.19	Isaiah 2:19	And they shall goe into the holes of the rocks, and into the caues of the earth for feare of the LORD, and for the glory of his Maiestie; when hee ariseth to shake terribly the earth.
is.2.20	Isaiah 2:20	In that day a man shall cast his idoles of siluer, and his idoles of golde which they made each one for himselfe to worship, to the moules and to the battes:
is.2.21	Isaiah 2:21	To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rockes, for feare of the LORD, and for the glorie of his Maiestie; when hee ariseth to shake terribly the earth.
is.2.22	Isaiah 2:22	Cease ye from man whose breath is in his nostrels: for wherein is hee to be accounted of?

is.3.4	Isaiah 3:4	And I will giue children to bee their Princes, and babes shall rule ouer them.
is.3.5	Isaiah 3:5	And the people shall be oppressed, euery one by another, and euery one by his neighbour: the childe shall behaue himselfe proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.

is.3.8	Isaiah 3:8	For Ierusalem is ruined, & Iudah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to prouoke the eyes of his glorie.
is.3.9	Isaiah 3:9	¶ The shew of their countenance doeth witnesse against them, and they declare their sinne as Sodom, they hide it not: woe vnto their soule, for they haue rewarded euill vnto themselues.
is.3.10	Isaiah 3:10	Say yee to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eate the fruit of their doings.

is.3.12	Isaiah 3:12	¶ As for my people, children are their oppressours, and women rule ouer them: O my people, they which lead thee, cause thee to erre, and destroy the way of thy paths.

is.3.14	Isaiah 3:14	The LORD will enter into iudgement with the ancients of his people, and the Princes thereof: for ye haue eaten vp the Uineyard; the spoile of the poore is in your houses.

is.3.16	Isaiah 3:16	¶ Moreouer the LORD saith; Because the daughters of Zion are hautie, and walke with stretched forth necks, and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they goe, and making a tinkeling with their feet:

is.3.18	Isaiah 3:18	In that day the Lord will take away the brauery of their tinckling ornaments about their feete, and their caules, and their round tyres like the Moone.

is.3.20	Isaiah 3:20	The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legges, and the headbands, and the tablets, and the earerings,
is.3.21	Isaiah 3:21	The rings, and nose-iewels,
is.3.22	Isaiah 3:22	The changeable sutes of apparell, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pinnes,
is.3.23	Isaiah 3:23	The glasses, and the fine linnen, and the hoods, and the vailes.
is.3.24	Isaiah 3:24	And it shall come to passe, that in steade of sweete smell, there shall bee stinke; and in stead of a girdle, a rent; and in stead of well set haire, baldnesse; and in stead of a stomacher, a girding of sackecloth; and burning, in stead of beautie.

is.5.3	Isaiah 5:3	And now, O inhabitants of Ierusalem, and men of Iudah, Iudge, I pray you, betwixt me and my Uineyard.

is.5.20	Isaiah 5:20	¶ Woe vnto them that call euill good, and good euill, that put darkenes for light, and light for darkenesse, that put bitter for sweete, and sweete for bitter.
is.5.21	Isaiah 5:21	Woe vnto them that are wise in their owne eyes, and prudent in their owne sight.
is.5.22	Isaiah 5:22	Woe vnto them that are mightie to drinke wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drinke.
is.5.23	Isaiah 5:23	Which iustifie the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousnes of the righteous from him.

is.6.1	Isaiah 6:1	In the yeere that King Uzziah died, I saw also the Lord sitting vpon a throne, high and lifted vp, and his traine filled the Temple.
is.6.2	Isaiah 6:2	Aboue it stood the Seraphims: each one had sixe wings, with twaine he couered his face, and with twaine hee couered his feete, and with twaine hee did flie.
is.6.3	Isaiah 6:3	And one cryed vnto another, and sayd; Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hostes, the whole earth is full of his glory.
is.6.4	Isaiah 6:4	And the posts of the doore moued at the voyce of him that cryed, and the house was filled with smoke.
is.6.5	Isaiah 6:5	¶ Then sayd I; woe is me; for I am vndone, because I am a man of vncleane lippes, and I dwell in the midst of a people of vncleane lippes: for mine eyes haue seene the king, the LORD of hostes.
is.6.6	Isaiah 6:6	Then flew one of the Seraphims vnto mee, hauing a liue-cole in his hand, which hee had taken with the tongs from off the altar.
is.6.7	Isaiah 6:7	And he laide it vpon my mouth, and sayd, Loe, this hath touched thy lippes, and thine iniquitie is taken away, and thy sinne purged.
is.6.8	Isaiah 6:8	Also I heard the voyce of the Lord, saying; Whom shall I send, and who will goe for vs? Then I saide; Heere am I, send me.
is.6.9	Isaiah 6:9	¶ And he sayd, Goe and tell this people; Heare yee indeede, but vnderstand not: and see yee indeed, but perceiue not.
is.6.10	Isaiah 6:10	Make the heart of this people fat, and make their eares heauy, and shut their eyes: lest they see with their eyes, and heare with their eares, and vnderstand with their heart, and conuert and be healed.
is.6.11	Isaiah 6:11	Then sayd I; Lord, how long? And hee answered, Untill the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be vtterly desolate,

is.30.9	Isaiah 30:9	That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not heare the Law of the LORD:
is.30.10	Isaiah 30:10	Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophecie not vnto vs right things: speake vnto vs smooth things, prophecie deceits.
is.30.11	Isaiah 30:11	Get ye out of the way: turne aside out of the path: cause the Holy one of Israel to cease from before vs.
is.30.12	Isaiah 30:12	Wherefore, thus saith the Holy one of Israel: Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and peruersnesse, and stay thereon:
is.30.13	Isaiah 30:13	Therefore this iniquitie shalbe to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking commeth suddenly at an instant.
is.30.14	Isaiah 30:14	And he shall breake it as the breaking of the potters vessell, that is broken in pieces, he shall not spare; so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it, a sheard to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withall out of the pit.
is.30.15	Isaiah 30:15	For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy one of Israel, In returning and rest shall ye be saued, in quietnesse and in confidence shalbe your strength, and ye would not:
is.30.16	Isaiah 30:16	But ye said; No, for we will flee vpon horses; therefore shall ye flee. And we will ride vpon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you, be swift.
is.30.17	Isaiah 30:17	One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one: at the rebuke of fiue, shall ye flee, till ye be left as a beacon vpon the top of a mountaine, and as an ensigne on a hill.
is.30.18	Isaiah 30:18	¶ And therefore wil the LORD wait that he may be gracious vnto you, and therefore wil he be exalted that he may haue mercy vpon you: for the LORD is a God of Iudgment. Blessed are all they that wait for him.
is.30.19	Isaiah 30:19	For the people shall dwel in Zion at Ierusalem: thou shalt weepe no more: hee will be very gracious vnto thee, at the voice of thy cry; when he shall heare it, he will answere thee.
is.30.20	Isaiah 30:20	And though the Lord giue you the bread of aduersitie, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be remooued into a corner any more: but thine eyes shall see thy teachers.
is.30.21	Isaiah 30:21	And thine eares shall heare a word behinde thee, saying; This is the way, walke ye in it, when ye turne to the right hand, and when ye turne to the left.
is.30.22	Isaiah 30:22	Ye shall defile also the couering of thy grauen images of siluer, and the ornament of thy moulten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth, thou shalt say vnto it; Get thee hence.
is.30.23	Isaiah 30:23	Then shall he giue the raine of thy seed that thou shalt sow the ground withall; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shalbe fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattell feed in large pastures.
is.30.24	Isaiah 30:24	The oxen likewise and the yong asses that eare the ground, shall eate cleane prouender which hath bene winnowed with the shouell and with the fanne.
is.30.25	Isaiah 30:25	And there shall be vpon euery high mountaine, and vpon euery high hill, riuers and streames of waters, in the day of the great slaughter when the towers fall.
is.30.26	Isaiah 30:26	Moreouer the light of the Moone shalbe as the light of the Sunne, and the light of the Sunne shall be seuenfold, as the light of seuen dayes, in the day that the LORD bindeth vp the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.
is.30.27	Isaiah 30:27	¶ Beholde, the Name of the LORD commeth from farre, burning with his anger, and the burden thereof is heauy: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a deuouring fire.
is.30.28	Isaiah 30:28	And his breath as an ouerflowing streame, shall reach to the midst of the necke, to sift the nations with the sieue of vanitie: and there shalbe a bridle in the iawes of the people causing them to erre.
is.30.29	Isaiah 30:29	Yee shall haue a song as in the night, when a holy solemnitie is kept, and gladnesse of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come into the mountaine of the LORD, to the mighty one of Israel.
is.30.30	Isaiah 30:30	And the LORD shall cause his glorious voice to be heard, and shall shew the lighting downe of his arme, with the indignation of his anger, and with the flame of a deuouring fire, with scattering and tempest and hailestones.
is.30.31	Isaiah 30:31	For through the voyce of the LORD shall the Assyrian be beaten downe, which smote with a rod.
is.30.32	Isaiah 30:32	And in euery place where the grounded staffe shall passe, which the LORD shall lay vpon him, it shall be with tabrets and harpes: and in battels of shaking will he fight with it.
is.30.33	Isaiah 30:33	For Tophet is ordained of olde; yea, for the king it is prepared, he hath made it deepe and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood, the breath of the LORD, like a streame of brimstone, doeth kindle it.
is.31.1	Isaiah 31:1	Woe to them that go down to Egypt for helpe, and stay on horses, and trust in charets, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong: but they looke not vnto the Holy one of Israel, neither seeke the LORD.
is.31.2	Isaiah 31:2	Yet he also is wise, and will bring euill, and wil not call backe his words: but will arise against the house of the euill doers, and against the helpe of them that worke iniquitie.
is.31.3	Isaiah 31:3	Now the Egyptians are men and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit: when the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and hee that is holpen shall fall downe, and they all shall faile together.
is.31.4	Isaiah 31:4	For thus hath the LORD spoken vnto me; Like as the lyon and the yong lyon roaring on his pray, when a multitude of shepheards is called foorth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himselfe for the noyse of them: so shall the LORD of hostes come downe to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.
is.31.5	Isaiah 31:5	As birds flying, so wil the LORD of hostes defend Ierusalem, defending also hee will deliuer it, and passing ouer, he will preserue it.
is.31.6	Isaiah 31:6	¶ Turne yee vnto him from whom the children of Israel haue deeply reuolted.
is.31.7	Isaiah 31:7	For in that day euery man shall cast away his idoles of siluer, and his idoles of gold, which your owne hands haue made vnto you for a sinne.
is.31.8	Isaiah 31:8	¶ Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mightie man; and the sword, not of a meane man, shal deuoure him: but hee shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall be discomfited.
is.31.9	Isaiah 31:9	And hee shall passe ouer to his strong holde for feare, and his princes shall be afraid of the ensigne, sayth the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his fornace in Ierusalem.
is.32.1	Isaiah 32:1	Behold, a King shal reigne in righteousnes, and princes shal rule in iudgement.
is.32.2	Isaiah 32:2	And a man shall be as an hiding place from the winde, and a couert from the tempest: as riuers of water in a drie place, as the shadow of a great rocke in a wearie land.
is.32.3	Isaiah 32:3	And the eyes of them that see, shall not be dimme; and the eares of them that heare, shall hearken.
is.32.4	Isaiah 32:4	The heart also of the rash shall vnderstand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall bee readie to speake plainely.
is.32.5	Isaiah 32:5	The vile person shall be no more called liberall, nor the churle sayd to be bountifull.
is.32.6	Isaiah 32:6	For the vile person wil speake villenie, and his heart will worke iniquitie, to practise hypocrisie, and to vtter errour against the LORD, to make emptie the soule of the hungry, and hee will cause the drinke of the thirstie to faile.
is.32.7	Isaiah 32:7	The instruments also of the churle are euill: he deuiseth wicked deuices, to destroy the poore with lying wordes, euen when the needie speaketh right.
is.32.8	Isaiah 32:8	But the liberall deuiseth liberall things, and by liberall things shall hee stand.
is.32.9	Isaiah 32:9	¶ Rise vp ye women that are at ease: heare my voice, ye carelesse daughters, giue eare vnto my speech.
is.32.10	Isaiah 32:10	Many dayes and yeeres shall ye be troubled, yee carelesse women: for the vintage shall faile, the gathering shall not come.
is.32.11	Isaiah 32:11	Tremble yee women that are at ease: be troubled, ye carelesse ones, strip ye and make ye bare, and gird sackecloth vpon your loynes.
is.32.12	Isaiah 32:12	They shall lament for the teats, for the pleasant fieldes, for the fruitfull vine.
is.32.13	Isaiah 32:13	Upon the land of my people shall come vp thornes, and briars, yea vpon all the houses of ioy in the ioyous citie.
is.32.14	Isaiah 32:14	Because the palaces shall be forsaken, the multitude of the citie shall be left, the forts and towres shall be for dennes for euer, a ioy of wild asses, a pasture of flockes;
is.32.15	Isaiah 32:15	Untill the spirit be powred vpon vs from on high, and the wildernesse be a fruitfull field, and the fruitfull field be counted for a forrest.
is.32.16	Isaiah 32:16	Then iudgement shall dwell in the wildernesse, and righteousnesse remaine in the fruitfull field.
is.32.17	Isaiah 32:17	And the worke of righteousnesse shalbe peace, and the effect of righteousnesse, quietnesse and assurance for euer.
is.32.18	Isaiah 32:18	And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places:
is.32.19	Isaiah 32:19	When it shall haile, comming downe on the forrest; and the citie shall be low in a low place.
is.32.20	Isaiah 32:20	Blessed are yee that sow beside all waters, that send forth thither the feete of the oxe and the asse.
is.33.1	Isaiah 33:1	Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee: when thou shalt cease to spoile, thou shalt bee spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deale treacherously, they shall deale treacherously with thee.
is.33.2	Isaiah 33:2	O LORD, be gratious vnto vs, we haue waited for thee: be thou their arme euery morning, our saluation also in the time of trouble.
is.33.3	Isaiah 33:3	At the noise of the tumult the people fled: at the lifting vp of thy selfe the nations were scattered.
is.33.4	Isaiah 33:4	And your spoile shall be gathered like the gathering of the caterpiller: as the running to and fro of Locusts shall he runne vpon them.

is.33.13	Isaiah 33:13	¶ Heare yee that are farre off, what I haue done; and yee that are neere, acknowledge my might.
is.33.14	Isaiah 33:14	The sinners in Zion are afraid, fearefulnesse hath surprised the hypocrites: who among vs shall dwell with the deuouring fire? who amongst vs shall dwell with euerlasting burnings?
is.33.15	Isaiah 33:15	He that walketh righteously, and speaketh vprightly, hee that despiseth the gaine of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his eares from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing euill:
is.33.16	Isaiah 33:16	He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shalbe the munitions of rocks, bread shalbe giuen him, his waters shall be sure.

is.33.21	Isaiah 33:21	But there the glorious LORD will be vnto vs a place of broad riuers and streames; wherein shall goe no galley with oares, neither shall gallant ship passe thereby.

is.35.1	Isaiah 35:1	The wildernesse and the solitarie place shall be glad for them: and the desert shall reioyce and blossome as the rose.

is.36.1	Isaiah 36:1	Nowe it came to passe in the fourteenth yeere of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came vp against all the defenced cities of Iudah, and tooke them.

is.36.12	Isaiah 36:12	¶ But Rabshakeh sayd; Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee, to speake these words? Hath he not sent me to the men that sit vpon the wall, that they may eate their owne dongue, and drinke their owne pisse with you?

is.36.17	Isaiah 36:17	Until I come and take you away to a land like your owne land, a land of corne and wine, a land of bread and vineyards:
is.36.18	Isaiah 36:18	Beware lest Hezekiah perswade you, saying; The LORD will deliuer vs. Hath any of the gods of the nations deliuered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
