mt.28.19	Matthew 28:19	¶ Goe ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the Name of the Father, and of the Sonne, and of the holy Ghost:
mt.28.20	Matthew 28:20	Teaching them to obserue all things, whatsoeuer I haue commanded you: and loe, I am with you alway, euen vnto the end of the world. Amen.
mk.1.1	Mark 1:1	The beginning of the Gospel of Iesus Christ, the Sonne of God,
mk.1.2	Mark 1:2	As it is written in the Prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
mk.1.3	Mark 1:3	The voice of one crying in the wildernesse, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
mk.1.4	Mark 1:4	Iohn did baptize in the wildernesse, and preach the baptisme of repentance, for the remission of sinnes.
mk.1.5	Mark 1:5	And there went out vnto him all the land of Iudea, and they of Ierusalem, and were all baptized of him in the riuer of Iordane, cōfessing their sinnes.
mk.1.6	Mark 1:6	And Iohn was clothed with camels haire, and with a girdle of a skin about his loines: and he did eat locusts and wilde honie,
mk.1.7	Mark 1:7	And preached, saying, There commeth one mightier then I after me, the latchet of whose shooes I am not worthy to stoupe downe, and vnloose.
mk.1.8	Mark 1:8	I indeed haue baptized you with water: but hee shall baptize you with the holy Ghost.
mk.1.9	Mark 1:9	And it came to passe in those daies, that Iesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of Iohn in Iordane.
mk.1.10	Mark 1:10	And straightway comming vp out of the water, hee saw the heauens opened, and the Spirit like a doue descending vpon him.
mk.1.11	Mark 1:11	And there came a voice from heauen, saying, Thou art my beloued Sonne, in whom I am well pleased.
mk.1.12	Mark 1:12	And immediately the Spirit driueth him into the wildernesse.
mk.1.13	Mark 1:13	And he was there in the wildernesse fourtie daies tempted of Satan, and was with the wildbeasts, and the Angels ministred vnto him.
mk.1.14	Mark 1:14	Now after that Iohn was put in prison, Iesus came into Galilee, preaching the Gospell of the kingdome of God,
mk.1.15	Mark 1:15	And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdome of God is at hand: repent ye, and beleeue the Gospell.
mk.1.16	Mark 1:16	Now as he walked by the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the Sea (for they were fishers.)
mk.1.17	Mark 1:17	And Iesus said vnto them, Come ye after me; and I will make you to become fishers of men.
mk.1.18	Mark 1:18	And straightway they forsooke their nets, and followed him.
mk.1.19	Mark 1:19	And when hee had gone a little further thence, hee saw Iames the sonne of Zebedee, and Iohn his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
mk.1.20	Mark 1:20	And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired seruants, and went after him.
mk.1.21	Mark 1:21	And they went into Capernaum, and straightway on the Sabbath day he entred into the Synagogue, and taught.
mk.1.22	Mark 1:22	And they were astonished at his doctrine: for hee taught them as one that had authority, and not as the Scribes.
mk.1.23	Mark 1:23	And there was in their Synagogue a man with an vncleane spirit, and he cried out,
mk.1.24	Mark 1:24	Saying, Let vs alone, what haue we to doe with thee, thou Iesus of Nazareth? Art thou come to destroy vs? I know thee who thou art, the holy One of God.
mk.1.25	Mark 1:25	And Iesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.
mk.1.26	Mark 1:26	And when the vncleane spirit had torne him, and cried with a lowd voice, he came out of him.
mk.1.27	Mark 1:27	And they were all amased, insomuch that they questioned among themselues, saying, What thing is this? What new doctrine is this? For with authoritie commandeth he euen the vncleane spirits, and they doe obey him.
mk.1.28	Mark 1:28	And immediatly his fame spread abroad throughout al the region round about Galilee.
mk.1.29	Mark 1:29	And forth with, when they were come out of the Synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon, and Andrew, with Iames and Iohn.
mk.1.30	Mark 1:30	But Simons wiues mother lay sicke of a feuer: and anone they tell him of her.
mk.1.31	Mark 1:31	And he came and tooke her by the hand, and lift her vp, and immediately the feuer left her, and she ministred vnto them.
mk.1.32	Mark 1:32	And at euen, when the Sunne did set, they brought vnto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with diuels:
mk.1.33	Mark 1:33	And all the citie was gathered together at the doore.
mk.1.34	Mark 1:34	And he healed many that were sicke of diuers diseases, and cast out many deuils, and suffered not the deuils to speake, because they knew him.
mk.1.35	Mark 1:35	And in the morning, rising vp a great while before day, hee went out, and departed into a solitarie place, and there prayed.
mk.1.36	Mark 1:36	And Simon, and they that were with him, followed after him:
mk.1.37	Mark 1:37	And when they had found him, they said vnto him, All men seek for thee.
mk.1.38	Mark 1:38	And he said vnto them, Let vs goe into þ next townes, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I foorth.
mk.1.39	Mark 1:39	And he preached in their Synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out deuils.
mk.1.40	Mark 1:40	And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling downe to him, and saying vnto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me cleane.
mk.1.41	Mark 1:41	And Iesus mooued with compassion, put foorth his hand, and touched him, and saith vnto him, I will, be thou cleane.
mk.1.42	Mark 1:42	And assoone as he had spoken, immediately the leprosie departed from him, and he was cleansed.
mk.1.43	Mark 1:43	And he straitly charged him, and forth with sent him away,
mk.1.44	Mark 1:44	And saith vnto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but goe thy way, shew thy selfe to the Priest, and offer for thy clensing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony vnto them.
mk.1.45	Mark 1:45	But he went out, and beganne to publish it much, and to blase abroad the matter: insomuch that Iesus could no more openly enter into the citie, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from euery quarter.
mk.2.1	Mark 2:1	And againe hee entred into Capernaum after some dayes, and it was noysed that he was in the house.
mk.2.2	Mark 2:2	And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no roome to receiue them, no not so much as about the doore: and he preached the word vnto them.
mk.2.3	Mark 2:3	And they come vnto him, bringing one sicke of the palsie, which was borne of foure.
mk.2.4	Mark 2:4	And when they could not come nigh vnto him for preasse, they vncouered the roofe where he was: and when they had broken it vp, they let downe the bed wherin the sick of the palsie lay.
mk.2.5	Mark 2:5	When Iesus saw their faith, hee said vnto the sicke of the palsie, Sonne, thy sinnes be forgiuen thee.
mk.2.6	Mark 2:6	But there were certaine of the Scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
mk.2.7	Mark 2:7	Why doeth this man thus speake blasphemies? Who can forgiue sinnes but God onely?
mk.2.8	Mark 2:8	And immediatly, when Iesus perceiued in his Spirit, that they so reasoned within themselues, he said vnto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?
mk.2.9	Mark 2:9	Whether is it easier to say to the sicke of the palsie, Thy sinnes be forgiuen thee: or to say, Arise, and take vp thy bed and walke?
mk.2.10	Mark 2:10	But that yee may know that the Sonne of man hath power on earth to forgiue sinnes, (Hee saith to the sicke of the palsie,)
mk.2.11	Mark 2:11	I say vnto thee, Arise, & take vp thy bed, & goe thy way into thine house.
mk.2.12	Mark 2:12	And immediatly he arose, tooke vp the bed, and went foorth before them all, insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, Wee neuer saw it on this fashion.
mk.2.13	Mark 2:13	And he went foorth againe by the sea side, and all the multitude resorted vnto him, and he taught them.
mk.2.14	Mark 2:14	And as he passed by, he saw Leui the son of Alpheus sitting at the receit of Custome, and said vnto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
mk.2.15	Mark 2:15	And it came to passe, that as Iesus sate at meate in his house, many Publicanes and sinners sate also together with Iesus and his disciples: for there were many, & they followed him.
mk.2.16	Mark 2:16	And when the Scribes and Pharisees saw him eate with Publicanes and sinners, they said vnto his disciples, How is it that hee eateth and drinketh with Publicanes and sinners?
mk.2.17	Mark 2:17	When Iesus heard it, he saith vnto them, They that are whole, haue no need of the Physition, but they that are sicke: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
mk.2.18	Mark 2:18	And the disciples of Iohn, and of the Pharisees vsed to fast; and they come, and say vnto him, Why doe the disciples of Iohn, and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?
mk.2.19	Mark 2:19	And Iesus said vnto them, Can the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the Bridegrome is with them? As long as they haue the Bridegrome with them, they cannot fast.
mk.2.20	Mark 2:20	But the dayes will come, when the Bridegrome shall bee taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those dayes.
mk.2.21	Mark 2:21	No man also soweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it vp, taketh away from the old, & the rent is made worse.
mk.2.22	Mark 2:22	And no man putteth new wine into old bottles, else the new wine doeth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will bee marred: But new wine must bee put into new bottles.
mk.2.23	Mark 2:23	And it came to passe, that he went thorow the corne fields on the Sabbath day, & his disciples began as they went, to plucke the eares of corne.
mk.2.24	Mark 2:24	And the Pharisees saide vnto him, Behold, why do they on the Sabbath day that which is not lawfull?
mk.2.25	Mark 2:25	And he said vnto them, Haue ye neuer read what Dauid did, when hee had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?
mk.2.26	Mark 2:26	How hee went into the house of God in the dayes of Abiathar the high Priest, and did eate the Shew-bread, which is not lawfull to eate, but for the Priests, and gaue also to them which were with him?
mk.2.27	Mark 2:27	And hee said vnto them, The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath:
mk.2.28	Mark 2:28	Therefore the Sonne of man is Lord also of the Sabbath.
mk.3.1	Mark 3:1	And he entred againe into the Synagogue, and there was a man there which had a withered hand:
mk.3.2	Mark 3:2	And they watched him, whether hee would heale him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.
mk.3.3	Mark 3:3	And he saith vnto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.
mk.3.4	Mark 3:4	And hee saith vnto them, Is it lawfull to doe good on the Sabbath dayes, or to doe euill? to saue life, or to kill? but they held their peace.
mk.3.5	Mark 3:5	And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieued for the hardnesse of their hearts, He saith vnto the man, Stretch foorth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
mk.3.6	Mark 3:6	And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway tooke counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
mk.3.7	Mark 3:7	But Iesus withdrew himselfe with his disciples to the Sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Iudea,
mk.3.8	Mark 3:8	And from Hierusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond Iordane, and they about Tyre & Sydon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came vnto him.
mk.3.9	Mark 3:9	And he spake to his disciples that a small ship should wait on him, because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.
mk.3.10	Mark 3:10	For he had healed many, insomuch that they preassed vpon him, for to touch him, as many as had plagues.
mk.3.11	Mark 3:11	And vncleane spirits, when they saw him, fell downe before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Sonne of God.
mk.3.12	Mark 3:12	And he straitly charged them, that they should not make him knowen.
mk.3.13	Mark 3:13	And he goeth vp into a mountaine, and calleth vnto him whom he would: and they came vnto him.
mk.3.14	Mark 3:14	And he ordeined twelue, that they should be with him, and that hee might send them foorth to preach:
mk.3.15	Mark 3:15	And to haue power to heale sickenesses, and to cast out deuils.
mk.3.16	Mark 3:16	And Simon he surnamed Peter.
mk.3.17	Mark 3:17	And Iames the sonne of Zebedee, and Iohn the brother of Iames (and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sonnes of thunder.)
mk.3.18	Mark 3:18	And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and Iames the sonne of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
mk.3.19	Mark 3:19	And Iudas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
mk.3.20	Mark 3:20	And the multitude commeth together againe, so that they could not so much as eate bread.
mk.3.21	Mark 3:21	And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him, for they said, He is beside himselfe.
mk.3.22	Mark 3:22	¶ And the Scribes which came downe from Hierusalem, said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the deuils, casteth he out deuils.
mk.3.23	Mark 3:23	And he called them vnto him, and said vnto them in parables, Howe can Satan cast out Satan?
mk.3.24	Mark 3:24	And if a kingdome be diuided against it selfe, that kingdome cannot stand.
mk.3.25	Mark 3:25	And if a house be diuided against it selfe, that house cannot stand.
mk.3.26	Mark 3:26	And if Satan rise vp against himselfe, and be diuided, hee cannot stand, but hath an end.
mk.3.27	Mark 3:27	No man can enter into a strong mans house, and spoile his goods, except he will first bind the strong man, and then he will spoile his house.
mk.3.28	Mark 3:28	Uerely I say vnto you, All sinnes shalbe forgiuen vnto the sonnes of men, and blasphemies, wherewith soeuer they shall blaspheme:
mk.3.29	Mark 3:29	But he that shal blaspheme against the holy Ghost, hath neuer forgiuenesse, but is in danger of eternall damnation.
mk.3.30	Mark 3:30	Because they said, He hath an vncleane spirit.
mk.3.31	Mark 3:31	¶ There came then his brethren, and his mother, and standing without, sent vnto him, calling him.
mk.3.32	Mark 3:32	And the multitude sate about him and they said vnto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seeke for thee.
mk.3.33	Mark 3:33	And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?
mk.3.34	Mark 3:34	And he looked round about on them which sate about him, and saide, Behold my mother and my brethren.
mk.3.35	Mark 3:35	For whosoeuer shall doe the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
mk.4.1	Mark 4:1	And he beganne againe to teach by the Sea side: and there was gathered vnto him a great multitude, so that he entred into a ship, and sate in the Sea: and the whole multitude was by the Sea on the land.
mk.4.2	Mark 4:2	And he taught them many things by parables, and said vnto them in his doctrine,
mk.4.3	Mark 4:3	Hearken, Behold, there went out a sower to sow:
mk.4.4	Mark 4:4	And it came to passe as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the foules of the aire came, & deuoured it vp.
mk.4.5	Mark 4:5	And some fell on stonie ground, where it had not much earth: and immediately it sprang vp, because it had no depth of earth.
mk.4.6	Mark 4:6	But when the Sunne was vp, it was scorched, and because it had no roote, it withered away.
mk.4.7	Mark 4:7	And some fell among thornes, and the thornes grew vp, and choked it, and it yeelded no fruite.
mk.4.8	Mark 4:8	And other fell on good ground, and did yeeld fruite that sprang vp, and increased, and brought foorth some thirtie, & some sixtie, & some an hundred.
mk.4.9	Mark 4:9	And he said vnto them, He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.
mk.4.10	Mark 4:10	And when hee was alone, they that were about him, with the twelue, asked of him the parable.
mk.4.11	Mark 4:11	And he said vnto them, Unto you it is giuen to know the mystery of the kingdome of God: but vnto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:
mk.4.12	Mark 4:12	That seeing they may see, and not perceiue, and hearing they may heare, and not vnderstand, lest at any time they should be conuerted, and their sinnes should be forgiuen them.
mk.4.13	Mark 4:13	And he said vnto them, Know ye not this parable? And how then will you know all parables?
mk.4.14	Mark 4:14	¶ The Sower soweth the word.
mk.4.15	Mark 4:15	And these are they by the way side, where the word is sowen, but when they haue heard, Satan commeth immediately, and taketh away the word that was sowen in their hearts.
mk.4.16	Mark 4:16	And these are they likewise which are sowen on stonie ground, who when they haue heard the word, immediately receiue it with gladnesse:
mk.4.17	Mark 4:17	And haue no roote in themselues, and so endure but for a time: afterward when affliction or persecution ariseth for the words sake, immediately they are offended.
mk.4.18	Mark 4:18	And these are they which are sowen among thorns: such as heare the word,
mk.4.19	Mark 4:19	And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulnesse of riches, and the lusts of other things entring in, choke the word, and it becommeth vnfruitfull.
mk.4.20	Mark 4:20	And these are they which are sowen on good ground, such as heare the word, and receiue it, & bring foorth fruit, some thirty fold, some sixtie, and some an hundred.
mk.4.21	Mark 4:21	¶ And he said vnto them, Is a candle brought to be put vnder a bushell, or vnder a bed? & not to be set on a candlesticke?
mk.4.22	Mark 4:22	For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested: neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.
mk.4.23	Mark 4:23	If any man haue eares to heare, let him heare.
mk.4.24	Mark 4:24	And he said vnto them, Take heed what you heare: With what measure ye mete, it shalbe measured to you: And vnto you that heare, shal more be giuen.
mk.4.25	Mark 4:25	For he that hath, to him shall be giuen: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken, euen that which he hath.
mk.4.26	Mark 4:26	¶ And he said, So is the kingdome of God, as if a man should cast seede into the ground,
mk.4.27	Mark 4:27	And should sleepe, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring, and grow vp, he knoweth not how.
mk.4.28	Mark 4:28	For the earth bringeth foorth fruite of herselfe, first the blade, then the eare, after that the full corne in the eare.
mk.4.29	Mark 4:29	But when the fruite is brought foorth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the haruest is come.
mk.4.30	Mark 4:30	¶ And he said, Wherunto shal we liken the kingdome of God? Or with what comparison shall we compare it?
mk.4.31	Mark 4:31	It is like a graine of mustard seed: which when it is sowen in the earth, is lesse then all the seedes that be in the earth.
mk.4.32	Mark 4:32	But when it is sowen, it groweth vp, and becommeth greater then all herbes, & shooteth out great branches, so that the fowles of the aire may lodge vnder the shadow of it.
mk.4.33	Mark 4:33	And with many such parables spake hee the word vnto them, as they were able to heare it.
mk.4.34	Mark 4:34	But without a parable spake he not vnto them, and when they were alone, hee expounded all things to his disciples.
mk.4.35	Mark 4:35	And the same day, when the Euen was come, he saith vnto them, Let vs passe ouer vnto the other side.
mk.4.36	Mark 4:36	And when they had sent away the multitude, they tooke him, euen as he was in the ship, and there were also with him other litle ships.
mk.4.37	Mark 4:37	And there arose a great storme of wind, and the waues beat into the ship, so that it was now full.
mk.4.38	Mark 4:38	And he was in the hinder part of the ship asleepe on a pillow: and they awake him, and say vnto him, Master, carest thou not, that we perish?
mk.4.39	Mark 4:39	And hee arose, and rebuked the winde, and said vnto the sea, Peace, be still: and the winde ceased, and there was a great calme.
mk.4.40	Mark 4:40	And he said vnto them, Why are ye so fearefull? How is it that you haue no faith?
mk.4.41	Mark 4:41	And they feared exceedingly, and saide one to another, What maner of man is this, that euen the winde and the sea obey him?
mk.5.1	Mark 5:1	And they came ouer vnto the other side of the sea, into the countrey of the Gadarenes.
mk.5.2	Mark 5:2	And when hee was come out of the ship, immediatly there met him out of the tombes, a man with an vncleane spirit,
mk.5.3	Mark 5:3	Who had his dwelling among the tombs, and no man could binde him, no not with chaines:
mk.5.4	Mark 5:4	Because that hee had bene often bound with fetters and chaines, and the chaines had bene plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
mk.5.5	Mark 5:5	And alwayes night and day, hee was in the mountaines, and in the tombes, crying, and cutting himselfe with stones.
mk.5.6	Mark 5:6	But when hee saw Iesus afarre off, he came and worshipped him,
mk.5.7	Mark 5:7	And cried with a lowd voice, and said, What haue I to doe with thee, Iesus, thou Sonne of the most high God? I adiure thee by God, that thou torment me not.
mk.5.8	Mark 5:8	(For he said vnto him, Come out of the man, thou vncleane spirit.)
mk.5.9	Mark 5:9	And he asked him, What is thy name? And hee answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
mk.5.10	Mark 5:10	And hee besought him much, that he would not send them away out of the countrey.
mk.5.11	Mark 5:11	Now there was there nigh vnto the mountaines a great herd of swine, feeding.
mk.5.12	Mark 5:12	And all the deuils besought him, saying, Send vs into the swine, that we may enter into them.
mk.5.13	Mark 5:13	And forthwith Iesus gaue them leaue. And the vncleane spirits went out, and entred into the swine, and the herd ranne violently downe a steepe place into the sea (they were about two thousand) and were choked in the sea.
mk.5.14	Mark 5:14	And they that fed the swine fled, and tolde it in the citie, and in the countrey. And they went out to see what it was that was done.
mk.5.15	Mark 5:15	And they come to Iesus, and see him that was possessed with the deuill, and had the Legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right minde: and they were afraid.
mk.5.16	Mark 5:16	And they that saw it, tolde them how it befell to him that was possessed with the deuill, and also concerning the swine.
mk.5.17	Mark 5:17	And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.
mk.5.18	Mark 5:18	And when hee was come into the ship, he that had bene possessed with the deuill prayed him that hee might bee with him.
mk.5.19	Mark 5:19	Howbeit Iesus suffered him not, but saith vnto him, Goe home to thy friends, and tel them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
mk.5.20	Mark 5:20	And hee departed, and began to publish in Decapolis, how great things Iesus had done for him: and all men did marueile.
mk.5.21	Mark 5:21	And when Iesus was passed ouer againe by ship vnto the other side, much people gathered vnto him, and he was nigh vnto the Sea.
mk.5.22	Mark 5:22	And behold, there commeth one of the Rulers of the Synagogue, Iairus by name, and when he saw him, he fell at his feete,
mk.5.23	Mark 5:23	And besought him greatly, saying, My litle daughter lieth at the point of death, I pray thee come and lay thy hands on her, that shee may be healed, and she shall liue.
mk.5.24	Mark 5:24	And Iesus went with him, and much people followed him, and thronged him.
mk.5.25	Mark 5:25	And a certaine woman which had an issue of blood twelue yeeres,
mk.5.26	Mark 5:26	And had suffered many things of many Physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,
mk.5.27	Mark 5:27	When shee had heard of Iesus, came in the prease behinde, and touched his garment.
mk.5.28	Mark 5:28	For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shalbe whole.
mk.5.29	Mark 5:29	And straightway the fountaine of her blood was dried vp: and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.
mk.5.30	Mark 5:30	And Iesus immediatly knowing in himselfe that vertue had gone out of him, turned him about in the preasse, and said, Who touched my clothes?
mk.5.31	Mark 5:31	And his disciples said vnto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
mk.5.32	Mark 5:32	And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.
mk.5.33	Mark 5:33	But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell downe before him, and tolde him all the trueth.
mk.5.34	Mark 5:34	And he said vnto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole, goe in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
mk.5.35	Mark 5:35	While hee yet spake, there came from the Ruler of the Synagogues house, certaine which said, Thy daughter is dead, why troublest thou the Master any further?
mk.5.36	Mark 5:36	Assoone as Iesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith vnto the Ruler of the Synagogue, Be not afraid, onely beleeue.
mk.5.37	Mark 5:37	And he suffered no man to follow him, saue Peter, & Iames, and Iohn the brother of Iames.
mk.5.38	Mark 5:38	And hee commeth to the house of the Ruler of the Synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.
mk.5.39	Mark 5:39	And when he was come in, hee saith vnto them, Why make yee this adoe, and weepe? the damosell is not dead, but sleepeth.
mk.5.40	Mark 5:40	And they laughed him to scorne: but when he had put them all out, hee taketh the father and the mother of the damosell, and them that were with him, and entreth in where the damosell was lying.
mk.5.41	Mark 5:41	And he tooke the damosell by the hand, and said vnto her, Talitha cumi, which is, being interpreted, Damosell (I say vnto thee) Arise.
mk.5.42	Mark 5:42	And straightway the damosell arose, and walked, for shee was of the age of twelue yeeres: and they were astonished with a great astonishment.
mk.5.43	Mark 5:43	And hee charged them straitly, that no man should know it: and commanded that some thing should be giuen her to eate.
mk.6.1	Mark 6:1	And hee went out from thence, and came into his owne countrey, and his disciples follow him.
mk.6.2	Mark 6:2	And when the Sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the Synagogue: and many hearing him, were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? And what wisedome is this which is giuen vnto him, that euen such mightie workes are wrought by his hands?
mk.6.3	Mark 6:3	Is not this the carpenter, the sonne of Mary, the brother of Iames and Ioses, and of Iuda, and Simon? And are not his sisters heere with vs? And they were offended at him.
mk.6.4	Mark 6:4	But Iesus sayde vnto them, A Prophet is not without honour, but in his owne countrey, and among his owne kinne, and in his owne house.
mk.6.5	Mark 6:5	And he could there doe no mightie worke, saue that he laid his hands vpon a few sicke folke, and healed them.
mk.6.6	Mark 6:6	And he marueiled because of their vnbeliefe. And he went round about the villages, teaching.
mk.6.7	Mark 6:7	¶ And he calleth vnto him the twelue, and began to send them foorth, by two and two, and gaue them power ouer vncleane spirits,
mk.6.8	Mark 6:8	And commanded them that they should take nothing for their iourney, saue a staffe onely: no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:
mk.6.9	Mark 6:9	But be shod with sandales: and not put on two coats.
mk.6.10	Mark 6:10	And he said vnto them, In what place soeuer yee enter into an house, there abide til ye depart from that place.
mk.6.11	Mark 6:11	And whosoeuer shall not receiue you, nor heare you, when yee depart thence, shake off the dust vnder your feet, for a testimonie against them: Uerely I say vnto you, it shalbe more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of iudgement, then for that citie.
mk.6.12	Mark 6:12	And they went out, and preached that men should repent.
mk.6.13	Mark 6:13	And they cast out many deuils, and anointed with oyle many, that were sicke, and healed them.
mk.6.14	Mark 6:14	And king Herod heard of him (for his name was spread abroad:) and hee said that Iohn the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mightie workes doe shew foorth themselues in him.
mk.6.15	Mark 6:15	Others said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a Prophet, or as one of the Prophets.
mk.6.16	Mark 6:16	But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is Iohn, whome I beheaded, he is risen from the dead.
mk.6.17	Mark 6:17	For Herod himselfe had sent forth and laid hold vpon Iohn, and bound him in prison for Herodias sake, his brother Philips wife, for hee had maried her.
mk.6.18	Mark 6:18	For Iohn had said vnto Herod, It is not lawfull for thee to haue thy brothers wife.
mk.6.19	Mark 6:19	Therfore Herodias had a quarrel against him, & would haue killed him, but she could not.
mk.6.20	Mark 6:20	For Herod feared Iohn, knowing that he was a iust man, and an holy, and obserued him: and when he heard him, hee did many things, and heard him gladly.
mk.6.21	Mark 6:21	And when a conuenient day was come, that Herod on his birth day made a supper to his lords, high captaines, and chiefe estates of Galilee:
mk.6.22	Mark 6:22	And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod, and them that sate with him, the king said vnto the damosell, Aske of me whatsoeuer thou wilt, and I will giue it thee.
mk.6.23	Mark 6:23	And he sware vnto her, Whatsoeuer thou shalt aske of me, I will giue it thee, vnto the halfe of my kingdome.
mk.6.24	Mark 6:24	And she went forth, and said vnto her mother, What shall I aske? And she said, The head of Iohn þ Baptist.
mk.6.25	Mark 6:25	And she came in straightway with haste, vnto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou giue me by and by in a charger, the head of Iohn the Baptist.
mk.6.26	Mark 6:26	And the king was exceeding sory, yet for his othes sake, and for their sakes which sate with him, hee would not reiect her.
mk.6.27	Mark 6:27	And immediatly the king sent an executioner, and commaunded his head to be brought, and he went, and beheaded him in the prison,
mk.6.28	Mark 6:28	And brought his head in a charger, and gaue it to the damosell, and the damosell gaue it to her mother.
mk.6.29	Mark 6:29	And when his disciples heard of it, they came and tooke vp his corpse, and laid it in a tombe.
mk.6.30	Mark 6:30	And the Apostles gathered themselues together vnto Iesus, and tolde him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
mk.6.31	Mark 6:31	And he said vnto them, Come yee your selues apart into a desert place, and rest a while. For there were many comming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eate.
mk.6.32	Mark 6:32	And they departed into a desert place by ship priuately.
mk.6.33	Mark 6:33	And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ranne afoote thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together vnto him.
mk.6.34	Mark 6:34	And Iesus when he came out, saw much people, and was moued with compassion toward them, because they were as sheepe not hauing a shepherd: and hee beganne to teach them many things.
mk.6.35	Mark 6:35	And when the day was now far spent, his Disciples came vnto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is farre passed.
mk.6.36	Mark 6:36	Send them away, that they may goe into the countrey round about, and into the villages, and buy themselues bread: for they haue nothing to eate.
mk.6.37	Mark 6:37	He answered and said vnto them, Giue yee them to eate. And they say vnto him, Shall we goe and buy two hundred penniworth of bread, and giue them to eate?
mk.6.38	Mark 6:38	He saith vnto them, How many loaues haue yee? goe, and see. And when they knew, they say, Fiue, and two fishes.
mk.6.39	Mark 6:39	And he commanded them to make all sit downe by companies vpon the greene grasse.
mk.6.40	Mark 6:40	And they sate downe in rankes by hundreds, and by fifties.
mk.6.41	Mark 6:41	And when he had taken the fiue loaues, and the two fishes, he looked vp to heauen, and blessed, and brake the loaues, and gaue them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes diuided he among them all.
mk.6.42	Mark 6:42	And they did all eate, and were filled.
mk.6.43	Mark 6:43	And they tooke vp twelue baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
mk.6.44	Mark 6:44	And they that did eate of the loaues, were about fiue thousand men.
mk.6.45	Mark 6:45	And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to goe to the other side before vnto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
mk.6.46	Mark 6:46	And when hee had sent them away, he departed into a mountaine to pray.
mk.6.47	Mark 6:47	And when Euen was come, the ship was in the midst of the Sea, and he alone on the land.
mk.6.48	Mark 6:48	And he saw them toiling in rowing (for the wind was contrary vnto them:) and about the fourth watch of the night, he commeth vnto them, walking vpon the Sea, and would haue passed by them.
mk.6.49	Mark 6:49	But when they saw him walking vpon the Sea, they supposed it had bene a spirit, and cried out.
mk.6.50	Mark 6:50	(For they all saw him, and were troubled) and immediately hee talked with them, and saith vnto them, Be of good cheere, It is I, be not afraid.
mk.6.51	Mark 6:51	And hee went vp vnto them into the ship, and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselues beyond measure, and wondered.
mk.6.52	Mark 6:52	For they considered not the miracle of the loaues, for their heart was hardened.
mk.6.53	Mark 6:53	And when they had passed ouer, they came into the land of Genesareth, and drew to the shore.
mk.6.54	Mark 6:54	And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,
mk.6.55	Mark 6:55	And ran through that whole region round about, and beganne to carrie about in beds, those that were sicke, where they heard he was.
mk.6.56	Mark 6:56	And whithersouer he entred, into villages, or cities, or countrie, they laide the sicke in the streetes, & besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him, were made whole.
mk.7.1	Mark 7:1	Then came together vnto him the Pharises, and certain of the Scribes, which came from Hierusalem.
mk.7.2	Mark 7:2	And when they saw some of his disciples eate bread with defiled (that is to say, with vnwashen) hands, they found fault.
mk.7.3	Mark 7:3	For the Pharises and all the Iewes, except they wash their hands oft, eate not, holding the tradition of the elders.
mk.7.4	Mark 7:4	And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eate not. And many other things there be, which they haue receiued to hold, as the washing of cups and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
mk.7.5	Mark 7:5	Then the Pharises and Scribes asked him, Why walke not thy disciples according to the tradition of the Elders, but eate bread with vnwashen hands?
mk.7.6	Mark 7:6	He answered and said vnto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you Hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth mee with their lips, but their heart is farre from me.
mk.7.7	Mark 7:7	Howbeit in vaine doe they worship me, teaching for doctrines, the commandements of men.
mk.7.8	Mark 7:8	For laying aside the Commandement of God, yee hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots, and cups: and many other such like things ye doe.
mk.7.9	Mark 7:9	And he said vnto them, Full well ye reiect the Commandement of God, that ye may keepe your owne tradition.
mk.7.10	Mark 7:10	For Moses said, Honour thy father & thy mother: and who so curseth father or mother, let him die the death.
mk.7.11	Mark 7:11	But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoeuer thou mightest be profited by me: he shalbe free.
mk.7.12	Mark 7:12	And ye suffer him no more to doe ought for his father, or his mother:
mk.7.13	Mark 7:13	Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye haue deliuered: And many such like things doe ye.
mk.7.14	Mark 7:14	¶ And when he had called all the people vnto him, hee said vnto them, Hearken vnto me euery one of you, and vnderstand.
mk.7.15	Mark 7:15	There is nothing from without a man that entring into him, can defile him: but the things which come out of of him, those are they that defile the man.
mk.7.16	Mark 7:16	If any man haue eares to heare, let him heare.
mk.7.17	Mark 7:17	And when hee was entred into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
mk.7.18	Mark 7:18	And he saith vnto them, Are ye so without vnderstanding also? Doe yee not perceiue that whatsoeuer thing from without entreth into the man, it cannot defile him,
mk.7.19	Mark 7:19	Because it entreth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
mk.7.20	Mark 7:20	And he said, That which commeth out of the man, that defileth the man.
mk.7.21	Mark 7:21	For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed euill thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
mk.7.22	Mark 7:22	Thefts, couetousnesse, wickednesse, deceit, lasciuiousnesse, an euill eye, blasphemie, pride, foolishnesse:
mk.7.23	Mark 7:23	All these euill things come from within, and defile the man.
mk.7.24	Mark 7:24	¶ And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entred into an house, and would haue no man know it, but hee could not be hid.
mk.7.25	Mark 7:25	For a certaine woman, whose yong daughter had an vncleane spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feete.
mk.7.26	Mark 7:26	(The woman was a Greek: a Syrophenician by nation:) and she besought him that he would cast forth the deuill out of her daughter.
mk.7.27	Mark 7:27	But Iesus said vnto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the childrens bread, and to cast it vnto the dogges.
mk.7.28	Mark 7:28	And she answered and said vnto him, Yes Lord, yet the dogges vnder the table eat of the childrens crummes.
mk.7.29	Mark 7:29	And hee said vnto her, For this saying, goe thy way, the deuill is gone out of thy daughter.
mk.7.30	Mark 7:30	And when shee was come to her house, she found the deuill gone out, and her daughter laied vpon the bed.
mk.7.31	Mark 7:31	¶ And againe departing from the coastes of Tyre and Sidon, he came vnto the sea of Galilee, thorow the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
mk.7.32	Mark 7:32	And they bring vnto him one that was deafe, and had an impediment in his speech: and they beseech him to put his hand vpon him.
mk.7.33	Mark 7:33	And he tooke him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his eares, and he spit, and touched his tongue,
mk.7.34	Mark 7:34	And looking vp to heauen, hee sighed, and saith vnto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
mk.7.35	Mark 7:35	And straightway his eares were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plaine.
mk.7.36	Mark 7:36	And hee charged them that they should tell no man: but the more hee charged them, so much the more a great deale they published it,
mk.7.37	Mark 7:37	And were beyond measure astonished, saying, Hee hath done all things well: hee maketh both the deafe to heare, and the dumbe to speake.
mk.8.1	Mark 8:1	In those dayes the multitude being very great, and hauing nothing to eat. Iesus called his disciples vnto him, & saith vnto them,
mk.8.2	Mark 8:2	I haue compassion on the multitude, because they haue now bene with me three daies, and haue nothing to eat:
mk.8.3	Mark 8:3	And if I send them away fasting to their owne houses, they will faint by the way: for diuers of them came from farre.
mk.8.4	Mark 8:4	And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfie these men with bread here in the wildernes?
mk.8.5	Mark 8:5	And hee asked them, How many loaues haue ye? And they said, Seuen.
mk.8.6	Mark 8:6	And he commanded the people to sit downe on the ground: and he tooke the seuen loaues, and gaue thanks, and brake, and gaue to his disciples to set before them: and they did set them before the people.
mk.8.7	Mark 8:7	And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commaunded to set them also before them.
mk.8.8	Mark 8:8	So they did eate, and were filled: and they tooke vp, of the broken meate that was left, seuen baskets.
mk.8.9	Mark 8:9	And they that had eaten were about foure thousand, and he sent them away.
mk.8.10	Mark 8:10	¶ And straightway he entred into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
mk.8.11	Mark 8:11	And the Pharisees came foorth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a signe from heauen, tempting him.
mk.8.12	Mark 8:12	And he sighed deepely in his spirit, and saith, Why doeth this generation seeke after a signe? Uerely I say vnto you, There shall no signe be giuen vnto this generation.
mk.8.13	Mark 8:13	And he left them, & entring into the ship againe, departed to the other side.
mk.8.14	Mark 8:14	¶ Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more then one loafe.
mk.8.15	Mark 8:15	And hee charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leauen of the Pharisees, and of the leauen of Herode.
mk.8.16	Mark 8:16	And they reasoned among themselues, saying, It is, because we haue no bread.
mk.8.17	Mark 8:17	And when Iesus knew it, he saith vnto them, Why reason ye, because yee haue no bread? Perceiue ye not yet, neither vnderstand? Haue yee your heart yet hardened?
mk.8.18	Mark 8:18	Hauing eyes, see ye not? and hauing eares heare ye not? And doe ye not remember?
mk.8.19	Mark 8:19	When I brake the fiue loaues among fiue thousand, how many baskets full of fragments tooke yee vp? They say vnto him, Twelue.
mk.8.20	Mark 8:20	And when the seuen among foure thousand: how many baskets full of fragments tooke ye vp? And they said, Seuen.
mk.8.21	Mark 8:21	And he said vnto them, How is it that ye doe not vnderstand?
mk.8.22	Mark 8:22	¶ And he commeth to Bethsaida, and they bring a blind man vnto him, and besought him to touch him:
mk.8.23	Mark 8:23	And he tooke the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the towne, and when he had spit on his eyes, & put his hands vpon him, he asked him, if hee saw ought.
mk.8.24	Mark 8:24	And he looked vp, and saide, I see men as trees, walking.
mk.8.25	Mark 8:25	After that hee put his handes againe vpon his eies, and made him look vp: and he was restored, and saw euery man clearely.
mk.8.26	Mark 8:26	And hee sent him away to his house, saying, Neither goe into the towne, nor tell it to any in the towne.
mk.8.27	Mark 8:27	¶ And Iesus went out, and his disciples, into the townes of Cesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying vnto them, Whom doe men say that I am?
mk.8.28	Mark 8:28	And they answered, Iohn the Baptist: but some say, Elias: & others, one of the Prophets.
mk.8.29	Mark 8:29	And hee saith vnto them, But whom say yee that I am? And Peter answereth and saith vnto him, Thou art the Christ.
mk.8.30	Mark 8:30	And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
mk.8.31	Mark 8:31	And hee beganne to teach them, that the Sonne of man must suffer many things, and be reiected of the Elders, and of the chiefe Priests, & Scribes, and be killed, & after three dayes rise againe.

mk.8.33	Mark 8:33	But when he had turned about, and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou sauourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.
mk.8.34	Mark 8:34	¶ And when he had called the people vnto him, with his disciples also, he said vnto them, Whosoeuer will come after me, let him denie himselfe, and take vp his crosse and follow mee.
mk.8.35	Mark 8:35	For whosoeuer will saue his life shall lose it, but whosoeuer shall lose his life for my sake and the Gospels, the same shall saue it.
mk.8.36	Mark 8:36	For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gaine the whole world, and lose his owne soule?
mk.8.37	Mark 8:37	Or what shall a man giue in exchange for his soule?
mk.8.38	Mark 8:38	Whosoeuer therefore shall be ashamed of me, and of my words, in this adulterous and sinfull generation, of him also shall the Sonne of man bee ashamed, when he commeth in the glory of his Father, with the holy Angels.
mk.9.1	Mark 9:1	And hee said vnto them, Uerely I say vnto you, that there be some of them that stand here, which shal not taste of death, till they haue seene the kingdome of God come with power.

mk.9.32	Mark 9:32	But they vnderstood not that saying, and were afraid to aske him.
mk.9.33	Mark 9:33	¶ And he came to Capernaum; and being in the house, he asked them, What was it that yee disputed among your selues by the way?
mk.9.34	Mark 9:34	But they held their peace: For by the way they had disputed among themselues, who should be the greatest.
mk.9.35	Mark 9:35	And he sate downe, and called the twelue, and saith vnto them, If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and seruant of all.
mk.9.36	Mark 9:36	And he tooke a child, and set him in the midst of them: & when he had taken him in his arms, he said vnto them,
mk.9.37	Mark 9:37	Whosoeuer shall receiue one of such children in my Name, receiueth me: and whosoeuer shall receiue me, receiueth not me, but him that sent me.
mk.9.38	Mark 9:38	¶ And Iohn answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out deuils in thy Name, and he followeth not vs, and we forbade him, because he followeth not vs.
mk.9.39	Mark 9:39	But Iesus said, Forbid him not, for there is no man, which shall doe a miracle in my Name, that can lightly speake euill of me.
mk.9.40	Mark 9:40	For he that is not against vs, is on our part.
mk.9.41	Mark 9:41	For whosoeuer shall giue you a cup of water to drinke in my Name, because yee belong to Christ: Uerily I say vnto you, he shall not lose his reward.
mk.9.42	Mark 9:42	And whosoeuer shall offend one of these litle ones that beleeue in me, it is better for him, that a milstone were hanged about his necke, and he were cast into the Sea.
mk.9.43	Mark 9:43	And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: It is better for thee to enter into life maimed, then hauing two hands, to goe into hell, into the fire that neuer shall be quenched:
mk.9.44	Mark 9:44	Where their worme dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
mk.9.45	Mark 9:45	And if thy foote offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, then hauing two feete, to be cast into hell, into the fire that neuer shall be quenched:
mk.9.46	Mark 9:46	Where their worme dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
mk.9.47	Mark 9:47	And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, then hauing two eyes, to be cast into helfire:
mk.9.48	Mark 9:48	Where their worme dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
mk.9.49	Mark 9:49	For euery one shall be salted with fire, and euery sacrifice shall be salted with salt.
mk.9.50	Mark 9:50	Salt is good: but if the salt haue lost his saltnesse, wherewith will you season it? Haue salt in your selues, and haue peace one with another.
mk.10.1	Mark 10:1	And he rose from thence, & commeth into the coasts of Iudea by the farther side of Iordan: and the people resort vnto him againe, and as he was wont, he taught them againe.
mk.10.2	Mark 10:2	¶ And the Pharises came to him, and asked him, Is it lawfull for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.
mk.10.3	Mark 10:3	And he answered, and saide vnto them, What did Moses command you?
mk.10.4	Mark 10:4	And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of diuorcement, and to put her away.

mk.10.7	Mark 10:7	For this cause shall a man leaue his father and mother, and cleaue to his wife,
mk.10.8	Mark 10:8	And they twaine shalbe one flesh: so then they are no more twaine, but one flesh.
mk.10.9	Mark 10:9	What therefore God hath ioyned together, let not man put asunder.

mk.10.11	Mark 10:11	And he saith vnto them, Whosoeuer shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.
mk.10.12	Mark 10:12	And if a woman shall put away her husband, and bee married to another, she committeth adulterie.

mk.10.14	Mark 10:14	But when Iesus saw it, hee was much displeased, and said vnto them, Suffer the little children to come vnto mee, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdome of God.
mk.10.15	Mark 10:15	Uerily I say vnto you, Whosoeuer shall not receiue the kingdome of God as a little childe, he shall not enter therein.
mk.10.16	Mark 10:16	And hee tooke them vp in his armes, put his handes vpon them, and blessed them.
mk.10.17	Mark 10:17	¶ And when he was gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good master, what shall I doe that I may inherit eternall life?
mk.10.18	Mark 10:18	And Iesus said vnto him, Why callest thou me good? There is no man good, but one, that is God.
mk.10.19	Mark 10:19	Thou knowest the Commandements, Doe not commit adulterie, Doe not kill, Doe not steale, Doe not beare false witnesse, Defraud not, Honour thy father, and mother.
mk.10.20	Mark 10:20	And hee answered, and saide vnto him, Master, all these haue I obserued from my youth.
mk.10.21	Mark 10:21	Then Iesus beholding him, loued him, and said vnto him, One thing thou lackest; Goe thy way, sell whatsoeuer thou hast, and giue to the poore, and thou shalt haue treasure in heauen, and come, take vp the crosse & folow me.
mk.10.22	Mark 10:22	And hee was sad at that saying, and went away grieued: for hee had great possessions.
mk.10.23	Mark 10:23	¶ And Iesus looked round about, and saith vnto his disciples, How hardly shall they that haue riches enter into the kingdome of God?
mk.10.24	Mark 10:24	And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Iesus answereth againe, and saith vnto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches, to enter into the kingdom of God?
mk.10.25	Mark 10:25	It is easier for a camel to goe thorow the eye of a needle, then for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
mk.10.26	Mark 10:26	And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselues, Who then can be saued?
mk.10.27	Mark 10:27	And Iesus looking vpon them, saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.
mk.10.28	Mark 10:28	¶ Then Peter began to say vnto him, Loe, we haue left all, and haue followed thee.
mk.10.29	Mark 10:29	And Iesus answered, and said, Uerily I say vnto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the Gospels,
mk.10.30	Mark 10:30	But hee shall receiue an hundred fold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternall life:
mk.10.31	Mark 10:31	But many that are first, shall be last: and the last, first.
mk.10.32	Mark 10:32	¶ And they were in the way going vp to Hierusalem: and Iesus went before them, and they were amazed, and as they followed, they were afraid: and he tooke againe the twelue, and began to tell them what things should happen vnto him,
mk.10.33	Mark 10:33	Saying, Behold, we go vp to Hierusalem, and the Sonne of man shall be deliuered vnto the chiefe Priests, and vnto the Scribes: and they shall condemne him to death, and shall deliuer him to the Gentiles.
mk.10.34	Mark 10:34	And they shall mocke him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit vpon him, and shall kill him, and the third day he shall rise againe.
mk.10.35	Mark 10:35	¶ And Iames, and Iohn the sonnes of Zebedee come vnto him, saying, Master, we would þ thou shouldest do for vs whatsoeuer we shall desire.
mk.10.36	Mark 10:36	And hee saide vnto them, What would ye that I should doe for you?
mk.10.37	Mark 10:37	They said vnto him, Grant vnto vs that wee may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory.
mk.10.38	Mark 10:38	But Iesus said vnto them, Yee know not what ye aske: Can ye drinke of the cup that I drinke of? and be baptized with the baptisme that I am baptized with?
mk.10.39	Mark 10:39	And they said vnto him, Wee can. And Iesus said vnto them, Ye shall indeed drinke of the cup that I drinke of: and with the baptisme that I am baptized withall, shall ye be baptized:
mk.10.40	Mark 10:40	But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand, is not mine to giue, but it shall be giuen to them for whom it is prepared.
mk.10.41	Mark 10:41	And when the ten heard it, they beganne to bee much displeased with Iames and Iohn.
mk.10.42	Mark 10:42	But Iesus called them to him, and saith vnto them, Yee know that they which are accompted to rule ouer the Gentiles, exercise Lordship ouer them: and their great ones exercise authoritie vpon them.
mk.10.43	Mark 10:43	But so shall it not be among you: but whosoeuer will bee great among you, shall be your minister:
mk.10.44	Mark 10:44	And whosoeuer of you will bee the chiefest, shalbe seruant of all.
mk.10.45	Mark 10:45	For euen the Sonne of man came not to bee ministred vnto, but to minister, and to giue his life a ransome for many.
mk.10.46	Mark 10:46	¶ And they came to Iericho: and as he went out of Iericho with his disciples, and a great number of people; blinde Bartimeus, the son of Timeus, sate by the high wayes side, begging.
mk.10.47	Mark 10:47	And when he heard that it was Iesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Iesus thou Sonne of Dauid, haue mercie on me.
mk.10.48	Mark 10:48	And many charged him, that he should hold his peace: But he cried the more a great deale, Thou Sonne of Dauid, haue mercy on me.
mk.10.49	Mark 10:49	And Iesus stood still, and commanded him to bee called: and they call the blinde man, saying vnto him, Be of good comfort, rise, he calleth thee.
mk.10.50	Mark 10:50	And hee casting away his garment, rose, and came to Iesus.
mk.10.51	Mark 10:51	And Iesus answered, and said vnto him, What wilt thou that I should doe vnto thee? The blinde man said vnto him, Lord, that I might receiue my sight.
mk.10.52	Mark 10:52	And Iesus saide vnto him, Goe thy way, thy faith hath made thee whole: And immediatly hee receiued his sight, & followed Iesus in the way.
mk.11.1	Mark 11:1	And when they came nigh to Hierusalem, vnto Bethphage, and Bethanie, at the mount of Oliues, hee sendeth foorth two of his disciples,

mk.11.13	Mark 11:13	And seeing a figtree a farre off, hauing leaues, hee came, if haply hee might find any thing thereon, & when he came to it, hee found nothing but leaues: for the time of figs was not yet.

mk.11.19	Mark 11:19	And when Euen was come, Hee went out of the citie.
mk.11.20	Mark 11:20	¶ And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried vp from the roots.

mk.11.24	Mark 11:24	Therfore I say vnto you, What things soeuer ye desire when ye pray, beleeue that ye receiue them, and ye shall haue them.

mk.11.26	Mark 11:26	But if you doe not forgiue, neither will your Father which is in heauen, forgiue your trespasses.

mk.11.32	Mark 11:32	But if we shall say, Of men, they feared the people: for all men counted Iohn, that he was a Prophet indeed.
mk.11.33	Mark 11:33	And they answered and said vnto Iesus, We cannot tell. And Iesus answering, saith vnto them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I doe these things.
mk.12.1	Mark 12:1	And hee began to speake vnto them by parables. A certaine man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the wine fat, and built a towre, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a farre countrey.
mk.12.2	Mark 12:2	And at the season, he sent to the husbandmen a seruant, that he might receiue from the husbandmen of the fruite of the vineyard.
mk.12.3	Mark 12:3	And they caught him, and beat him, and sent him away emptie.
mk.12.4	Mark 12:4	And againe, hee sent vnto them another seruant; and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.
mk.12.5	Mark 12:5	And againe, he sent another, and him they killed: and many others, beating some, and killing some.
mk.12.6	Mark 12:6	Hauing yet therefore one sonne his welbeloued, he sent him also last vnto them, saying, They will reuerence my sonne.
mk.12.7	Mark 12:7	But those husbandmen said amongst themselues, This is the heire, come, let vs kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.
mk.12.8	Mark 12:8	And they tooke him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
mk.12.9	Mark 12:9	What shall therefore the Lord of the vineyard doe? He will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will giue the vineyard vnto others.
mk.12.10	Mark 12:10	And haue ye not read this Scripture? The stone which the builders reiected, is become the head of the corner:
mk.12.11	Mark 12:11	This was the Lords doing, and it is maruellous in our eies.
mk.12.12	Mark 12:12	And they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people, for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way.
mk.12.13	Mark 12:13	¶ And they send vnto him certaine of the Pharises, and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.
mk.12.14	Mark 12:14	And when they were come, they say vnto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth. Is it lawfull to giue tribute to Cesar, or not?
mk.12.15	Mark 12:15	Shall we giue, or shall we not giue? But he knowing their hypocrisie, said vnto them, Why tempt yee mee? Bring me a penny that I may see it.
mk.12.16	Mark 12:16	And they brought it: and he saith vnto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said vnto him, Cesars.
mk.12.17	Mark 12:17	And Iesus answering, said vnto them, Render to Cesar the things that are Cesars: and to God the things that are Gods. And they maruailed at him.
mk.12.18	Mark 12:18	¶ Then come vnto him the Sadducees, which say there is no resurrection, and they asked him, saying,
mk.12.19	Mark 12:19	Master, Moses wrote vnto vs, If a mans brother die, and leaue his wife behind him, and leaue no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise vp seed vnto his brother.
mk.12.20	Mark 12:20	Now there were seuen brethren: and the first tooke a wife, and dying left no seede.
mk.12.21	Mark 12:21	And the second tooke her, and died, neither left he any seed, and the third likewise.
mk.12.22	Mark 12:22	And the seuen had her, and left no seede: last of all the woman died also.
mk.12.23	Mark 12:23	In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? for the seuen had her to wife.
mk.12.24	Mark 12:24	And Iesus answering, said vnto them, Doe ye not therefore erre, because yee know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?
mk.12.25	Mark 12:25	For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are giuen in marriage: but are as the Angels which are in heauen.
mk.12.26	Mark 12:26	And as touching the dead, that they rise: haue ye not read in the booke of Moses, how in the bush God spake vnto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isahac, and the God of Iacob?
mk.12.27	Mark 12:27	Hee is not the God of the dead, but the God of the liuing: yee therefore doe greatly erre.
mk.12.28	Mark 12:28	¶ And one of the Scribes came, and hauing heard them reasoning together, and perceiuing that he had answered them well, asked him which is the first commandement of all.
mk.12.29	Mark 12:29	And Iesus answered him, The first of al the commandements is, Heare, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord:

mk.12.31	Mark 12:31	And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt loue thy neighbour as thy selfe: there is none other commandement greater then these.

mk.12.33	Mark 12:33	And to loue him with all the heart, and with all the vnderstanding, and with all the soule, and with all the strength, and to loue his neighbour as himselfe, is more then all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

mk.12.37	Mark 12:37	Dauid therefore himselfe calleth him Lord, and whence is hee then his sonne? And the common people heard him gladly.

mk.12.43	Mark 12:43	And he called vnto him his disciples, and saith vnto them, Uerily I say vnto you, that this poore widow hath cast more in, then all they which haue cast into the treasurie.
mk.12.44	Mark 12:44	For all they did cast in of their aboundance: but she of her want, did cast in all that she had, euen all her liuing.
mk.13.1	Mark 13:1	And as he went out of the Temple, one of his disciples saith vnto him, Master, see what maner of stones, and what buildings are here.

mk.13.5	Mark 13:5	And Iesus answering them, began to say, Take heed lest any man deceiue you.

mk.13.9	Mark 13:9	¶ But take heed to your selues: for they shall deliuer you vp to councels, and in the Synagogues ye shall be beaten, and ye shalbe brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.
mk.13.10	Mark 13:10	And the Gospel must first be published among all nations.
mk.13.11	Mark 13:11	But when they shall lead you, and deliuer you vp, take no thought before hand what ye shall speake, neither doe yee premeditate: but whatsoeuer shall bee giuen you in that houre, that speake yee: for it is not yee that speake, but the holy Ghost.
