mk.13.14	Mark 13:14	¶ But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing where it ought not (let him that readeth vnderstand) then let them that be in Iudea, flee to the mountaines:
mk.13.15	Mark 13:15	And let him that is on the house top, not goe downe into the house, neither enter therin, to take any thing out of his house.
mk.13.16	Mark 13:16	And let him that is in the field, not turne backe againe for to take vp his garment.
mk.13.17	Mark 13:17	But woe to them that are with child, and to them that giue suck in those dayes.
mk.13.18	Mark 13:18	And pray ye that your flight bee not in the winter.
mk.13.19	Mark 13:19	For in those dayes shall be affliction, such as was not from the beginning of the creation which God created, vnto this time, neither shall be.
mk.13.20	Mark 13:20	And except that the Lord had shortened those dayes, no flesh should be saued: but for the elects sake whome he hath chosen, he hath shortned the daies.
mk.13.21	Mark 13:21	And then, if any man shall say to you, Loe, here is Christ, or loe, hee is there: beleeue him not.
mk.13.22	Mark 13:22	For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shewe signes and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, euen the elect.
mk.13.23	Mark 13:23	But take ye heed: behold, I haue foretold you all things.
mk.13.24	Mark 13:24	¶ But in those dayes, after that tribulation, the Sunne shalbe darkned, and the Moone shall not giue her light.
mk.13.25	Mark 13:25	And the Starres of heauen shall fall, and the powers that are in heauen shall be shaken.
mk.13.26	Mark 13:26	And then shal they see the Sonne of man comming in the cloudes, with great power and glory.
mk.13.27	Mark 13:27	And then shal he send his Angels, and shall gather together his elect from the foure winds, from the vttermost part of the earth, to the vttermost part of heauen.
mk.13.28	Mark 13:28	Now learne a parable of the fig tree. When her branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaues, ye know that summer is neere:
mk.13.29	Mark 13:29	So ye in like maner, when ye shal see these things come to passe, knowe that it is nigh, euen at the doores.
mk.13.30	Mark 13:30	Uerely I say vnto you, that this generation shall not passe, till all these things be done.
mk.13.31	Mark 13:31	Heauen and earth shal passe away: but my words shall not passe away.
mk.13.32	Mark 13:32	¶ But of that day and that houre knoweth no man, no not the Angels which are in heauen, neither the Son, but the Father.
mk.13.33	Mark 13:33	Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.
mk.13.34	Mark 13:34	For the Sonne of man is as a man taking a farre iourney, who left his house, and gaue authority to his seruants, and to euery man his worke, and commanded the porter to watch:
mk.13.35	Mark 13:35	Watch ye therefore (for ye knowe not when the master of the house commeth, at Euen, or at midnight, or at the cocke crowing, or in the morning.)
mk.13.36	Mark 13:36	Lest comming suddenly, he finde you sleeping.
mk.13.37	Mark 13:37	And what I say vnto you, I say vnto all, Watch.
mk.14.1	Mark 14:1	After two dayes was the feast of the Passeouer, and of vnleauened bread: and the chiefe Priests, and the Scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
mk.14.2	Mark 14:2	But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an vprore of the people.
mk.14.3	Mark 14:3	¶ And being in Bethanie, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sate at meat, there came a woman, hauing an Alabaster boxe of oyntment of spikenard very precious, and shee brake the boxe, and powred it on his head.
mk.14.4	Mark 14:4	And there were some that had indignation within themselues, and said, Why was this waste of the oyntment made?
mk.14.5	Mark 14:5	For it might haue bene solde for more then three hundred pence, and haue bene giuen to the poore: and they murmured against her.
mk.14.6	Mark 14:6	And Iesus said, Let her alone, why trouble you her? Shee hath wrought a good worke on me.
mk.14.7	Mark 14:7	For ye haue the poore with you alwayes, and whensoeuer ye will yee may doe them good: but me ye haue not alwayes.
mk.14.8	Mark 14:8	She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.
mk.14.9	Mark 14:9	Uerely I say vnto you, Wheresoeuer this Gospel shalbe preached thorowout the whole world, this also that she hath done, shall be spoken of for a memoriall of her.
mk.14.10	Mark 14:10	¶ And Iudas Iscariot, one of the twelue, went vnto the chiefe Priests, to betray him vnto them.
mk.14.11	Mark 14:11	And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to giue him money. And he sought how he might conueniently betray him.
mk.14.12	Mark 14:12	¶ And the first day of vnleauened bread, when they killed the Passeouer, his disciples said vnto him, Where wilt thou that we goe, and prepare, that thou mayest eate the Passeouer?
mk.14.13	Mark 14:13	And he sendeth forth two of his disciples, and saith vnto them, Goe yee into the citie, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.
mk.14.14	Mark 14:14	And wheresoeuer he shall goe in, say yee to the good man of the house, The Master saith, Where is the guest chamber, where I shall eate the Passeouer with my disciples?
mk.14.15	Mark 14:15	And he will shew you a large vpper roome furnished, and prepared: there make ready for vs.
mk.14.16	Mark 14:16	And his disciples went forth, and came into the citie, and found as hee had said vnto them: and they made readie the Passeouer.
mk.14.17	Mark 14:17	And in the euening hee commeth with the twelue.
mk.14.18	Mark 14:18	And as they sate, and did eat, Iesus said, Uerily I say vnto you, one of you which eateth with me, shall betray mee.
mk.14.19	Mark 14:19	And they began to be sorowfull, and to say vnto him, one by one, Is it I? And another said, Is it I?
mk.14.20	Mark 14:20	And he answered, and saide vnto them, It is one of the twelue, that dippeth with me in the dish.
mk.14.21	Mark 14:21	The sonne of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Sonne of man is betrayed: Good were it for that man, if he had neuer bene borne.
mk.14.22	Mark 14:22	¶ And as they did eate, Iesus tooke bread, and blessed, and brake it, and gaue to them, and said, Take, eate: this is my body.
mk.14.23	Mark 14:23	And he tooke the cup, and when he had giuen thanks, he gaue it to them: and they all dranke of it.
mk.14.24	Mark 14:24	And he said vnto them, This is my blood of the new Testament, which is shed for many.
mk.14.25	Mark 14:25	Uerely I say vnto you, I will drinke no more of the fruit of the Uine, vntill that day that I drinke it new in the kingdome of God.
mk.14.26	Mark 14:26	¶ And when they had sung an hymne, they went out into the mount of Oliues.
mk.14.27	Mark 14:27	And Iesus saith vnto them, All ye shall be offended because of mee this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepheard, and the sheepe shall be scattered.
mk.14.28	Mark 14:28	But after that I am risen, I will goe before you into Galilee.
mk.14.29	Mark 14:29	But Peter said vnto him, Although al shalbe offended, yet wil not I.
mk.14.30	Mark 14:30	And Iesus saith vnto him, Uerily I say vnto thee, that this day, euen in this night before the cocke crow twise, thou shalt denie me thrise.
mk.14.31	Mark 14:31	But he spake the more vehemently, If I should die with thee, I will not denie thee in any wise. Likewise also said they all.
mk.14.32	Mark 14:32	And they came to a place which was named Gethsemani, and hee saith to his disciples, Sit yee here, while I shall pray.
mk.14.33	Mark 14:33	And hee taketh with him Peter, and Iames, and Iohn, and began to be sore amazed, and to be very heauy,
mk.14.34	Mark 14:34	And saith vnto them, My soule is exceeding sorowful vnto death: tarie ye here, and watch.
mk.14.35	Mark 14:35	And he went forward a litle, and fell on the ground, and prayed, that if it were possible, the houre might passe from him.
mk.14.36	Mark 14:36	And he said, Abba, father, all things are possible vnto thee, take away this cup from me: Neuerthelesse, not that I will, but what thou wilt.
mk.14.37	Mark 14:37	And hee commeth, and findeth them sleeping, and saith vnto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? Couldest not thou watch one houre?
mk.14.38	Mark 14:38	Watch ye and pray, lest yee enter into temptation: The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weake.
mk.14.39	Mark 14:39	And againe he went away, and prayed, and spake the same words.
mk.14.40	Mark 14:40	And when he returned, he found them asleepe againe, (for their eies were heauie) neither wist they what to answere him.
mk.14.41	Mark 14:41	And he commeth the third time, and saith vnto them, Sleepe on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the houre is come, behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
mk.14.42	Mark 14:42	Rise vp, let vs goe, Loe, he that betrayeth me, is at hand.
mk.14.43	Mark 14:43	¶ And immediately, while hee yet spake, commeth Iudas, one of the twelue, and with him a great multitude with swords, and staues, from the chiefe Priests, and the Scribes, & the Elders.
mk.14.44	Mark 14:44	And he that betrayed him, had giuen them a token, saying, Whomsoeuer I shall kisse, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.
mk.14.45	Mark 14:45	And assoone as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and sayeth, Master, Master, and kissed him.
mk.14.46	Mark 14:46	¶ And they layed their hands on him, and tooke him.
mk.14.47	Mark 14:47	And one of them that stood by, drew a sword, and smote a seruant of the high Priest, and cut off his eare.
mk.14.48	Mark 14:48	And Iesus answered, & said vnto thē, Are ye come out as against a theefe, with swords, & with staues to take me?
mk.14.49	Mark 14:49	I was daily with you in the Temple, teaching, and yee tooke me not; but the Scriptures must be fulfilled.
mk.14.50	Mark 14:50	And they all forsooke him, & fled.
mk.14.51	Mark 14:51	And there followed him a certaine yong man, hauing a linnen cloth cast about his naked body, and the yong men laid hold on him.
mk.14.52	Mark 14:52	And he left the linnen cloth, and fled from them naked.
mk.14.53	Mark 14:53	¶ And they led Iesus away to the high Priest, and with him were assembled all the chiefe Priests, and the Elders, and the Scribes.
mk.14.54	Mark 14:54	And Peter followed him a farre off, euen into the pallace of the high Priest: and he sate with the seruants, and warmed himselfe at the fire.
mk.14.55	Mark 14:55	And the chiefe Priests, and all the counsell sought for witnesse against Iesus, to put him to death, & found none.
mk.14.56	Mark 14:56	For many bare false witnesse against him, but their witnesse agreed not together.
mk.14.57	Mark 14:57	And there arose certaine, and bare false witnesse against him, saying,
mk.14.58	Mark 14:58	We heard him say, I will destroy this Temple that is made with hands, and within three dayes I will build another made without hands.
mk.14.59	Mark 14:59	But neither so did their witnesse agree together.
mk.14.60	Mark 14:60	And the high Priest stood vp in the mids, and asked Iesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? What is it which these witnesse against thee?
mk.14.61	Mark 14:61	But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Againe, the high Priest asked him, and said vnto him, Art thou the Christ, the sonne of the Blessed?
mk.14.62	Mark 14:62	And Iesus said, I am: and yee shall see the sonne of man sitting on the right hand of power, and comming in the clouds of heauen.
mk.14.63	Mark 14:63	Then the high Priest rent his clothes, and saith, What neede we any further witnesses?
mk.14.64	Mark 14:64	Yee haue heard the blasphemy: what thinke yee? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.
mk.14.65	Mark 14:65	And some beganne to spit on him, and to couer his face, and to buffet him, and to say vnto him, Prophecie: And the seruants did stricke him with the palmes of their hands.
mk.14.66	Mark 14:66	¶ And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there commeth one of the maides of the high Priest.
mk.14.67	Mark 14:67	And when she saw Peter warning himselfe, she looked vpon him, and said, And thou also wast with Iesus of Nazareth.
mk.14.68	Mark 14:68	But hee denied, saying, I know not, neither vnderstand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch, and the cocke crew.
mk.14.69	Mark 14:69	And a maide saw him againe, and beganne to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
mk.14.70	Mark 14:70	And he denied it againe. And a little after, they that stood by said againe to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speach agreeth thereto.
mk.14.71	Mark 14:71	But he beganne to curse and to sweare, saying, I know not this man of whom yee speake.
mk.14.72	Mark 14:72	And the second time the cocke crew: and Peter called to minde the word that Iesus said vnto him, Before the cockecrow twise, thou shalt denie me thrise. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
mk.15.1	Mark 15:1	And straightway in the morning the chiefe Priests helde a consultation with the Elders and Scribes, and the whole Councell, and bound Iesus, and caried him away, and deliuered him to Pilate.
mk.15.2	Mark 15:2	And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Iewes? And hee answering, said vnto him, Thou sayest it.
mk.15.3	Mark 15:3	And the chiefe Priests accused him of many things: but hee answered nothing.
mk.15.4	Mark 15:4	And Pilate asked him againe, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they witnesse against thee.
mk.15.5	Mark 15:5	But Iesus yet answered nothing, so that Pilate marueiled.
mk.15.6	Mark 15:6	Now at that Feast he released vnto them one prisoner, whomsoeuer they desired.
mk.15.7	Mark 15:7	And there was one named Barabbas, which lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.
mk.15.8	Mark 15:8	And the multitude crying alowd, began to desire him to doe as he had euer done vnto them.
mk.15.9	Mark 15:9	But Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release vnto you the King of the Iewes?
mk.15.10	Mark 15:10	(For hee knew that the chiefe Priests had deliuered him for enuie.)
mk.15.11	Mark 15:11	But the chiefe Priests mooued the people, that hee should rather release Barabbas vnto them.
mk.15.12	Mark 15:12	And Pilate answered, and said againe vnto them, What will yee then that I shall do vnto him whom ye call the King of the Iewes?
mk.15.13	Mark 15:13	And they cried out againe, Crucifie him.
mk.15.14	Mark 15:14	Then Pilate saide vnto them, Why, what euill hath hee done? And they cried out the more exceedingly, Crucifie him.
mk.15.15	Mark 15:15	¶ And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas vnto them, and deliuered Iesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.
mk.15.16	Mark 15:16	And the souldiers led him away into the hall, called Pretorium, and they call together the whole band.
mk.15.17	Mark 15:17	And they clothed him with purple, and platted a crowne of thornes, and put it about his head,
mk.15.18	Mark 15:18	And beganne to salute him, Haile King of the Iewes.
mk.15.19	Mark 15:19	And they smote him on the head with a reed, and did spit vpon him, and bowing their knees, worshipped him.
mk.15.20	Mark 15:20	And when they had mocked him, they tooke off the purple from him, and put his owne clothes on him, and led him out to crucifie him.
mk.15.21	Mark 15:21	And they compell one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, comming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to beare his Crosse.
mk.15.22	Mark 15:22	And they bring him vnto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, the place of a skull.
mk.15.23	Mark 15:23	And they gaue him to drinke, wine mingled with myrrhe: but he receiued it not.
mk.15.24	Mark 15:24	And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots vpon them, what euery man should take.
mk.15.25	Mark 15:25	And it was the third houre, and they crucified him.
mk.15.26	Mark 15:26	And the superscription of his accusation was written ouer, THE KING OF THE IEWES.
mk.15.27	Mark 15:27	And with him they crucifie two theeues, the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
mk.15.28	Mark 15:28	And the Scripture was fulfilled, which sayeth, And hee was numbred with the transgressours.
mk.15.29	Mark 15:29	And they that passed by, railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah thou that destroyest the Temple, and buildest it in three dayes,
mk.15.30	Mark 15:30	Saue thy selfe, and come downe from the Crosse.
mk.15.31	Mark 15:31	Likewise also the chiefe Priests mocking, said among themselues with the Scribes, He saued others, himselfe he cannot saue.
mk.15.32	Mark 15:32	Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the Crosse, that we may see and beleeue: And they that were crucified with him, reuiled him.
mk.15.33	Mark 15:33	And when the sixth houre was come, there was darkenesse ouer the whole land, vntill the ninth houre.
mk.15.34	Mark 15:34	And at the ninth houre, Iesus cryed with a loude voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lamasabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
mk.15.35	Mark 15:35	And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elias.
mk.15.36	Mark 15:36	And one ranne, and filled a spunge full of vineger, and put it on a reed, and gaue him to drinke, saying, Let alone, let vs see whether Elias will come to take him downe.
mk.15.37	Mark 15:37	And Iesus cryed with a loude voice, and gaue vp the ghost.
mk.15.38	Mark 15:38	And the vaile of the Temple was rent in twaine, from the top to the bottome.
mk.15.39	Mark 15:39	¶ And when the Centurion which stood ouer against him, saw that hee so cryed out, and gaue vp the ghost, hee said, Truely this man was the Sonne of God.
mk.15.40	Mark 15:40	There were also women looking on afarre off, among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of Iames the lesse, and of Ioses, and Salome:
mk.15.41	Mark 15:41	Who also when hee was in Galile, followed him, and ministred vnto him, and many other women which came vp with him vnto Hierusalem.
mk.15.42	Mark 15:42	¶ And now when the euen was come, (because it was the Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath)
mk.15.43	Mark 15:43	Ioseph of Arimathea, an honourable counseller, which also waited for the kingdome of God, came, and went in boldly vnto Pilate, and craued the body of Iesus.
mk.15.44	Mark 15:44	And Pilate marueiled if he were already dead, and calling vnto him the Centurion, hee asked him whether hee had beene any while dead.
mk.15.45	Mark 15:45	And when he knew it of the Centurion, he gaue the body to Ioseph.
mk.15.46	Mark 15:46	And hee bought fine linnen, and tooke him downe, and wrapped him in the linnen, and laide him in a sepulchre, which was hewen out of a rocke, and rolled a stone vnto the doore of the sepulchre.
mk.15.47	Mark 15:47	And Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of Ioses behelde where he was laide.
mk.16.1	Mark 16:1	And when the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of Iames, and Salome, had bought sweete spices, that they might come and anoint him.
mk.16.2	Mark 16:2	And very early in the morning, the first day of the week they came vnto the sepulchre, at the rising of the sunne:
mk.16.3	Mark 16:3	And they said among themselues, who shall roll vs away the stone from the doore of the sepulchre?
mk.16.4	Mark 16:4	(And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away) for it was very great.
mk.16.5	Mark 16:5	And entring into the sepulchre, they sawe a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment, and they were affrighted.
mk.16.6	Mark 16:6	And hee sayth vnto them, Be not affrighted; ye seeke Iesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen, hee is not here: behold the place where they laide him.
mk.16.7	Mark 16:7	But goe your way, tell his disciples, and Peter, that hee goeth before you into Galile, there shall ye see him, as he said vnto you.
mk.16.8	Mark 16:8	And they went out quickely, and fledde from the sepulchre, for they trembled, and were amazed, neither sayd they any thing to any man, for they were afraid.
mk.16.9	Mark 16:9	¶ Now when Iesus was risen early, the first day of the weeke, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seuen deuils.
mk.16.10	Mark 16:10	And she went and told them that had beene with him, as they mourned and wept.
mk.16.11	Mark 16:11	And they, when they had heard that he was aliue, and had beene seene of her, beleeued not.
mk.16.12	Mark 16:12	¶ After that, he appeared in another forme vnto two of them, as they walked, and went into the countrey.
mk.16.13	Mark 16:13	And they went and tolde it vnto the residue, neither beleeued they them.
mk.16.14	Mark 16:14	¶ Afterward he appeared vnto the eleuen, as they sate at meat, and vpbraided them with their vnbeliefe, and hardnesse of heart, because they beleeued not them, which had seene him after he was risen.
mk.16.15	Mark 16:15	And he said vnto them, Goe yee into all the world, and preach the Gospel to euery creature.
mk.16.16	Mark 16:16	He that beleeueth and is baptized, shalbe saued, but he that beleeueth not, shall be damned.
mk.16.17	Mark 16:17	And these signes shal follow them that beleeue, In my Name shall they cast out deuils, they shall speake with new tongues,
mk.16.18	Mark 16:18	They shall take vp serpents, and if they drinke any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them, they shall lay hands on the sicke, and they shall recouer.
mk.16.19	Mark 16:19	¶ So then after the Lord had spoken vnto them, he was receiued vp into heauen, and sate on the right hand of God.
mk.16.20	Mark 16:20	And they went foorth, and preached euery where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the worde with signes following. Amen.
lk.1.1	Luke 1:1	Forasmuch as many haue taken in hande to set foorth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely beleeued among vs,
lk.1.2	Luke 1:2	Euen as they deliuered them vnto vs, which from the beginning were eye-witnesses, & ministers of the word:
lk.1.3	Luke 1:3	It seemed good to me also, hauing had perfect vnderstanding of things from the very first, to write vnto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus,
lk.1.4	Luke 1:4	That thou mightest know the certainetie of those things wherein thou hast bene instructed.
lk.1.5	Luke 1:5	¶ There was in the dayes of Herode the king of Iudea, a certaine Priest, named Zacharias, of the course of Abia, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
lk.1.6	Luke 1:6	And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the Commandements and ordinances of the Lord, blamelesse.
lk.1.7	Luke 1:7	And they had no childe, because that Elizabeth was barren, and they both were now well striken in yeeres.
lk.1.8	Luke 1:8	And it came to passe, that while he executed the Priests office before God in the order of his course,
lk.1.9	Luke 1:9	According to the custome of the Priests office, his lot was to burne incense when he went into the Temple of the Lord.
lk.1.10	Luke 1:10	And the whole multitude of the people were praying without, at the time of incense.
lk.1.11	Luke 1:11	And there appeared vnto him an Angel of the Lord, standing on the right side of the Altar of incense.
lk.1.12	Luke 1:12	And when Zacharias sawe him, hee was troubled, and feare fell vpon him.
lk.1.13	Luke 1:13	But the Angel said vnto him, Feare not, Zacharias, for thy prayer is heard, and thy wife Elizabeth shall beare thee a sonne, and thou shalt call his name Iohn.
lk.1.14	Luke 1:14	And thou shalt haue ioy and gladnesse, and many shall reioyce at his birth:
lk.1.15	Luke 1:15	For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shal drinke neither wine, nor strong drinke, and he shall bee filled with the holy Ghost, euen from his mothers wombe.
lk.1.16	Luke 1:16	And many of the children of Israel shall hee turne to the Lord their God.
lk.1.17	Luke 1:17	And hee shall goe before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turne the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisedome of the iust, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
lk.1.18	Luke 1:18	And Zacharias said vnto the Angel, Whereby shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife well striken in yeeres.
lk.1.19	Luke 1:19	And the Angel answering, said vnto him, I am Gabriel that stand in the presence of God, and am sent to speake vnto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.
lk.1.20	Luke 1:20	And behold, thou shalt be dumbe, and not able to speake, vntill the day that these things shall bee performed, because thou beleeuest not my words, which shall bee fulfilled in their season.
lk.1.21	Luke 1:21	And the people waited for Zacharias, and maruelled that hee taried so long in the temple.
lk.1.22	Luke 1:22	And when he came out, he could not speake vnto them: and they perceiued that he had seene a vision in the temple: for he beckened vnto them, and remained speechlesse.
lk.1.23	Luke 1:23	And it came to passe, that as soone as the dayes of his ministration were accomplished, he departed to his owne house.
lk.1.24	Luke 1:24	And after those dayes his wife Elizabeth conceiued, and hid her selfe fiue moneths, saying,
lk.1.25	Luke 1:25	Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the dayes wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproch among men.
lk.1.26	Luke 1:26	And in the sixt moneth, the Angel Gabriel was sent from God, vnto a citie of Galilee, named Nazareth,
lk.1.27	Luke 1:27	To a virgine espoused to a man whose name was Ioseph, of the house of Dauid, and the virgins name was Marie.
lk.1.28	Luke 1:28	And the Angel came in vnto her, and said, Haile thou that art highly fauoured, the Lord is with thee: Blessed art thou among women.
lk.1.29	Luke 1:29	And when she saw him, she was troubled at his saying, and cast in her minde what maner of salutation this should be.
lk.1.30	Luke 1:30	And the Angel said vnto her, Feare not, Marie, for thou hast found fauour with God.
lk.1.31	Luke 1:31	And behold, thou shalt conceiue in thy wombe, and bring forth a sonne, and shalt call his name Iesus.
lk.1.32	Luke 1:32	He shall be great, and shall be called the sonne of the Highest, and the Lord God shall giue vnto him the throne of his father Dauid.
lk.1.33	Luke 1:33	And hee shall reigne ouer the house of Iacob for euer, and of his kingdome there shall be no end.
lk.1.34	Luke 1:34	Then said Marie vnto the Angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?
lk.1.35	Luke 1:35	And the Angel answered and said vnto her, The holy Ghost shall come vpon thee, and the power of the Highest shall ouershadow thee. Therefore also that holy thing which shall bee borne of thee, shall bee called the sonne of God.
lk.1.36	Luke 1:36	And behold, thy cousin Elizabeth, she hath also conceiued a sonne in her old age, and this is the sixt moneth with her, who was called barren.
lk.1.37	Luke 1:37	For with God no thing shall be vnpossible.
lk.1.38	Luke 1:38	And Marie said, Behold the handmaide of the Lord, be it vnto me according to thy word: and the Angel departed from her.
lk.1.39	Luke 1:39	And Marie arose in those dayes, and went into the hill countrey with haste, into a citie of Iuda,
lk.1.40	Luke 1:40	And entred into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elizabeth.
lk.1.41	Luke 1:41	And it came to passe that when Elizabeth heard the salutation of Marie, the babe leaped in her wombe, and Elizabeth was filled with the holy Ghost.
lk.1.42	Luke 1:42	And she spake out with a loud voyce, and saide, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruite of thy wombe.
lk.1.43	Luke 1:43	And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to mee?
lk.1.44	Luke 1:44	For loe, assoone as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine eares, the babe leaped in my wombe for ioy.
lk.1.45	Luke 1:45	And blessed is she that beleeued, for there shalbe a performance of those things, which were told her from the Lord.
lk.1.46	Luke 1:46	And Marie said, My soule doth magnifie the Lord.
lk.1.47	Luke 1:47	And my spirit hath reioyced in God my sauiour.
lk.1.48	Luke 1:48	For hee hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for behold, from hencefoorth all generations shall call me blessed.
lk.1.49	Luke 1:49	For he that is mighty hath done to mee great things, and holy is his Name.
lk.1.50	Luke 1:50	And his mercy is on them that feare him, from generation to generation.
lk.1.51	Luke 1:51	Hee hath shewed strength with his arme, he hath scattered the proud, in the imagination of their hearts.
lk.1.52	Luke 1:52	He hath put downe the mighty from their seates, and exalted them of low degree.
lk.1.53	Luke 1:53	Hee hath filled the hungry with good things, and the rich hee hath sent emptie away.
lk.1.54	Luke 1:54	Hee hath holpen his seruant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy,
lk.1.55	Luke 1:55	As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for euer.
lk.1.56	Luke 1:56	And Mary abode with her about three moneths, and returned to her owne house.
lk.1.57	Luke 1:57	Now Elizabeths full time came, that shee should be deliuered, and shee brought foorth a sonne.
lk.1.58	Luke 1:58	And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy vpon her, and they reioyced with her.
lk.1.59	Luke 1:59	And it came to passe that on the eight day they came to circumcise the childe, and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
lk.1.60	Luke 1:60	And his mother answered, and said, Not so, but he shalbe called Iohn.
lk.1.61	Luke 1:61	And they said vnto her, There is none of thy kinred that is called by this name.
lk.1.62	Luke 1:62	And they made signes to his father, how he would haue him called.
lk.1.63	Luke 1:63	And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is Iohn: and they marueiled all.
lk.1.64	Luke 1:64	And his mouth was opened immediatly, and his tongue loosed, and hee spake, and praised God.
lk.1.65	Luke 1:65	And feare came on all that dwelt round about them, and all these sayings were noised abroad thorowout all the hill countrey of Iudea.
lk.1.66	Luke 1:66	And all they that had heard them, layde them vp in their hearts, saying, What maner of childe shal this be? And the hand of the Lord was with him.
lk.1.67	Luke 1:67	And his father Zacharias was filled with the holy Ghost, and prophesied, saying,
lk.1.68	Luke 1:68	Blessed bee the Lord God of Israel, for hee hath visited and redeemed his people,
lk.1.69	Luke 1:69	And hath raised vp an horne of saluation for vs, in the house of his seruant Dauid,
lk.1.70	Luke 1:70	As he spake by the mouth of his holy Prophets, which haue bene since the world began:
lk.1.71	Luke 1:71	That wee should be saued from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate vs,
lk.1.72	Luke 1:72	To performe the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy Couenant,
lk.1.73	Luke 1:73	The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,
lk.1.74	Luke 1:74	That hee would grant vnto vs, that wee beeing deliuered out of the hands of our enemies, might serue him without feare,
lk.1.75	Luke 1:75	In holinesse and righteousnesse before him, all the dayes of our life.
lk.1.76	Luke 1:76	And thou childe shalt bee called the Prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt goe before the face of the Lord to prepare his wayes.
lk.1.77	Luke 1:77	To giue knowledge of saluation vnto his people, by the remission of their sinnes,
lk.1.78	Luke 1:78	Through the tender mercy of our God, whereby the day-spring from on high hath visited vs,
lk.1.79	Luke 1:79	To giue light to them that sit in darknes, and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
lk.1.80	Luke 1:80	And the childe grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts, till the day of his shewing vnto Israel.
lk.2.1	Luke 2:1	And it came to passe in those dayes, that there went out a decree from Cesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.
lk.2.2	Luke 2:2	(And this taxing was first made whē Cyrenius was gouernor of Syria)
lk.2.3	Luke 2:3	And all went to bee taxed, euery one into his owne citie.
lk.2.4	Luke 2:4	And Ioseph also wēt vp frō Galilee, out of the citie of Nazareth, into Iudea, vnto the citie of Dauid, which is called Bethlehem, (because he was of the house and linage of Dauid,)
lk.2.5	Luke 2:5	To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.
lk.2.6	Luke 2:6	And so it was, that while they were there, the dayes were accomplished that she should be deliuered.
lk.2.7	Luke 2:7	And she brought foorth her first borne sonne, and wrapped him in swadling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no roome for them in the Inne.
lk.2.8	Luke 2:8	And there were in the same countrey shepheards abiding in þ field, keeping watch ouer their flocke by night.
lk.2.9	Luke 2:9	And loe, the Angel of the Lord came vpon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them, and they were sore afraid.
lk.2.10	Luke 2:10	And the Angel said vnto them, Feare not: For behold, I bring you good tidings of great ioy, which shall be to all people.
lk.2.11	Luke 2:11	For vnto you is borne this day, in the citie of Dauid, a Sauiour, which is Christ the Lord.
lk.2.12	Luke 2:12	And this shall be a signe vnto you; yee shall find the babe wrapped in swadling clothes lying in a manger.
lk.2.13	Luke 2:13	And suddenly there was with the Angel a multitude of the heauenly hoste praising God, and saying,
lk.2.14	Luke 2:14	Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good wil towards men.
lk.2.15	Luke 2:15	And it came to passe, as the Angels were gone away from them into heauen, the shepheards said one to another, Let vs now goe euen vnto Bethlehem, and see this thing which is come to passe, which the Lord hath made knowen vnto vs.
lk.2.16	Luke 2:16	And they came with haste, and found Mary and Ioseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
lk.2.17	Luke 2:17	And when they had seene it, they made knowen abroad the saying, which was told them, concerning this child.
lk.2.18	Luke 2:18	And all they that heard it, wondered at those things, which were tolde them by the shepheards.
lk.2.19	Luke 2:19	But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
lk.2.20	Luke 2:20	And the shepheards returned, glorifying & praising God for all the things that they had heard and seene, as it was told vnto them.
lk.2.21	Luke 2:21	And when eight dayes were accomplished for the circumcising of the childe, his name was called Iesus, which was so named of the Angel before he was conceiued in the wombe.
lk.2.22	Luke 2:22	And when the dayes of her purification according to the law of Moses, were accomplished, they brought him to Hierusalem, to present him to the Lord,
lk.2.23	Luke 2:23	(As it is written in the law of the Lord, Euery male that openeth the wombe, shalbe called holy to the Lord)
lk.2.24	Luke 2:24	And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the Law of the Lord, a paire of turtle doues, or two yong pigeons.
lk.2.25	Luke 2:25	And behold, there was a man in Hierusalem, whose name was Simeon, and the same man was iust and deuout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the holy Ghost was vpon him.
lk.2.26	Luke 2:26	And it was reuealed vnto him by the holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seene the Lords Christ.
lk.2.27	Luke 2:27	And hee came by the spirit into the Temple: and when the parents brought in the child Iesus, to doe for him after the custome of the Lawe,
lk.2.28	Luke 2:28	Then tooke hee him vp in his armes, and blessed God, and said,
lk.2.29	Luke 2:29	Lord now lettest thou thy seruant depart in peace, according to thy word.
lk.2.30	Luke 2:30	For mine eyes haue seene thy saluation.
lk.2.31	Luke 2:31	Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people.
lk.2.32	Luke 2:32	A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.
lk.2.33	Luke 2:33	And Ioseph and his mother marueiled at those things which were spoken of him.
lk.2.34	Luke 2:34	And Simeon blessed them, and said vnto Marie his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising againe of many in Israel: and for a signe which shall be spoken against,
lk.2.35	Luke 2:35	(Yea a sword shall pearce thorow thy owne soule also) that the thoughts of many hearts may be reuealed.
lk.2.36	Luke 2:36	And there was one Anna a Prophetesse, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser; she was of a great age, and had liued with an husband seuen yeeres from her virginitie.
lk.2.37	Luke 2:37	And she was a widow of about fourescore and foure yeeres, which departed not from the Temple, but serued God with fastings and prayers night and day.
lk.2.38	Luke 2:38	And she comming in that instant, gaue thankes likewise vnto the Lord, and spake of him to al them that looked for redemption in Hierusalem.
lk.2.39	Luke 2:39	And when they had performed all things according to the Lawe of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their owne citie Nazareth.
lk.2.40	Luke 2:40	And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit filled with wisedome, and the grace of God was vpon him.
lk.2.41	Luke 2:41	Now his parents went to Hierusalem euery yeere, at the feast of the Passeouer.
lk.2.42	Luke 2:42	And when he was twelue yeeres old, they went vp to Hierusalem, after the custome of the feast.
lk.2.43	Luke 2:43	And when they had fulfilled the dayes, as they returned, the childe Iesus taried behind in Hierusalem, and Ioseph and his mother knew not of it.
lk.2.44	Luke 2:44	But they supposing him to haue bene in the company, went a daies iourney, and they sought him among their kinsefolke and acquaintance.
lk.2.45	Luke 2:45	And when they found him not, they turned backe againe to Hierusalem, seeking him.
lk.2.46	Luke 2:46	And it came to passe, that after three daies they found him in the Temple, sitting in the midst of the Doctours, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
lk.2.47	Luke 2:47	And all that heard him were astonished at his vnderstanding, and answeres.
lk.2.48	Luke 2:48	And when they sawe him, they were amazed: and his mother said vnto him, Sonne, why hast thou thus dealt with vs? Behold, thy father and I haue sought thee sorrowing.
lk.2.49	Luke 2:49	And he said vnto them, How is it that ye sought me? Wist yee not that I must bee about my fathers businesse?
lk.2.50	Luke 2:50	And they vnderstood not the saying which he spake vnto them.
lk.2.51	Luke 2:51	And he went downe with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subiect vnto them: But his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
lk.2.52	Luke 2:52	And Iesus increased in wisedom and stature, and in fauour with God and man.
lk.3.1	Luke 3:1	Now in the fifteenth yeere of the reigne of Tiberius Cesar, Pontius Pilate being Gouernour of Iudea, & Herode being Tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip Tetrarch of Iturea, and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the Tetrarch of Abilene,
lk.3.2	Luke 3:2	Annas and Caiaphas being the high Priests, the word of God came vnto Iohn the sonne of Zacharias, in the wildernesse.
lk.3.3	Luke 3:3	And he came into all the countrey about Iordane, preaching the baptisme of repentance, for the remissiō of sinnes,
lk.3.4	Luke 3:4	As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the Prophet, saying, The voyce of one crying in the wildernesse, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
lk.3.5	Luke 3:5	Euery valley shall be filled, and euery mountaine and hill shalbe brought low, and the crooked shall bee made straight, and the rough wayes shall be made smooth.
lk.3.6	Luke 3:6	And all flesh shal see the saluation of God.
lk.3.7	Luke 3:7	Then said hee to the multitude that came forth to bee baptized of him, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
lk.3.8	Luke 3:8	Bring forth therfore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within your selues, We haue Abraham to our father: For I say vnto you, that God is able of these stones to raise vp children vnto Abraham.
lk.3.9	Luke 3:9	And now also the axe is laid vnto the root of the trees: Euery tree therefore which bringeth not foorth good fruit, is hewen downe, and cast into the fire.
lk.3.10	Luke 3:10	And the people asked him, saying, What shall we doe then?
lk.3.11	Luke 3:11	He answereth, and saith vnto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none, and he that hath meat, let him doe likewise.
lk.3.12	Luke 3:12	Then came also Publicanes to be baptized, and said vnto him, Master, what shall we doe?
lk.3.13	Luke 3:13	And he said vnto them, Exact no more then that which is appointed you.
lk.3.14	Luke 3:14	And the souldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we doe? And he said vnto them, Doe violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, & be content with your wages.
lk.3.15	Luke 3:15	And as the people were in expectation, and all men mused in their hearts of Iohn, whether he were the Christ or not:
lk.3.16	Luke 3:16	Iohn answered, saying vnto them all, I indeede baptize you with water, but one mightier then I commeth, the latchet of whose shooes I am not worthy to vnloose, he shall baptize you with the holy Ghost, and with fire.
lk.3.17	Luke 3:17	Whose fanne is in his hand, and he will thorowly purge his floore, and will gather the wheat into his garner, but the chaffe he will burne with fire vnquencheable.
lk.3.18	Luke 3:18	And many other things in his exhortation preached he vnto the people.
lk.3.19	Luke 3:19	But Herode the Tetrarch being reprooued by him for Herodias his brother Philips wife, and for all the euils which Herode had done,
lk.3.20	Luke 3:20	Added yet this aboue all, that he shut vp Iohn in prison.
lk.3.21	Luke 3:21	Now when all the people were baptized, and it came to passe that Iesus also being baptized, and praying, the heauen was opened:
lk.3.22	Luke 3:22	And the holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a Doue vpon him, and a voice came from heauen, which said, Thou art my beloued sonne, in thee I am well pleased.
lk.3.23	Luke 3:23	And Iesus himselfe began to be about thirty yeeres of age, being (as was supposed) the sonne of Ioseph, which was the sonne of Heli,
lk.3.24	Luke 3:24	Which was the sonne of Matthat, which was the sonne of Leui, which was the sonne of Melchi, which was the sonne of Ianna, which was the sonne of Ioseph,

lk.4.1	Luke 4:1	And Iesus being full of the holy Ghost, returned from Iordane, and was led by the spirit into the wildernesse,
lk.4.2	Luke 4:2	Being fourtie dayes tempted of the deuil, and in those dayes he did eat nothing: and when they were ended, he afterward hungred.
lk.4.3	Luke 4:3	And the deuil saide vnto him, If thou be the Sonne of God, command this stone that it be made bread.
lk.4.4	Luke 4:4	And Iesus answered him, saying, It is written, that man shall not liue by bread alone, but by euery word of God.
lk.4.5	Luke 4:5	And the deuil taking him vp into an high mountaine, shewed vnto him all the kingdomes of the world in a moment of time.
lk.4.6	Luke 4:6	And the deuil said vnto him, All this power will I giue thee, and the glory of them; for that is deliuered vnto me, & to whomsoeuer I will, I giue it.
lk.4.7	Luke 4:7	If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shalbe thine.
lk.4.8	Luke 4:8	And Iesus answered and said vnto him, Get thee behinde me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him onely shalt thou serue.
lk.4.9	Luke 4:9	And hee brought him to Hierusalem, and set him on a pinacle of the Temple, and said vnto him, If thou be the Sonne of God, cast thy selfe downe from hence.
lk.4.10	Luke 4:10	For it is written, He shall giue his Angels charge ouer thee, to keepe thee.
lk.4.11	Luke 4:11	And in their handes they shall beare thee vp, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
lk.4.12	Luke 4:12	And Iesus answering, said vnto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
lk.4.13	Luke 4:13	And when the deuil had ended all the temptation, hee departed from him for a season.
lk.4.14	Luke 4:14	¶ And Iesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and there went out a fame of him through all the region round about.
lk.4.15	Luke 4:15	And hee taught in their Synagogues, being glorified of all.
lk.4.16	Luke 4:16	¶ And hee came to Nazareth, where he had bene brought vp, and as his custome was, he went into the Synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood vp for to reade.
lk.4.17	Luke 4:17	And there was deliuered vnto him the booke of the Prophet Esaias, and when he had opened the Booke, he found the place where it was written,
lk.4.18	Luke 4:18	The Spirit of the Lord is vpon mee, because hee hath anointed mee, to preach the Gospel to the poore, he hath sent mee to heale the broken hearted, to preach deliuerance to the captiues, and recouering of sight to the blinde, to set at libertie them that are bruised,
lk.4.19	Luke 4:19	To preach the acceptable yeere of the Lord.
lk.4.20	Luke 4:20	And he closed the booke, and hee gaue it againe to the minister, and sate downe: and the eyes of all them that were in the Synagogue were fastened on him.
lk.4.21	Luke 4:21	And hee began to say vnto them, This day is this Scripture fulfilled in your eares.
lk.4.22	Luke 4:22	And all bare him witnesse, and wondered at the gracious wordes, which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Iosephs sonne?
lk.4.23	Luke 4:23	And hee said vnto them, Yee will surely say vnto me this prouerbe, Physition, heale thy selfe: Whatsoeuer wee haue heard done in Capernaum, doe also here in thy countrey.
lk.4.24	Luke 4:24	And hee said, Verely I say vnto you, no Prophet is accepted in his owne countrey.
lk.4.25	Luke 4:25	But I tell you of a trueth, many widowes were in Israel in the dayes of Elias, when the heauen was shut vp three yeres and sixe moneths: when great famine was throughout all the land:
lk.4.26	Luke 4:26	But vnto none of them was Elias sent, saue vnto Sarepta a citie of Sidon, vnto a woman that was a widow.
lk.4.27	Luke 4:27	And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Elizeus the Prophet: and none of them was cleansed, sauing Naaman the Syrian.
lk.4.28	Luke 4:28	And all they in the Synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
lk.4.29	Luke 4:29	And rose vp, and thrust him out of the citie, & led him vnto the brow of the hill (whereon their city was built) that they might cast him downe headlong.
lk.4.30	Luke 4:30	But he passing thorow the mids of them, went his way:
lk.4.31	Luke 4:31	And came downe to Capernaum, a citie of Galile, and taught them on the Sabbath dayes.
lk.4.32	Luke 4:32	And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his worde was with power.
lk.4.33	Luke 4:33	¶ And in the Synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an vncleane deuill, and cryed out with a loud voice,
lk.4.34	Luke 4:34	Saying, Let vs alone, what haue wee to doe with thee, thou Iesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy vs? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
lk.4.35	Luke 4:35	And Iesus rebuked him, saying, Holde thy peace, and come out of him. And when the deuill had throwen him in the middes, hee came out of him, and hurt him not.
lk.4.36	Luke 4:36	And they were all amazed, and spake among themselues, saying, What a word is this? for with authoritie and power hee commaundeth the vncleane spirits, and they come out.
lk.4.37	Luke 4:37	And the fame of him went out into euery place of the countrey round about.
lk.4.38	Luke 4:38	¶ And he arose out of the Synagogue, and entred into Simons house: and Simons wiues mother was taken with a great feuer, and they besought him for her.
lk.4.39	Luke 4:39	And he stood ouer her, and rebuked the feuer, & it left her. And immediatly she arose, & ministred vnto them.
lk.4.40	Luke 4:40	¶ Now when the Sunne was setting, all they that had any sicke with diuers diseases, brought them vnto him: and hee laid his handes on euery one of them, and healed them.
lk.4.41	Luke 4:41	And deuils also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Sonne of God. And hee rebuking them, suffered them not to speake: for they knewe that hee was Christ.
lk.4.42	Luke 4:42	And when it was day, he departed, and went into a desert place: and the people sought him, and came vnto him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.
lk.4.43	Luke 4:43	And hee said vnto them, I must preach the kingdome of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.
lk.4.44	Luke 4:44	And hee preached in the Synagogues of Galile.
lk.5.1	Luke 5:1	And it came to passe, that as the people preassed vpon him to heare the word of God, hee stood by the lake of Genesareth,
lk.5.2	Luke 5:2	And sawe two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
lk.5.3	Luke 5:3	And he entred into one of the ships, which was Simons, and prayed him, that he would thrust out a little from the land: and he sate downe, and taught the people out of the ship.
lk.5.4	Luke 5:4	Now when he had left speaking, he said vnto Simon, Lanch out into the deepe, and let downe your nets for a draught.
lk.5.5	Luke 5:5	And Simon answering, said vnto him, Master, wee haue toiled all the night, and haue taken nothing: neuerthelesse at thy word I will let downe the net.
lk.5.6	Luke 5:6	And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes, and their net brake:
lk.5.7	Luke 5:7	And they beckened vnto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and helpe them. And they came, & filled both the ships, so that they began to sinke.
lk.5.8	Luke 5:8	When Simon Peter saw it, he fell downe at Iesus knees, saying, Depart from me, for I am a sinfull man, O Lord.
lk.5.9	Luke 5:9	For he was astonished, and al that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken.
lk.5.10	Luke 5:10	And so was also Iames, and Iohn the sonnes of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Iesus said vnto Simon, Feare not, from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
lk.5.11	Luke 5:11	And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsooke all, and followed him.
lk.5.12	Luke 5:12	¶ And it came to passe, when he was in a certaine citie, behold a man full of leprosie: who seeing Iesus, fell on his face, & besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me cleane.
lk.5.13	Luke 5:13	And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I wil: be thou cleane. And immediatly the leprosie departed from him.
lk.5.14	Luke 5:14	And hee charged him to tell no man: but, Goe, and shewe thy selfe to the Priest, and offer for thy clensing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimonie vnto them.
lk.5.15	Luke 5:15	But so much the more went there a fame abroad of him, and great multitudes came together to heare, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
lk.5.16	Luke 5:16	¶ And he withdrew himselfe into the wildernesse, and prayed.
lk.5.17	Luke 5:17	And it came to passe on a certaine day, as hee was teaching, that there were Pharisees and Doctours of the Law sitting by, which were come out of euery towne of Galilee, and Iudea, and Hierusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heale them.
lk.5.18	Luke 5:18	¶ And behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsie: and they sought meanes to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
lk.5.19	Luke 5:19	And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in, because of the multitude, they went vpon the house top, & let him downe through the tiling with his couch, into the midst before Iesus.
lk.5.20	Luke 5:20	And when he saw their faith, hee said vnto him, Man, thy sinnes are forgiuen thee.
lk.5.21	Luke 5:21	And the Scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgiue sinnes, but God alone?
lk.5.22	Luke 5:22	But when Iesus perceiued their thoughts, he answering, saide vnto them, What reason ye in your hearts?
lk.5.23	Luke 5:23	Whether is easier to say, Thy sinnes be forgiuen thee: or to say, Rise vp and walke?
lk.5.24	Luke 5:24	But that ye may know that the Sonne of man hath power vpon earth to forgiue sinnes (he said vnto the sicke of the palsie,) I say vnto thee, Arise, and take vp thy couch, and go into thine house.
lk.5.25	Luke 5:25	And immediatly he rose vp before them, and tooke vp that whereon hee lay, and departed to his owne house, glorifying God.
lk.5.26	Luke 5:26	And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with feare, saying, Wee haue seene strange things to day.
lk.5.27	Luke 5:27	¶ And after these things hee went foorth, and sawe a Publicane, named Leui, sitting at the receit of custome: and hee said vnto him, Follow me.
lk.5.28	Luke 5:28	And he left all, rose vp, and followed him.
lk.5.29	Luke 5:29	And Leui made him a great feast in his owne house: and there was a great company of Publicanes, and of others that sate downe with them.
lk.5.30	Luke 5:30	But their Scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why doe ye eate and drinke with Publicanes and sinners?
lk.5.31	Luke 5:31	And Iesus answering, said vnto them, They that are whole need not a physician: but they that are sicke.
lk.5.32	Luke 5:32	I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
lk.5.33	Luke 5:33	¶ And they said vnto him, Why doe the disciples of Iohn fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees: but thine eat and drinke?
lk.5.34	Luke 5:34	And he said vnto them, Can yee make the children of the Bride-chamber fast, while the Bridegrome is with them?
lk.5.35	Luke 5:35	But the dayes will come, when the Bridegrome shall bee taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those dayes.
lk.5.36	Luke 5:36	¶ And he spake also a parable vnto them, No man putteth a piece of a newe garment vpon an olde: if otherwise, then both the newe maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new, agreeth not with the olde.
lk.5.37	Luke 5:37	And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.
lk.5.38	Luke 5:38	But newe wine must be put into newe bottles, and both are preserued.
lk.5.39	Luke 5:39	No man also hauing drunke olde wine, straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.
lk.6.1	Luke 6:1	And it came to passe on the second Sabbath after the first, that he went thorow the corne fields: and his disciples plucked the eares of corne, and did eate, rubbing them in their hands.
lk.6.2	Luke 6:2	And certaine of the Pharisees said vnto them, Why doe yee that which is not lawfull to doe on the Sabbath dayes?
lk.6.3	Luke 6:3	And Iesus answering them, said, Haue yee not read so much as this what Dauid did, when himselfe was an hungred, and they which were with him:
lk.6.4	Luke 6:4	How he went into the house of God, and did take and eate the Shew bread, and gaue also to them that were with him, which it is not lawful to eate but for the Priests alone?
lk.6.5	Luke 6:5	And he said vnto them, That the sonne of man is Lord also of the Sabbath.
lk.6.6	Luke 6:6	And it came to passe also on another Sabbath, that he entred into the Synagogue, and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.
lk.6.7	Luke 6:7	And the Scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heale on the Sabbath day: that they might find an accusation against him.
lk.6.8	Luke 6:8	But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise vp, and stand foorth in the mids. And he arose, and stood foorth.
lk.6.9	Luke 6:9	Then said Iesus vnto them, I will aske you one thing, Is it lawfull on the Sabbath dayes to doe good, or to doe euill? to saue life, or to destroy it?
lk.6.10	Luke 6:10	And looking round about vpon them all, he said vnto the man, Stretch foorth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
lk.6.11	Luke 6:11	And they were filled with madnesse, and communed one with another what they might doe to Iesus.
lk.6.12	Luke 6:12	And it came to passe in those dayes, that hee went out into a mountaine to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
lk.6.13	Luke 6:13	¶ And when it was day, he called vnto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelue; whom also hee named Apostles:
lk.6.14	Luke 6:14	Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother: Iames and Iohn, Philip and Bartholomew,
lk.6.15	Luke 6:15	Matthew and Thomas, Iames the sonne of Alpheus, and Simon, called Zelotes,
lk.6.16	Luke 6:16	And Iudas the brother of Iames, and Iudas Iscariot, which also was the traitour.
lk.6.17	Luke 6:17	¶ And hee came downe with them, and stood in the plaine, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people, out of all Iudea and Hierusalem, and from the Sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to heare him, and to be healed of their diseases,
lk.6.18	Luke 6:18	And they that were vexed with vncleane spirits: and they were healed.
lk.6.19	Luke 6:19	And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went vertue out of him, and healed them all.
lk.6.20	Luke 6:20	¶ And hee lifted vp his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be yee poore: for yours is the kingdome of God.
lk.6.21	Luke 6:21	Blessed are yee that hunger now: for yee shall be filled. Blessed are yee that weepe now, for yee shall laugh.
lk.6.22	Luke 6:22	Blessed are yee when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shal reproach you, and cast out your name as euill, for the Sonne of mans sake.
lk.6.23	Luke 6:23	Reioice yee in that day, and leape for ioy: for behold, your reward is great in heauen for in the like maner did their fathers vnto the Prophets.
lk.6.24	Luke 6:24	But woe vnto you that are rich: for yee haue receiued your consolation.
lk.6.25	Luke 6:25	Woe vnto you that are full: for yee shall hunger. Woe vnto you that laugh now: for yee shall mourne and weepe.
lk.6.26	Luke 6:26	Woe vnto you when all men shall speake well of you: for so did their fathers to the false Prophets.
lk.6.27	Luke 6:27	¶ But I say vnto you which heare, Loue your enemies, doe good to them which hate you,
lk.6.28	Luke 6:28	Blesse them that curse you, & pray for them which despitefully vse you.
lk.6.29	Luke 6:29	And vnto him that smiteth thee on the one cheeke, offer also the other: and him that taketh away thy cloake, forbid not to take thy coat also.
lk.6.30	Luke 6:30	Giue to euery man that asketh of thee, and of him that taketh away thy goods, aske them not againe.
lk.6.31	Luke 6:31	And as yee would that men should doe to you, doe yee also to them likewise.
lk.6.32	Luke 6:32	For if yee loue them which loue you, what thanke haue ye? for sinners also loue those that loue them.
lk.6.33	Luke 6:33	And if ye doe good to them which doe good to you, What thanke haue ye? for sinners also doe euen the same.
lk.6.34	Luke 6:34	And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receiue, What thanke haue ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receiue as much againe.
lk.6.35	Luke 6:35	But loue yee your enemies, and doe good, and lend, hoping for nothing againe: and your reward shall bee great, and ye shalbe the children of the Highest: for hee is kinde vnto the vnthankfull, and to the euill.
lk.6.36	Luke 6:36	Be ye therefore mercifull, as your Father also is mercifull.
lk.6.37	Luke 6:37	Iudge not, and ye shall not bee iudged: condemne not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgiue, and ye shall be forgiuen.
lk.6.38	Luke 6:38	Giue, and it shall bee giuen vnto you, good measure, preassed downe, and shaken together, and running ouer, shall men giue into your bosome: for with the same measure that ye mete withall, it shall bee measured to you againe.
lk.6.39	Luke 6:39	And hee spake a parable vnto them, Can the blinde leade the blinde? Shall they not both fall into the ditch?
lk.6.40	Luke 6:40	The disciple is not aboue his master: but euery one that is perfect shalbe as his master.
lk.6.41	Luke 6:41	And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brothers eye, but perceiuest not the beame that is in thine owne eye?
lk.6.42	Luke 6:42	Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let mee pull out the mote that is in thine eye: when thou thy selfe beholdest not the beame that is in thine owne eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beame out of thine owne eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pul out the mote that is in thy brothers eye.
lk.6.43	Luke 6:43	For a good tree bringeth not foorth corrupt fruit: neither doeth a corrupt tree bring foorth good fruit.
lk.6.44	Luke 6:44	For euery tree is knowen by his owne fruit: for of thornes men doe not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.
lk.6.45	Luke 6:45	A good man out of the good treasure of his heart, bringeth foorth that which is good: and an euill man out of the euill treasure of his heart, bringeth foorth that which is euill: For of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaketh.
lk.6.46	Luke 6:46	¶ And why call ye mee Lord, Lord, and doe not the things which I say?
lk.6.47	Luke 6:47	Whosoeuer commeth to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like.
lk.6.48	Luke 6:48	He is like a man which built an house, and digged deepe, and layd the foundation on a rocke. And when the flood arose, the streame beat vehemently vpon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded vpon a rocke.
lk.6.49	Luke 6:49	But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house vpon the earth: against which the streame did beate vehemently, and immediatly it fell, and the ruine of that house was great.

lk.8.1	Luke 8:1	And it came to passe afterward, þ he went throughout euery citie and village preaching, and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdome of God: and the twelue were with him,
lk.8.2	Luke 8:2	And certaine women which had bene healed of euill spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene out of whom went seuen deuils,
lk.8.3	Luke 8:3	And Ioanna the wife of Chuza, Herods steward, and Susanna, and many others which ministred vnto him of their substance.
lk.8.4	Luke 8:4	¶ And when much people were gathered together, and were come to him out of euery citie, he spake by a parable:
lk.8.5	Luke 8:5	A Sower went out to sowe his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the wayes side, and it was troden downe, and the foules of the aire deuoured it.
lk.8.6	Luke 8:6	And some fell vpon a rocke, and assoone as it was sprung vp, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.
lk.8.7	Luke 8:7	And some fell among thornes, and the thornes sprang vp with it, and choked it.
lk.8.8	Luke 8:8	And other fell on good ground, and sprang vp, and bare fruite an hundred fold. And when hee saide these things, he cryed, He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.
lk.8.9	Luke 8:9	And his disciples asked him, saying, What might this parable be?
lk.8.10	Luke 8:10	And he said, Unto you it is giuen to know the mysteries of the kingdome of God: but to others in parables, that seeing, they might not see, and hearing, they might not vnderstand.
lk.8.11	Luke 8:11	Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
lk.8.12	Luke 8:12	Those by the way side, are they that heare: then commeth the deuil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, least they should beleeue, and be saued.
lk.8.13	Luke 8:13	They on the rocke, are they which when they heare, receiue the word with ioy; and these haue no roote, which for a while beleeue, and in time of temptation fall away.
lk.8.14	Luke 8:14	And that which fell among thornes, are they, which when they haue heard, goe forth, and are choked with cares and riches, and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruite to perfection.
lk.8.15	Luke 8:15	But that on the good ground, are they, which in an honest and good heart hauing heard the word, keepe it, and bring foorth fruite with patience.
lk.8.16	Luke 8:16	¶ No man when he hath lighted a candle, couereth it with a vessell, or putteth it vnder a bed: but setteth it on a candlesticke, that they which enter in, may see the light.
lk.8.17	Luke 8:17	For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest: neither any thing hid, that shall not be knowen, and come abroad.
lk.8.18	Luke 8:18	Take heede therefore how yee heare: for whosoeuer hath, to him shall bee giuen; and whosoeuer hath not, from him shall be taken, euen that which he seemeth to haue.
lk.8.19	Luke 8:19	¶ Then came to him his mother and his brethren, and could not come at him for the prease.
lk.8.20	Luke 8:20	And it was told him by certaine which saide, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.
lk.8.21	Luke 8:21	And hee answered and said vnto them, My mother and my brethren are these which heare the word of God, and doe it.
lk.8.22	Luke 8:22	¶ Now it came to passe on a certaine day, that he went into a ship, with his disciples: and hee said vnto them, Let vs goe ouer vnto the other side of the lake, and they lanched foorth.
lk.8.23	Luke 8:23	But as they sailed, he fell asleepe, and there came downe a storme of wind on the lake, and they were filled with water, and were in ieopardie.
lk.8.24	Luke 8:24	And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he rose, and rebuked the wind, and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calme.
lk.8.25	Luke 8:25	And he saide vnto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraide wondred, saying one to another, What maner of man is this? For he commandeth euen the winds and water, and they obey him.
lk.8.26	Luke 8:26	¶ And they arriued at the countrey of the Gadarenes, which is ouer against Galilee.
lk.8.27	Luke 8:27	And when he went forth to land, there met him out of the citie a certaine man which had deuils long time, and ware no clothes, neither abode in any house, but in the tombes.
lk.8.28	Luke 8:28	When he saw Iesus, he cried out, and fell downe before him, and with a loud voyce said, What haue I to doe with thee, Iesus, thou sonne of God most high? I beseech thee torment me not.
lk.8.29	Luke 8:29	(For he had commanded the vncleane spirit to come out of the man: For oftentimes it had caught him, and he was kept bound with chaines, and in fetters: and he brake the bands, and was driuen of the deuil into the wildernesse.)
lk.8.30	Luke 8:30	And Iesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many deuils were entred into him.
lk.8.31	Luke 8:31	And they besought him, that he would not command them to goe out into the deepe.
lk.8.32	Luke 8:32	And there was there an herd of many swine feeding on the mountaine: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them: and he suffered them.
lk.8.33	Luke 8:33	Then went the deuils out of the man, and entred into the swine: and the herd ran violently downe a steepe place into the lake, and were choked.
lk.8.34	Luke 8:34	When they that fed them saw what was done, they fled, and went, and tolde it in the citie, and in the countrey.
lk.8.35	Luke 8:35	Then they went out to see what was done, and came to Iesus, and found the man, out of whom the deuils were departed, sitting at the feete of Iesus, clothed, and in his right minde: and they were afraid.
lk.8.36	Luke 8:36	They also which saw it, told them by what meanes he that was possessed of the deuils, was healed.
lk.8.37	Luke 8:37	¶ Then the whole multitude of the countrey of the Gadarenes round about, besought him to depart from them, for they were taken with great feare: and he went vp into the ship, and returned back againe.
lk.8.38	Luke 8:38	Now the man, out of whom the deuils were departed, besought him that he might be with him: but Iesus sent him away, saying,

lk.8.40	Luke 8:40	And it came to passe, that when Iesus was returned, the people gladly receiued him: for they were all waiting for him.
lk.8.41	Luke 8:41	¶ And behold, there came a man named Iairus, and hee was a ruler of the Synagogue, and hee fell downe at Iesus feete, and besought him that hee would come into his house:
lk.8.42	Luke 8:42	For hee had one onely daughter about twelue yeeres of age, and she lay a dying. (But as hee went the people thronged him.
lk.8.43	Luke 8:43	¶ And a woman hauing an issue of blood twelue yeres, which had spent all her liuing vpon Phisitions, neither could be healed of any,
lk.8.44	Luke 8:44	Came behinde him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediatly her issue of blood stanched.
lk.8.45	Luke 8:45	And Iesus saide, Who touched mee? When all denied, Peter and they that were with him, said, Master, the multitude throng thee, and preasse thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
lk.8.46	Luke 8:46	And Iesus saide, Some body hath touched mee: for I perceiue that vertue is gone out of me.
lk.8.47	Luke 8:47	And when the woman saw that she was not hid, shee came trembling, and falling downe before him, shee declared vnto him before all the people, for what cause shee had touched him, and how she was healed immediatly.
lk.8.48	Luke 8:48	And he said vnto her, Daughter, be of good comfort, thy faith hath made thee whole, goe in peace.)
lk.8.49	Luke 8:49	¶ While hee yet spake, there commeth one from the ruler of the Synagogues house, saying to him, Thy daughter is dead, trouble not the Master.
lk.8.50	Luke 8:50	But when Iesus heard it, he answered him, saying, Feare not, beleeue onely, and she shalbe made whole.
lk.8.51	Luke 8:51	And when hee came into the house, hee suffered no man to goe in, saue Peter, and Iames, and Iohn, and the father and the mother of the mayden.
lk.8.52	Luke 8:52	And all wept, and bewailed her: but he said, Weepe not, she is not dead, but sleepeth.
lk.8.53	Luke 8:53	And they laughed him to scorne, knowing that she was dead.
lk.8.54	Luke 8:54	And hee put them all out, and tooke her by the hand, and called, saying, Mayd, arise.
lk.8.55	Luke 8:55	And her spirit came againe, and shee arose straightway: and hee commanded to giue her meat.
lk.8.56	Luke 8:56	And her parents were astonished: but hee charged them that they should tell no man what was done.
lk.9.1	Luke 9:1	Then he called his twelue disciples together, and gaue them power and authority ouer all deuils, and to cure diseases.

lk.9.3	Luke 9:3	And he said vnto them, Take nothing for your iourney, neither staues, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money, neither haue two coates apeece.
lk.9.4	Luke 9:4	And whatsoeuer house yee enter into, there abide, and thence depart.

lk.9.8	Luke 9:8	And of some, that Elias had appeared: and of others, that one of the olde Prophets was risen againe.

lk.9.12	Luke 9:12	And when the day beganne to weare away, then came the twelue, and said vnto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the townes and countrey round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.
lk.9.13	Luke 9:13	But he said vnto them, Giue yee them to eate. And they said, Wee haue no more but fiue loaues and two fishes, except we should goe and buy meate for all this people.
lk.9.14	Luke 9:14	For they were about fiue thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit downe by fifties in a company.
lk.9.15	Luke 9:15	And they did so, and made them all sit downe.
lk.9.16	Luke 9:16	Then he tooke the fiue loaues and the two fishes, and looking vp to heauen, hee blessed them, and brake, and gaue to the disciples to set before the multitude.
lk.9.17	Luke 9:17	And they did eate, and were all filled. And there was taken vp of fragments that remained to them, twelue baskets.
lk.9.18	Luke 9:18	¶ And it came to passe, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
lk.9.19	Luke 9:19	They answering, said, Iohn the Baptist: but some say, Elias: and others say, that one of the old Prophets is risen againe.
lk.9.20	Luke 9:20	He said vnto them, But whom say yee that I am? Peter answering, said, The Christ of God.
lk.9.21	Luke 9:21	And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing,
lk.9.22	Luke 9:22	Saying, The Sonne of man must suffer many things, and be reiected of the Elders, and chiefe Priests, and Scribes, and be slaine, and be raised the third day.
lk.9.23	Luke 9:23	¶ And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him denie himselfe, and take vp his crosse daily, and follow me.
lk.9.24	Luke 9:24	For whosoeuer will saue his life, shall lose it: but whosoeuer will lose his life for my sake, the same shall saue it.
lk.9.25	Luke 9:25	For what is a man aduantaged, if hee gaine the whole world, and lose himselfe, or be cast away?
lk.9.26	Luke 9:26	For whosoeuer shall bee ashamed of me, and of my wordes, of him shall the Sonne of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his owne glory, and in his Fathers, and of the holy Angels.
lk.9.27	Luke 9:27	But I tell you of a trueth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdome of God.
lk.9.28	Luke 9:28	¶ And it came to passe, about an eight dayes after these sayings, hee tooke Peter, and Iohn, and Iames, and went vp into a mountaine to pray:

lk.11.25	Luke 11:25	And when hee commeth, hee findeth it swept and garnished.

lk.11.27	Luke 11:27	¶ And it came to passe as hee spake these things, a certaine woman of the company lift vp her voice, and said vnto him, Blessed is the wombe that bare thee, and the pappes which thou hast sucked.
lk.11.28	Luke 11:28	But hee said, Yea, rather blessed are they that heare the word of God, and keepe it.
lk.11.29	Luke 11:29	¶ And when the people were gathered thicke together, hee began to say, This is an euill generation, they seeke a signe, and there shall no signe be giuen it, but the signe of Ionas the Prophet:

lk.11.31	Luke 11:31	The Queene of the South shall rise vp in the iudgement with the men of this generation, & condemne them: for shee came from the vtmost parts of the earth, to heare the wisedome of Solomon: and behold, a greater then Solomon is here.
lk.11.32	Luke 11:32	The men of Nineue shall rise vp in the iudgement with this generation, and shall condemne it: for they repented at the preaching of Ionas, and behold, a greater then Ionas is here.
lk.11.33	Luke 11:33	No man when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither vnder a bushell, but on a candlesticke, that they which come in may see the light.
lk.11.34	Luke 11:34	The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light: but when thine eye is euill, thy body also is full of darkenesse.
lk.11.35	Luke 11:35	Take heede therefore, that the light which is in thee, be not darknesse.
lk.11.36	Luke 11:36	If thy whole body therefore be full of light, hauing no part darke, the whole shalbe full of light, as when the bright shining of a candle doeth giue thee light.
lk.11.37	Luke 11:37	¶ And as he spake, a certaine Pharise besought him to dine with him: and he went in, and sate downe to meate.
lk.11.38	Luke 11:38	And when the Pharise saw it, he marueiled that he had not first washed before dinner.

lk.11.41	Luke 11:41	But rather giue almes of such things as you haue: and behold, all things are cleane vnto you.
lk.11.42	Luke 11:42	But woe vnto you Pharises: for ye tythe Mint and Rue, and all maner of herbes, and passe ouer iudgement, and the loue of God: these ought yee to haue done, and not to leaue the other vndone.
lk.11.43	Luke 11:43	Woe vnto you Pharisees: for ye loue the vppermost seats in the Synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
lk.11.44	Luke 11:44	Woe vnto you Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: for ye are as graues which appeare not, and the men that walk ouer them, are not aware of them.

lk.11.47	Luke 11:47	Woe vnto you: for ye build the sepulchres of the Prophets, and your fathers killed them.

lk.11.52	Luke 11:52	Woe vnto you Lawyers: for ye haue taken away the key of knowledge: ye entred not in your selues, and them that were entring in, ye hindred.
