jn.19.35	John 19:35	And he that saw it, bare record, and his record is true, and he knoweth that hee saith true, that yee might beleeue.
jn.19.36	John 19:36	For these things were done, that the Scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
jn.19.37	John 19:37	And againe another Scripture saith, They shall looke on him whom they piersed.
jn.19.38	John 19:38	¶ And after this, Ioseph of Arimathea (being a disciple of Iesus, but secretly for feare of the Iewes) besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Iesus, and Pilate gaue him leaue: he came therefore, and tooke the body of Iesus.
jn.19.39	John 19:39	And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Iesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrhe and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.
jn.19.40	John 19:40	Then tooke they the body of Iesus, & wound it in linnen clothes, with the spices, as the maner of the Iewes is to burie:
jn.19.41	John 19:41	Now in the place where he was crucified, there was a garden, and in the garden a new Sepulchre, wherein was neuer man yet layd.
jn.19.42	John 19:42	There laid they Iesus therefore, because of the Iewes preparation day, for the Sepulchre was nigh at hand.
jn.20.1	John 20:1	The first day of the weeke, commeth Mary Magdalene earely when it was yet darke, vnto the Sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the Sepulchre.
jn.20.2	John 20:2	Then she runneth and commeth to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Iesus loued, and saith vnto them, They haue taken away the Lord out of the Sepulchre, and we know not where they haue laid him.
jn.20.3	John 20:3	Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the Sepulchre.
jn.20.4	John 20:4	So they ranne both together, and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the Sepulchre.
jn.20.5	John 20:5	And he stouping downe and looking in, saw the linnen clothes lying, yet went he not in.
jn.20.6	John 20:6	Then commeth Simon Peter following him, and went into the Sepulchre, and seeth the linnen clothes lie,
jn.20.7	John 20:7	And the napkin that was about his head, not lying with the linnen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by it selfe.
jn.20.8	John 20:8	Then went in also that other disciple which came first to the Sepulchre, and he saw, and beleeued.
jn.20.9	John 20:9	For as yet they knew not the Scripture, that hee must rise againe from the dead.
jn.20.10	John 20:10	Then the disciples went away againe vnto their owne home.
jn.20.11	John 20:11	¶ But Mary stood without at the sepulchre, weeping: & as shee wept, she stouped downe, and looked into the Sepulchre,
jn.20.12	John 20:12	And seeth two Angels in white, sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feete, where the body of Iesus had layen:
jn.20.13	John 20:13	And they say vnto her, Woman, why weepest thou? Shee saith vnto them, Because they haue taken away my Lord, and I know not where they haue laied him.
jn.20.14	John 20:14	And when she had thus said, she turned herselfe backe, and saw Iesus standing, and knew not that it was Iesus.
jn.20.15	John 20:15	Iesus saith vnto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She supposing him to be the gardiner, saith vnto him, Sir, if thou haue borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laied him, and I will take him away.
jn.20.16	John 20:16	Iesus saith vnto her, Mary. She turned herselfe, and saith vnto him, Rabboni, which is to say, Master.
jn.20.17	John 20:17	Iesus saith vnto her, Touch me not: for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but goe to my brethren, and say vnto them, I ascend vnto my Father, and your Father, and to my God, and your God.
jn.20.18	John 20:18	Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that shee had seene the Lord, and that hee had spoken these things vnto her.
jn.20.19	John 20:19	¶ Then the same day at euening, being the first day of the weeke, when the doores were shut, where the disciples were assembled for feare of the Iewes, came Iesus, and stood in the midst, and saith vnto them, Peace bee vnto you.
jn.20.20	John 20:20	And when hee had so saide, hee shewed vnto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord.
jn.20.21	John 20:21	Then said Iesus to them againe, Peace be vnto you: As my Father hath sent me, euen so send I you.
jn.20.22	John 20:22	And when he had said this, hee breathed on them, and saith vnto them, Receiue ye the holy Ghost.
jn.20.23	John 20:23	Whose soeuer sinnes yee remit, they are remitted vnto them, and whose soeuer sinnes yee retaine, they are retained.
jn.20.24	John 20:24	¶ But Thomas one of the twelue, called Didymus, was not with them when Iesus came.
jn.20.25	John 20:25	The other disciples therefore said vnto him, We haue seene the Lord. But he said vnto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nailes, and put my finger into the print of the nailes, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not beleeue.
jn.20.26	John 20:26	¶ And after eight dayes, againe his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: Then came Iesus, the doores being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be vnto you.
jn.20.27	John 20:27	Then saith he to Thomas Reach hither thy finger, and beholde my hands, and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side, and bee not faithlesse, but beleeuing.
jn.20.28	John 20:28	And Thomas answered, and said vnto him, My Lord, and my God.
jn.20.29	John 20:29	Iesus saith vnto him, Thomas, because thou hast seene mee, thou hast beleeued: blessed are they that haue not seene, and yet haue beleeued.
jn.20.30	John 20:30	¶ And many other signes truely did Iesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this booke:
jn.20.31	John 20:31	But these are written, that yee might beleeue that Iesus is the Christ the Sonne of God, and that beleeuing ye might haue life through his Name.
jn.21.1	John 21:1	After these things Iesus shewed himselfe againe to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias, and on this wise shewed he himselfe.
jn.21.2	John 21:2	There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathaneel of Cana in Galilee, and the sonnes of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
jn.21.3	John 21:3	Simon Peter saith vnto them, I goe a fishing. They say vnto him, Wee also goe with thee. They went foorth and entred into a ship immediatly, and that night they caught nothing.
jn.21.4	John 21:4	But when the morning was now come, Iesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knewe not that it was Iesus.
jn.21.5	John 21:5	Then Iesus saith vnto them, Children, haue ye any meat? They answered him, No.
jn.21.6	John 21:6	And he said vnto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and yee shall finde. They cast therfore, and now they were not able to draw it, for the multitude of fishes.
jn.21.7	John 21:7	Therefore that Disciple whome Iesus loued, saith vnto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fishers coate vnto him, (for hee was naked) & did cast himselfe into the sea.
jn.21.8	John 21:8	And the other disciples came in a litle ship (for they were not farre from land, but as it were two hundred cubites) dragging the net with fishes.
jn.21.9	John 21:9	Assoone then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coales there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
jn.21.10	John 21:10	Iesus saith vnto them, Bring of the fish, which ye haue now caught.
jn.21.11	John 21:11	Simon Peter went vp, & drewe the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fiftie and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken.
jn.21.12	John 21:12	Iesus saith vnto them, Come, and dine. And none of the disciples durst aske him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
jn.21.13	John 21:13	Iesus then commeth, and taketh bread, and giueth them, and fish likewise.
jn.21.14	John 21:14	This is nowe the third time that Iesus shewed himselfe to his disciples, after that hee was risen from the dead.
jn.21.15	John 21:15	¶ So when they had dined, Iesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, sonne of Ionas, louest thou mee more then these? He saith vnto him, Yea, Lord, thou knowest that I loue thee. He saith vnto him, Feed my lambes.
jn.21.16	John 21:16	He saith to him againe the second time, Simon sonne of Ionas, louest thou me? He saith vnto him, Yea Lord, thou knowest that I loue thee. He saith vnto him, Feed my sheepe.
jn.21.17	John 21:17	He said vnto him the third time, Simon sonne of Ionas, louest thou mee? Peter was grieued, because hee saide vnto him the third time, Louest thou me? And he said vnto him, Lord, thou knowest all things, thou knowest that I loue thee. Iesus sayth vnto him, Feed my sheepe.
jn.21.18	John 21:18	Uerily, verily I say vnto thee, whē thou wast yong, thou girdedst thy selfe, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carie thee whither thou wouldest not.
jn.21.19	John 21:19	This spake hee, signifying by what death he should glorifie God. And when he had spoken this, he sayth vnto him, Follow me.
jn.21.20	John 21:20	Then Peter turning about, seeth the Disciple whom Iesus loued, following, which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is hee that betraieth thee?
jn.21.21	John 21:21	Peter seeing him, saith to Iesus, Lord, and what shall this man doe?
jn.21.22	John 21:22	Iesus saith vnto him, If I will that he tary till I come, what is that to thee? Follow thou me.
jn.21.23	John 21:23	Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that Disciple should not die: yet Iesus sayd not vnto him, He shall not die: but, If I will that he tary till I come, what is that to thee?
jn.21.24	John 21:24	This is the Disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things, and we know that his testimonie is true.
jn.21.25	John 21:25	And there are also many other things which Iesus did, the which if they should be written euery one, I suppose that euen the world it selfe could not conteine the bookes that should be written, Amen.
ac.1.1	Acts 1:1	The former treatise haue I made, O Theophilus, of al that Iesus began both to doe and teach,
ac.1.2	Acts 1:2	Untill the day in which hee was taken vp, after that he through the holy Ghost had giuen commaundements vnto the Apostles, whom he had chosen.
ac.1.3	Acts 1:3	To whom also he shewed himselfe aliue after his passion, by many infallible proofes, being seene of them fourty dayes, and speaking of the things perteining to the kingdome of God:
ac.1.4	Acts 1:4	And being assembled together with them, commanded them that they should not depart from Hierusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he, ye haue heard of me.
ac.1.5	Acts 1:5	For Iohn truely baptized with water, but ye shall be baptized with the holy Ghost, not many dayes hence.
ac.1.6	Acts 1:6	When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore againe the kingdome to Israel?
ac.1.7	Acts 1:7	And he said vnto them, It is not for you to knowe the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his owne power.
ac.1.8	Acts 1:8	But ye shall receiue power after that the holy Ghost is come vpon you, and ye shall be witnesses vnto me, both in Hierusalem, and in all Iudea, and in Samaria, and vnto the vttermost part of the earth.
ac.1.9	Acts 1:9	And when hee had spoken these things, while they beheld, hee was taken vp, and a cloud receiued him out of their sight.
ac.1.10	Acts 1:10	And while they looked stedfastly toward heauen, as he went vp, behold, two men stood by them in white apparell,
ac.1.11	Acts 1:11	Which also said, Yee men of Galililee, why stand yee gazing vp into heauen? This same Iesus, which is taken vp from you into heauen, shall so come, in like maner as yee haue seene him goe into heauen.
ac.1.12	Acts 1:12	Then returned they vnto Hierusalem, from the mount called Oliuet, which is from Hierusalem a Sabbath dayes iourney.
ac.1.13	Acts 1:13	And when they were come in, they went vp into an vpper roome, where abode both Peter & Iames, & Iohn, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, Iames the sonne of Alpheus, and Simon Zelotes, and Iudas the brother of Iames.
ac.1.14	Acts 1:14	These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Iesus, and with his brethen.
ac.1.15	Acts 1:15	¶ And in those dayes Peter stood vp in the mids of the disciples, and said, (The number of names together were about an hundred and twentie)
ac.1.16	Acts 1:16	Men and brethren, This Scripture must needs haue beene fulfilled, which the holy Ghost by the mouth of Dauid spake before concerning Iudas, which was guide to them þ took Iesus.
ac.1.17	Acts 1:17	For hee was numbred with vs, and had obtained part of this ministerie.
ac.1.18	Acts 1:18	Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity, and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the mids, and all his bowels gushed out.
ac.1.19	Acts 1:19	And it was knowen vnto all the dwellers at Hierusalem, insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.
ac.1.20	Acts 1:20	For it is written in the booke of Psalmes, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: And his Bishopricke let another take.
ac.1.21	Acts 1:21	Wherefore of these men which haue companied with vs all the time that the Lord Iesus went in and out among vs,
ac.1.22	Acts 1:22	Beginning from the baptisme of Iohn, vnto that same day that he was taken vp from vs, must one be ordained to be a witnesse with vs of his resurrection.
ac.1.23	Acts 1:23	And they appointed two, Ioseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Iustus, and Matthias.
ac.1.24	Acts 1:24	And they prayed, and said, Thou Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,
ac.1.25	Acts 1:25	That hee may take part of this ministerie and Apostleship, from which Iudas by transgression fell, that hee might goe to his owne place.
ac.1.26	Acts 1:26	And they gaue foorth their lots, and the lot fell vpon Matthias, and hee was numbred with the eleuen Apostles.
ac.2.1	Acts 2:1	And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.

ac.2.3	Acts 2:3	And there appeared vnto them clouen tongues, like as of fire, and it sate vpon each of them.
ac.2.4	Acts 2:4	And they were all filled with the holy Ghost, and began to speake with other tongues, as the spirit gaue them vtterance.
ac.2.5	Acts 2:5	And there were dwelling at Hierusalem Iewes, deuout men, out of euery nation vnder heauen.
ac.2.6	Acts 2:6	Now when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded, because that euery man heard them speake in his owne language.
ac.2.7	Acts 2:7	And they were all amazed, and marueiled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speake, Galileans?

ac.2.11	Acts 2:11	Cretes, and Arabians, we doe heare them speake in our tongues the wonderfull workes of God.
ac.2.12	Acts 2:12	And they were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying one to another, What meaneth this?
ac.2.13	Acts 2:13	Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine.
ac.2.14	Acts 2:14	¶ But Peter standing vp with the eleuen, lift vp his voyce, and said vnto them, Ye men of Iudea, & all ye that dwell at Hierusalem, be this knowen vnto you, and hearken to my words:
ac.2.15	Acts 2:15	For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third houre of the day.
ac.2.16	Acts 2:16	But this is that which was spoken by the Prophet Ioel,
ac.2.17	Acts 2:17	And it shall come to passe in the last dayes (saith God) I will powre out of my Spirit vpon all flesh: and your sonnes and your daughters shall prophesie, and your yong men shall see visions, and your old men shall dreame dreames:
ac.2.18	Acts 2:18	And on my seruants, and on my handmaidens, I will powre out in those daies of my Spirit, and they shall prophesie:

ac.2.20	Acts 2:20	The Sunne shall be turned into darkenesse, and the Moone into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord come.
ac.2.21	Acts 2:21	And it shall come to passe, that whosoeuer shall call on the Name of the Lord, shalbe saued.
ac.2.22	Acts 2:22	Yee men of Israel, heare these words, Iesus of Nazareth, a man approued of God among you, by miracles, wonders, and signes, which God did by him in the midst of you, as yee your selues also know:
ac.2.23	Acts 2:23	Him, being deliuered by the determinate counsell and foreknowledge of God, yee haue taken, and by wicked hands, haue crucified, and slaine:
ac.2.24	Acts 2:24	Whom God hath raised vp, hauing loosed the paines of death: because it was not possible that hee should be holden of it.
ac.2.25	Acts 2:25	For Dauid speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord alwayes before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moued.
ac.2.26	Acts 2:26	Therefore did my heart reioyce, and my tongue was glad: Moreouer also, my flesh shall rest in hope,
ac.2.27	Acts 2:27	Because thou wilt not leaue my soule in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy one to see corruption.
ac.2.28	Acts 2:28	Thou hast made knowen to mee the wayes of life, thou shalt make mee full of ioy with thy countenance.

ac.3.1	Acts 3:1	Nowe Peter and Iohn went vp together into the Temple at the houre of prayer, beeing the ninth houre.

ac.3.3	Acts 3:3	Who seeing Peter & Iohn about to go into the Temple, asked an almes.
ac.3.4	Acts 3:4	And Peter fastening his eyes vpon him, with Iohn, said, Looke on vs.
ac.3.5	Acts 3:5	And he gaue heede vnto them, expecting to receiue something of them.

ac.3.7	Acts 3:7	And hee tooke him by the right hand, & lift him vp: aud immediatly his feete and ancle bones receiued strength.
ac.3.8	Acts 3:8	And hee leaping vp, stood, and walked, and entred with them into the Temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
ac.3.9	Acts 3:9	And all the people saw him walking, and praising God.
ac.3.10	Acts 3:10	And they knew that it was hee which sate for almes at the beautifull gate of the Temple: and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened vnto him.
ac.3.11	Acts 3:11	And as the lame man which was healed, helde Peter and Iohn, all the people ranne together vnto them in the porch, that is called Solomons, greatly wondring.
ac.3.12	Acts 3:12	¶ And when Peter sawe it, hee answered vnto the people, Yee men of Israel, why marueile ye at this? or why looke yee so earnestly on vs, as though by our owne power or holinesse we had made this man to walke?
ac.3.13	Acts 3:13	The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Iacob, the God of our fathers hath glorified his sonne Iesus, whom ye deliuered vp, and denied him in the presence of Pilate, when hee was determined to let him goe.

ac.4.3	Acts 4:3	And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold vnto the next day: for it was now euentide.
ac.4.4	Acts 4:4	Howbeit, many of them which heard the word, beleeued, and the number of the men was about fiue thousand.
ac.4.5	Acts 4:5	¶ And it came to passe on the morow, that their rulers, and Elders, and Scribes,
ac.4.6	Acts 4:6	And Annas the high Priest, and Caiphas, and Iohn, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kinred of the high Priest, were gathered together at Hierusalem.
ac.4.7	Acts 4:7	And when they had set them in the middest, they asked, By what power, or by what name haue ye done this?
ac.4.8	Acts 4:8	Then Peter filled with the holy Ghost, said vnto them, Ye rulers of the people, and Elders of Israel,
ac.4.9	Acts 4:9	If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what meanes he is made whole,
ac.4.10	Acts 4:10	Be it knowen vnto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the Name of Iesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whome God raised from the dead, euen by him, doeth this man stand here before you, whole.
ac.4.11	Acts 4:11	This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.
ac.4.12	Acts 4:12	Neither is there saluation in any other: for there is none other name vnder heauen giuen among men whereby we must be saued.
ac.4.13	Acts 4:13	¶ Now when they sawe the boldnesse of Peter and Iohn, and perceiued that they were vnlearned and ignorant men, they marueiled, and they tooke knowledge of them, that they had bene with Iesus.
ac.4.14	Acts 4:14	And beholding the man which was healed, standing with them, they could say nothing against it.
ac.4.15	Acts 4:15	But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the Council, they conferred among themselues,
ac.4.16	Acts 4:16	Saying, What shall we do to these men? for that indeed a notable miracle hath bene done by them, is manifest to all them that dwell in Hierusalem, and we cannot denie it.
ac.4.17	Acts 4:17	But that it spread no farther among the people, let vs straitly threaten them, that they speake henceforth to no man in this Name.
ac.4.18	Acts 4:18	And they called them, and commanded them, not to speake at all, nor teach in the Name of Iesus.
ac.4.19	Acts 4:19	But Peter and Iohn answered, and said vnto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God, to hearken vnto you more then vnto God, iudge ye.
ac.4.20	Acts 4:20	For wee cannot but speake the things which we haue seene and heard.
ac.4.21	Acts 4:21	So when they had further threatned them, they let them goe, finding nothing how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified God for that which was done.
ac.4.22	Acts 4:22	For the man was aboue fourtie yeeres olde, on whome this miracle of healing was shewed.
ac.4.23	Acts 4:23	¶ And being let goe, they went to their owne company, and reported all that the chiefe Priests and Elders had said vnto them.
ac.4.24	Acts 4:24	And when they heard that, they lift vp their voyce to God with one accord, & said, Lord, thou art God which hast made heauen and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is,
ac.4.25	Acts 4:25	Who by the mouth of thy seruant Dauid hast saide, Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vaine things?
ac.4.26	Acts 4:26	The Kings of the earth stood vp, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, & against his Christ.
ac.4.27	Acts 4:27	For of a trueth against thy holy child Iesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together,
ac.4.28	Acts 4:28	For to doe whatsoeuer thy hand and thy counsell determined before to be done.
ac.4.29	Acts 4:29	And now Lord, behold their threatnings, and graunt vnto thy seruants, that with all boldnesse they may speake thy word,
ac.4.30	Acts 4:30	By stretching foorth thine hand to heale: and that signes and wonders may be done by the Name of thy holy child Iesus.
ac.4.31	Acts 4:31	¶ And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together, and they were all filled with the holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldnesse.
ac.4.32	Acts 4:32	And the multitude of them that beleeued, were of one heart, and of one soule: Neither said any of them, that ought of the things which he possessed, was his owne, but they had all things common.
ac.4.33	Acts 4:33	And with great power gaue the Apostles witnesse of the resurrection of the Lord Iesus, and great grace was vpon them all.
ac.4.34	Acts 4:34	Neither was there any among them that lacked: For as many as were possessors of lands, or houses, sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were solde,
ac.4.35	Acts 4:35	And laide them downe at the Apostles feete: And distribution was made vnto euery man according as hee had neede.
ac.4.36	Acts 4:36	And Ioses, who by the Apostles was surnamed Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, The sonne of consolation) a Leuite, and of the Countrey of Cyprus,
ac.4.37	Acts 4:37	Hauing land, sold it, and brought the money, & laid it at the Apostles feet.
ac.5.1	Acts 5:1	But a certaine man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, solde a possession,
ac.5.2	Acts 5:2	And kept backe part of the price, his wife also being priuy to it, and brought a certaine part, and layd it at the Apostles feete.
ac.5.3	Acts 5:3	But Peter said, Ananias, Why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the holy Ghost, and to keepe backe part of the price of the land?
ac.5.4	Acts 5:4	Whiles it remained, was it not thine owne? and after it was sold, was it not in thine owne power? why hast thou conceiued this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied vnto men, but vnto God.
ac.5.5	Acts 5:5	And Ananias hearing these words, fell downe, and gaue vp the ghost: and great feare came on all them that heard these things.
ac.5.6	Acts 5:6	And the yong men arose, wound him vp, and caried him out, and buried him.
ac.5.7	Acts 5:7	And it was about the space of three houres after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.
ac.5.8	Acts 5:8	And Peter answered vnto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much. And she saide, Yea, for so much.
ac.5.9	Acts 5:9	Then Peter saide vnto her, How is it that ye haue agreed together, to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feete of them which haue buried thy husband, are at the doore, and shall cary thee out.
ac.5.10	Acts 5:10	Then fell she downe straightway at his feete, and yeelded vp the ghost: And the yong men came in, and found her dead, and carying her forth, buried her by her husband.
ac.5.11	Acts 5:11	And great feare came vpon all the Church, and vpon as many as heard these things.
ac.5.12	Acts 5:12	¶ And by the hands of the Apostles, were many signes and wonders wrought among the people. (And they were all with one accord in Solomons porch.
ac.5.13	Acts 5:13	And of the rest durst no man ioyne himselfe to them: But the people magnified them.
ac.5.14	Acts 5:14	And beleeuers were the more added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and women.)
ac.5.15	Acts 5:15	Insomuch þ they brought foorth the sicke into the streetes, and layed them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by, might ouershadow some of them.
ac.5.16	Acts 5:16	There came also a multitude out of the cities round about vnto Hierusalem, bringing sicke folkes, and them which were vexed with vncleane spirits: and they were healed euery one.
ac.5.17	Acts 5:17	¶ Then the high Priest rose vp, and al they that were with him, (which is the sect of the Sadduces) and were filled with indignation,
ac.5.18	Acts 5:18	And laid their hands on the Apostles, & put them in the common prison.
ac.5.19	Acts 5:19	But the Angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doores, and brought them foorth, and said,
ac.5.20	Acts 5:20	Goe, stand and speake in the Temple to the people all the words of this life.
ac.5.21	Acts 5:21	And when they heard that, they entred into the Temple early in the morning, & taught: but the high Priest came, and they that were with him, and called the Councill together, and all the Senate of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to haue them brought.
ac.5.22	Acts 5:22	But when the officers came, and found them not in the prison, they returned, and told,
ac.5.23	Acts 5:23	Saying, The prison truely found we shut with all safety, and the keepers standing without before the doores, but when we had opened, we found no man within.
ac.5.24	Acts 5:24	Now when the high Priest, and the captaine of the Temple, and the chiefe Priests heard these things, they doubted of them wherunto this would grow.
ac.5.25	Acts 5:25	Then came one, and told them, saying, Behold, the men whom ye put in prison, are standing in the Temple, and teaching the people.
ac.5.26	Acts 5:26	Then went the captaine with the officers, and brought them without violence: (For they feared the people, lest they should haue bene stoned.)
ac.5.27	Acts 5:27	And when they had brought them, they set them before the Councill, and the high Priest asked them,
ac.5.28	Acts 5:28	Saying, Did not wee straitly command you, that you should not teach in this Name? And behold, yee haue filled Hierusalem with your doctrine, and intend to bring this mans blood vpon vs.
ac.5.29	Acts 5:29	¶ Then Peter, and the other Apostles answered, and saide, Wee ought to obey God rather then men.
ac.5.30	Acts 5:30	The God of our fathers raised vp Iesus, whom yee slew and hanged on a tree.
ac.5.31	Acts 5:31	Him hath God exalted with his right hand to bee a Prince and a Sauiour, for to giue repentance to Israel, and forgiuenesse of sinnes.
ac.5.32	Acts 5:32	And we are his witnesses of these things, and so is also the holy Ghost, whom God hath giuen to them that obey him.
ac.5.33	Acts 5:33	¶ When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and tooke counsell to slay them.
ac.5.34	Acts 5:34	Then stood there vp one in the Councill, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctour of Law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded to put the Apostles forth a litle space,
ac.5.35	Acts 5:35	And said vnto them, Yee men of Israel, take heed to your selues, what ye intend to doe as touching these men.
ac.5.36	Acts 5:36	For before these dayes rose vp Theudas, boasting himselfe to be some body, to whom a number of men, about foure hundred, ioyned themselues: who was slaine, and all, as many as obeied him, were scattered, & brought to nought.
ac.5.37	Acts 5:37	After this man rose vp Iudas of Galilee, in the dayes of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: hee also perished, and all, euen as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.
ac.5.38	Acts 5:38	And now I say vnto you, refraine from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsell or this worke be of men, it will come to nought.
ac.5.39	Acts 5:39	But if it be of God, ye cannot ouerthrow it, lest haply yee be found euen to fight against God.
ac.5.40	Acts 5:40	And to him they agreed: and when they had called the Apostles, and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speake in the Name of Iesus, and let them goe.
ac.5.41	Acts 5:41	¶ And they departed from the presence of the Councill, reioycing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his Name.
ac.5.42	Acts 5:42	And dayly in the Temple, and in euery house, they ceased not to teach and preach Iesus Christ.
ac.6.1	Acts 6:1	And in those dayes when the number of the Disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrewes, because their widowes were neglected in the daily ministration.
ac.6.2	Acts 6:2	Then the twelue called the multitude of the disciples vnto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leaue the word of God, and serue tables.
ac.6.3	Acts 6:3	Wherefore brethren, looke ye out among you seuen men of honest report, full of the holy Ghost, and wisedome, whom we may appoint ouer this businesse.
ac.6.4	Acts 6:4	But we will giue our selues continually to prayer, and to the ministerie of the word.
ac.6.5	Acts 6:5	¶ And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Steuen, a man full of faith and of the holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Permenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch.
ac.6.6	Acts 6:6	Whom they set before the Apostles: and when they had praied, they layd their hands on them.
ac.6.7	Acts 6:7	And the word of God encreased, and the number of the Disciples multiplied in Hierusalem greatly, and a great company of the Priests were obedient to the faith.
ac.6.8	Acts 6:8	And Steuen full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people.
ac.6.9	Acts 6:9	¶ Then there arose certaine of the Synagogue, which is called the Synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia, and of Asia, disputing with Steuen.
ac.6.10	Acts 6:10	And they were not able to resist the wisedome and the spirit by which he spake.
ac.6.11	Acts 6:11	Then they suborned men which said, We haue heard him speake blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.
ac.6.12	Acts 6:12	And they stirred vp the people, and the Elders, and the Scribes, and came vpon him, and caught him, and brought him to the Councell,
ac.6.13	Acts 6:13	And set vp false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speake blasphemous words against this holy place, and the Law.
ac.6.14	Acts 6:14	For we haue heard him say, that this Iesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place, & shall change the Customes which Moses deliuered vs.
ac.6.15	Acts 6:15	And all that sate in the Councell, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had bene the face of an Angel.
ac.7.1	Acts 7:1	Then said the high Priest, Are these things so?
ac.7.2	Acts 7:2	And hee said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken: The God of glory appeared vnto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,
ac.7.3	Acts 7:3	And said vnto him, Get thee out of thy countrey, and from thy kinred, and come into the land which I shall shew thee.
ac.7.4	Acts 7:4	Then came he out of the land of the Chaldeans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he remoued him into this lande wherein ye now dwell.
ac.7.5	Acts 7:5	And he gaue him none inheritance in it, no not so much as to set his foote on: yet he promised that he would giue it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him, when as yet he had no child.
ac.7.6	Acts 7:6	And God spake on this wise, that his seede should soiourne in a strange land, and that they should bring them into bondage, and intreate them euill foure hundreth yeeres.
ac.7.7	Acts 7:7	And the nation to whom they shal bee in bondage, will I iudge, saide God: And after that shall they come forth, and serue me in this place.
ac.7.8	Acts 7:8	And he gaue him the couenant of Circumcision: and so Abraham begate Isaac, and circumcised him the eight day: and Isaac begate Iacob, and Iacob begate the twelue Patriarchs.
ac.7.9	Acts 7:9	And the Patriarchs moued with enuie, sold Ioseph into Egypt: but God was with him,
ac.7.10	Acts 7:10	And deliuered him out of all his afflictions, and gaue him fauour and wisedome in the sight of Pharao king of Egypt: and he made him gouernour ouer Egypt and all his house.
ac.7.11	Acts 7:11	Now there came a dearth ouer all the land of Egypt, and Chanaan, and great affliction, and our fathers found no sustenance.
ac.7.12	Acts 7:12	But when Iacob heard that there was corne in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.
ac.7.13	Acts 7:13	And at the second time Ioseph was made knowen to his brethren, and Iosephs kinred was made knowen vnto Pharao.
ac.7.14	Acts 7:14	Then sent Ioseph, and called his father Iacob to him, and all his kinred, threescore and fifteeene soules.
ac.7.15	Acts 7:15	So Iacob went downe into Egypt, and died, he and our fathers,
ac.7.16	Acts 7:16	And were caried ouer into Sichem, and laid in the sepulchre that Abraham bought for a summe of money of the sonnes of Emor the father of Sichem.
ac.7.17	Acts 7:17	But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which God had sworne to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
ac.7.18	Acts 7:18	Till another king arose, which knew not Ioseph.
ac.7.19	Acts 7:19	The same dealt subtilly with our kinred, and euill intreated our fathers, so that they cast out their yong children, to the end they might not liue.
ac.7.20	Acts 7:20	In which time Moses was borne, and was exceeding faire, and nourished vp in his fathers house three moneths:
ac.7.21	Acts 7:21	And when he was cast out, Pharaohs daughter tooke him vp, and nourished him for her owne sonne.
ac.7.22	Acts 7:22	And Moses was learned in all the wisedome of the Egyptians, and was mightie in words and in deeds.
ac.7.23	Acts 7:23	And when he was full forty yeres old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.
ac.7.24	Acts 7:24	And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and auenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian:
ac.7.25	Acts 7:25	For he supposed his brethren would haue vnderstood, how that God by his hand would deliuer them, but they vnderstood not.
ac.7.26	Acts 7:26	And the next day he shewed himselfe vnto them as they stroue, and would haue set them at one againe, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren, Why doe yee wrong one to another?
ac.7.27	Acts 7:27	But hee that did his neighbour wrong, thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a Iudge ouer vs?
ac.7.28	Acts 7:28	Wilt thou kill me, as thou diddest the Egyptian yesterday?
ac.7.29	Acts 7:29	Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begate two sonnes.
ac.7.30	Acts 7:30	And when fourtie yeeres were expired, there appeared to him in the wildernes of mount Sina, an Angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.
ac.7.31	Acts 7:31	When Moses saw it, he wondred at the sight: and as he drew neere to behold it, the voyce of the Lord came vnto him,
ac.7.32	Acts 7:32	Saying, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Iacob. Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.
ac.7.33	Acts 7:33	Then said the Lord to him, Put off thy shooes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest, is holy ground.
ac.7.34	Acts 7:34	I haue seene, I haue seene the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I haue heard their groning, & am come downe to deliuer them: And now come, I will send thee into Egypt.
ac.7.35	Acts 7:35	This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a Iudge? the same did God send to bee a ruler and a deliuerer, by the handes of the Angel which appeared to him in the bush.
ac.7.36	Acts 7:36	He brought them out, after that he had shewed wonders and signes in the land of Egypt, and in the red Sea, and in the wildernesse fortie yeeres.
ac.7.37	Acts 7:37	¶ This is that Moses which said vnto the children of Israel, A Prophet shall the Lord your God raise vp vnto you of your brethren, like vnto mee: him shall ye heare.
ac.7.38	Acts 7:38	This is he that was in þ Church in the wildernesse with the Angel, which spake to him in the mount Sina, and with our fathers: who receiued the liuely oracles, to giue vnto vs.
ac.7.39	Acts 7:39	To whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned backe againe into Egypt,
ac.7.40	Acts 7:40	Saying vnto Aaron, Make vs gods to goe before vs. For as for this Moses, which brought vs out of the land of Egypt, we wote not what is become of him.
ac.7.41	Acts 7:41	And they made a calfe in those dayes, and offered sacrifice vnto the idole, and reioyced in the workes of their owne hands.
ac.7.42	Acts 7:42	Then God turned, and gaue them vp to worship the hoste of heauen, as it is written in the booke of the Prophets, O ye house of Israel, haue ye offered to me slaine beasts, and sacrifices, by the space of fourty yeeres in the wildernesse?
ac.7.43	Acts 7:43	Yea, ye tooke vp the Tabernacle of Moloch, and the starre of your God Remphan, figures which ye made, to worship them: and I will carie you away beyond Babylon.
ac.7.44	Acts 7:44	Our fathers had the Tabernacle of witnesse in the wildernesse, as hee had appointed, speaking vnto Moses, that he should make it according to the fashion that he had seene.
ac.7.45	Acts 7:45	Which also our fathers that came after, brought in with Iesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom God draue out before the face of our fathers, vnto the dayes of Dauid,
ac.7.46	Acts 7:46	Who found fauour before God, and desired to find a Tabernacle for the God of Iacob.
ac.7.47	Acts 7:47	But Solomon built him an house.
ac.7.48	Acts 7:48	Howbeit the most high dwelleth not in temples made with hands, as saith the Prophet,
ac.7.49	Acts 7:49	Heauen is my throne, and earth is my footestoole: What house will ye build me, saith the Lord? Or what is the place of my rest?
ac.7.50	Acts 7:50	Hath not my hand made all these things?
ac.7.51	Acts 7:51	¶ Ye stifnecked and vncircumcised in heart, and eares, ye doe alwayes resist the holy Ghost? as your fathers did, so doe ye.
ac.7.52	Acts 7:52	Which of the Prophets haue not your fathers persecuted? And they haue slaine them which shewed before of the comming of the Iust one, of whom ye haue bene now the betrayers and murderers:
ac.7.53	Acts 7:53	Who haue receiued the Lawe by the disposition of Angels, and haue not kept it.
ac.7.54	Acts 7:54	¶ When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.
ac.7.55	Acts 7:55	But hee being full of the holy Ghost, looked vp stedfastly into heauen, and saw the glory of God, and Iesus standing on the right hand of God,
ac.7.56	Acts 7:56	And said, Behold, I see the heauens opened, and the Sonne of man standing on the right hand of God.
ac.7.57	Acts 7:57	Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their eares, and ran vpon him with one accord,
ac.7.58	Acts 7:58	And cast him out of the citie, and stoned him: and the witnesses layd downe their clothes at a yong mans feete, whose name was Saul.
ac.7.59	Acts 7:59	And they stoned Steuen, calling vpon God, and saying, Lord Iesus receiue my spirit.
ac.7.60	Acts 7:60	And he kneeled downe, and cried with a loud voice, Lord lay not this sinne to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleepe.
ac.8.1	Acts 8:1	And Saul was consenting vnto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the Church which was at Hierusalem, and they were all scattered abroad through out the regions of Iudea, and Samaria, except the Apostles.
ac.8.2	Acts 8:2	And deuout men carried Steuen to his buriall, and made great lamentation ouer him.
ac.8.3	Acts 8:3	As for Saul, he made hauocke of the Church, entring into euery house, and hailing men and women, committed them to prison.
ac.8.4	Acts 8:4	Therefore they that were scattered abroad, went euery where preaching the word.
ac.8.5	Acts 8:5	Then Philip went downe to the citie of Samaria, and preached Christ vnto them.
ac.8.6	Acts 8:6	And the people with one accord gaue heed vnto those things which Philip spake, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.
ac.8.7	Acts 8:7	For vncleane spirits, crying with lowd voyce, came out of many that were possessed with them: and many taken with palsies, and that were lame, were healed.
ac.8.8	Acts 8:8	And there was great ioy in that citie.
ac.8.9	Acts 8:9	But there was a certaine man called Simon, which before time in the same citie vsed sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria, giuing out that himselfe was some great one.
ac.8.10	Acts 8:10	To whom they all gaue heed from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God.
ac.8.11	Acts 8:11	And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.
ac.8.12	Acts 8:12	But when they beleeued Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdome of God, and the Name of Iesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
ac.8.13	Acts 8:13	Then Simon himselfe beleeued also: and when hee was baptized, hee continued with Philip, and wondered, beholding the miracles and signes which were done.
ac.8.14	Acts 8:14	Now when the Apostles which were at Hierusalem, heard that Samaria had receiued the word of God, they sent vnto them Peter and Iohn.
ac.8.15	Acts 8:15	Who when they were come downe, praied for them that they might receiue the holy Ghost.
ac.8.16	Acts 8:16	(For as yet hee was fallen vpon none of them: onely they were baptized in the Name of the Lord Iesus.)
ac.8.17	Acts 8:17	Then layde they their hands on them, and they receiued the holy Ghost.
ac.8.18	Acts 8:18	And when Simon saw that through laying on of the Apostles hands, the holy Ghost was giuen, hee offered them money,
ac.8.19	Acts 8:19	Saying, Giue me also this power, that on whomsoeuer I lay handes, hee may receiue the holy Ghost.
ac.8.20	Acts 8:20	But Peter said vnto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

ac.8.27	Acts 8:27	And hee arose, and went: and behold, a man of Ethiopia, an Eunuch of great authority vnder Candace queene of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Hierusalem for to worship,
ac.8.28	Acts 8:28	Was returning, and sitting in his charet, read Esaias the Prophet.

ac.8.30	Acts 8:30	And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him reade the Prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?
ac.8.31	Acts 8:31	And hee said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip, that hee would come vp, and sit with him.
ac.8.32	Acts 8:32	The place of the Scripture, which hee read, was this, Hee was led as a sheepe to the slaughter, & like a Lambe dumbe before the shearer, so opened he not his mouth:
ac.8.33	Acts 8:33	In his humiliation, his Iudgement was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? For his life is taken from the earth.
ac.8.34	Acts 8:34	And the Eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the Prophet this? of himselfe, or of some other man?
ac.8.35	Acts 8:35	Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same Scripture, and preached vnto him Iesus.
ac.8.36	Acts 8:36	And as they went on their way, they came vnto a certaine water: and the Eunuch said, See, here is water, what doeth hinder me to be baptized?
ac.8.37	Acts 8:37	And Philip said, If thou beleeuest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered, and said, I beleeue that Iesus Christ is the Sonne of God.
ac.8.38	Acts 8:38	And he commanded the charet to stand still: and they went downe both into the water, both Philip, and the Eunuch, and he baptized him.

ac.9.1	Acts 9:1	And Saul yet breathing out threatnings & slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went vnto the high Priest,

ac.9.6	Acts 9:6	And he trembling and astonished, said, Lord, what wilt thou haue mee to doe? And the Lord said vnto him, Arise, and goe into the citie, and it shall be told thee what thou must doe.

ac.9.18	Acts 9:18	And immediatly there fell from his eyes as it had bene scales, and he receiued sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

ac.9.21	Acts 9:21	But all that heard him, were amazed, and said, Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this Name in Hierusalem, and came hither for that intent that he might bring them bound vnto the chiefe Priests?

ac.9.24	Acts 9:24	But their laying awaite was knowen of Saul: and they watched the gates day and night to kill him.
ac.9.25	Acts 9:25	Then the disciples tooke him by night, and let him downe by the wall in a basket.

ac.9.27	Acts 9:27	But Barnabas tooke him, and brought him to the Apostles, and declared vnto them how hee had seene the Lord in the way, and that hee had spoken to him, and how hee had preached boldly at Damascus in the Name of Iesus.
ac.9.28	Acts 9:28	And he was with them comming in, and going out at Hierusalem.

ac.9.30	Acts 9:30	Which when the brethren knewe, they brought him downe to Cesarea, and sent him foorth to Tarsus.
ac.9.31	Acts 9:31	Then had the Churches rest thorowout all Iudea, and Galilee, and Samaria, and were edified, and walking in the feare of the Lord, and in the comfort of the holy Ghost, were multiplied.

ac.9.33	Acts 9:33	And there he found a certaine man named Aeneas, which had kept his bed eight yeeres, and was sicke of the palsie.

ac.9.37	Acts 9:37	And it came to passe in those dayes that she was sicke, and died: whome when they had washed, they laid her in an vpper chamber.

ac.10.1	Acts 10:1	There was a certaine man in Cesarea, called Cornelius, a Centurion of þ band called the Italian band,

ac.11.4	Acts 11:4	But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order vnto them, saying,
ac.11.5	Acts 11:5	I was in the citie of Ioppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision, a certaine vessell descend, as it had beene a great sheete, let downe from heauen by foure corners, and it came euen to me.

ac.11.7	Acts 11:7	And I heard a voyce, saying vnto me, Arise Peter, slay, and eate.

ac.12.1	Acts 12:1	Now about that time, Herode the King stretched foorth his hands, to vexe certaine of the Church.
ac.12.2	Acts 12:2	And he killed Iames the brother of Iohn with the sword.
ac.12.3	Acts 12:3	And because he saw it pleased the Iewes, hee proceeded further, to take Peter also. (Then were the dayes of vnleauened bread.)
ac.12.4	Acts 12:4	And when hee had apprehended him, hee put him in prison, and deliuered him to foure quaternions of souldiers to keepe him, intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people.
ac.12.5	Acts 12:5	Peter therefore was kept in prison, but prayer was made without ceasing of the Church vnto God for him.
ac.12.6	Acts 12:6	And when Herode would haue brought him foorth, the same night Peter was sleeping betweene two Souldiers, bound with two chaines, and the Keepers before the doore kept the prison.
ac.12.7	Acts 12:7	And beholde, the Angel of the Lord came vpon him, and a light shined in the prison: and hee smote Peter on the side, and raised him vp, saying, Arise vp quickely. And his chaines fell off from his hands.
ac.12.8	Acts 12:8	And the Angel said vnto him, Girde thy selfe, and binde on thy sandales: And so he did. And he sayth vnto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.
ac.12.9	Acts 12:9	And hee went out, and followed him, and wist not that it was true which was done by the Angel: but thought he saw a vision.

ac.12.11	Acts 12:11	And when Peter was come to himselfe, hee said, Now I know of a suretie, that the Lord hath sent his Angel, and hath deliuered mee out of the hand of Herode, and from all the expectation of the people of the Iewes.
ac.12.12	Acts 12:12	And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of Iohn whose sirname was Marke, where many were gathered together praying.
ac.12.13	Acts 12:13	And as Peter knocked at the doore of the gate, a damosell came to hearken, named Rhoda.

ac.12.16	Acts 12:16	But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened the doore, and saw him, they were astonished.
ac.12.17	Acts 12:17	But he beckening vnto them with the hand, to hold their peace, declared vnto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison: And he said, Goe shew these things vnto Iames, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.
ac.12.18	Acts 12:18	Now assoone as it was day, there was no smal stirre among the souldiers, what was become of Peter.

ac.12.20	Acts 12:20	¶ And Herode was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: but they came with one accord to him, and hauing made Blastus the kings chamberlaine their friend, desired peace, because their countrey was nourished by the kings countrey.
ac.12.21	Acts 12:21	And vpon a set day Herod arayed in royall apparell, sate vpon his throne, and made an Oration vnto them.
ac.12.22	Acts 12:22	And the people gaue a shout, saying, It is the voice of a God, and not of a man.

ac.12.24	Acts 12:24	¶ But the word of God grewe, and multiplied.

ac.13.1	Acts 13:1	Nowe there were in the Church that was at Antioch, certaine Prophets and teachers: as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, which had bene brought vp with Herod the Tetrarch, and Saul.
ac.13.2	Acts 13:2	As they ministred to the Lord, and fasted, the holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul, for the worke whereunto I haue called them.
ac.13.3	Acts 13:3	And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their handes on them, they sent them away.
ac.13.4	Acts 13:4	¶ So they being sent forth by the holy Ghost, departed vnto Seleucia, and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.

ac.13.6	Acts 13:6	And when they had gone thorow the Ile vnto Paphos, they found a certaine sorcerer, a false prophet, a Iewe, whose name was Bariesus:
ac.13.7	Acts 13:7	Which was with the deputie of the countrey Sergius Paulus, a prudent man: who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to heare the word of God.
ac.13.8	Acts 13:8	But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turne away the deputy from the faith.
ac.13.9	Acts 13:9	Then Saul (who also is called Paul) filled with the holy Ghost, set his eyes on him,
ac.13.10	Acts 13:10	And said, O full of all subtilty and all mischiefe, thou child of the deuil, thou enemie of all righteousnesse, wilt thou not cease to peruert the right wayes of the Lord?
ac.13.11	Acts 13:11	And now behold, the hand of the Lord is vpon thee, & thou shalt be blind, not seeing the Sunne for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkenes, and he went about, seeking some to lead him by the hand.
ac.13.12	Acts 13:12	Then the Deputie when he sawe what was done, beleeued, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.
ac.13.13	Acts 13:13	Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia: and Iohn departing from them, returned to Hierusalem.
ac.13.14	Acts 13:14	¶ But when they departed from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia, and went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and sate downe.
ac.13.15	Acts 13:15	And after the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent vnto them, saying, Ye men and brethren, if ye haue any word of exhortation for the people, say on.

ac.13.18	Acts 13:18	And about the time of fourtie yeeres suffered he their maners in the wildernesse.
ac.13.19	Acts 13:19	And when he had destroyed seuen nations in the land of Chanaan, he diuided their land to them by lot:
ac.13.20	Acts 13:20	And after that he gaue vnto them iudges, about the space of foure hundred and fifty yeeres vntill Samuel the Prophet.
ac.13.21	Acts 13:21	And afterward they desired a King, and God gaue vnto them Saul the sonne of Cis, a man of the tribe of Beniamin, by the space of fourty yeres.
ac.13.22	Acts 13:22	And when he had remoued him, hee raised vp vnto them Dauid to be their king, to whom also he gaue testimonie, and said, I haue found Dauid the sonne of Iesse, a man after mine own heart, which shal fulfill all my wil.
ac.13.23	Acts 13:23	Of this mans seed hath God, according to his promise, raised vnto Israel a Sauiour, Iesus:
ac.13.24	Acts 13:24	When Iohn had first preached before his coming, the baptisme of repentance to all the people of Israel.

ac.13.26	Acts 13:26	Men and brethren, children of the stocke of Abraham, and whosoeuer among you feareth God, to you is the word of this saluation sent.

ac.13.30	Acts 13:30	But God raised him frō the dead:

ac.13.32	Acts 13:32	And we declare vnto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made vnto the fathers,

ac.13.37	Acts 13:37	But hee whom God raised againe, saw no corruption.
ac.13.38	Acts 13:38	¶ Be it knowen vnto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached vnto you the forgiuenesse of sinnes.
ac.13.39	Acts 13:39	And by him all þ beleeue, are iustified from all things, from which ye could not be iustified by the Law of Moses.
ac.13.40	Acts 13:40	Beware therefore, least that come vpon you which is spoken of in the Prophets,
ac.13.41	Acts 13:41	Behold, yee despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I worke a worke in your dayes, a worke which you shall in no wise beleeue, though a man declare it vnto you.
ac.13.42	Acts 13:42	And when the Iewes were gone out of the Synagogue, the Gentiles besought that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath.
ac.13.43	Acts 13:43	Now when the Congregation was broken vp, many of the Iewes, and religious Proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who speaking to them, perswaded them to continue in the grace of God.
ac.13.44	Acts 13:44	¶ And the next Sabbath day came almost the whole citie together to heare the word of God.
ac.13.45	Acts 13:45	But when the Iewes saw the multitudes, they were filled with enuie, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting, and blaspheming.
ac.13.46	Acts 13:46	Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first haue bene spoken to you: but seeing yee put it from you, and iudge your selues vnworthy of euerlasting life, loe, we turne to the Gentiles.
ac.13.47	Acts 13:47	For so hath the Lord cōmanded vs, saying, I haue set thee to bee a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for saluation vnto the ends of the earth.
ac.13.48	Acts 13:48	And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordeined to eternall life, beleeued.
ac.13.49	Acts 13:49	And the word of the Lord was published throughout all the region.
ac.13.50	Acts 13:50	But the Iewes stirred vp the deuout and honourable women, and the chiefe men of the citie, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their coasts.
ac.13.51	Acts 13:51	But they shooke off the dust of their feete against them, and came vnto Iconium.
ac.13.52	Acts 13:52	And the disciples were filled with ioy, and with the holy Ghost.
ac.14.1	Acts 14:1	And it came to passe in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Iewes, and so spake, that a great multitude both of the Iewes, and also of the Greekes, beleeued.
ac.14.2	Acts 14:2	But the vnbeleeuing Iewes stirred vp the Gentiles, and made their mindes euill affected against the brethren.
ac.14.3	Acts 14:3	Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gaue testimonie vnto the word of his grace, and granted signes and wonders to be done by their hands.
ac.14.4	Acts 14:4	But the multitude of the city was diuided: and part held with the Iewes, and part with the Apostles.
ac.14.5	Acts 14:5	And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Iewes, with their rulers, to vse them despitefully, and to stone them,

ac.14.8	Acts 14:8	¶ And there sate a certaine man at Lystra, impotent in his feete, being a creeple from his mothers wombe, who neuer had walked.

ac.14.11	Acts 14:11	And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lift vp their voyces, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come downe to vs in the likenesse of men.
ac.14.12	Acts 14:12	And they called Barnabas Iupiter, and Paul Mercurius, because hee was the chiefe speaker.
ac.14.13	Acts 14:13	Then the priest of Iupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen, and garlands vnto the gates, and would haue done sacrifice with the people.

ac.14.16	Acts 14:16	Who in times past, suffred all nations to walke in their owne wayes.
ac.14.17	Acts 14:17	Neuerthelesse, he left not himselfe without witnesse, in that he did good, and gaue vs raine from heauen, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladnesse.

ac.14.19	Acts 14:19	¶ And there came thither certaine Iewes from Antioch and Iconium, who perswaded the people, and hauing stoned Paul, drew him out of the citie, supposing he had beene dead.

ac.14.22	Acts 14:22	Confirming the soules of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, aud that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdome of God.

ac.15.24	Acts 15:24	Forasmuch as we haue heard, that certaine which went out from vs, haue troubled you with words, subuerting your soules, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keepe the Law, to whom we gaue no such commandement:
