ac.17.5	Acts 17:5	¶ But the Iewes which beleeued not, mooued with enuie, tooke vnto them certaine lewd fellowes of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the citie on an vprore, and assaulted the house of Iason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
ac.17.6	Acts 17:6	And when they found them not, they drew Iason, and certaine brethren vnto the rulers of the citie, crying, These that haue turned the world vpside downe, are come hither also,
ac.17.7	Acts 17:7	Whom Iason hath receiued: and these all doe contrary to the decrees of Cesar, saying, that there is another King, one Iesus.
ac.17.8	Acts 17:8	And they troubled the people, and the rulers of the citie, when they heard these things.
ac.17.9	Acts 17:9	And when they had taken securitie of Iason, and of the other, they let them goe.
ac.17.10	Acts 17:10	¶ And the brethren immediatly sent away Paul and Silas by night vnto Berea: who comming thither, went into the Synagogue of the Iewes.
ac.17.11	Acts 17:11	These were more noble then those in Thessalonica, in that they receiued the word with all readinesse of minde, and searched the Scriptures dayly, whether those things were so.
ac.17.12	Acts 17:12	Therefore many of them beleeued: also of honourable women which were Greekes, and of men not a few.
ac.17.13	Acts 17:13	But when the Iewes of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred vp the people.
ac.17.14	Acts 17:14	And then immediatly the brethren sent away Paul, to goe as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
ac.17.15	Acts 17:15	And they that conducted Paul, brought him vnto Athens, and receiuing a commaundement vnto Silas and Timotheus, for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
ac.17.16	Acts 17:16	¶ Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when hee saw the city wholy giuen to idolatrie.
ac.17.17	Acts 17:17	Therefore disputed he in the Synagogue with the Iewes, and with the deuout persons, and in the market dayly with them that met with him.
ac.17.18	Acts 17:18	Then certaine Philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoikes, encountred him: and some said, What will this babbler say? Othersome, He seemeth to be a setter foorth of strange gods: because hee preached vnto them Iesus, and the resurrection.
ac.17.19	Acts 17:19	And they tooke him, and brought him vnto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
ac.17.20	Acts 17:20	For thou bringest certaine strange things to our eares: we would know therefore what these things meane.
ac.17.21	Acts 17:21	(For all the Athenians and strangers which were there, spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to heare some new thing.)
ac.17.22	Acts 17:22	¶ Then Paul stood in the mids of Mars-hill, and said, Yee men of Athens, I perceiue that in all things yee are too superstitious.
ac.17.23	Acts 17:23	For as I passed by, and beheld your deuotions, I found an Altar with this inscription, TO THE VNKNOWEN GOD. Whom therefore yee ignorantly worship, him declare I vnto you.
ac.17.24	Acts 17:24	God that made the world, and all things therein, seeing that hee is Lord of heauen and earth, dwelleth not in Temples made with hands:
ac.17.25	Acts 17:25	Neither is worshipped with mens hands as though he needed any thing, seeing hee giueth to all, life and breath, and all things,
ac.17.26	Acts 17:26	And hath made of one blood all nations of men, for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation:
ac.17.27	Acts 17:27	That they should seeke the Lord, if haply they might feele after him and finde him, though he be not farre from euery one of vs.
ac.17.28	Acts 17:28	For in him we liue, and mooue, and haue our being, as certaine also of your owne Poets haue said, For we are also his offspring.
ac.17.29	Acts 17:29	Forasmuch then as wee are the offspring of God, wee ought not to thinke that the Godhead is like vnto golde, or siluer, or stone grauen by arte, and mans deuice.
ac.17.30	Acts 17:30	And the times of this ignorance God winked at, but now commandeth all men euery where to repent:
ac.17.31	Acts 17:31	Because hee hath appointed a day in the which he will iudge the world in righteousnesse, by that man whom hee hath ordeined, whereof he hath giuen assurance vnto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
ac.17.32	Acts 17:32	¶ And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, Wee will heare thee againe of this matter.
ac.17.33	Acts 17:33	So Paul departed from among them.
ac.17.34	Acts 17:34	Howbeit, certaine men claue vnto him, and beleeued: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
ac.18.1	Acts 18:1	After these things, Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth,
ac.18.2	Acts 18:2	And found a certaine Iewe named Aquila, borne in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla, (because that Claudius had commanded all Iewes to depart from Rome) and came vnto them.
ac.18.3	Acts 18:3	And because hee was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought (for by their occupation they were tentmakers.)
ac.18.4	Acts 18:4	And hee reasoned in the Synagogue euery Sabbath, and perswaded the Iewes, and the Greekes.
ac.18.5	Acts 18:5	And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in spirit, and testified to the Iewes, that Iesus was Christ.
ac.18.6	Acts 18:6	And when they opposed themselues, and blasphemed, he shooke his raiment, and said vnto them, Your blood be vpon your owne heads, I am cleane: from henceforth I will goe vnto the Gentiles.
ac.18.7	Acts 18:7	¶ And hee departed thence, and entred into a certaine mans house, named Iustus, one that worshipped God, whose house ioyned hard to the Synagogue.
ac.18.8	Acts 18:8	And Crispus, the chiefe ruler of the Synagogue, beleeued on the Lord, with all his house: and many of the Corinthians, hearing, beleeued, and were baptized.
ac.18.9	Acts 18:9	Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speake, and holde not thy peace:
ac.18.10	Acts 18:10	For I am with thee, and no man shal set on thee, to hurt thee: for I haue much people in this city.
ac.18.11	Acts 18:11	And hee continued there a yeere and sixe monethes, teaching the word of God among them.
ac.18.12	Acts 18:12	¶ And when Gallio was the Deputie of Achaia, the Iewes made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the iudgement seat,
ac.18.13	Acts 18:13	Saying, This fellow perswadeth men to worship God contrary to the Law.
ac.18.14	Acts 18:14	And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said vnto the Iewes, If it were a matter of wrong, or wicked lewdnesse, O yee Iewes, reason would that I should beare with you.
ac.18.15	Acts 18:15	But if it be a question of words, and names, and of your law, looke ye to it: for I wil be no iudge of such matters.
ac.18.16	Acts 18:16	And he draue them from the iudgment seate.
ac.18.17	Acts 18:17	Then all the Greekes tooke Sosthenes the chiefe ruler of the Synagogue, and beat him before the Iudgement seat: and Gallio cared for none of those things.
ac.18.18	Acts 18:18	¶ And Paul after this taried there yet a good while, and then tooke his leaue of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila: hauing shorne his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
ac.18.19	Acts 18:19	And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himselfe entred into the Synagogue, and reasoned with the Iewes.
ac.18.20	Acts 18:20	When they desired him to tary longer time with them, hee consented not:
ac.18.21	Acts 18:21	But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all meanes keepe this feast that commeth, in Hierusalem; but I will returne againe vnto you, if God will: and he sailed from Ephesus.
ac.18.22	Acts 18:22	And when he had landed at Cesarea, and gone vp, and saluted the Church, he went downe to Antioch.
ac.18.23	Acts 18:23	And after he had spent some time there, hee departed, and went ouer all the countrey of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
ac.18.24	Acts 18:24	¶ And a certaine Iew, named Apollos, borne at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mightie in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus.
ac.18.25	Acts 18:25	This man was instructed in the way of the Lord, and being feruent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing onely the baptisme of Iohn.
ac.18.26	Acts 18:26	And he began to speake boldly in the Synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they tooke him vnto them, and expounded vnto him the way of God more perfectly.
ac.18.27	Acts 18:27	And when hee was disposed to passe into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receiue him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had beleeued throgh grace.
ac.18.28	Acts 18:28	For hee mightily conuinced the Iewes, and that publikely, shewing by the scriptures, that Iesus was Christ.
ac.19.1	Acts 19:1	And it came to passe, that while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul hauing passed thorow the vpper coasts, came to Ephesus, and finding certaine disciples,
ac.19.2	Acts 19:2	He said vnto them, Haue ye receiued the holy Ghost since yee beleeued? And they saide vnto him, Wee haue not so much as heard whether there be any holy Ghost.
ac.19.3	Acts 19:3	And he said vnto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they saide, Unto Iohns Baptisme.
ac.19.4	Acts 19:4	Then saide Paul, Iohn verely baptized with the baptisme of repentance, saying vnto the people, that they should beleeue on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Iesus.
ac.19.5	Acts 19:5	When they heard this, they were baptized in the Name of the Lord Iesus.
ac.19.6	Acts 19:6	And when Paul had laide his hands vpon them, the holy Ghost came on them, and they spake with tongues, and prophecied.
ac.19.7	Acts 19:7	And all þ men were about twelue.
ac.19.8	Acts 19:8	And hee went into the Synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three moneths, disputing and perswading the things concerning the Kingdome of God.
ac.19.9	Acts 19:9	But when diuers were hardened, and beleeued not, but spake euill of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the schoole of one Tyrannus.
ac.19.10	Acts 19:10	And this continued by the space of two yeeres, so that all they which dwelt in Asia, heard the word of the Lord Iesus, both Iewes and Greeks.
ac.19.11	Acts 19:11	And God wrought speciall miracles by the hands of Paul:
ac.19.12	Acts 19:12	So that from his body were brought vnto the sicke handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the euill spirits went out of them.
ac.19.13	Acts 19:13	¶ Then certaine of the vagabond Iewes, exorcistes, tooke vpon them to call ouer them which had euill spirits, the Name of the Lord Iesus, saying, We adiure you by Iesus whom Paul preacheth.
ac.19.14	Acts 19:14	And there were seuen sonnes of one Sceua a Iewe, and chiefe of the Priests, which did so.
ac.19.15	Acts 19:15	And the euill spirit answered, and said, Iesus I knowe, and Paul I know, but who are ye?
ac.19.16	Acts 19:16	And the man in whom the euill spirit was, leapt on them, and ouercame them, and preuailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
ac.19.17	Acts 19:17	And this was knowen to all the Iewes and Greekes also dwelling at Ephesus, and feare fell on them all, and the Name of the Lord Iesus was magnified.
ac.19.18	Acts 19:18	And many that beleeued came, and confessed, and shewed their deedes.
ac.19.19	Acts 19:19	Many also of them which vsed curious arts, brought their bookes together and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of siluer.
ac.19.20	Acts 19:20	So mightily grew the word of God, and preuailed.
ac.19.21	Acts 19:21	¶ After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when hee had passed thorow Macedonia and Athaia, to go to Hierusalem, saying, After I haue bin there, I must also see Rome.
ac.19.22	Acts 19:22	So hee sent into Macedonia two of them that ministred vnto him, Timotheus and Erastus, but he himselfe stayed in Asia for a season.
ac.19.23	Acts 19:23	And the same time there arose no small stirre about that way.
ac.19.24	Acts 19:24	For a certaine man named Demetrius, a siluer smith, which made siluer shrines for Diana, brought no small gaine vnto the craftsmen:
ac.19.25	Acts 19:25	Whom he called together, with the workemen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we haue our wealth.
ac.19.26	Acts 19:26	Moreouer, ye see & heare, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath perswaded and turned away much people, saying, that they bee no gods, which are made with hands.
ac.19.27	Acts 19:27	So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought: but also that the Temple of the great goddesse Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia, and the world worshippeth.
ac.19.28	Acts 19:28	And when they heard these sayings, they were ful of wrath, & cried out, saying, Great is Diana of þ Ephesians.
ac.19.29	Acts 19:29	And the whole citie was filled with confusion, and hauing caught Gaius and Aristarchus men of Macedonia Pauls companions in trauaile, they rushed with one accord into the Theatre.
ac.19.30	Acts 19:30	And when Paul would haue entred in vnto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
ac.19.31	Acts 19:31	And certaine of the chiefe of Asia, which were his friends, sent vnto him, desiring him that he would not aduenture himselfe into the Theatre.
ac.19.32	Acts 19:32	Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused, and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
ac.19.33	Acts 19:33	And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Iewes putting him forward. And Alexander beckened with the hand, and would haue made his defence vnto the people.
ac.19.34	Acts 19:34	But when they knew that he was a Iewe, all with one voyce about the space of two houres cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
ac.19.35	Acts 19:35	And when the towne clarke had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there þ knoweth not how that the citie of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddesse Diana, and of the image which fell downe from Iupiter?
ac.19.36	Acts 19:36	Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to doe nothing rashly.
ac.19.37	Acts 19:37	For ye haue brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of Churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddesse:
ac.19.38	Acts 19:38	Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftesmen which are with him, haue a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies, let them implead one another.
ac.19.39	Acts 19:39	But if yee enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shalbe determined in a lawfull assembly.
ac.19.40	Acts 19:40	For we are in danger to be called in question for this dayes vprore, there being no cause whereby we may giue an accompt of this concourse.
ac.19.41	Acts 19:41	And when hee had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
ac.20.1	Acts 20:1	And after the vprore was ceased, Paul called vnto him the disciples, and imbraced them, & departed, for to go into Macedonia.
ac.20.2	Acts 20:2	And when he had gone ouer those parts, and had giuen them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
ac.20.3	Acts 20:3	And there abode three moneths: and when the Iewes layed waite for him, as hee was about to saile into Syria, hee purposed to returne thorow Macedonia.
ac.20.4	Acts 20:4	And there accompanied him into Asia, Sopater of Berea: and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus, and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus: and of Asia Tychicus and Trophimus.
ac.20.5	Acts 20:5	These going before, taried for vs at Troas:
ac.20.6	Acts 20:6	And wee sailed away from Philippi, after the dayes of vnleauened bread, and came vnto them to Troas in fiue dayes, where we abode seuen daies.
ac.20.7	Acts 20:7	And vpon the first day of the weeke, when the disciples came together to breake bread, Paul preached vnto them, ready to depart on the morrow, and continued his speach vntill midnight.
ac.20.8	Acts 20:8	And there were many lights in the vpper chamber where they were gathered together.
ac.20.9	Acts 20:9	And there sate in a window a certaine yong man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deepe sleepe, and as Paul was long preaching, hee sunke downe with sleepe, and fel downe from the third loft, and was taken vp dead.
ac.20.10	Acts 20:10	And Paul went downe, and fell on him, and embracing him, saide, Trouble not your selues, for his life is in him.
ac.20.11	Acts 20:11	When hee therefore was come vp againe, & had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, euen till breake of day, so he departed.
ac.20.12	Acts 20:12	And they brought the yong man aliue, and were not a little comforted.
ac.20.13	Acts 20:13	¶ And wee went before to ship, and sailed vnto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had hee appointed, minding himselfe to goe afoote.
ac.20.14	Acts 20:14	And when he met with vs at Assos, wee tooke him in, and came to Mitylene.
ac.20.15	Acts 20:15	And wee sailed thence, and came the next day ouer against Chios, and the next day we arriued at Samos, and taried at Trogyllium: and the next day we came to Miletus.
ac.20.16	Acts 20:16	For Paul had determined to saile by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Hierusalem the day of Pentecost.
ac.20.17	Acts 20:17	¶ And from Miletus hee sent to Ephesus, and called the Elders of the Church.
ac.20.18	Acts 20:18	And when they were come to him, he said vnto them, Ye know from the first day that I came into Asia, after what maner I haue bene with you at all seasons,
ac.20.19	Acts 20:19	Seruing the Lord with all humilitie of minde, and with many teares, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Iewes:
ac.20.20	Acts 20:20	And how I kept backe nothing that was profitable vnto you, but haue shewed you, and haue taught you publikely, and from house to house,
ac.20.21	Acts 20:21	Testifying both to the Iewes and also to the Greekes, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Iesus Christ.
ac.20.22	Acts 20:22	And now behold, I goe bound in the spirit vnto Hierusalem, not knowing the things that shal befall me there:
ac.20.23	Acts 20:23	Saue that the holy Ghost witnesseth in euery city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
ac.20.24	Acts 20:24	But none of these things mooue me, neither count I my life deare vnto my self, so that I might finish my course with ioy, & the ministery which I haue receiued of the Lord Iesus, to testifie the Gospel of the grace of God.
ac.20.25	Acts 20:25	And now behold, I know that ye all, among whom I haue gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
ac.20.26	Acts 20:26	Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
ac.20.27	Acts 20:27	For I haue not shunned to declare vnto you all the counsell of God.
ac.20.28	Acts 20:28	¶ Take heed therefore vnto your selues, & to all the flocke, ouer the which the holy Ghost hath made you ouerseers, to feed the Church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
ac.20.29	Acts 20:29	For I know this, that after my departing shall grieuous wolues enter in among you, not sparing the flocke.
ac.20.30	Acts 20:30	Also of your owne selues shal men arise, speaking peruerse things, to draw away disciples after them.
ac.20.31	Acts 20:31	Therefore watch, and remember that by the space of three yeeres, I ceased not to warne euery one night and day with teares.
ac.20.32	Acts 20:32	And now brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you vp, and to giue you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
ac.20.33	Acts 20:33	I haue coueted no mans siluer, or golde, or apparell.
ac.20.34	Acts 20:34	Yea, you your selues know, that these handes haue ministred vnto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
ac.20.35	Acts 20:35	I haue shewed you all things, how that so labouring, yee ought to support the weake, and to remember the words of the Lord Iesus, how he said, It is more blessed to giue, then to receiue.
ac.20.36	Acts 20:36	¶ And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled downe, & prayed with them all.
ac.20.37	Acts 20:37	And they all wept sore, and fell on Pauls necke, and kissed him,
ac.20.38	Acts 20:38	Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him vnto the ship.
ac.21.1	Acts 21:1	And it came to passe, that after wee were gotten frō them, and had lanched, wee came with a straight course vnto Choos, and the day following vnto Rhodes, and from thence vnto Patara.
ac.21.2	Acts 21:2	And finding a ship sailing ouer vnto Phenicea, wee went abroad, and set foorth.
ac.21.3	Acts 21:3	Now when wee had discouered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the shippe was to vnlade her burden.
ac.21.4	Acts 21:4	And finding disciples, wee taried there seuen dayes: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that hee should not goe vp to Hierusalem.
ac.21.5	Acts 21:5	And when we had accomplished those dayes, we departed, and went our way, and they all brought vs on our way, with wiues and children, till wee were out of the citie: and wee kneeled downe on the shore, and prayed.
ac.21.6	Acts 21:6	And when we had taken our leaue one of another, we tooke ship, and they returned home againe.
ac.21.7	Acts 21:7	And when wee had finished our course from Tyre, wee came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
ac.21.8	Acts 21:8	And the next day we that were of Pauls company, departed, and came vnto Cesarea, and wee entred into the house of Philip the Euangelist (which was one of the seuen) & abode with him.
ac.21.9	Acts 21:9	And þ same man had foure daughters, virgins, which did prophesie.
ac.21.10	Acts 21:10	And as wee taried there many dayes, there came downe from Iudea a certaine Prophet, named Agabus.
ac.21.11	Acts 21:11	And when he was come vnto vs, he tooke Pauls girdle, and bound his owne hands and feete, and said, Thus sayth the holy Ghost, So shall the Iewes at Hierusalem binde the man that oweth this girdle, and shall deliuer him into the hands of the Gentiles.
ac.21.12	Acts 21:12	And when we heard these things, both we and they of that place, besought him not to goe vp to Hierusalem.
ac.21.13	Acts 21:13	Then Paul answered, What meane ye to weepe and to breake mine heart? for I am ready, not to bee bound onely, but also to die at Hierusalem for the Name of the Lord Iesus.
ac.21.14	Acts 21:14	And when he would not bee perswaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
ac.21.15	Acts 21:15	And after those dayes we tooke vp our cariages, & went vp to Hierusalem.
ac.21.16	Acts 21:16	There went with vs also certaine of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whō we should lodge.
ac.21.17	Acts 21:17	And when we were come to Hierusalem, the brethren receiued vs gladly
ac.21.18	Acts 21:18	And the day following Paul went in with vs vnto Iames, and all the Elders were present.
ac.21.19	Acts 21:19	And when hee had saluted them, hee declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministerie.
ac.21.20	Acts 21:20	And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, & said vnto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Iewes there are which beleeue, and they are all zealous of the Law.
ac.21.21	Acts 21:21	And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Iewes which are among the Gentiles, to forsake Moses, saying, that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walke after the customes.
ac.21.22	Acts 21:22	What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will heare that thou art come.
ac.21.23	Acts 21:23	Doe therefore this that we say to thee: Wee haue foure men which haue a vow on them,
ac.21.24	Acts 21:24	Then take, and purifie thy selfe with them, & bee at charges with them, that they may shaue their heads: and all may know that those things wherof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing, but that thou thy selfe also walkest orderly, and keepest the Law.
ac.21.25	Acts 21:25	As touching the Gentiles which beleeue, wee haue written and concluded, that they obserue no such thing, saue onely that they keepe themselues from things offered to idoles, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
ac.21.26	Acts 21:26	Then Paul tooke the men, and the next day purifying himselfe with them, entred into the Temple, to signifie the accomplishment of the dayes of purification, vntill that an offering should be offered for euery one of them:

ac.21.29	Acts 21:29	(For they had seene before with him in the citie, Trophimus an Ephesian, whome they supposed that Paul had brought into the Temple.)

ac.21.32	Acts 21:32	Who immediatly tooke souldiers, and Centurions, and ran downe vnto them: and when they saw the chiefe captaine and the souldiers, they left beating of Paul.

ac.21.34	Acts 21:34	And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certaintie for the tumult, he commanded him to be caried into the castle.
ac.21.35	Acts 21:35	And when he came vpon þ staires, so it was that he was borne of the souldiers, for the violence of the people.
ac.21.36	Acts 21:36	For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
ac.21.37	Acts 21:37	And as Paul was to bee led into the castle, hee saide vnto the chiefe captaine, May I speake vnto thee? Who saide, Canst thou speake Greeke?
ac.21.38	Acts 21:38	Art not thou that Egyptian which before these daies madest an vprore, and leddest out into the wildernesse foure thousand men that were murtherers?
ac.21.39	Acts 21:39	But Paul said, I am a man which am a Iew of Tarsus, a citie in Cilicia, a citizen of no meane citie: & I beseech thee suffer me to speake vnto the people.
ac.21.40	Acts 21:40	And when he had giuen him licence, Paul stood on the staires, and beckened with the hand vnto the people: and when there was made a great silence, he spake vnto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying.
ac.22.1	Acts 22:1	Men, brethren, and fathers, heare ye my defence which I make now vnto you.
ac.22.2	Acts 22:2	(And when they heard that hee spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
ac.22.3	Acts 22:3	I am verely a man which am a Iew, borne in Tarsus a citie in Cilicia, yet brought vp in this citie at the feete of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect maner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous towards God, as ye all are this day.
ac.22.4	Acts 22:4	And I persecuted this way vnto the death, binding and deliuering into prisons both men and women,
ac.22.5	Acts 22:5	As also the high Priest doth beare me witnesse, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I receiued letters vnto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there, bound vnto Hierusalem, for to be punished.
ac.22.6	Acts 22:6	And it came to passe, that as I made my iourney, & was come nigh vnto Damascus about noone, suddenly there shone from heauen a great light round about me.
ac.22.7	Acts 22:7	And I fell vnto the ground, and heard a voice saying vnto mee, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
ac.22.8	Acts 22:8	And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said vnto me, I am Iesus of Nazareth whō thou persecutest.
ac.22.9	Acts 22:9	And they that were with me saw indeede the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
ac.22.10	Acts 22:10	And I saide, What shall I doe, Lord? And the Lord said vnto me, Arise, and goe into Damascus, and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to doe.
ac.22.11	Acts 22:11	And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
ac.22.12	Acts 22:12	And one Ananias, a deuout man according to the law, hauing a good report of al the Iewes which dwelt there,
ac.22.13	Acts 22:13	Came vnto me, and stood, & said vnto me, Brother Saul, receiue thy sight. And the same houre I looked vp vpon him.
ac.22.14	Acts 22:14	And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, þ thou shouldest know his will, & see that Iust one, and shouldest heare the voice of his mouth.
ac.22.15	Acts 22:15	For thou shalt be his witnes vnto al men, of what thou hast seene & heard.

ac.22.17	Acts 22:17	And it came to passe, that when I was come againe to Hierusalem, euen while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance,
ac.22.18	Acts 22:18	And saw him saying vnto mee, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Hierusalem: for they will not receiue thy testimony concerning me.
ac.22.19	Acts 22:19	And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned, and beat in euery synagogue them that beleeued on thee.
ac.22.20	Acts 22:20	And when þ blood of thy martyr Steuen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting vnto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
ac.22.21	Acts 22:21	And he said vnto me, Depart: for I will send thee farre hence, vnto the Gentiles.
ac.22.22	Acts 22:22	And they gaue him audience vnto this word, and then lift vp their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should liue.
ac.22.23	Acts 22:23	And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, & threw dust into the aire,
ac.22.24	Acts 22:24	The chiefe captaine commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that hee should be examined by scourging: that he might know wherfore they cried so against him.
ac.22.25	Acts 22:25	And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said vnto the Centurion that stood by, Is it lawfull for you to scourge a man that is a Romane, and vncondemned?
ac.22.26	Acts 22:26	When the Centurion heard that, hee went and told the chiefe captaine, saying, Take heede what thou doest, for this man is a Romane.
ac.22.27	Acts 22:27	Then the chiefe captaine came; and said vnto him, Tell me, art thou a Romane? He said, Yea.
ac.22.28	Acts 22:28	And the chiefe captaine answered, With a great summe obteined I this freedome. And Paul said, But I was free borne.
ac.22.29	Acts 22:29	Then straightway they departed from him which should haue examined him: and the chiefe captaine also was afraid after he knew that he was a Romane, & because he had bound him.
ac.22.30	Acts 22:30	On the morrow, because he would haue knowen the certaintie wherefore he was accused of the Iewes, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chiefe Priests and all their Councill to appeare, and brought Paul downe, and set him before them.
ac.23.1	Acts 23:1	And Paul earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I haue liued in all good conscience before God vntill this day.
ac.23.2	Acts 23:2	And the high Priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him, to smite him on the mouth.
ac.23.3	Acts 23:3	Then saith Paul vnto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to iudge mee after the Law, and commandest mee to be smitten contrary to the Law?
ac.23.4	Acts 23:4	And they that stood by, said, Reuilest thou Gods high Priest?
ac.23.5	Acts 23:5	Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that hee was the high Prist: For it is written, Thou shalt not speake euill of the ruler of thy people.
ac.23.6	Acts 23:6	But when Paul perceiued that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, hee cryed out in the Councill, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the sonne of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead, I am called in question.
ac.23.7	Acts 23:7	And when hee had so said, there arose a dissension betweene the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was diuided.
ac.23.8	Acts 23:8	For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither Angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confesse both.
ac.23.9	Acts 23:9	And there arose a great cry: and the Scribes that were of the Pharisees part arose, and stroue, saying, Wee finde no euill in this man: but if a spirit or an Angel hath spoken to him, let vs not fight against God.
ac.23.10	Acts 23:10	And when there arose a great dissension, the chiefe captaine fearing lest Paul should haue bene pulled in pieces of them, commanded the souldiers to goe downe, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
ac.23.11	Acts 23:11	And the night folowing, the Lord stood by him, and saide, Bee of good cheere, Paul: for as thou hast testified of mee in Hierusalem, so must thou beare witnesse also at Rome.

ac.23.13	Acts 23:13	And they were more then fourtie which had made this conspiracie.
ac.23.14	Acts 23:14	And they came to the chiefe Priests and Elders, and said, Wee haue bound our selues vnder a great curse, that wee will eate nothing vntill wee haue slaine Paul.

ac.23.16	Acts 23:16	And when Pauls sisters sonne heard of their laying in wait, hee went and entred into the castle, & told Paul.

ac.23.18	Acts 23:18	So he took him, and brought him to the chiefe captaine, and said, Paul the prisoner called me vnto him, and praied mee to bring this yong man vnto thee, who hath something to say vnto thee.

ac.23.21	Acts 23:21	But do not thou yeeld vnto them: for there lie in wait for him of them moe then fourtie men, which haue bound themselues with an othe, that they will neither eate nor drinke, till they haue killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
ac.23.22	Acts 23:22	So the chiefe captaine then let the yong man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man, that thou hast shewed these things to me.
ac.23.23	Acts 23:23	And he called vnto him two Centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred souldiers to goe to Cesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearemen two hundred, at the third houre of the night.
ac.23.24	Acts 23:24	And prouide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe vnto Felix the gouernour.

ac.23.28	Acts 23:28	And when I would haue knowen the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him foorth into their Council.
ac.23.29	Acts 23:29	Whom I perceiued to be accused of questions of their lawe, but to haue nothing laide to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
ac.23.30	Acts 23:30	And when it was tolde me, how that the Iewes laid waite for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gaue commandement to his accusers also, to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.

ac.24.1	Acts 24:1	And after fiue dayes, Ananias the hie Priest descended with the Elders, and with a certaine Oratour named Tertullus, who enformed the gouernour against Paul.
ac.24.2	Acts 24:2	And when he was called foorth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enioy great quietnesse, and that very worthy deeds are done vnto this natiō by thy prouidence:

ac.24.4	Acts 24:4	Notwithstanding, that I be not farther tedious vnto thee, I pray thee, that thou wouldest heare vs of thy clemencie a few words.

ac.24.11	Acts 24:11	Because that thou mayest vnderstand, that there are yet but twelue dayes, since I went vp to Hierusalem for to worship.
ac.24.12	Acts 24:12	And they neither found me in the Temple disputing with any man, neither raising vp the people, neither in the Synagogues, nor in the citie:
ac.24.13	Acts 24:13	Neither can they proue the things whereof they now accuse me.

ac.24.16	Acts 24:16	And herein doe I exercise my selfe to haue alwayes a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

ac.24.18	Acts 24:18	Wherupon certaine Iewes from Asia found me purified in the Temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult:
ac.24.19	Acts 24:19	Who ought to haue beene here before thee, and obiect, if they had ought against me.

ac.24.22	Acts 24:22	And when Felix heard these things, hauing more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them and said, When Lysias the chiefe captaine shall come downe, I will know the vttermost of your matter.
ac.24.23	Acts 24:23	And he commanded a Centurion to keepe Paul, and to let him haue libertie, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister, or come vnto him.
ac.24.24	Acts 24:24	And after certaine dayes, when Felix came with his wife Orusilla, which was a Iew, he sent for Paul, and heard him cōcerning the faith in Christ.
ac.24.25	Acts 24:25	And as he reasoned of righteousnesse, temperance, and iudgement to come, Felix trembled and answered, Go thy way for this time, when I haue a conuenient season, I will call for thee.
ac.24.26	Acts 24:26	He hoped also that money should haue bene giuen him of Paul, that hee might loose him: wherefore hee sent for him the oftner, and cōmuned with him.
ac.24.27	Acts 24:27	But after two yeeres, Portius Festus came into Felix roome: and Felix willing to shew the Iewes a pleasure, left Paul bound.

ac.25.2	Acts 25:2	Then the high Priest, and the chiefe of the Iewes informed him against Paul, and besought him,

ac.25.23	Acts 25:23	And on the morrow when Agrippa was come and Bernice, with great pompe, and was entred into the place of hearing, with the chiefe captaines, and principall men of the citie; at Festus commaundement Paul was brought foorth.
ac.25.24	Acts 25:24	And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are heere present with vs, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Iewes haue dealt with me, both at Hierusalem, and also heere, crying that he ought not to liue any longer.
ac.25.25	Acts 25:25	But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himselfe hath appealed to Augustus, I haue determined to send him.
ac.25.26	Acts 25:26	Of whom I haue no certaine thing to write vnto my Lord: Wherefore I haue brought him foorth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that after examination had, I might haue somewhat to write.
ac.25.27	Acts 25:27	For it seemeth to me vnreasonable, to send a prisoner, and not withall to signifie the crimes laid against him.
ac.26.1	Acts 26:1	Then Agrippa said vnto Paul, Thou art permitted to speake for thy selfe. Then Paul stretched foorth the hand, and answered for himselfe,
ac.26.2	Acts 26:2	I thinke my selfe happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answere for my selfe this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Iewes:
ac.26.3	Acts 26:3	Especially, because I know thee to be expert in all customes and questions which are among the Iewes: wherefore I beseech thee to heare mee patiently.
ac.26.4	Acts 26:4	My maner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine owne nation at Hierusalem, know all the Iewes,
ac.26.5	Acts 26:5	Which knew me from the beginning, (if they would testifie) that after the most straitest sect of our religion, I liued a Pharisee.
ac.26.6	Acts 26:6	And now I stand, and am iudged for the hope of the promise made of God vnto our fathers:
ac.26.7	Acts 26:7	Vnto which promise our twelue tribes instantly seruing God day and night, hope to come: For which hopes sake, King Agrippa, I am accused of the Iewes.
ac.26.8	Acts 26:8	Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
ac.26.9	Acts 26:9	I verily thought with my selfe, that I ought to doe many things contrary to the name of Iesus of Nazareth:
ac.26.10	Acts 26:10	Which thing I also did in Hierusalem, and many of the Saints did I shut vp in prison, hauing receiued authoritie from the chiefe Priests, and when they were put to death, I gaue my voyce against them.
ac.26.11	Acts 26:11	And I punished them oft in euery Synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme, and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them euen vnto strange cities.
ac.26.12	Acts 26:12	Whereupon, as I went to Damascus, with authoritie and commission from the chiefe Priests:
