2th.3.12	2 Thessalonians 3:12	Now them that are such, we command, and exhort by our Lord Iesus Christ, that with quietnesse they worke, and eat their owne bread.
2th.3.13	2 Thessalonians 3:13	But ye, brethren, be not wearie in well doing.
2th.3.14	2 Thessalonians 3:14	And if any man obey not our word, by this Epistle note that man, and haue no company with him, that he may be ashamed,
2th.3.15	2 Thessalonians 3:15	Yet count him not as an enemie, but admonish him as a brother.
2th.3.16	2 Thessalonians 3:16	Now the Lord of peace himselfe, giue you peace alwayes, by all meanes. The Lord be with you all.
2th.3.17	2 Thessalonians 3:17	The salutation of Paul, with mine owne hand, which is the token in euery Epistle: so I write.
2th.3.18	2 Thessalonians 3:18	The grace of our Lord Iesus Christ be with you all, Amen. The second Epistle to the Thessalonians was written from Athens.
1tm.1.1	1 Timothy 1:1	Paul an Apostle of Iesus Christ by the commaundement of God our Sauiour, & Lord Iesus Christ which is our hope,
1tm.1.2	1 Timothy 1:2	Unto Timothie my own sonne in the Faith: Grace, mercie, and peace from God our Father, and Iesus Christ our Lord.
1tm.1.3	1 Timothy 1:3	As I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine,
1tm.1.4	1 Timothy 1:4	Neither giue heed to fables, and endlesse genealogies, which minister questions, rather then edifying which is in faith: so doe.
1tm.1.5	1 Timothy 1:5	Now the end of the commandement is charity, out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith vnfained.
1tm.1.6	1 Timothy 1:6	From which some hauing swarued, haue turned aside vnto vaine iangling,
1tm.1.7	1 Timothy 1:7	Desiring to bee teachers of the Law, vnderstāding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirme.
1tm.1.8	1 Timothy 1:8	But we know that the Law is good, if a man vse it lawfully.
1tm.1.9	1 Timothy 1:9	Knowing this, that the Law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawlesse and disobedient, for the vngodly, and for sinners, for vnholy, and profane, for murderers of fathers, and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
1tm.1.10	1 Timothy 1:10	For whoremongers, for them that defile themselues with mankinde, for men-stealers, for liars, for periured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine,
1tm.1.11	1 Timothy 1:11	According to the glorious Gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
1tm.1.12	1 Timothy 1:12	And I thanke Christ Iesus our Lord, who hath enabled mee: for that he counted me faithfull, putting me into the Ministerie,
1tm.1.13	1 Timothy 1:13	Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecuter, and iniurious. But I obtained mercie, because I did it ignorantly, in vnbeliefe.
1tm.1.14	1 Timothy 1:14	And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant, with faith, & loue, which is in Christ Iesus.
1tm.1.15	1 Timothy 1:15	This is a faithfull saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Iesus came into the world to saue sinners, of whom I am chiefe.
1tm.1.16	1 Timothy 1:16	Howbeit, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Iesus Christ might shew foorth all long suffering, for a paterne to them which should hereafter beleeue on him to life euerlasting.
1tm.1.17	1 Timothy 1:17	Now vnto þ king eternal, immortall, inuisible, the onely wise God, be honour and glory for euer & euer. Amen.
1tm.1.18	1 Timothy 1:18	This charge I commit vnto thee, sonne Timothie, according to the prophesies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest warre a good warfare,
1tm.1.19	1 Timothy 1:19	Holding faith, and a good conscience, which some hauing put away, concerning faith, haue made shipwracke.
1tm.1.20	1 Timothy 1:20	Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander, whome I haue deliuered vnto Satan, that they may learne not to blaspheme.
1tm.2.1	1 Timothy 2:1	I exhort therefore, that first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giuing of thanks be made for all men:
1tm.2.2	1 Timothy 2:2	For Kings, and for all that are in authoritie, that we may leade a quiet and peaceable life in all godlinesse and honestie.
1tm.2.3	1 Timothy 2:3	For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Sauiour,
1tm.2.4	1 Timothy 2:4	Who will haue all men to bee saued, and to come vnto the knowledge of the trueth.
1tm.2.5	1 Timothy 2:5	For there is one God, and one Mediatour betweene God and men, the man Christ Iesus,
1tm.2.6	1 Timothy 2:6	Who gaue himselfe a ransome for all, to be testified in due time.
1tm.2.7	1 Timothy 2:7	Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an Apostle (I speake the trueth in Christ, and lie not) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and veritie.
1tm.2.8	1 Timothy 2:8	I will therefore that men pray euery where, lifting vp holy handes without wrath, and doubting.
1tm.2.9	1 Timothy 2:9	In like maner also, that women adorne themselues in modest apparell, with shamefastnesse and sobrietie, not with broided haire, or gold, or pearles, or costly aray,
1tm.2.10	1 Timothy 2:10	But (which becommeth women professing godlines) with good works.
1tm.2.11	1 Timothy 2:11	Let the woman learne in silence with all subiection:
1tm.2.12	1 Timothy 2:12	But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to vsurpe authoritie ouer the man, but to be in silence.
1tm.2.13	1 Timothy 2:13	For Adam was first formed, then Eue:
1tm.2.14	1 Timothy 2:14	And Adam was not deceiued, but the woman being deceiued was in the transgression:
1tm.2.15	1 Timothy 2:15	Notwithstanding she shall be saued in child-bearing, if they continue in faith and charitie, and holinesse, with sobrietie.
1tm.3.1	1 Timothy 3:1	This is a true saying: If a man desire the office of a Bishop, he desireth a good worke.
1tm.3.2	1 Timothy 3:2	A Bishop then must be blamelesse, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behauiour, giuen to hospitalitie, apt to teach;
1tm.3.3	1 Timothy 3:3	Not giuen to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre, but patient, not a brawler, not couetous;
1tm.3.4	1 Timothy 3:4	One that ruleth well his owne house, hauing his children in subiection with all grauitie.
1tm.3.5	1 Timothy 3:5	(For if a man know not how to rule his owne house, how shall he take care of the Church of God?)
1tm.3.6	1 Timothy 3:6	Not a nouice, lest being lifted vp with pride, hee fall into the condemnation of the deuill.
1tm.3.7	1 Timothy 3:7	Moreouer, hee must haue a good report of them which are without, lest he fall into reproch, and the snare of the deuill.
1tm.3.8	1 Timothy 3:8	Likewise must the Deacons bee graue, not double tongued, not giuen to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre,
1tm.3.9	1 Timothy 3:9	Holding the mysterie of the faith in a pure conscience.
1tm.3.10	1 Timothy 3:10	And let these also first be proued; then let them vse the office of a Deacon, being found blamelesse.
1tm.3.11	1 Timothy 3:11	Euen so must their wiues be graue; not slanderers, sober, faithfull in all things.
1tm.3.12	1 Timothy 3:12	Let the Deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children, and their owne houses well.
1tm.3.13	1 Timothy 3:13	For they that haue vsed the office of a Deacon well, purchase to themselues a good degree, and great boldnesse in the faith, which is in Christ Iesus.
1tm.3.14	1 Timothy 3:14	These things write I vnto thee, hoping to come vnto thee shortly.
1tm.3.15	1 Timothy 3:15	But if I tary long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behaue thy selfe in the House of God, which is the Church of the liuing God, the pillar and ground of the trueth.
1tm.3.16	1 Timothy 3:16	And without controuersie, great is the mysterie of godlinesse: God was manifest in the flesh, iustified in the Spirit, seene of Angels, preached vnto the Gentiles, beleeued on in the world, receiued vp into glory.
1tm.4.1	1 Timothy 4:1	Now the Spirit speaketh expresly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giuing heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of deuils:
1tm.4.2	1 Timothy 4:2	Speaking lies in hypocrisie, hauing their conscience seared with a hote iron,
1tm.4.3	1 Timothy 4:3	Forbidding to marry, and commanding to absteine from meates, which God hath created to bee receiued with thankesgiuing of them which beleeue, and know the trueth.
1tm.4.4	1 Timothy 4:4	For euery creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be receiued with thankesgiuing:
1tm.4.5	1 Timothy 4:5	For it is sanctified by the word of God, and prayer.
1tm.4.6	1 Timothy 4:6	If thou put the brethren in remembrance of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Iesus Christ, nourished vp in the wordes of faith, and of good doctrine, whereunto thou hast attained.
1tm.4.7	1 Timothy 4:7	But refuse prophane and olde wiues fables, and exercise thy selfe rather vnto godlinesse.
1tm.4.8	1 Timothy 4:8	For bodily exercise profiteth litle, but godlinesse is profitable vnto all things, hauing promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.
1tm.4.9	1 Timothy 4:9	This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation:
1tm.4.10	1 Timothy 4:10	For therfore we both labour, and suffer reproch, because we trust in the liuing God, who is the Sauiour of all men, specially of those that beleeue.
1tm.4.11	1 Timothy 4:11	These things command & teach.
1tm.4.12	1 Timothy 4:12	Let no man despise thy youth, but be thou an example of the beleeuers, in word, in conuersation, in charitie, in spirit, in faith, in puritie.
1tm.4.13	1 Timothy 4:13	Till I come, giue attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
1tm.4.14	1 Timothy 4:14	Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was giuen thee by prophesie, with the laying on of the hands of the Presbyterie.
1tm.4.15	1 Timothy 4:15	Meditate vpon these things, giue thy selfe wholly to them, that thy profiting may appeare to all.
1tm.4.16	1 Timothy 4:16	Take heed vnto thy selfe, and vnto the doctrine: continue in them: for in doing this, thou shalt both saue thy selfe, and them that heare thee.
1tm.5.1	1 Timothy 5:1	Rebuke not an Elder, but intreate him as a father, and the yonger men as brethren:
1tm.5.2	1 Timothy 5:2	The elder women as mothers, the yonger as sisters with all puritie.
1tm.5.3	1 Timothy 5:3	Honour widowes that are widowes indeed.
1tm.5.4	1 Timothy 5:4	But if any widow haue children or nephewes, let them learne first to shew pietie at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God.
1tm.5.5	1 Timothy 5:5	Now she that is a widow in deed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.
1tm.5.6	1 Timothy 5:6	But she that liueth in pleasure, is dead while she liueth.
1tm.5.7	1 Timothy 5:7	And these things giue in charge, that they may be blamelesse.
1tm.5.8	1 Timothy 5:8	But if any prouide not for his owne, & specially for those of his owne house, hee hath denied the faith, and is worse then an infidel.
1tm.5.9	1 Timothy 5:9	Let not a widow bee taken into the number, vnder threescore yeeres old, hauing bene the wife of one man,
1tm.5.10	1 Timothy 5:10	Well reported of for good works, if shee haue brought vp children, if shee haue lodged strangers, if she haue washed the Saints feet, if shee haue releeued the afflicted, if shee haue diligently followed euery good worke.
1tm.5.11	1 Timothy 5:11	But the yonger widowes refuse: for when they haue begunne to waxe wanton against Christ, they will marry,
1tm.5.12	1 Timothy 5:12	Hauing damnation, because they haue cast off their first faith.
1tm.5.13	1 Timothy 5:13	And withall they learne to bee idle, wandering about from house to house; and not onely idle, but tatlers also, and busibodies, speaking things which they ought not.
1tm.5.14	1 Timothy 5:14	I will therefore that the yonger women marry, beare children, guid the house, giue none occasion to the aduersary to speake reprochfully.
1tm.5.15	1 Timothy 5:15	For some are already turned aside after Satan.
1tm.5.16	1 Timothy 5:16	If any man or woman that beleeueth haue widowes, let them relieue them, and let not the Church be charged, that it may relieue them that are widowes indeed.
1tm.5.17	1 Timothy 5:17	Let the Elders that rule well, be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.
1tm.5.18	1 Timothy 5:18	For the Scripture saith, Thou shalt not mousell the oxe that treadeth out the corne: and, The labourer is worthy of his reward.
1tm.5.19	1 Timothy 5:19	Against an Elder receiue not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
1tm.5.20	1 Timothy 5:20	Them that sinne rebuke before all, that others also may feare.
1tm.5.21	1 Timothy 5:21	I charge thee before God, and the Lord Iesus Christ, and the elect Angels, that thou obserue these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partialitie.
1tm.5.22	1 Timothy 5:22	Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither bee partaker of other mens sinnes. Keepe thy selfe pure.
1tm.5.23	1 Timothy 5:23	Drinke no longer water, but vse a little wine for thy stomackes sake, and thine often infirmities.
1tm.5.24	1 Timothy 5:24	Some mens sinnes are open before hand, going before to iudgement: and some men they follow after.
1tm.5.25	1 Timothy 5:25	Likewise also the good works of some are manifest before hand, and they that are otherwise, cannot be hid.
1tm.6.1	1 Timothy 6:1	Let as many seruants as are vnder the yoke, count their owne masters worthy of all honour, that the Name of God, and his doctrine be not blasphemed.
1tm.6.2	1 Timothy 6:2	And they that haue beleeuing masters, let them not despise them because they are brethren: but rather doe them seruice, because they are faithfull and beloued, partakers of the benefite: These things teach and exhort.
1tm.6.3	1 Timothy 6:3	If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, euen the wordes of our Lord Iesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godlinesse:
1tm.6.4	1 Timothy 6:4	Hee is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions, and strifes of wordes, whereof commeth enuie, strife, railings, euill surmisings,
1tm.6.5	1 Timothy 6:5	Peruerse disputings of men of corrupt mindes, and destitute of the trueth, supposing that gaine is godlinesse: From such withdraw thy selfe.
1tm.6.6	1 Timothy 6:6	But godlinesse with contentment is great gaine.
1tm.6.7	1 Timothy 6:7	For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certaine we can cary nothing out.
1tm.6.8	1 Timothy 6:8	And hauing food and raiment let vs be therewith content.
1tm.6.9	1 Timothy 6:9	But they that will be rich, fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish & hurtfull lusts, which drowne men in destruction and perdition.
1tm.6.10	1 Timothy 6:10	For the loue of money is the root of all euill, which while some coueted after, they haue erred from the faith, and pierced themselues through with many sorrowes.
1tm.6.11	1 Timothy 6:11	But thou, O man of God, flie these things; and follow after righteousnesse, godlinesse, faith, loue, patience, meekenesse.
1tm.6.12	1 Timothy 6:12	Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternall life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
1tm.6.13	1 Timothy 6:13	I giue thee charge in the sight of God, who quickneth all things, and before Christ Iesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good Confession,
1tm.6.14	1 Timothy 6:14	That thou keepe this commandement without spot, vnrebukeable, vntill the appearing of our Lord Iesus Christ.
1tm.6.15	1 Timothy 6:15	Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed, and onely Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords:
1tm.6.16	1 Timothy 6:16	Who onely hath immortalitie, dwelling in the light, which no man can approch vnto, whom no man hath seene, nor can see: to whom be honour and power euerlasting. Amen.
1tm.6.17	1 Timothy 6:17	Charge them that are rich in this world, that they bee not high minded, nor trust in vncertaine riches, but in the liuing God, who giueth vs richly all things to enioy,
1tm.6.18	1 Timothy 6:18	That they doe good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate,
1tm.6.19	1 Timothy 6:19	Laying vp in store for themselues a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay holde on eternall life.
1tm.6.20	1 Timothy 6:20	O Timothie, keepe that which is committed to thy trust, auoyding prophane and vaine bablings, and oppositions of science, fasly so called:
1tm.6.21	1 Timothy 6:21	Which some professing, haue erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen. The first to Timothie was written from Laodicea, which is the chiefest citie of Phrygia Pacaciana.
2tm.1.1	2 Timothy 1:1	Paul an Apostle of Iesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life, which is in Christ Iesus,
2tm.1.2	2 Timothy 1:2	To Timothie my dearely beloued sonne: grace, mercie, and peace from God the Father, and Christ Iesus our Lord.
2tm.1.3	2 Timothy 1:3	I thanke God, whom I serue from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I haue remembrance of thee in my prayers night and day,
2tm.1.4	2 Timothy 1:4	Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindfull of thy teares, that I may bee filled with ioy,
2tm.1.5	2 Timothy 1:5	When I call to remembrance the vnfained faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice: and I am perswaded that in thee also.
2tm.1.6	2 Timothy 1:6	Wherefore I put thee in remembrance, that thou stirre vp the gift of God which is in thee, by the putting on of my hands.
2tm.1.7	2 Timothy 1:7	For God hath not giuen vs the spirit of feare, but of power, of loue, and of a sound minde.
2tm.1.8	2 Timothy 1:8	Bee not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but bee thou partaker of the afflictions of the Gospel according to the power of God,
2tm.1.9	2 Timothy 1:9	Who hath saued vs, and called vs with an holy calling, not according to our workes, but according to his owne purpose and grace, which was giuen vs in Christ Iesus, before the world began,
2tm.1.10	2 Timothy 1:10	But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Sauiour Iesus Christ, who hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortalitie to light, through the Gospel:
2tm.1.11	2 Timothy 1:11	Whereunto I am appointed a Preacher, and an Apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
2tm.1.12	2 Timothy 1:12	For the which cause I also suffer these things; neuerthelesse, I am not ashamed: for I know whom I haue beleeued, and I am perswaded that he is able to keepe that which I haue committed vnto him against that day.
2tm.1.13	2 Timothy 1:13	Holde fast the fourme of sound words, which thou hast heard of mee, in faith and loue, which is in Christ Iesus.
2tm.1.14	2 Timothy 1:14	That good thing which was committed vnto thee, keepe, by the holy Ghost which dwelleth in vs.
2tm.1.15	2 Timothy 1:15	This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me, of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes.
2tm.1.16	2 Timothy 1:16	The Lord giue mercie vnto the house of Onesiphorus, for hee oft refreshed mee, and was not ashamed of my chaine.
2tm.1.17	2 Timothy 1:17	But when he was in Rome, hee sought mee out very diligently, and found me.
2tm.1.18	2 Timothy 1:18	The Lord grant vnto him, that he may finde mercie of the Lord in that day: And in how many things hee ministred vnto mee at Ephesus, thou knowest very well.
2tm.2.1	2 Timothy 2:1	Thou therefore, my sonne, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Iesus.
2tm.2.2	2 Timothy 2:2	And the things that thou hast heard of mee among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithfull men, who shall be able to teach others also.
2tm.2.3	2 Timothy 2:3	Thou therefore indure hardnesse, as a good souldier of Iesus Christ.
2tm.2.4	2 Timothy 2:4	No man that warreth, intangleth himselfe with the affaires of this life, that hee may please him who hath chosen him to be a souldier.
2tm.2.5	2 Timothy 2:5	And if a man also striue for masteries, yet is hee not crowned except hee striue lawfully.
2tm.2.6	2 Timothy 2:6	The husbandman that laboureth, must bee first partaker of the fruites.
2tm.2.7	2 Timothy 2:7	Consider what I say, and the Lord giue thee vnderstanding in all things.
2tm.2.8	2 Timothy 2:8	Remember that Iesus Christ of the seede of Dauid, was raised from the dead, according to my Gospel:
2tm.2.9	2 Timothy 2:9	Wherein I suffer trouble as an euill doer, euen vnto bonds: but the word of God is not bound.
2tm.2.10	2 Timothy 2:10	Therefore I indure all things for the elects sakes, that they may also obtaine the saluation which is in Christ Iesus, with eternall glory.
2tm.2.11	2 Timothy 2:11	It is a faithfull saying: for if we bee dead with him, wee shall also liue with him.
2tm.2.12	2 Timothy 2:12	If we suffer, we shall also reigne with him: if wee denie him, hee also will denie vs.
2tm.2.13	2 Timothy 2:13	If we beleeue not, yet he abideth faithfull, he cannot denie himselfe.
2tm.2.14	2 Timothy 2:14	Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord, that they striue not about words to no profite, but to the subuerting of the hearers.
2tm.2.15	2 Timothy 2:15	Studie to shewe thy selfe approued vnto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly diuiding the word of trueth.
2tm.2.16	2 Timothy 2:16	But shun profane and vaine bablings, for they will increase vnto more vngodlinesse.
2tm.2.17	2 Timothy 2:17	And their word will eate as doth a canker: of whom is Hymeneus and Philetus.
2tm.2.18	2 Timothy 2:18	Who concerning the trueth haue erred, saying that the resurrection is past alreadie, and ouerthrow the faith of some.
2tm.2.19	2 Timothy 2:19	Neuerthelesse the foundation of God standeth sure, hauing the seale, the Lord knoweth them that are his. And, let euery one that nameth the Name of Christ, depart from iniquitie.
2tm.2.20	2 Timothy 2:20	But in a great house, there are not onely vessels of gold, and of siluer, but also a wood, & of earth: and some to honour, and some to dishonour.
2tm.2.21	2 Timothy 2:21	If a man therefore purge himselfe from these, he shal be a vessell vnto honour, sanctified, and meete for the Masters vse, and prepared vnto euery good worke.
2tm.2.22	2 Timothy 2:22	Flie also youthfull lusts: but follow righteousnesse, faith, charitie, peace with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
2tm.2.23	2 Timothy 2:23	But foolish and vnlearned questions auoid, knowing that they doe gender strifes.
2tm.2.24	2 Timothy 2:24	And the seruant of the Lord must not striue: but bee gentle vnto all men, apt to teach, patient,
2tm.2.25	2 Timothy 2:25	In meekenesse instructing those that oppose themselues, if God peraduenture will giue them repentance to the acknowledging of the trueth.
2tm.2.26	2 Timothy 2:26	And that they may recouer themselues out of the snare of the deuill, who are taken captiue by him at his will.

tt.1.1	Titus 1:1	Paul a seruant of God, and an Apostle of Iesus Christ, according to the Faith of Gods Elect, and the acknowledging of the trueth which is after godlinesse,
tt.1.2	Titus 1:2	In hope of eternall life, which God that cannot lie, promised before the world began:
tt.1.3	Titus 1:3	But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed vnto mee according to the commandement of God our Sauiour:
tt.1.4	Titus 1:4	To Titus mine owne Sonne after the common faith, Grace, mercie, and peace from God the Father, and the Lord Iesus Christ our Sauiour.
tt.1.5	Titus 1:5	For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordaine Elders in euery citie, as I had appointed thee.
tt.1.6	Titus 1:6	If any be blamelesse, the husband of one wife, hauing faithfull children, not accused of riot, or vnruly.
tt.1.7	Titus 1:7	For a Bishop must be blameles, as the steward of God: not selfewilled, not soone angry, not giuen to wine, no striker, not giuen to filthie lucre,
tt.1.8	Titus 1:8	But a louer of hospitality, a louer of good men, sober, iust, holy, temperate,
tt.1.9	Titus 1:9	Holding fast the faithfull word, as hee hath beene taught, that he may bee able by sound doctrine, both to exhort and to conuince the gainsayers.
tt.1.10	Titus 1:10	For there are many vnruly and vaine talkers and deceiuers, specially they of the circumcision:
tt.1.11	Titus 1:11	Whose mouthes must be stopped, who subuert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthie lucres sake.
tt.1.12	Titus 1:12	One of themselues, euen a Prophet of their owne, said: The Cretians are alway lyers, euill beasts, slow bellies.
tt.1.13	Titus 1:13	This witnesse is true: wherefore rebuke them sharpely that they may be sound in the faith;
tt.1.14	Titus 1:14	Not giuing heede to Iewish fables, and commandements of men that turne from the trueth.
tt.1.15	Titus 1:15	Unto the pure all things are pure, but vnto them that are defiled, and vnbeleeuing, is nothing pure: but euen their mind and conscience is defiled.
tt.1.16	Titus 1:16	They professe that they know God; but in workes they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and vnto euery good worke reprobate.
tt.2.1	Titus 2:1	But speake thou the things which become sound doctrine:
tt.2.2	Titus 2:2	That the aged men be sober, graue, temperate, sound in faith, in charitie, in patience.
tt.2.3	Titus 2:3	The aged women likewise that they be in behauiour as becommeth holinesse, not false accusers, not giuen to much wine, teachers of good things,
tt.2.4	Titus 2:4	That they may teach the young women to bee sober, to loue their husbands, to loue their children,
tt.2.5	Titus 2:5	To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God bee not blasphemed.
tt.2.6	Titus 2:6	Yong men likewise exhort, to bee sober minded.
tt.2.7	Titus 2:7	In all things shewing thy selfe a patterne of good workes: in doctrine shewing vncorruptnesse, grauity, sinceritie,
tt.2.8	Titus 2:8	Sound speech that cannot be condemned, that hee that is of the contrarie part, may bee ashamed, hauing no euill thing to say of you.
tt.2.9	Titus 2:9	Exhort seruants to be obedient vnto their own masters, and to please them well in all things, not answering againe:
tt.2.10	Titus 2:10	Not purloyning, but shewing all good fidelitie, that they may adorne the doctrine of God our Sauiour in all things.
tt.2.11	Titus 2:11	For the grace of God that bringeth saluatiō, hath appeared to all men,
tt.2.12	Titus 2:12	Teaching vs that denying vngodlinesse and worldly lusts we should liue soberly, righteously and godly in this present world,
tt.2.13	Titus 2:13	Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God, and our Sauiour Iesus Christ,
tt.2.14	Titus 2:14	Who gaue himselfe for vs, that he might redeeme vs from all iniquitie, and purifie vnto himselfe a peculiar people, zealous of good workes.
tt.2.15	Titus 2:15	These things speake and exhort, and rebuke with all authoritie. Let no man despise thee.
tt.3.1	Titus 3:1	Put them in minde to bee subiect to Principalities & Powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to euery good worke,
tt.3.2	Titus 3:2	To speake euill of no man, to bee no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekenesse vnto all men.
tt.3.3	Titus 3:3	For we our selues also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceiued, seruing diuers lusts and pleasures, liuing in malice and enuy, hatefull, and hating one another.
tt.3.4	Titus 3:4	But after that the kindnesse and loue of God our Sauiour toward man appeared,
tt.3.5	Titus 3:5	Not by workes of righteousnesse which wee haue done, but according to his mercy he saued vs, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the holy Ghost,
tt.3.6	Titus 3:6	Which hee shed on vs abundantly, through Iesus Christ our Sauiour:
tt.3.7	Titus 3:7	That being iustified by his grace, we should bee made heires according to the hope of eternall life.
tt.3.8	Titus 3:8	This is a faithfull saying, and these things I will that thou affirme constantly, that they which haue beleeued in God, might be carefull to maintaine good works: these things are good and profitable vnto men.
tt.3.9	Titus 3:9	But auoyd foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and striuings about the lawe; for they are vnprofitable and vaine.
tt.3.10	Titus 3:10	A man that is an heretike, after the first and second admonition, reiect:
tt.3.11	Titus 3:11	Knowing that hee that is such, is subuerted, and sinneth, being condemned of himselfe.
tt.3.12	Titus 3:12	When I shall send Artemas vnto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come vnto mee to Nicopolis: for I haue determined there to winter.
tt.3.13	Titus 3:13	Bring Zenas the Lawyer, and Apollos, on their iourney diligently, that nothing be wanting vnto them.
tt.3.14	Titus 3:14	And let ours also learne to maintaine good workes for necessarie vses, that they be not vnfruitfull.
tt.3.15	Titus 3:15	All that are with mee salute thee. Greete them that loue vs in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
phm.1.1	Philemon 1:1	Paul a prisoner of Iesus Christ, & Timothie our brother vnto Philemon our dearely beloued, and fellow labourer,
phm.1.2	Philemon 1:2	And to our beloued Apphia, and Archippus our fellow Souldier, and to the Church in thy house.
phm.1.3	Philemon 1:3	Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Iesus Christ.
phm.1.4	Philemon 1:4	I thanke my God, making mention of thee alwayes in my prayers,
phm.1.5	Philemon 1:5	Hearing of thy loue, and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Iesus, and toward all Saints:
phm.1.6	Philemon 1:6	That the communication of thy faith may become effectuall by the acknowledging of euery good thing, which is in you in Christ Iesus.
phm.1.7	Philemon 1:7	For wee haue great ioy and consolation in thy loue, because the bowels of the Saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
phm.1.8	Philemon 1:8	Wherefore, though I might bee much bolde in Christ to enioyne thee that which is conuenient;
phm.1.9	Philemon 1:9	Yet for loues sake I rather beseech thee, being such a one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Iesus Christ.
phm.1.10	Philemon 1:10	I beseech thee for my sonne Onesimus, whome I haue begotten in my bonds,
phm.1.11	Philemon 1:11	Which in time past was to thee vnprofitable: but now profitable to thee and to me:
phm.1.12	Philemon 1:12	Whom I haue sent againe: thou therfore receiue him, that is mine owne bowels.
phm.1.13	Philemon 1:13	Whome I would haue reteined with mee, that in thy stead hee might haue ministred vnto me in the bonds of the Gospel.
phm.1.14	Philemon 1:14	But without thy minde would I doe nothing, that thy benefite should not bee as it were of necessitie, but willingly.
phm.1.15	Philemon 1:15	For perhaps hee therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receiue him for euer:
phm.1.16	Philemon 1:16	Not now as a seruant, but aboue a seruant, a brother beloued, specially to mee, but how much more vnto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
phm.1.17	Philemon 1:17	If thou count mee therefore a partner, receiue him as my selfe.
phm.1.18	Philemon 1:18	If hee hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account.
phm.1.19	Philemon 1:19	I Paul haue written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I doe not say to thee how thou owest vnto me, euen thine owne selfe besides:
phm.1.20	Philemon 1:20	Yea, brother, let mee haue ioy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowles in the Lord.
phm.1.21	Philemon 1:21	Hauing confidence in thy obedience, I wrote vnto thee, knowing that thou wilt also doe more then I say.
phm.1.22	Philemon 1:22	But withall prepare mee also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be giuen vnto you.
phm.1.23	Philemon 1:23	There salute thee Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Iesus:
phm.1.24	Philemon 1:24	Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellow labourers.
phm.1.25	Philemon 1:25	The grace of our Lord Iesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a seruant.
hb.1.1	Hebrews 1:1	God who at sundry times, and in diuers manners, spake in time past vnto the Fathers by the Prophets,
hb.1.2	Hebrews 1:2	Hath in these last dayes spoken vnto vs by his Sonne, whom he hath appointed heire of all things, by whom also he made the worlds,
hb.1.3	Hebrews 1:3	Who being the brightnesse of his glory, and the expresse image of his person, and vpholding all things by the word of his power, when hee had by himselfe purged our sinnes, sate down on þ right hand of the Maiestie on high,
hb.1.4	Hebrews 1:4	Being made so much better then the Angels, as hee hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent Name then they.
hb.1.5	Hebrews 1:5	For vnto which of the Angels said he at any time, Thou art my sonne, this day haue I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Sonne.
hb.1.6	Hebrews 1:6	And againe, when he bringeth in the first begotten into the world, hee saith, And let all the Angels of God worship him.
hb.1.7	Hebrews 1:7	And of the Angels he saith: Who maketh his Angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
hb.1.8	Hebrews 1:8	But vnto the Sonne, he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for euer and euer: a scepter of righteousnesse is the scepter of thy kingdome.
hb.1.9	Hebrews 1:9	Thou hast loued righteousnesse, and hated iniquitie, therefore God, euen thy God hath anointed thee with the oyle of gladnesse aboue thy fellowes.
hb.1.10	Hebrews 1:10	And, thou Lord in the beginning hast layed the foundation of the earth: and the heauens are the works of thine hands.
hb.1.11	Hebrews 1:11	They shall perish, but thou remainest: and they all shal waxe old as doth a garment.
hb.1.12	Hebrews 1:12	And as a vesture shalt thou fold them vp, and they shall be changed, but thou art the same, and thy yeeres shall not faile?
hb.1.13	Hebrews 1:13	But to which of the Angels said hee at any time, Sit on my right hand, vntill I make thine enemies thy footstoole?
hb.1.14	Hebrews 1:14	Are they not all ministring spirits, sent foorth to minister for them, who shall be heires of saluation?
hb.2.1	Hebrews 2:1	Therefore we ought to giue the more earnest heede to the things which we haue heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
hb.2.2	Hebrews 2:2	For if the word spoken by Angels was stedfast, and euery transgression and disobedience receiued a iust recompense of reward:
hb.2.3	Hebrews 2:3	How shall we escape, if we neglect so great saluation, which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed vnto vs by them that heard him,
hb.2.4	Hebrews 2:4	God also bearing them witnesse, both with signes & wonders, and with diuers miracles, and gifts of the holy Ghost, according to his owne will?
hb.2.5	Hebrews 2:5	For vnto the Angels hath he not put in subiection the world to come, whereof we speake.
hb.2.6	Hebrews 2:6	But one in a certaine place testified, saying: What is man, that thou art mindfull of him: or the Sonne of man that thou visitest him?
hb.2.7	Hebrews 2:7	Thou madest him a little lower then the Angels, thou crownedst him with glory and honor, and didst set him ouer the workes of thy hands.
hb.2.8	Hebrews 2:8	Thou hast put all things in subiection vnder his feete. For in that he put all in subiection vnder him, hee left nothing that is not put vnder him. But now wee see not yet all things put vnder him.
hb.2.9	Hebrews 2:9	But wee see Iesus, who was made a little lower then the Angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour, that hee by the grace of God should taste death for euery man.
hb.2.10	Hebrews 2:10	For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sonnes vnto glory, to make the Captaine of their saluation perfect through sufferings.
hb.2.11	Hebrews 2:11	For both hee that sanctifieth, and they who are sanctified, are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to cal them brethren,
hb.2.12	Hebrews 2:12	Saying, I will declare thy Name vnto my brethren, in the midst of the Church will I sing praise vnto thee.
hb.2.13	Hebrews 2:13	And againe, I will put my trust in him: and againe, Behold, I, and the children which God hath giuen me.
hb.2.14	Hebrews 2:14	Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himselfe likewise took part of the same, that through death hee might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the deuill:
hb.2.15	Hebrews 2:15	And deliuer them, who through feare of death were all their life time subiect to bondage.
hb.2.16	Hebrews 2:16	For verely he tooke not on him the nature of Angels: but he tooke on him the seed of Abraham.
hb.2.17	Hebrews 2:17	Wherfore in all things it behooued him to bee made like vnto his brethren, that he might be a mercifull and faithfull high Priest, in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sinnes of the people.
hb.2.18	Hebrews 2:18	For in that he himselfe hath suffered, being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
hb.3.1	Hebrews 3:1	Wherfore holy brethrē, partakers of the heauenly calling, consider the Apostle and high Priest of our profession Christ Iesus,
hb.3.2	Hebrews 3:2	Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithfull in all his house.
hb.3.3	Hebrews 3:3	For this man was counted worthy of more glory then Moses, in as much as he who hath builded the house, hath more honour then the house.
hb.3.4	Hebrews 3:4	For euery house is builded by some man, but hee that built all things is God.
hb.3.5	Hebrews 3:5	And Moses verely was faithfull in all his house as a seruant, for a testimonie of those things which were to be spoken after.
hb.3.6	Hebrews 3:6	But Christ as a Sonne ouer his owne house, whose house are wee, if we hold fast the confidence, and the reioycing of the hope firme vnto the end.
hb.3.7	Hebrews 3:7	Wherfore as the holy Ghost saith, To day if ye will heare his voyce,
hb.3.8	Hebrews 3:8	Harden not your hearts, as in the prouocation, in the day of temptation in the wildernesse:
hb.3.9	Hebrews 3:9	When your fathers tempted me, prooued me, and saw my works fourty yeeres.
hb.3.10	Hebrews 3:10	Wherefore I was grieued with that generation, and sayd, They doe alway erre in their hearts, and they haue not knowen my wayes.
hb.3.11	Hebrews 3:11	So I sware in my wrath: they shall not enter into my rest.
hb.3.12	Hebrews 3:12	Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an euill heart of vnbeleefe, in departing from the liuing God.
hb.3.13	Hebrews 3:13	But exhort one another dayly, while it is called To day, least any of you be hardned through the deceitfulnesse of sinne.
hb.3.14	Hebrews 3:14	For wee are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast vnto the end.
hb.3.15	Hebrews 3:15	Whilest it is sayd, To day if yee will heare his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the prouocation.
hb.3.16	Hebrews 3:16	For some when they had heard, did prouoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
hb.3.17	Hebrews 3:17	But with whom was he grieued fourty yeeres? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wildernesse?
hb.3.18	Hebrews 3:18	And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that beleeued not?
hb.3.19	Hebrews 3:19	So we see that they could not enter in, because of vnbeleefe.
hb.4.1	Hebrews 4:1	Let vs therefore feare, lest a promise being left vs, of entring into his rest, any of you should seeme to come short of it.
hb.4.2	Hebrews 4:2	For vnto vs was the Gospel preached, as well as vnto thē: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
hb.4.3	Hebrews 4:3	For we which haue beleeued do enter into rest, as hee said, As I haue sworne in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest, although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
hb.4.4	Hebrews 4:4	For he spake in a certaine place of the seuenth day on this wise: And God did rest the seuenth day from all his works.
hb.4.5	Hebrews 4:5	And in this place againe: If they shall enter into my rest.
hb.4.6	Hebrews 4:6	Seeing therfore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and they to whom it was first preached, entred not in because of vnbeleefe:
hb.4.7	Hebrews 4:7	Againe, hee limiteth a certaine day, saying in Dauid, To day, after so long a time; as it is saide, To day if ye will heare his voyce, harden not your hearts.
hb.4.8	Hebrews 4:8	For if Iesus had giuen them rest, then would he not afterward haue spoken of another day.
hb.4.9	Hebrews 4:9	There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
hb.4.10	Hebrews 4:10	For he that is entred into his rest, hee also hath ceased from his owne works, as God did from his.
hb.4.11	Hebrews 4:11	Let vs labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of vnbeleefe.
hb.4.12	Hebrews 4:12	For the word of God is quicke and powerfull, and sharper then any two edged sword, pearcing euen to the diuiding asunder of soule and spirit, and of the ioynts and marrowe, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
hb.4.13	Hebrews 4:13	Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked, and opened vnto the eyes of him with whome wee haue to doe.
hb.4.14	Hebrews 4:14	Seeing then that wee haue a great high Priest, that is passed into the heauens, Iesus the Sonne of God, let vs hold fast our profession.
hb.4.15	Hebrews 4:15	For wee haue not an high Priest which cannot bee touched with the feeling of our infirmities: but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sinne.
hb.4.16	Hebrews 4:16	Let vs therefore come boldly vnto the throne of grace, that wee may obtaine mercy, and finde grace to helpe in time of need.
hb.5.1	Hebrews 5:1	For euery high Priest taken from among men, is ordeined for men in things pertaining to God, that hee may offer both giftes & sacrifices for sins.
hb.5.2	Hebrews 5:2	Who can haue compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way, for that he himselfe also is compassed with infirmitie.
hb.5.3	Hebrews 5:3	And by reason heereof hee ought as for the people, so also for himselfe, to offer for sinnes.
hb.5.4	Hebrews 5:4	And no man taketh this honour vnto himselfe, but hee that is called of God, as was Aaron.
hb.5.5	Hebrews 5:5	So also, Christ glorified not himselfe, to bee made an High Priest: but hee that saide vnto him, Thou art my Sonne, to day haue I begotten thee.
hb.5.6	Hebrews 5:6	As he saith also in another place, Thou art a Priest for euer after the order of Melchisedec.
hb.5.7	Hebrews 5:7	Who in the dayes of his flesh, when hee had offered vp prayers and supplications, with strong crying and teares, vnto him that was able to saue him from death, and was heard, in that he feared.
hb.5.8	Hebrews 5:8	Though hee were a Sonne, yet learned hee obedience, by the things which he suffered:
hb.5.9	Hebrews 5:9	And being made perfect, he became the authour of eternall saluation vnto all them that obey him,
hb.5.10	Hebrews 5:10	Called of God an high Priest after the order of Melchisedec:
hb.5.11	Hebrews 5:11	Of whom we haue many things to say, and hard to be vttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.
hb.5.12	Hebrews 5:12	For when for the time yee ought to bee teachers, yee haue neede that one teach you againe which be the first principles of the Oracles of God, and are become such as haue need of milke, and not of strong meat.
hb.5.13	Hebrews 5:13	For euery one that vseth milke, is vnskilful in the word of righteousnes: for he is a babe.
hb.5.14	Hebrews 5:14	But strong meate belongeth to them that are of full age, euen those who by reason of vse haue their senses exercised to discerne both good and euil.
hb.6.1	Hebrews 6:1	Therefore leauing the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let vs goe on vnto perfection, not laying againe the foundation of repentance from dead workes, and of faith towards God,
hb.6.2	Hebrews 6:2	Of the doctrine of Baptismes, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternall iudgement.
hb.6.3	Hebrews 6:3	And this will we doe, if God permit.
hb.6.4	Hebrews 6:4	For it is impossible for those who were once inlightned, and haue tasted of the heauenly gift, and were made partakers of the holy Ghost,
hb.6.5	Hebrews 6:5	And haue tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come;
hb.6.6	Hebrews 6:6	If they shall fall away, to renue them againe vnto repentance: seeing they crucifie to themselues the Sonne of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
hb.6.7	Hebrews 6:7	For the earth which drinketh in the raine that commeth oft vpon it, and bringeth forth herbes meet for them by whome it is dressed, receiueth blessing from God.
hb.6.8	Hebrews 6:8	But that which beareth thornes and briers, is reiected, and is nigh vnto cursing, whose end is to be burned.
hb.6.9	Hebrews 6:9	But beloued, wee are perswaded better things of you, and things that accompany saluation, though we thus speake.
hb.6.10	Hebrews 6:10	For God is not vnrighteous, to forget your worke and labour of loue, which yee haue shewed toward his Name, in that yee haue ministred to the Saints, and doe minister.
hb.6.11	Hebrews 6:11	And wee desire, that euery one of you doe shewe the same diligence, to the full assurance of hope vnto the ende:
hb.6.12	Hebrews 6:12	That yee be not slothfull, but followers of them, who through faith and patience inherite the promises.
hb.6.13	Hebrews 6:13	For when God made promise to Abraham, because hee could sweare by no greater, he sware by himselfe,
hb.6.14	Hebrews 6:14	Saying, Surely, blessing I will blesse thee, and multiplying I wil multiply thee.
hb.6.15	Hebrews 6:15	And so after he had patiently indured, he obtained the promise.
hb.6.16	Hebrews 6:16	For men verily sweare by the greater, and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
hb.6.17	Hebrews 6:17	Wherein God willing more abundantly to shewe vnto the heyres of promise the immutabilitie of his counsell, confirmed it by an oath:
hb.6.18	Hebrews 6:18	That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lye, wee might haue a strong consolation, who haue fled for refuge to lay hold vpon the hope set before vs.
hb.6.19	Hebrews 6:19	Which hope we haue as an anker of the soule both sure and stedfast, and which entreth into that within the vaile,
hb.6.20	Hebrews 6:20	Whither the forerunner is for vs entrrd; euen Iesus, made an high Priest for euer after the order of Melchisedec.
hb.7.1	Hebrews 7:1	For this Melchisedec king of Salem, Priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the Kings, and blessed him:
hb.7.2	Hebrews 7:2	To whom also Abraham gaue a tenth part of all: first being by interpretation king of righteousnesse, and after that also king of Salem, which is, king of peace.
hb.7.3	Hebrews 7:3	Without father, without mother, without descent, hauing neither beginning of dayes nor end of life: but made like vnto the Sonne of God, abideth a Priest continually.
hb.7.4	Hebrews 7:4	Now consider how great this man was, vnto whō euen the patriarch Abraham gaue the tenth of the spoiles.
hb.7.5	Hebrews 7:5	And verily they that are of the sonnes of Leui, who receiue the office of the Priesthood, haue a commandement to take Tithes of the people according to the Law, that is of their brethren, though they come out of the loines of Abraham:
hb.7.6	Hebrews 7:6	But he whose descent is not counted from them, receiued tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
hb.7.7	Hebrews 7:7	And without all contradiction, the lesse is blessed of the better.
hb.7.8	Hebrews 7:8	And here men that die receiue tithes: but there hee receiueth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liueth.
hb.7.9	Hebrews 7:9	And as I may so say, Leui also who receiueth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
hb.7.10	Hebrews 7:10	For hee was yet in the loynes of his Father when Melchisedec met him.
hb.7.11	Hebrews 7:11	If therefore perfection were by the Leuiticall Priesthood (for vnder it the people receiued the Law) what further neede was there, that another Priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not bee called after the order of Aaron?
hb.7.12	Hebrews 7:12	For the Priesthood being chaunged, there is made of necessitie a change also of the Law.
hb.7.13	Hebrews 7:13	For hee of whom these things are spoken, pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gaue attendance at the Altar.
hb.7.14	Hebrews 7:14	For it is euident that our Lorde sprang out of Iuda, of which tribe Moses spake nothing cōcerning Priesthood.
hb.7.15	Hebrews 7:15	And it is yet farre more euident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another Priest,
hb.7.16	Hebrews 7:16	Who is made not after the Law of a carnall commandement, but after the power of an endles life.
hb.7.17	Hebrews 7:17	For hee testifieth; Thou art a Priest for euer, after the order of Melchisedec.
hb.7.18	Hebrews 7:18	For there is verily a disanulling of the commandement going before, for the weakenesse and vnprofitablenesse thereof.
hb.7.19	Hebrews 7:19	For the Law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did: by the which wee draw nigh vnto God.
hb.7.20	Hebrews 7:20	And in as much as not without an othe he was made Priest,
hb.7.21	Hebrews 7:21	(For those Priests were made without an oath: but this with an oath, by him þ said vnto him, The Lord sware and wil not repent, thou art a Priest for euer after the order of Melchisedec)
hb.7.22	Hebrews 7:22	By so much was Iesus made a suertie of a better Testament.
hb.7.23	Hebrews 7:23	And they truely were many Priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death.
hb.7.24	Hebrews 7:24	But this man because hee continueth euer, hath an vnchangeable Priesthood.
hb.7.25	Hebrews 7:25	Wherefore he is able also to saue them to the vttermost, that come vnto God by him, seeing hee euer liueth to make intercession for them.
hb.7.26	Hebrews 7:26	For such an high Priest became vs, who is holy, harmelesse, vndefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher then the heauens.
hb.7.27	Hebrews 7:27	Who needeth not daily, as those high Priests, to offer vp sacrifice, first for his owne sins and then for the peoples: for this he did once, when he offered vp himselfe.
hb.7.28	Hebrews 7:28	For the Law maketh men high Priests which haue infirmitie, but the word of the othe which was since the Law, maketh the Sonne, who is consecrated for euermore.
hb.8.1	Hebrews 8:1	Now of the things which we haue spoken, this is the summe: wee haue such an high Priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Maiestie in the heauens:
hb.8.2	Hebrews 8:2	A minister of the Sanctuary, and of the true Tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
hb.8.3	Hebrews 8:3	For euery high Priest is ordeined to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessitie that this man haue somewhat also to offer.
hb.8.4	Hebrews 8:4	For if he were on earth, he should not bee a Priest, seeing that there are Priests that offer gifts according to the Law:
hb.8.5	Hebrews 8:5	Who serue vnto the example and shadow of heauenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the Tabernacle. For see (saith he) that thou make all things according to the paterne shewed to thee in the mount.
hb.8.6	Hebrews 8:6	But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministerie, by how much also he is the Mediatour of a better Couenant, which was established vpon better promises.
hb.8.7	Hebrews 8:7	For if that first Couenant had bene faultles, then should no place haue bene sought for the second.
hb.8.8	Hebrews 8:8	For finding fault with them, hee saith, Behold, the dayes come (saith the Lord) when I will make a new couenant with the house of Israel, and the house of Iudah.
hb.8.9	Hebrews 8:9	Not according to the Couenant that I made with their fathers, in the day when I tooke them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they continued not in my Couenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.
hb.8.10	Hebrews 8:10	For this is the Couenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those dayes, saith the Lord: I wil put my Lawes into their minde, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shalbe to me a people.
hb.8.11	Hebrews 8:11	And they shall not teach euery man his neighbour, and euery man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: For all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
hb.8.12	Hebrews 8:12	For I will be mercifull to their vnrighteousnes, and their sins & their iniquities will I remember no more.
hb.8.13	Hebrews 8:13	In that he saith, A new Couenant, he hath made the first olde. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old, is readie to vanish away.
hb.9.1	Hebrews 9:1	Then verily the first Couenant had also ordinances of diuine Seruice, and a worldly Sanctuary.
hb.9.2	Hebrews 9:2	For there was a Tabernacle made, the first, wherein was the Candlesticke, and the Table, and the Shewbread, which is called the Sanctuarie.
hb.9.3	Hebrews 9:3	And after the second vaile, the Tabernacle which is called þ Holiest of all:
hb.9.4	Hebrews 9:4	Which had the golden Censor, and the Arke of the Couenant ouerlayed round about with gold, wherein was the Golden pot that had Manna, and Aarons rod that budded, and the Tables of the Couenant.
hb.9.5	Hebrews 9:5	And ouer it the Cherubims of glory shadowing the Mercyseat; of which we cannot now speake particularly.
hb.9.6	Hebrews 9:6	Now when these things were thus ordained, the Priestes went alwayes into the first Tabernacle, accomplishing the seruice of God.
hb.9.7	Hebrews 9:7	But into the second went the high Priest alone once euery yeere, not without blood, which he offered for himselfe, and for the errors of the people.
hb.9.8	Hebrews 9:8	The holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the Holiest of all, was not yet made manifest, while as the first Tabernacle was yet standing:
hb.9.9	Hebrews 9:9	Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offred both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the seruice perfect, as pertayning to the conscience,
hb.9.10	Hebrews 9:10	Which stood onely in meates and drinkes, and diuers washings, and carnall ordinances imposed on them vntill the time of reformation.
hb.9.11	Hebrews 9:11	But Christ being come an high Priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect Tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building:
hb.9.12	Hebrews 9:12	Neither by the blood of Goats and Calues: but by his owne blood hee entred in once into the Holy place, hauing obtained eternall redemption for vs.
hb.9.13	Hebrews 9:13	For if the blood of Bulls, and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the vncleane, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:
hb.9.14	Hebrews 9:14	How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit, offered himselfe without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead workes, to serue the liuing God?
hb.9.15	Hebrews 9:15	And for this cause hee is the Mediatour of the New Testament, that by meanes of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were vnder the first Testament, they which are called, might receiue the promise of eternall inheritance.
hb.9.16	Hebrews 9:16	For where a Testament is, there must also of necessitie bee the death of the Testatour.
hb.9.17	Hebrews 9:17	For a Testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all whilest the Testatour liueth.
hb.9.18	Hebrews 9:18	Whereupon, neither the first Testament was dedicated without blood.
hb.9.19	Hebrews 9:19	For when Moses had spoken euery precept to all the people according to the Law, he tooke the blood of Calues and of Goates, with water and scarlet wooll, and hysope, and sprinckled both the booke and all the people,
hb.9.20	Hebrews 9:20	Saying, This is the blood of the Testament which God hath enioyned vnto you.
hb.9.21	Hebrews 9:21	Moreouer, hee sprinkled with blood both the Tabernacle, and all the vessels of the Ministery.
hb.9.22	Hebrews 9:22	And almost all things are by the Law purged with blood: and without shedding of blood is no remission.
hb.9.23	Hebrews 9:23	It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heauens should bee purified with these, but the heauenly things themselues with better sacrifices then these.
hb.9.24	Hebrews 9:24	For Christ is not entred into the Holy places made with handes, which are the figures of the true, but into heauen it selfe, now to appeare in the presence of God for vs.
hb.9.25	Hebrews 9:25	Nor yet that he should offer himselfe often, as the high Priest entreth into the Holy place, euery yeere with blood of others:
hb.9.26	Hebrews 9:26	For then must hee often haue suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world, hath he appeared to put away sinne by the sacrifice of himselfe.
hb.9.27	Hebrews 9:27	And as it is appointed vnto men once to die, but after this the Iudgement:
hb.9.28	Hebrews 9:28	So Christ was once offered to beare the sinnes of many, & vnto them that looke for him shall hee appeare the second time without sinne, vnto saluation.
hb.10.1	Hebrews 10:1	For the Law hauing a shadow of good things to come, and not the very Image of the things, can neuer with those sacrifices which they offered yeere by yeere continually, make the commers thereunto perfect:
hb.10.2	Hebrews 10:2	For then would they not haue ceased to be offered, because that the worshippers once purged, should haue had no more conscience of sinnes?
hb.10.3	Hebrews 10:3	But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance againe made of sinnes euery yeere.
hb.10.4	Hebrews 10:4	For it is not possible that the blood of Bulles and of Goats, should take away sinnes.
hb.10.5	Hebrews 10:5	Wherefore when hee commeth into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared mee:
hb.10.6	Hebrews 10:6	In burnt offerings, and sacrifices for sinne thou hast had no pleasure:
hb.10.7	Hebrews 10:7	Then said I, Loe, I come. (In the volume of the booke it is written of me) to doe thy will, O God.
hb.10.8	Hebrews 10:8	Aboue when hee said, Sacrifice, and offering, and burnt offerings, and offering for sinne thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein, which are offered by the Law:
hb.10.9	Hebrews 10:9	Then said he, Loe, I come to doe thy will (O God:) He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
hb.10.10	Hebrews 10:10	By the which will wee are sanctified, through the offering of the body of Iesus Christ once for all.
hb.10.11	Hebrews 10:11	And euery Priest standeth dayly ministring and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices which can neuer take away sinnes.
hb.10.12	Hebrews 10:12	But this man after he had offered one sacrifice for sinnes for euer, sate downe on the right hand of God,
hb.10.13	Hebrews 10:13	From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstoole.
hb.10.14	Hebrews 10:14	For by one offering hee hath perfected for euer them that are sanctified.
hb.10.15	Hebrews 10:15	Whereof the holy Ghost also is a witnesse to vs: for after that he had said before,
hb.10.16	Hebrews 10:16	This is the Couenant that I wil make with them after those dayes, saith the Lord: I will put my Lawes into their hearts, and in their mindes will I write them:
hb.10.17	Hebrews 10:17	And their sinnes and iniquities will I remember no more.
hb.10.18	Hebrews 10:18	Now, where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sinne.
hb.10.19	Hebrews 10:19	Hauing therefore, brethren, boldnesse to enter into the Holiest by the blood of Iesus,
hb.10.20	Hebrews 10:20	By a new and liuing way which hee hath consecrated for vs, through the vaile, that is to say, His flesh:
hb.10.21	Hebrews 10:21	And hauing an high Priest ouer the house of God:
hb.10.22	Hebrews 10:22	Let vs drawe neere with a true heart in full assurance of faith, hauing our hearts sprinkled from an euill conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
hb.10.23	Hebrews 10:23	Let vs hold fast the profession of our faith without wauering (for he is faithfull that promised)
hb.10.24	Hebrews 10:24	And let vs consider one another to prouoke vnto loue, and to good workes:
hb.10.25	Hebrews 10:25	Not forsaking the assembling of our selues together, as the manner of some is: but exhorting one another, and so much the more, as ye see the day approching.
hb.10.26	Hebrews 10:26	For if we sinne wilfully after that we haue receiued the knowledge of the trueth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sinnes,
hb.10.27	Hebrews 10:27	But a certaine fearefull looking for of iudgement, and fiery indignation, which shall deuoure the aduersaries.
hb.10.28	Hebrews 10:28	Hee that despised Moses Lawe, died without mercy, vnder two or three witnesses.
hb.10.29	Hebrews 10:29	Of how much sorer punishment suppose ye, shall hee be thought worthy, who hath troden vnder foote þ Sonne of God, and hath counted the blood of the couenant wherwith he was sanctified, an vnholy thing, and hath done despite vnto the spirit of grace?
hb.10.30	Hebrews 10:30	For we know him that hath said, Uengeance belongeth vnto me, I wil recompence, saith the Lord: and again, The Lord shall iudge his people.
hb.10.31	Hebrews 10:31	It is a fearefull thing to fall into the hands of the liuing God.
hb.10.32	Hebrews 10:32	But call to remembrance the former dayes, in which after yee were illuminated, ye indured a great fight of afflictions:
hb.10.33	Hebrews 10:33	Partly whilest ye were made a gazing stocke both by reproches & afflictions, and partly whilest ye became companions of them that were so vsed.
hb.10.34	Hebrews 10:34	For yee had compassion of me in my bonds, and tooke ioyfully the spoyling of your goods, knowing in your selues that yee haue in heauen a better and an induring substance.
hb.10.35	Hebrews 10:35	Cast not away therfore your confidence which hath great recompense of reward.
hb.10.36	Hebrews 10:36	For ye haue need of patience, that shall after ye haue done the will of God ye might receiue the promise.
hb.10.37	Hebrews 10:37	For yet a litle while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tary.
hb.10.38	Hebrews 10:38	Now the iust shall liue by faith: but if any man drawe backe, my soule shall haue no pleasure in him.
hb.10.39	Hebrews 10:39	But wee are not of them who draw backe vnto perdition: but of them that beleeue, to the sauing of the soule.
hb.11.1	Hebrews 11:1	Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the euidence of things not seen.
hb.11.2	Hebrews 11:2	For by it the Elders obtained a good report.
hb.11.3	Hebrews 11:3	Through faith we vnderstand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seene were not made of things which doe appeare.
hb.11.4	Hebrews 11:4	By faith Abel offered vnto God a more excellent sacrifice then Kain, by which he obtained witnes that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead, yet speaketh.
hb.11.5	Hebrews 11:5	By faith Enoch was translated, that he should not see death, and was not found, because God had translated him: For before his translation he had this testimonie, that he pleased God.
hb.11.6	Hebrews 11:6	But without faith it is impossible to please him: for hee that commeth to God, must beleeue that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seeke him.
hb.11.7	Hebrews 11:7	By faith Noah being warned of God of things not seene as yet, moued with feare, prepared an Arke to the sauing of his house, by the which he condemned the world, and became heire of the righteousnesse which is by faith.
hb.11.8	Hebrews 11:8	By faith Abraham when he was called to goe out into a place which hee should after receiue for an inheritance, obeyed, and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
hb.11.9	Hebrews 11:9	By faith hee soiourned in the land of promise, as in a strange countrey, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Iacob, the heires with him of the same promise.
hb.11.10	Hebrews 11:10	For hee looked for a citie which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
hb.11.11	Hebrews 11:11	Through faith also Sara her selfe receiued strength to conceiue seede, and was deliuered of a child when she was past age, because she iudged him faithful who had promised.
hb.11.12	Hebrews 11:12	Therfore sprang there euen of one, and him as good as dead, so many as the starres of the skie in multitude, and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable.
hb.11.13	Hebrews 11:13	These all died in faith, not hauing receiued the promises, but hauing seene them a farre off, and were perswaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
hb.11.14	Hebrews 11:14	For they that say such things, declare plainly that they seeke a countrey.
hb.11.15	Hebrews 11:15	And truly if they had been mindfull of that countrey, from whence they came out, they might haue had opportunitie to haue returned:
hb.11.16	Hebrews 11:16	But now they desire a better countrey, that is, an heauenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to bee called their God: for he hath prepared for thē a city.
hb.11.17	Hebrews 11:17	By faith Abraham when he was tried, offered vp Isaac: and he that had receiued the promises, offered vp his onely begotten sonne,
hb.11.18	Hebrews 11:18	Of whom it was said, That, in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
hb.11.19	Hebrews 11:19	Accounting that God was able to raise him vp, euen from the dead: from whence also he receiued him in a figure.
hb.11.20	Hebrews 11:20	By faith Isaac blessed Iacob and Esau concerning things to come.
hb.11.21	Hebrews 11:21	By faith Iacob when hee was a dying, blessed both the sonnes of Ioseph, and worshipped leaning vpon the top of his staffe.
hb.11.22	Hebrews 11:22	By faith, Ioseph when hee died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel: and gaue commandement concerning his bones.
hb.11.23	Hebrews 11:23	By faith; Moses when hee was borne was hid three moneths of his parents, because they saw he was a proper childe, and they not afraid of the Kings commandement.
hb.11.24	Hebrews 11:24	By faith Moses when hee was come to yeeres, refused to bee called the sonne of Pharaohs daughter,
hb.11.25	Hebrews 11:25	Chusing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, then to enioy the pleasures of sinne for a season:
hb.11.26	Hebrews 11:26	Esteeming the reproch of Christ greater riches then the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect vnto the recompense of the reward.
hb.11.27	Hebrews 11:27	By faith hee forsooke Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he indured, as seeing him who is inuisible.
hb.11.28	Hebrews 11:28	Through faith he kept the Passeouer, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the first borne, should touch them.
hb.11.29	Hebrews 11:29	By faith they passed through the red sea, as by drie land: which the Egyptians assaying to do, were drowned.
hb.11.30	Hebrews 11:30	By faith the walles of Iericho fell downe, after they were compassed about seuen dayes.
hb.11.31	Hebrews 11:31	By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that beleeued not, when shee had receiued the spies with peace.
hb.11.32	Hebrews 11:32	And what shall I more say? for the time would faile mee to tell of Gideon, and of Barak, and of Sampson, and of Iephthah, of Dauid also and Samuel, and of the Prophets:
hb.11.33	Hebrews 11:33	Who through faith subdued kingdomes, wrought righteousnesse, obteined promises, stopped the mouthes of Lions,
hb.11.34	Hebrews 11:34	Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakenesse were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens.
hb.11.35	Hebrews 11:35	Women receiued their dead raised to life againe: and others were tortured, not accepting deliuerance, that they might obtaine a better resurrection.
hb.11.36	Hebrews 11:36	And others had triall of cruell mockings and scourgings, yea moreouer, of bonds and imprisonment.
hb.11.37	Hebrews 11:37	They were stoned, they were sawen asunder, were tempted, were slaine with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskinnes, and goat skins, being destitute, afflicted, tormented.
hb.11.38	Hebrews 11:38	Of whome the world was not worthy: they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dennes and caues of the earth.
hb.11.39	Hebrews 11:39	And these all hauing obtained a good report through faith, receiued not the promise:
hb.11.40	Hebrews 11:40	God hauing prouided some better thing for vs, that they without vs, should not be made perfect.
hb.12.1	Hebrews 12:1	Wherefore, seeing wee also are compassed about with so great a cloude of witnesses, let vs lay aside euery weight, & the sinne which doth so easily beset vs, and let vs runne with patience vnto the race that is set before vs,
hb.12.2	Hebrews 12:2	Looking vnto Iesus the Authour and finisher of our faith, who for the ioy that was set before him, endured the crosse, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
hb.12.3	Hebrews 12:3	For consider him that indured such contradiction of sinners against himselfe, lest ye be wearied and faint in your mindes.
hb.12.4	Hebrews 12:4	Yee haue not yet resisted vnto blood, striuing against sinne.
hb.12.5	Hebrews 12:5	And ye haue forgotten the exhortation which speaketh vnto you as vnto children, My sonne, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him.
hb.12.6	Hebrews 12:6	For whome the Lord loueth hee chasteneth, and scourgeth euery sonne whom he receiueth.
hb.12.7	Hebrews 12:7	If yee endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sonnes: for what sonne is he whom the father chasteneth not?
hb.12.8	Hebrews 12:8	But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sonnes.
hb.12.9	Hebrews 12:9	Furthermore, wee haue had fathers of our flesh, which corrected vs, and we gaue them reuerence: shall we not much rather bee in subiection vnto the Father of Spirits, and liue?
hb.12.10	Hebrews 12:10	For they verily for a fewe dayes chastened vs after their owne pleasure, but hee for our profit, that we might bee partakers of his holinesse.
hb.12.11	Hebrews 12:11	Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be ioyous, but grieuous: neuerthelesse, afterward it yeeldeth the peaceable fruite of righteousnesse, vnto them which are exercised thereby.
hb.12.12	Hebrews 12:12	Wherefore lift vp the handes which hang downe, and the feeble knees.
hb.12.13	Hebrews 12:13	And make straight paths for your feete, lest that which is lame bee turned out of the way, but let it rather bee healed.
hb.12.14	Hebrews 12:14	Followe peace with all men, and holinesse, without which no man shall see the Lord:
hb.12.15	Hebrews 12:15	Looking diligently, lest any man faile of the grace of God, lest any roote of bitternesse springing vp, trouble you, and thereby many be defiled:
hb.12.16	Hebrews 12:16	Lest there bee any fornicatour, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsell of meat sold his birthright.
hb.12.17	Hebrews 12:17	For yee know how that afterward when hee would haue inherited the blessing, hee was reiected: for hee found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with teares.
hb.12.18	Hebrews 12:18	For yee are not come vnto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, nor vnto blacknesse, and darknes, and tempest,
hb.12.19	Hebrews 12:19	And the sound of a trumpet, and the voyce of wordes, which voyce they that heard, entreated that the word should not bee spoken to them any more.
hb.12.20	Hebrews 12:20	For they could not indure that which was commaunded: And if so much as a beast touch the Mountaine, it shall be stoned, or thrust thorow with a dart.
hb.12.21	Hebrews 12:21	And so terrible was the sight, that Moses sayde, I exceedingly feare, and quake.
hb.12.22	Hebrews 12:22	But ye are come vnto mount Sion, and vnto the citie of the liuing God the heauenly Ierusalem, and to an innumerable company of Angels:
hb.12.23	Hebrews 12:23	To the generall assembly, and Church of the first borne which are written in heauen, and to God the Iudge of all, and to the spirits of iust men made perfect:
hb.12.24	Hebrews 12:24	And to Iesus the mediatour of the new Couenant, and to the blood of sprinckling, that speaketh better things then that of Abel.
hb.12.25	Hebrews 12:25	See that yee refuse not him that speaketh: for if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape if wee turne away from him that speaketh from heauen.
hb.12.26	Hebrews 12:26	Whose voice then shooke the earth, but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth onely, but also heauen.
hb.12.27	Hebrews 12:27	And this word Yet once more, signifieth the remouing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remaine.
hb.12.28	Hebrews 12:28	Wherefore wee receiuing a kingdome which cannot bee moued, let vs haue grace, whereby wee may serue God acceptably, with reuerence and godly feare.
hb.12.29	Hebrews 12:29	For our God is a consuming fire.
hb.13.1	Hebrews 13:1	Let brotherly loue continue.
hb.13.2	Hebrews 13:2	Bee not forgetfull to entertaine strangers, for thereby some haue entertayned Angels vnawares.
hb.13.3	Hebrews 13:3	Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer aduersitie, as being your selues also in the body.
hb.13.4	Hebrews 13:4	Mariage is honorable in all, and the bed vndefiled: but whoremongers, and adulterers God will iudge.
hb.13.5	Hebrews 13:5	Let your conuersation bee without couetousnesse: and be content with such things as yee haue. For hee hath said, I will neuer leaue thee, nor forsake thee.
hb.13.6	Hebrews 13:6	So that wee may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not feare what man shall doe vnto me.
hb.13.7	Hebrews 13:7	Remember them which haue the rule ouer you, who haue spoken vnto you the word of God, whose faith follow, considering the end of their conuersation.
hb.13.8	Hebrews 13:8	Iesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for euer.
hb.13.9	Hebrews 13:9	Be not caried about with diuers and strange doctrines: for it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace, not with meates, which haue not profited them that haue beene occupied therein.
hb.13.10	Hebrews 13:10	Wee haue an altar whereof they haue no right to eate, which serue the Tabernacle.
hb.13.11	Hebrews 13:11	For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the Sanctuary by the high Priest for sinne, are burnt without the campe.
hb.13.12	Hebrews 13:12	Wherefore Iesus also, that hee might sanctifie the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.
hb.13.13	Hebrews 13:13	Let vs goe foorth therefore vnto him without the campe, bearing his reproch.
hb.13.14	Hebrews 13:14	For here haue we no continuing citie, but we seeke one to come.
hb.13.15	Hebrews 13:15	By him therefore let vs offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lippes, giuing thankes to his Name.
hb.13.16	Hebrews 13:16	But to doe good, and to communicate forget not, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
hb.13.17	Hebrews 13:17	Obey them that haue the rule ouer you, and submit your selues: for they watch for your soules, as they that must giue account, that they may doe it with ioy, and not with griefe: for that is vnprofitable for you.
hb.13.18	Hebrews 13:18	Pray for vs: for we trust wee haue a good conscience in all things, willing to liue honestly.
hb.13.19	Hebrews 13:19	But I beseech you the rather to doe this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
hb.13.20	Hebrews 13:20	Now the God of peace, that brought againe from the dead our Lord Iesus, that great shepheard of the sheepe, through the blood of the euerlasting Couenant,
hb.13.21	Hebrews 13:21	Make you perfect in euery good worke to doe his will, working in you that which is well pleasing in his sight, through Iesus Christ, to whom be glorie for euer and euer. Amen.
hb.13.22	Hebrews 13:22	And I beseech you brethren, suffer the word of exhortation, for I haue written a letter vnto you in few words.
hb.13.23	Hebrews 13:23	Know yee, that our brother Timothie is set at libertie, with whom if he come shortly, I will see you.
hb.13.24	Hebrews 13:24	Salute all them that haue the rule ouer you, and al the Saints. They of Italy salute you.
hb.13.25	Hebrews 13:25	Grace be with you all. Amen.
jm.1.1	James 1:1	Iames a seruant of God, and of the Lord Iesus Christ, to the twelue Tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.
jm.1.2	James 1:2	My brethren, count it all ioy when ye fall into diuers temptations,
jm.1.3	James 1:3	Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience,
jm.1.4	James 1:4	But let patience haue her perfect worke, that ye may be perfect, and entier, wanting nothing.
jm.1.5	James 1:5	If any of you lacke wisedome, let him aske of God, that giueth to all men liberally, and vpbraideth not: and it shalbe giuen him.
jm.1.6	James 1:6	But let him aske in faith, nothing wauering: for he that wauereth is like a waue of the sea, driuen with the wind, and tossed.
jm.1.7	James 1:7	For let not that man thinke that he shall receiue any thing of the Lord.
jm.1.8	James 1:8	A double minded man is vnstable in all his wayes.
jm.1.9	James 1:9	Let the brother of low degree, reioyce in that he is exalted:
jm.1.10	James 1:10	But the rich, in that hee is made low: because as the floure of the grasse he shall passe away.
jm.1.11	James 1:11	For the Sunne is no sooner risen with a burning heate, but it withereth the grasse; and the flowre thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his wayes.
jm.1.12	James 1:12	Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when hee is tried, hee shall receiue the crowne of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that loue him.
jm.1.13	James 1:13	Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with euill, neither tempteth he any man.
jm.1.14	James 1:14	But euery man is tempted, when hee is drawen away of his owne lust, and entised.
jm.1.15	James 1:15	Then when lust hath conceiued, it bringeth forth sinne: and sinne, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.
jm.1.16	James 1:16	Doe not erre, my beloued brethren.
jm.1.17	James 1:17	Euery good gift, and euery perfect gift is from aboue, & commeth downe from the Father of lights, with whom is no variablenesse, neither shadow of turning.
jm.1.18	James 1:18	Of his owne will begate hee vs, with the word of Trueth, that wee should bee a kinde of first fruites of his creatures.
jm.1.19	James 1:19	Wherefore my beloued brethren, let euery man bee swift to heare, slow to speake, slow to wrath.
jm.1.20	James 1:20	For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousnesse of God.
jm.1.21	James 1:21	Wherefore lay apart all filthinesse, and superfluitie of naughtinesse, & receiue with meeknesse the engrafted word, which is able to saue your soules.
jm.1.22	James 1:22	But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers onely, receiuing your owne selues.
jm.1.23	James 1:23	For if any be a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like vnto a man beholding his naturall face in a glasse:
jm.1.24	James 1:24	For hee beholdeth himselfe, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what maner of man he was.
jm.1.25	James 1:25	But who so looketh into the perfect Law of libertie, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetfull hearer, but a doer of the worke, this man shall be blessed in his deed.
jm.1.26	James 1:26	If any man among you seeme to be religious, & bridleth not his tongue, but deceiueth his owne heart, this mans religion is vaine.
jm.1.27	James 1:27	Pure religion and vndefiled before God and the Facher, is this, to visit the fatherlesse and widowes in their affliction, and to keepe himselfe vnspotted from the world.
jm.2.1	James 2:1	My brethren, haue not the faith of our Lord Iesus Christ the Lord of glorie, with respect of persons.
jm.2.2	James 2:2	For if there come vnto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poore man, in vile raiment:
jm.2.3	James 2:3	And yee haue respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say vnto him, Sit thou here in a good place: and say to the poore, Stand thou there, or sit here vnder my footstoole:
jm.2.4	James 2:4	Are yee not then partiall in your selues, and are become iudges of euill thoughts?
